Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
1 
 
ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT 
[Enforcement Date: October 31, 2025]  
[Ordinance of the Prime Minister No. 2060; October 31, 2025] 
Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (Medical Device Policy Division) 
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe the matters mandated by the Medical 
Devices Act and the Enforcement Decree of that Act and matters necessary for the enforcement of 
said Act and Decree. 
 
Article 2 (Standards for Classification and Designation of Classes) The standards and 
procedures for the classification and designation of the class of each medical device under Article 3 
(2) of the Medical Devices Act (hereinafter the “Act”) shall be as specified in Annex 1. 
 
Article 3 (Procedures for Application for Manufacturing Business Approval) (1) A person who 
intends to obtain manufacturing business approval for medical devices under the text of Article 6 (1) 
of the Act shall submit an application in Form 1 (including an application in electronic form) to the 
Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety who has jurisdiction over the 
location of a manufacturing site, along with the following documents (including electronic 
documents). In such cases, where there exist at least two manufacturing sites in different locations, 
such person may submit the application to the Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and 
Drug Safety with jurisdiction over either of such locations. <amended on Jan. 16, 2024; Apr. 01, 
2025> 
1. 
A medical certificate for which 6 months have not elapsed since the issuance date and 
which is issued by a medical doctor evidencing that he or she does not fall under the text 
of Article 6 (1) 1 of the Act or by a medical specialist evidencing that he or she falls 
under the proviso of that subparagraph (a corporation shall not submit such medical 
certificate); 
2. 
A medical certificate for which 6 months have not elapsed since the issuance date and 
which is issued by a medical doctor evidencing that he or she does not fall under Article 6 
(1) 3 of the Act (a corporation shall not submit such medical certificate); 
3. 
Documents concerning the quality manager (hereinafter referred to as the “quality manager”), 
whose qualifications shall be verified pursuant to Article 6 (7) of the Act, as follows: 
(a)  Documents verifying the qualifications under Article 11 (2). Provided, however, that 
submission of such documents shall be exempted if the qualification of the quality 
manager has previously been verified through the integrated medical device 
information system pursuant to Article 31-3 (1) of the Act; 
(b)  Documents verifying employment status, such as a certificate of employment. 
(2) Upon receipt of an application under Paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Regional Office 
of Food and Drug Safety shall verify an applicant’s corporation registration certificate (limited 
to a corporation) through administrative data matching under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic 
Government Act. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
2 
 
(3) When an application for approval under Paragraph (1) meets the standards, the Commissioner 
of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety shall issue the license in Form 2 to the 
applicant and state the following matters in the manufacturing business license register: 
<Amended on Oct. 22, 2019> 
1. 
Approval number and approval date; 
2. 
The name and resident registration number of the manufacturer (in case of a 
corporation, the name and resident registration number of its representative); 
3. 
The name and location of the manufacturing site; 
4. 
The name, resident registration number, and classification of qualifications of the quality 
manager. 
 
Article 4 (Medical Devices Subject to Manufacturing Approval, Manufacturing Certification, 
or Manufacturing Notification) (1) Medical devices subject to manufacturing certification or 
manufacturing notification by item category under Article 6 (2) 1 of the Act shall be classified as 
follows: 
1. 
Manufacturing certification by item category: Medical devices determined and publicly 
notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, among Class II medical devices, the 
class of which is designated following Article 2 (hereinafter “class”); 
2. 
Manufacturing notification by item category: Medical devices determined and publicly 
notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, among Class I medical devices. 
(2) Medical devices subject to manufacturing approval, manufacturing certification, or 
manufacturing notification by item under Article 6 (2) 2 of the Act shall be classified as 
follows: <amended on Mar. 8, 2024; Aug. 7, 2024> 
1. 
Manufacturing approval by item: The following medical devices: 
(a) Class III and Class IV medical devices; 
(b) Medical devices excluding those under Paragraph (1) 1, Item (c) of this 
Subparagraph, and Subparagraph 2 of this Paragraph, among Class II medical 
devices; 
(c) Medical devices that are essentially different from those already approved, certified, 
or notified in terms of structure, mode of action, performance, intended uses, 
utilization methods, etc. among Class II medical devices (medical devices for export 
shall be excluded); 
2. 
Manufacturing certification by item: Medical devices determined and publicly notified by 
the Minister of Food and Drug Safety excluding those under Subparagraph 1 of Paragraph 
(1), among Class II medical devices; 
3. 
Manufacturing notification by item: Medical devices excluding those under Subparagraph 
2 of Paragraph (1), among Class I medical devices. 
 
 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
3 
 
Article 5 (Procedures for Manufacturing Approval) (1) A person who intends to obtain approval 
for medical device manufacturing under Article 6 (2) of the Act shall submit an application in Form 
3 (including an application in electronic form) to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, along with 
the following documents (including electronic documents): 
1. 
Documents evidencing that he or she secures facilities and manufacturing and quality 
management systems under Article 6 (4) of the Act; 
2. 
Technical documents, clinical investigation data, etc. (hereinafter “technical documents, 
etc.”) or a notice of the review result of technical documents, etc. under Article 9 (4) for 
which 2 years have not elapsed since the issuance date. Provided, that in cases falling 
under the proviso of Article 9 (1), a notice of the review result of technical documents, etc. 
shall be submitted; 
3.  A copy of a concluded contract for entrusting manufacturing processes or testing for 
quality management. 
(2) When a product of which an application for a manufacturing approval is filed under Paragraph 
(1) is deemed to meet the standards, the Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall issue the 
applicant with a manufacturing license in Form 4 and enter the following matters in the 
manufacturing approval register: 
1. 
Approval number and approval date 
2. 
The names (the product name, item name, and model name). 
(3) The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall determine and publicly notify the guidelines for 
preparing the supporting documents required for the application for manufacturing business 
approval of medical devices under Article 3 (including conditional manufacturing business 
approval and approval for change thereof) and documents required for the application for 
manufacturing approval under Paragraph (1) (including conditional manufacturing approval 
and approval for change thereof), requirements for each document, the scope of exemption, 
and other details. 
(4) If, while receiving an application for a manufacturing approval under Paragraph (1), the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety receives an application for a new health technology 
assessment under Article 3-2 (2) of the New Health Technology Assessment Rules, or an 
application, etc. for verification of eligibility for health care benefit or non-benefit, etc. under 
Article 9-2 (2) of the Rules on Standards for Health Care Benefits Covered by National 
Health Insurance, or a written objection under Article 9-2 (4) of the Rules on Standards for 
Health Care Benefits Covered by National Health Insurance, he or she shall, without delay, 
forward the relevant application, etc. to the Minister of Health and Welfare and the 
President of the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service. In such cases, the Minister 
of Food and Drug Safety may mutually share data related to the relevant application for a 
manufacturing approval with the Minister of Health and Welfare or the President of the Health 
Insurance Review and Assessment Service; present opinions on the new health technology 
assessment and whether the manufacturing falls under medical care benefit items or non-
benefit items; and refer to the data forwarded under Paragraph (5) when granting 
manufacturing approval. <Newly Inserted on Jul. 29, 2016; Apr. 13, 2020> 
 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
4 
 
(5) When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety receives the results of the new health technology 
assessment, the results of the verification of whether the manufacturing falls under the health 
care benefit items or non-benefit items by the Minister of Health and Welfare and the President 
of the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service following Article 4 (2) of the New 
Health Technology Assessment Rules or the main text of Article 9-2 (3) and Paragraph (4) 
thereof of the Rules on Standards for Health Care Benefits Covered by National Health 
Insurance, he or she shall immediately notify the relevant applicant of such results, etc. 
<Newly inserted on Jul. 29, 2016> 
(6) The matters prescribed in Paragraphs (4) and (5) shall also apply to the cases of conditional 
manufacturing approval granted under Article 7 (1) of the Act or approval for change granted 
under Article 12 (1) of the Act. <Newly Inserted on Jul. 29, 2016> 
(7) Except as provided in Paragraphs (4) through (6), details necessary for data and opinion 
provision, etc. among institutions shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety. <Newly Inserted on Jul. 29, 2016> 
 
Article 6 (Procedures for Manufacturing Certification) (1) A person who intends to obtain 
manufacturing certification of medical devices under Article 6 (2) of the Act shall submit an 
application in Form 5 (including an application in electronic form) to the head of the National 
Institute of Medical Device Safety Information established under Article 42 of the Act (hereinafter 
the “NIDS”) entrusted with the affairs concerning certification under Article 44 (2) of the Act, 
along with the documents referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 5 (1) (including electronic 
documents). <Amended on Jun. 14, 2018> 
(2)  When medical devices of which an application for manufacturing is filed under Paragraph (1) 
are deemed to meet the standards, the head of the NIDS shall issue the manufacturing 
certificate in Form 6 to the applicant and shall enter the following matters in the 
manufacturing certification register: <Amended on Jun. 14, 2018> 
1. 
Certification number and certification date; 
2. 
The names (the product name, item name, and model name); 
(3)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall determine and publicly notify the guidelines for 
preparing the supporting documents required for the application for manufacturing certification 
under Paragraph (1) (including conditional manufacturing certification and certification of 
change thereof), requirements for each document, the scope of exemption, and other details. 
 
Article 7 (Procedures for Manufacturing Notification) (1) A person who intends to file a 
manufacturing notification of medical devices under Article 6 (2) of the Act shall submit the 
notification in Form 7 (including a notification in electronic form) to the head of the NIDS entrusted 
with the affairs concerning notification under Article 44 (2) of the Act, along with the documents 
listed in Article 5 (1) 3. <Amended on Jun 14, 2018> 
(2)  When the head of the NIDS accepts a manufacturing notification filed pursuant to paragraph 
(1), he or she shall issue to the applicant a Certificate of Manufacturing Notification prescribed 
in Form 7-2, and shall enter the following matters in the Manufacturing Notification Register: 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
5 
 
<Amended on Jun. 14, 2018; Aug. 7, 2024> 
1. 
Notification number and notification date; 
2. 
The names (the product name, item name, and model name). 
(3)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall determine and publicly notify the guidelines for 
preparing supporting documents required to file a manufacturing notification under Paragraph 
(1) (including a conditional manufacturing notification and notification of change thereof), 
requirements for each document, the scope of exemption, and other details. 
 
Article 8 (Standards for Facilities and Manufacturing and Quality Management System) (1) 
Standards for facilities and manufacturing and quality management systems to be secured by a 
person who intends to obtain a manufacturing business approval, manufacturing approval, or 
manufacturing certification or file a manufacturing notification under the main text of Article 6 (4) 
of the Act shall be as specified in Annex 2. 
(2)  “Cases prescribed by Ordinance of the Prime Minister, such as those of entrusting testing for 
quality management or manufacturing processes” in the proviso of Article 6 (4) of the Act 
refers to cases where a person who intends to obtain a manufacturing business approval, 
manufacturing approval, or manufacturing certification or file a manufacturing notification 
entrusts manufacturing processes or quality management testing to a medical device testing 
and inspection institution under Article 6 (2) 4 of the Act on Testing and Inspection in the Food 
and Drug Industry (hereinafter “medical device testing and inspection institution”), an 
institution conducting non-clinical studies under Article 10-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter 
“institution conducting non-clinical studies”), or a manufacturer whose compliance is certified 
under subparagraph 2 (f) of Annex 2. In such cases, the person who intends to obtain 
manufacturing business approval, manufacturing approval, or manufacturing certification or 
file a manufacturing notification may not secure the facilities of a manufacturing site specified 
in Subparagraph 1 (a) of Annex 2 according to the following classifications: <Amended on 
May 1, 2017> 
1. 
When manufacturing processes are entrusted: Manufacturing facilities and instruments 
related to the entrusted processes; 
2. 
When quality management testing is entrusted to a medical device testing and inspection 
institution, an institution conducting non-clinical studies, or a manufacturer whose 
compliance is certified under Subparagraph 2 (f) of Annex 2: Laboratories for quality 
management, and facilities and instruments related to testing. 
 
Article 9 (Review of Technical Documents) (1) A person who intends to obtain manufacturing 
approval or manufacturing certification may undergo a review in advance by the Minister of Food 
and Drug Safety regarding the compliance of technical documents, etc., which shall be submitted 
under Article 6 (5) of the Act. Provided, that in the cases of the medical devices that are essentially 
equivalent to those already approved, certified, or notified in terms of structure, mode of action, 
performance, intended uses, utilization methods, etc. and fall under the items determined by the 
Minister of Food and Drug and Safety, the technical documents, etc. shall be reviewed by a 
technical documentation review body under Article 6-4 (1) of the Act (hereinafter “technical 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
6 
 
documentation review body”). <Amended on May 1, 2017> 
(2) For medical devices (in vitro diagnostic medical devices shall be excluded), a person who 
intends to have technical documents, etc. reviewed under Paragraph (1) shall submit a written 
request for review in Form 8 (including a written request for review in electronic form) to the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety or the head of an technical documentation review body, 
along with the following data (including data in electronic form): Provided, That in the cases 
of the medical devices that are essentially equivalent to those already approved in terms of 
structure, mode of action, performance, intended uses, utilization methods, etc. except for 
the medical devices determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety for which submission of data regarding clinical investigations is deemed necessary, 
the data referred to in Subparagraphs 5 through 7 may not be submitted. <Amended Jun. 12, 
2019; Dec 31, 2020; Jun. 24, 2021; Jan. 16, 2024> 
1. 
Data regarding comparison between the medical devices and products already approved; 
2. 
Data regarding intended uses; 
3. 
Data regarding modes of action; 
4. 
The following data regarding test specifications, grounds for establishing such 
specifications, and actual measured values for the verification of the performance and 
safety of products: Provided, That when neither domestic nor international test 
specifications exist, data regarding test specifications established by the person who 
intends to have technical documents, etc. reviewed to verify the performance and safety 
of products, grounds for establishing such specifications, and actual measured values: 
(a) Data regarding electrical and mechanical safety; 
(b) Data regarding biological safety; 
(c) Data regarding radiation safety; 
(d) Data regarding safety of electromagnetic waves; 
(e) Data regarding performance; 
(f) Data regarding physical and chemical properties; 
(g) Data regarding stability; 
5. 
Data regarding origins, discovery, and reasons for development; 
6. 
Data regarding clinical investigations; 
7. 
Data regarding the current status of use, etc. in foreign countries. 
(3) A person who intends to have technical documents, etc. reviewed regarding in vitro diagnostic 
medical devices pursuant to Paragraph (1) shall submit a written request for review in Form 8 
(including a written request for review in electronic form) to the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety or the head of an institution reviewing technical documents, along with the following 
data (including data in electronic form): <Amended on Jan. 4, 2017; Jun. 24, 2021; Jan. 16, 
2024> 
1. 
Data regarding reasons for development, measurement principles and methods, and the 
current status of domestic and international use; 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
7 
 
2. 
Data regarding raw materials and manufacturing methods; 
3. 
Data regarding intended uses; 
4. 
Data regarding storage methods and the period of use or expiration date; 
5. 
The following data to verify the performance of the products: 
(a)  Data regarding analytical performance tests; 
(b) Data regarding clinical performance tests; 
(c) Data regarding quality management tests; 
(d) Data regarding reference materials, specimen storage, etc. 
6. 
Data regarding the safety of the handlers of in vitro diagnostic medical devices; 
7. 
Data regarding the comparison between the medical devices and products already 
approved or certified. 
(4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (2) and (3), where a person who has undergone a preliminary 
review of manufacturing approval or notification pursuant to Article 11 of the Act submits a 
preliminary review result notice pursuant to Article 25 (3), such person may omit the 
submission of the data among the items under each subparagraph of paragraph (2) or paragraph 
(3) for which a determination of conformity has been made as a result of the preliminary 
review. <Newly Inserted on Jan. 16, 2024> 
(5) Upon receipt of a request for review under Paragraphs (2) and (3), the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety or the head of a technical documentation review body shall review the relevant 
technical documents, etc. and notify the applicant of the results as prepared in Form 9. 
<Amended on Jan. 16, 2024> 
(6) The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall determine and publicly notify the guidelines for 
preparing the supporting documents necessary to review technical documents, etc.; 
requirements for each supporting document and procedures for and scope of exemption thereof; 
scope of, standards and procedures for review; management standards for clinical 
performance tests; and other details. <Amended on Jan. 4, 2017; Jan. 16, 2024> 
 
Article 10 (Exemption from Manufacturing Business Approval for Medical Devices) The 
following medical devices may be manufactured without manufacturing business approval under 
Article 6 (1) of the Act or without manufacturing approval, manufacturing certification, or 
manufacturing notification under Paragraph (2) of that Article: <Amended on Jun. 15, 2016; Jun. 
14, 2018; Dec. 31, 2018> 
1. 
A medical device subject to clinical investigations for which approval of a clinical 
investigation plan is granted under the main text of Article 10 (1) of the Act; 
2. 
A separate medical device required for clinical investigations for which approval of a 
clinical investigation plan may not be granted under the proviso of Article 10 (1) of the 
Act; 
3. 
A separate medical device required for clinical investigations regarding drugs, etc. for 
which approval of a clinical investigation plan shall be granted under Article 34 of the 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
8 
 
Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; 
4. 
A medical device manufactured to obtain manufacturing approval or manufacturing 
certification for medical devices or file a manufacturing notification for medical devices; 
5. 
A medical device used for research purposes, such as product development; 
6. 
A medical device determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety, such as a medical device for self-use or for relief operations, etc.; 
7. 
Deleted. <Dec. 31, 2018> 
8. 
A medical device determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety which is used in clinical laboratories and is deemed suitable by the Minister based 
on the evaluations of quality management systems, inspection performance, competence, 
etc. (referring to places where the diagnosis, inspection, etc. of diseases are conducted; 
hereinafter the same shall apply). 
 
Article 11 (Qualifications for Quality Managers) (1) A person who intends to obtain 
manufacturing business approval under Article 6 (1) of the Act shall assign at least one quality 
manager to each manufacturing site. 
(2)  The affairs of a quality manager may be performed by a person with any of the following 
qualifications: <Amended on Jun. 15, 2016; Apr. 13, 2020; Dec. 19, 2022> 
1. 
A person with a license classified as follows under the Medical Service Technologists Act: 
(a) When manufacturing or importing eyeglass lenses or contact lenses: Opticians; 
(b) When manufacturing or importing materials used in dental clinics: Dental technicians 
or dental hygienists; 
(c) When manufacturing or importing radiation-generating devices: Radiological 
technologists; 
(d) Deleted. <May 1, 2020> 
(e) When manufacturing or importing medical devices required for physical therapy 
or rehabilitation training: Physical therapists. 
2. 
A person with qualifications as a biomedical engineer or quality management engineer 
under the National Technical Qualifications Act; 
 
2-2. A person with qualifications as a regulatory affairs (RA) specialist of medical devices 
accredited by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety under Article 19 (1) of the 
Framework Act On Qualifications; 
3. 
A person who has earned a bachelor’s degree (including a person deemed to have an 
educational attainment equal to or higher than such degree under statutes or regulations; 
hereinafter, in this Article, the same shall apply) from a school under the subparagraphs of 
Article 2 of the Higher Education Act (excluding a junior college under Subparagraph 4 
of that Article; hereinafter, in this Article, “university, college, etc.”) and who has 
majored in the field of natural science, engineering, or medicine under Article 2 (9) of the 
Regulations on the Establishment and Operation of Universities and Colleges (hereinafter, 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
9 
 
in this Article, “medical-device-related field”); 
4. 
A person who has earned a bachelor’s degree from a university, college, etc. in a field not 
related to medical devices and who has earned a master’s degree or higher from a 
graduate school under Article 29 of the Higher Education Act in a medical-device-related 
field; 
5. 
A person who has obtained a bachelor's degree in a field other than a medical-device-
related field at a university or equivalent institution, and who has at least one year of 
experience (including the acquisition of a degree or experience prior to the recognition of 
academic credentials) engaged in quality management duties at a medical device 
manufacturing or import company; 
6. 
A person who has graduated from a junior college as defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 
2 of the Higher Education Act (including a person deemed to have an educational 
attainment equal to or higher than such college under statutes or regulations; hereinafter, 
in this Article, the same shall apply), who majored in a medical-device-related field, and 
who has at least one year of experience (including graduation or experience prior to the 
recognition of academic credentials) engaged in quality management duties at a medical 
device manufacturing or import company; 
7. 
A person who has graduated from a junior college as defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 
2 of the Higher Education Act, who majored in a field other than a medical-device-related 
field, and who has at least three years of experience (including graduation or experience 
prior to the recognition of academic credentials) engaged in quality management duties at 
a medical device manufacturing or import company (or two years, in the case of a 
graduate of a junior college with a three-year course of study pursuant to Article 48 (1) of 
the Higher Education Act); 
8. 
A person who has graduated from a high school or high technical school under 
Subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (including a 
person deemed to have an educational attainment equal to or higher than such school 
under statutes or regulations, but excluding a person falling under Subparagraph 9) who 
has engaged in quality management work for at least 5 years in a company that 
manufactures or imports medical devices; 
9. 
A person who has graduated from a high school tailored to industry demands in a 
medical-device-related field under Article 90 (1) 10 of the Enforcement Decree of the 
Elementary and Secondary Education Act who has engaged in quality management work 
for at least three years in a company that manufactures or imports medical devices; 
10. A person who has engaged in quality management work for at least six years in a 
company that manufactures or imports medical devices. 
(3)  Where a manufacturer has 2 or more quality managers under Paragraph (1), the work shall be 
divided and the limits of the responsibilities of each quality manager shall be specified. 
 
Article 12 (Scope of Duties of Quality Managers) (1) The scope of duties to be performed by 
quality managers under Article 6-2 (1) of the Act shall be as follows: 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
10 
 
1. 
Inspecting the hygiene of employees thoroughly and providing them with the education 
and training necessary to produce and import medical devices with excellent quality; 
2. 
Supervising whether employees receive education and training under Subparagraph 1; 
3. 
Preparing a standard operating procedure (SOP) to manufacture medical devices in 
accordance with the standards for manufacturing and quality management systems 
specified in Subparagraph 2 of Annex 2 and requiring employees to manufacture medical 
devices according to such procedure; 
4. 
Thoroughly conducting the tests, inspections, or examinations required for the processes 
from the warehousing of raw materials to the release of finished products; preparing and 
keeping manufacturing management records and quality management records for each 
manufacturing unit; and retaining such records for 5 years from manufacturing dates 
(referring to a period corresponding to the life cycle of a product, where such life cycle 
exceeds 5 years); 
5. 
Evaluating the results of the quality management of manufacturing sites and determining 
whether to ship the products; 
6. 
Dealing with affairs related to the establishment, implementation, and maintenance of 
quality management systems in accordance with standards for manufacturing and quality 
management systems specified in Subparagraph 2 of Annex 2; 
7. 
Managing the facilities of manufacturing sites in a sanitary manner so as not to cause any 
harm to health and hygiene and preventing cross-contamination, contamination from the 
outside, etc.; 
8. 
Managing and supervising objects that are likely to cause any harm so that they are not 
placed in working places and preventing substances hazardous to public health from being 
generated in the working place; 
9. 
Handling other affairs determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety, which are related to manufacturing management, quality management, and safety 
management, among the matters to be observed by the manufacturers under Article 27 (1). 
(2) When a quality manager ceases to engage in quality management work in the relevant working 
places, he or she may submit a notification of his or her status of not working as a quality 
manager in Form 10 (including a notification in electronic form) to the Commissioner of the 
Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety. 
(3) No quality manager shall concurrently engage in affairs other than those referred to in 
Paragraph (1); Provided, that the same shall not apply in any of the following cases: 
1. 
When he or she handles affairs not affecting the duties of a quality manager; 
2. 
When a manufacturer concurrently engages in import business and a quality manager of 
the manufacturing company handles the affairs of a quality manager of the import 
company. 
 
Article 13 (Content and Hours of Education for Quality Managers) (1) The content of 
education under Article 6-2 (2) of the Act shall be as follows: 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
11 
 
1. 
The latest standard specifications for medical devices; 
2. 
Statutes, regulations, systems, and technology necessary for safety management, such 
as ensuring the safety and effectiveness of medical devices; 
3. 
Statutes, regulations, systems, and technology necessary for the manufacture and quality 
management of medical devices; 
4. 
Other matters determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety for the manufacturing 
management, quality management, and safety management of medical devices. 
(2) At least 8 hours of education shall be provided per year. 
(3) A quality manager shall receive education conducted by an institution offering education for 
quality managers under Article 14 (1) within 6 months from the date of commencement of 
work: Provided, That this shall not apply when he or she completes the provided education in 
the pertinent year before working as a quality manager. <Amended on Jun. 24, 2021> 
 
Article 14 (Designation of Institutions Offering Education for Quality Managers) (1) An 
institution that intends to be designated as an institution offering education for quality managers 
(hereinafter “institution offering education”) under Article 6-2 (5) of the Act shall satisfy the 
following requirements: <Amended on Jan. 21, 2022> 
1. 
Being the NIDS or medical device-related institutions or organizations publicly

Article 15 (Compliance for Institutions Offering Education) An institution offering education 
shall comply with the following matters in accordance with Article 6-2 (6) of the Act: 
1. 
To formulate an annual educational plan including educatees and educational content for 
the following year in accordance with the basic educational plan under Article 14 (2) 5 
and to submit it to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety before the following business 
year commences; 
2. 
To provide education in accordance with the annual educational plan in Subparagraph 1; 
3. 
To develop educational materials and provide them to educatees; 
4. 
To issue a certificate with a person who completes the education, to record matters 
regarding the provision of education, such as a list of persons who have completed the 
education, and to retain such records for 2 years from the date such matters are recorded; 
5. 
To report records regarding the provision of education of the preceding year to the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety by January 31 of the following year. 
(2) Required details regarding the establishment of an educational plan or methods of education

Article 18-3 (Methods and Procedures for Periodic Reports of Post-Marketing Surveillance) 
(1) A person who intends to report the data collected during post-marketing surveillance, the status 
of the execution of the surveillance, etc. following Article 8 (4) of the Act shall submit to the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety a periodic report on medical device post-marketing surveillance 
in Form 16-3 within the period prescribed in Paragraph (2), along with the following documents: 
1. 
Primary data, including a record of observations on the subject of the post-marketing 
surveillance; 
2. 
Data regarding the result of analysis and assessment on the post-marketing surveillance; 
3. 
Data regarding the side effects of the medical device subject to post-marketing 
surveillance. 
(2) The report under Paragraph (1) shall be submitted every 6 months in the first year and every 
year from the second year, and the deadline for the report shall be 2 months from the end of the 
period covered by each report. 
(3) Notwithstanding Paragraph (2), the document submitted with the application for review under 
Article 8-2 (1) of the Act may be in lieu of the last report of the post-marketing surveillance 
period. 
(4) Details regarding the guidelines, etc. for preparing documents to be submitted with the report 
under Paragraphs (1) and (3) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food 
and Drug Safety. 
[Newly Inserted on Jan. 21, 2022]

Data on domestic and foreign sales and approval in foreign countries.

Food and Drug Safety shall re-evaluate the relevant items, allow the perusal of the draft 
results of re-evaluation for at least 1 month so as to provide an opportunity for the

publicly announce the results of re-evaluation on the website of the Ministry of Food and Drug 
Safety.

Article 21-2 (Clinical Investigations Conducted at Institutions Other Than Clinical 
Investigation Sites) A clinical investigation for which participation of an institution other than a 
clinical investigation site is required due to the nature of the clinical investigation pursuant to the 
proviso to Article 10 (4) 1 of the Act means any clinical investigation falling under one of the 
following subparagraphs:

Article 24 (Standards for Conducting Clinical Investigations) (1) Pursuant to Article 10 (5) and 
(7) of the Act, clinical investigations shall be conducted according to the following standards and 
the Good Clinical Practice for Medical Devices specified in Annex 3: <Amended Jan. 16, 2024; 
Aug. 7, 2024> 
1. 
Clinical investigations shall be conducted safely and scientifically according to a clinical 
investigation plan; 
2. 
 Clinical investigations shall be conducted at a clinical investigation site designated by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety or at a clinical investigation participation institution 
pursuant to Article 20 (2) 2. Where the clinical investigation is conducted at a clinical 
investigation participation institution, the clinical investigation site shall supervise and 
oversee the institution. 
3. 
Clinical investigation principal investigators shall be selected from among those with 
expertise, ethical discipline, and considerable experience in conducting clinical 
investigations of the relevant medical devices; 
4. 
An explanation shall be provided to subjects of clinical investigations regarding clinical 
investigation details and the details of and procedures for compensation for potential harm 
that could affect the health of the subjects during the clinical investigations and other 
relevant matters, and informed consent (Including non-face-to-face consent provided 
through an electronic document bearing an electronic signature pursuant to the Electronic 
Signature Act; the same shall apply hereinafter in this Article.) thereto shall be obtained 
from the subjects: Provided, That when it is impracticable to obtain consent from a 
subject because of his or her lack of comprehension and communication ability or other 
reasons, consent shall be obtained from a person with parental authority, guardian, etc.; 
5. 
Safety measures for subjects of clinical investigations shall be prepared; 
6. 
Medical devices for clinical investigations shall not be used for purposes other than 
clinical investigations: Provided, that the same shall not apply to cases prescribed by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety, such as when the medical devices are used for patients 
with life-threatening and critical illnesses, including terminal cancer; 
7. 
Clinical investigations shall commence within 2 years from the date the approval of a 
clinical investigation plan or approval of modification thereof was obtained; 
8. 
Clinical investigation investigators shall be provided with clinical investigation data 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
25 
 
books before conducting the clinical investigations, as determined by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety; 
9. 
When new data, information, etc. on safety and effectiveness is obtained, clinical 
investigation investigators shall be informed thereof without delay and it shall be 
examined whether or not to reflect this new data, etc.; 
10. Medical devices for clinical investigations that are appropriately manufactured according 
to the standards for facilities and manufacturing and quality management systems under 
Annex 2 shall be used; 
11. When adverse events occur while using a medical device, a person who has obtained 
approval of a clinical investigation plan shall report them to the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety according to the Good Clinical Practices for Medical Devices specified in 
Annex 3; 
12. In the case of a clinical investigation under Article 20 (4) 2 that has not been approved 
pursuant to the proviso to Article 10 (1) of the Act, the performance and safety of the 
product shall be verified, prior to conducting the clinical investigation, through the data 
specified in each item of Article 9 (2) 4; 
13. Other matters determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety for the proper 
conduct of a clinical investigation shall be observed. 
(2) Regarding the status of a clinical investigation, a person who has obtained approval for a 
clinical investigation plan shall submit a report on the status of clinical investigation execution 
in Form 25 (including a report in electronic form) to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety by 
the end of February each year, along with summarized data related to the safety evaluation of 
medical devices for clinical investigations under Subparagraph 8 (q) (i) of Annex 3; and when 
the clinical investigation is completed, he or she shall submit a report in Form 26 (including a 
report in electronic form) to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety within 20 days from the date 
of completion. <Amended on Oct. 22, 2019> 
(3) A clinical investigation sponsor or the head of a clinical investigation site shall retain the 
clinical investigation plan and the records and data regarding the clinical investigation 
execution (including electronic documents) for the periods classified as follows: 
1. 
Data related to clinical investigations for manufacturing or import approval, or approval 
for modification thereof: 3 years from the approval date; 
2. 
Other data related to clinical investigations: 3 years from the date of the completion of 
clinical investigations. 
(4) Notwithstanding the text of Paragraph (1) 4, in the case of a clinical investigation that uses 
data such as patients’ medical records, where the personal information of the patients has been 
processed as pseudonymized information pursuant to Article 28-2 of the Personal Information 
Protection Act, the clinical investigation may be conducted without obtaining the subjects’ 
consent, upon approval of the Institutional Review Board in accordance with Subparagraph 6 
of Annex 3. In such cases, the processing of pseudonymized information shall be governed by 
the Personal Information Protection Act. <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024> 
(5) Details regarding the standards, etc. for designating clinical investigation sites under Paragraph 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act

conduct a fact-finding survey to evaluate whether the details of such application meet the 
standards for designation.

studies, he or she shall issue the applicant with a certificate of designation as an institution

changed matters (including electronic documents): 
1. 
The representative and operating officers of the institution conducting non-clinical studies; 
2. 
The name and location of the institution conducting non-clinical studies; 
3. 
Areas of non-clinical studies. 
(6) When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety modifies designation of an institution conducting 
non-clinical studies, he or she shall state the changed matters in a certificate of designation as 
an institution conducting non-clinical studies of medical devices and issue such certificate.

Article 27 (Compliance for Manufacturers) (1) Matters to be observed by Compliance 
obligations for medical device manufacturers following Article 13 (1) of the Act shall be as follows: 
<Amended on Dec. 4, 2020, Jan. 21, 2022> 
1. 
Manufacturers shall manage the facilities of sites in a sanitary manner so as to not cause 
any harm to health and hygiene, and shall prevent cross-contamination or contamination, 
etc. from the outside; 
2. 
Manufacturers shall not place objects likely to cause harm in working places, and shall 
prevent substances hazardous to public health from being discharged or released from 
working places; 
3. 
Manufacturers shall prepare and keep documents about warehousing and release of raw 
materials and finished products, manufacturing processes, and quality management 
(including testing standards and methods, etc.) and shall thoroughly conduct 
manufacturing and quality inspections based on such documents; 
4. 
Manufacturers shall prepare and keep the records of manufacturing and quality 
inspections under Subparagraph 3 by manufacturing unit and the records of handling 
customers’ complaints, and shall retain such records for 5 years from the date of 
manufacturing (referring to a period corresponding to the product life cycle, where such 
life cycle exceeds 5 years); 
5. 
When the safety and effectiveness of released medical devices are undermined or the 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
31 
 
quality thereof is poor, manufacturers shall take corrective measures, such as recall, 
without delay; 
6. 
Manufacturers shall release sterile products after verifying that they have been packaged 
and sterilized in new containers; 
7. 
Manufacturers shall release electronic or mechanical products after ensuring their 
electronic, mechanical, and electromagnetic safety; 
8. 
Manufacturers shall release products to come in direct or indirect contact with the human 
body after ensuring their biological safety; 
9. 
When manufacturers become aware of new data or information on the safety and 
effectiveness of approved, certified, or notified medical devices (including cases of side 
effects following the use of the devices), they shall report it and take necessary safety 
measures as determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety; 
10. Manufacturers shall maintain the standards for facilities and manufacturing and quality 
management systems under Annex 2; 
11. Manufacturers shall distribute medical devices manufactured in compliance with the 
standards under Subparagraph 2 of Annex 2. In such cases, medical devices manufactured 
for the purpose of the recognition of compliance following Subparagraph 2 (f) of Annex 2 
and recognized as compliant following that item shall be deemed manufactured after 
being recognized as compliant following that item; 
12. Manufacturers shall conduct manufacturing and quality management or production 
management by applying the latest standard specifications determined by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety following Article 19 of the Act; 
13. Manufacturers shall thoroughly inspect the hygiene of employees and provide them with 
the education and training necessary for the production of medical devices with excellent 
quality; 
14. Manufacturers shall thoroughly conduct the affairs of post-marketing safety management, 
such as post-marketing surveillance, re-evaluation, management of medical devices 
subject to tracking management, and management of information regarding safety 
(including the management of reports on side effects); 
15. When manufacturers purchase medical devices manufactured by their company from 
medical institutions, they shall observe the following: 
(a) They shall inspect whether such medical devices are in compliance with the 
standards for manufacturing and quality management systems for medical devices 
under Subparagraph 2 of Annex 2 and release them with certificates of inspection 
attached thereto only if they comply with such standards; 
(b) They shall prepare and keep the records of the content and results of inspections 
under item (a), the dates of issued certificates of inspection, etc., and shall retain 
such records for 2 years from the relevant date of release. 
16. When manufacturers are requested to conduct inspections by medical device distributors 
or lessors following Subparagraph 1 (a) of Article 39, they shall observe the following: 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
32 
 
(a) They shall inspect whether medical devices are in compliance with the standards for 
manufacturing and quality management systems for medical devices under 
Subparagraph 2 of Annex 2 and issue certificates of inspection only if they comply 
with such standards; 
(b) They shall observe the matters determined and publicly notified by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety regarding the procedures and methods for issuing certificates 
of inspection, the period of reply, instructions about distribution or lease, etc. 
(2)  Manufacturers shall report the following matters to the Minister of Health and Welfare and the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety following Article 13 (2) of the Act as determined and 
publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety: <Amended on Apr. 13, 2020> 
1. 
Results of producing and exporting medical devices for the pertinent year; 
2. 
Reasons for and the amount and schedule of suspension of medical devices (limited to 
cases involving the suspension of the production of medical devices that have grave 
effects on public health where such devices is are publicly notified by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety after consultation with the Minister of Health and Welfare).

Article 32 (Exemption from Approval for Medical Device Import Businesses) (1) Medical 
devices that may be imported without obtaining import business approval, import approval, or 
importing certification or without filing an importing notification following Article 6 (10) of the Act 
applied mutatis mutandis according to Article 15 (6) of the Act shall be as follows. <Amended on

1. 
A medical device subject to clinical investigations for which approval of a clinical 
investigation plan is granted under the text of Article 10 (1) of the Act; 
2. 
A separate medical device required for clinical investigations for which approval of a 
clinical investigation plan need not be granted under the proviso of Article 10 (1) of the 
Act; 
3. 
A separate medical device required for clinical trials regarding pharmaceuticals, etc. for 
which approval of a clinical trial protocol shall be granted under Article 34 (1) of the 
Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; 
3-2.  Medical devices separately required for conducting clinical trials of pharmaceuticals, etc. 
for which approval of the clinical trial protocol is not required pursuant to Article 34 (2) 
of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. 
4. 
A medical device imported to obtain import approval or certification of medical devices 
or to file an importing notification thereof; 
5. 
A medical device used for the purpose of research, such as product development; 
5-2. A medical device not for distribution, which is imported to help consumers purchase a 
product, such as checking the actual appearance of the product; 
5-3. A medical device imported to conduct testing and inspections under Article 27 of the Act; 
6. 
A medical device determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug

Safety, such as a medical device for self-use or for relief operations, etc.; 
7. 
Deleted. <Dec. 31, 2018> 
8.

the evaluations of quality management systems, inspection performance and competence,

(2) Matters regarding the import procedures, subject matters, issuance of a certificate, etc. of 
medical devices excluded from those subject to import business approval and import approval, 
certification, or notification following Paragraph (1) shall be determined and publicly notified

Article 33 (Compliance for Importers) (1) Compliance obligations for a medical device importer 
under Article 13 (1) of the Act applied mutatis mutandis according to Article 15 (6) of the Act shall 
be as follows: <Amended on Dec. 4, 2020; Jan. 21, 2022; Oct. 31, 2025> 
1. 
The importer shall manage the facilities of an import business in a sanitary manner so as 
to not cause any harm to health or hygiene and shall prevent cross-contamination or 
contamination, etc. from the outside; 
2. 
The importer shall prepare and keep documents regarding the warehousing, release, and 
quality management of medical devices (including testing standards and methods, 
labeling, packaging, etc.) and management records on storage and shipment of accessories, 
and shall thoroughly conduct import and quality inspections based on such documents and 
records; 
3. 
The importer shall prepare and keep the records of import and quality inspections under 
Subparagraph 2 by import unit and the records of handling customers’ complaints, and 
shall retain such records for 5 years from the date of import (referring to a period 
corresponding to the product life cycle, where the product life cycle exceeds 5 years); 
4. 
The importer shall release products only after verifying that the products have been 
sterilized; 
5. 
The importer shall release electronic or mechanical products after ensuring their 
electronic, mechanical, and electromagnetic safety; 
6. 
The importer shall release products to come in direct or indirect contact with the human 
body after ensuring their biological safety; 
7. 
The importer shall prepare and keep product standards by item including the following 
matters: 
(a) The name of a medical device (the product name, item name, and model name); 
(b) The name of a manufacturing company of an imported medical device and the 
country of manufacture thereof; 
(c) Self-quality-management-test specifications of the shapes, structures, and finished 
products; 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
36 
 
(d) Matters to be stated on the container, etc. of a medical device, as prescribed in 
Articles 20 through 23 of the Act; 
(e) The method for and order of installation (limited to medical devices for which 
installation management is required); 
(f) Matters regarding sterilization methods and standards, and assessment (limited to 
medical devices applied with sterile packaging); 
(g) The presenter and presentation date of product standards (if revised, the reviser and 
date and cause of revision shall be stated); 
8. 
The importer shall prepare and keep import management standards, including the 
following matters: 
(a) Matters regarding product management and testing and inspections; 
(b) Matters regarding an assessment of the results of testing and inspections and the 
handling of rejected products; 
(c) Matters regarding the management of testing and inspection facilities; 
(d) Methods for contacting the manufacturer of an imported medical device; 
(e) Matters regarding the conditions of manufacture and quality management by a 
manufacturer of an imported medical device; 
(f) The presenter and presentation date of import management standards (if revised, 
the reviser and date and cause of revision shall be stated). 
9. 
The importer shall check whether an imported medical device has proper and correct 
labeling and packaging and prepare the records thereon; 
10. The importer shall inspect product storage facilities and prepare the records thereon; 
11. The importer shall ensure that a quality manager implements the following matters; 
(a) When complaints against the quality of released medical devices are filed, the 
quality manager shall prepare and implement the relevant procedures to identify the 
causes thereof and take corrective measures and prepare and retain such records; 
(b) The quality manager shall keep and use product standards and import management 
standards for proper quality management of imported medical devices; 
(c) The quality manager shall prepare work instructions based on documents under item 
(b) and inspect and check whether they are properly operated in compliance with the 
standards; 
12. The importer shall take corrective measures, such as recall, without delay when the safety 
and effectiveness of released medical devices are undermined or the quality thereof is 
poor; 
13. The importer shall formulate education plans to enable his or her employees to ensure the 
quality of imported medical devices, hold regular education and training sessions based 
on the plans, and prepare and retain records thereon; 
14. When the importer becomes aware of new data or information on the safety and 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
37 
 
effectiveness of a medical device approved, certified, or notified (including cases of side 
effects related to the use of the medical device), he or she shall report it and prepare the 
necessary safety measures as determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety; 
15. For a manufacturing site of imported medical devices, the importer shall import and 
distribute medical devices manufactured in compliance with the standards specified in 
Subparagraph 3 of Annex 4. In such cases, medical devices imported for the purpose of 
the recognition of compliance under Subparagraph 3 of Annex 4 and recognized as 
compliant under that subparagraph shall be deemed imported after being recognized as 
compliant under that subparagraph; 
16. The importer shall comply with the guidelines for export and import of medical devices 
publicly announced by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy under Article 12 of the 
Foreign Trade Act and regulations for management of imported medical devices 
determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety; 
17. The importer shall apply the latest standard specifications determined by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety following Article 19 of the Act to maintain facilities and 
manufacturing and quality management systems, to import medical devices, and to 
conduct quality management or import management; 
18. The importer shall thoroughly perform the affairs of post-marketing safety management, 
including post-marketing surveillance, re-evaluation, management of medical devices 
subject to tracking management, and management of safety information (including 
management of reports on side effects); 
19. When the importer imports secondhand medical devices or purchases medical devices 
imported by his or her company from a medical institution, he or she shall observe the 
following: 
(a) He or she shall inspect whether the medical devices are in compliance with the test 
specifications referred to in Subparagraph 7 (c) and release them with certificates of 
inspection attached thereto only where they are in compliance with such 
specifications; 
(b) He or she shall prepare and keep the records of the details and results of inspections 
under item (a), the date of issuing certificates of inspection, etc. and retain such 
records for 2 years from the date of release; 
20. Where the importer is requested to conduct an inspection by a medical device distributor 
or lessor under Subparagraph 1 of Article 39, he or she shall observe the following: 
(a) He or she shall inspect whether the medical devices are in compliance with the 
standards specified in Subparagraph 2 of Annex 2 and issue certificates of inspection 
only where they are in compliance with such standards; 
(b) He or she shall comply with the matters determined and publicly notified by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety regarding the procedures and methods for issuing 
certificates of inspection, period of reply, instructions on distribution or lease, etc. 
(2)  An importer shall report to the Minister of Health and Welfare and the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety the following matters as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
38 
 
and Drug Safety under Article 13 (2) of the Act applied mutatis mutandis according to Article 
15 (6) of the Act: Provided, That such report on matters under Subparagraph 1 need not be 
filed when a standard customs clearance forecast report has been filed in an electronic trade 
document under the Electronic Trade Facilitation Act: <Amended on Apr. 13, 2020> 
1. 
Results of importing medical devices for the pertinent year; 
2. 
Reasons for and the amount and schedule of suspension of medical devices (limited to 
cases of suspension of the production of medical devices that have grave effects on public 
health where such devices are publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
after consultation with the Minister of Health and Welfare).

Article 34-2 (Method for Supplying Orphan Medical Devices or Those in Urgent Need of 
Introduction) (1) When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety intends to supply orphan medical 
devices or those in urgent need of introduction under Article 15-2 (1), with the exception of its 
subparagraphs, of the Act (hereinafter “orphan medical devices or those in urgent need of 
introduction”), he or she shall conduct surveys on demand thereof from the relevant administrative 
agencies, medical institutions, health and medical service-related institutions, organizations and 
experts, patients, etc. 
(2) When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety conducts surveys on demand under Paragraph (1), 
they shall establish quarterly, semi-annual, and annual plans to supply orphan medical devices 
or those in urgent need of introduction, including the following matters: 
1. 
Matters regarding supply quantities; 
2. 
Matters regarding supply prices; 
3. 
Matters regarding supply targets; 
4. 
Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety to supply 
orphan medical devices or those in urgent need of introduction. 
(3) When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety intends to supply orphan medical devices or those 
in urgent need of introduction according to the supply plans under Paragraph (2), he or she 
shall conclude a supply contract with a supply target. 
(4) Except as provided in Paragraphs (1) through (3), details necessary for methods for supplying 
orphan medical devices or those in urgent need of introduction shall be determined and 
publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety.

Article 36 (Compliance for Repairers) Compliance obligations for repairers of medical devices 
under Article 13 of the Act applied mutatis mutandis according to Article 16 (4) of the Act shall be 
as follows: <Amended on Jun. 14, 2018> 
1. 
They shall not repair a medical device by making alterations inconsistent with the 
details approved, certified, or notified. This shall not apply to a minor repair for change 
under Article 46-2; 
2. 
They shall state the trade name and address on the container or wrapper of a medical 
device where such device is repaired; 
3. 
They shall notify a person who requests the repair of a medical device of the repair details 
in writing (in cases of a minor repair for change under Article 46-2, the details of such 
repair for change shall be included); 
4. 
They shall maintain facilities and quality management systems under Article 35 (4).

Article 39 (Method for Ensuring Quality of Medical Devices by Distributor or Lessor) The 
method for ensuring the quality of medical devices under Article 18 (1) of the Act and 
Subparagraph 1 of Article 10-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Medical Devices Act (hereinafter 
the “Decree”) shall be as follows: <Amended on Jun. 15, 2016> 
1. 
When a distributor or lessor purchases medical devices from a medical institution, he or 
she shall comply with the following matters: 
(a) The distributor or lessor shall request the manufacturer or importer of the relevant 
medical devices for inspections or request a medical device testing and inspection 
institution for inspections; 
(b) The distributor or lessor shall distribute or lease only the medical devices that have 
received certificates of inspection issued following Article 27 (1) 15 (a) or 33 (1) 19 
(a) according to the results of the inspections under item (a); 
(c) When the distributor or lessor receives any instructions regarding distribution or 
lease following Article 27 (1) 16 (b) or 33 (1) 20 (b) according to the results of the 
inspections under item (a), he or she shall comply with such instructions. 
2. 
A distributor or lessor shall prepare the records of the details and results of an inspection 
under each item of Subparagraph 1, the issuer and issuance date of a certificate of 
inspection, instructions regarding distribution or lease, etc. and retain such records for 2 
years from the date of distribution; 
3. 
A distributor or lessor shall prepare and keep the records regarding the handling of 
defective medical devices and retain such records for 1 year from the date of the record; 
4. 
A distributor or lessor shall comply with the standards for distribution quality 
management of medical devices specified in Annex 6: Provided, That this shall not apply 
when the business is exempted from distribution business notification requirements under 
Article 17 (2) of the Act. 
 
Article 40 (Matters Regarding Maintenance of Order in Distribution by Distributor or Lessor) 
Matters regarding the maintenance of order in distribution in relation to the safety of medical 
devices, etc. under Article 18 (1) of the Act and Subparagraph 1 of Article 10-2 of the Decree shall 
be as follows: 
1. 
A distributor or lessor shall not purchase medical devices from persons other than 
manufacturers, importers, and distributors: Provided, That purchases from a medical 
institution shall be excluded; 
2. 
A distributor or lessor shall not use any of the following names or labels for the name, etc. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
43 
 
of a business place and shall not use them together with the label of the business place; 
(a) A name or label likely to be misunderstood as a business place of a manufacturer or 
an importer; 
(b) The name of a medical institution under Article 3 of the Medical Service Act or any 
name similar thereto. 
3. 
A distributor or lessor shall not distribute or lease any of the following medical devices 
and shall not store or display them for the purpose of distribution or lease: 
(a) Medical devices with no certificates of inspection attached under Subparagraph 1 (b) 
of Article 39; 
(b) Medical devices contaminated or damaged or those subject to an order of 
collection or destruction issued by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety or the 
Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety; 
(c) Medical devices whose use-by dates or expiration dates passed. 
4. 
A distributor or lessor shall not distribute medical devices for which approval or 
certification has not been obtained or a notification has not been filed and shall not store 
or display them for the purpose of distribution. 
 
Article 41 (Exemption from Certificates of Inspection of Secondhand Medical Devices) 
Medical devices determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, such as 
medical devices with low potential risk, may be distributed with no certificate of inspection 
attached, notwithstanding Articles 27 (1) 15 and 33 (1) 19, Subparagraph 1 (b) of Article 39, and 
Subparagraph 3 (a) of Article 40. 
 
Article 42 (Labeling on Container) The container or wrapper of a medical device need not be 
labeled following the proviso of Article 20, with the exception of its subparagraphs, of the Act, in 
any of the following cases: <Amended on Jun. 15, 2016> 
1. 
When the area of the container or wrapper is too small, or the container or wrapper 
cannot contain all the matters referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 20 of the Act, 
and therefore, such matters are stated on an outside container, outside package, or 
package insert: Provided, That even in such cases, the model name or the trade name of a 
manufacturer or importer shall be stated on the container or wrapper of a medical device; 
2. 
When a medical device for export has been labeled according to the standards of the 
export destination country. 
 
Article 43 (Labeling on Package Inserts) (1) "Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Prime 
Minister" in Article 22 (1) 4 of the Act refers to the following: <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024>

The matters prescribed in Subparagraphs 1 through 3 and 5 through 7 of Article 20 of the

The intended use of a product;

Article 45-3 (Notification and Monitoring of Voluntary Deliberation Agency) (1) A person who

Act and Article 10-5 (4) of the Decree shall submit an application for the notification of a voluntary 
deliberation agency for the advertisement of medical devices to the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety, along with the following documents. In such cases, the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
shall verify the corporation registration certificate (limited to a corporation) through administrative 
data matching under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: <Amended on Jan. 21, 
2022> 
1. 
Status of a department and full-time workers that are exclusively responsible for relevant 
affairs under Article 10-5 (3) 1 of the Decree; 
2. 
Status of computerized equipment and an office under Article 10-5 (3) 2 of the Decree; 
3. 
A copy of the articles of association of the institution or organization; 
4. 
A copy of the registration of a consumer organization made with the Fair Trade 
Commission under Article 29 of the Framework Act On Consumers (limited to cases 
under Article 25-2 (1) 2). 
(2)  A voluntary deliberation agency shall monitor whether an advertisement of medical devices 
that it has reviewed complies with Article 24 (2) or (3) under Article 25-4, and submit the 
results thereof to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety for each quarter within 30 days from 
the end of the pertinent quarter. 
[Newly inserted on Jun. 24, 2021] 
 
Article 45-4 (Medical Devices Subject to Sealing) (1) “Medical devices prescribed by Ordinance 
of the Prime Minister” in Article 25-5, with the exception of its subparagraphs, of the Act refers to 
any of the following medical devices: 
1. 
Medical devices that are subject to tracking management are to be inserted into the 
human body for at least 1 year, and have sterile packaging; 
2. 
The following medical devices that are likely to be contaminated or spoiled when 
distributed while being open: 
(a) Disposable syringes (limited to those with sterile packaging); 
(b) Disposable needles (limited to those with sterile packaging); 
(c) Sutures; 
(d) Wound dressings (limited to those with sterile packaging); 
(e) Contact lenses; 
(f) Other medical devices with sterile packaging, which are publicly notified by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety that such devices need to be enveloped during 
distribution. 
(2)  The seal under Article 25-5 shall ensure that a container or package cannot be opened without 
removing the seal thereon and is difficult to return to its original condition after being opened. 
[Newly inserted on Jan. 21, 2022] 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act

Article 46 (Approval for Display of Medical Devices for the Purpose of Exhibition) (1) A 
person who intends to display medical devices for the purpose of exhibition under the proviso of 
Article 26 (1) of the Act shall obtain approval therefor from the Commissioner of the Regional 
Office of Food and Drug Safety in advance. 
(2) A person who intends to display medical devices approved under Paragraph (1) shall not 
engage in acts other than those determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety, such as the simple operation of devices to explain the utilization methods, etc. 
and attachment or keeping of promotional materials regarding the notified details. 
(3) When medical devices approved under Paragraph (1) fall under any of the following cases, the 
Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety shall revoke such approval, and 
may take measures including the enveloping or sealing of the relevant medical devices or the 
suspension of the display thereof: 
1. 
When medical devices are displayed or used differently from what have been approved; 
2. 
When acts other than those approved under Paragraph (2) are performed; 
3. 
When other acts likely to cause harm to public health are performed. 
(4) After the certified medical devices under Paragraph (1) are used following their certification, 
the relevant medical devices may be used as medical devices under Subparagraph 4 of Article 
10, Article 32 (1) 5-2 and 5-3 as determined and publicly noticed by the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety. <Newly inserted on Jun. 24, 2021> 
(5) Details regarding methods and procedures for filing an application for approval under 
Paragraph (1), approval standards, and other matters shall be determined and publicly notified 
by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. <Amended on Jun. 24, 2021> 
 
Article 46-2 (Minor Repair for Change of Medical Devices) A medical device repairer may make 
repairs to change any of the following appearances within the extent not to affect the safety and 
effectiveness of the medical devices under the proviso of Article 26 (3) of the Act: 
1. 
Repairs to change the colors, materials, etc. of outer packages aimed at protecting the 
medical devices from external shock; 
2. 
Repairs to change the shapes, structures, etc. of external appearances, such as holders, 
handles, or wheels, not directly related to the performance of medical devices. 
[Newly inserted on Jun. 14, 2018] 
 
Article 47 (Scope of Approval to Alter or Remodel Medical Devices) Medical devices that 
manufacturers and importers may alter or remodel under Article 26 (4) 1 of the Act shall be as 
follows. In such cases, such medical devices shall be altered or remodeled to the extent not to 
change the unique characteristics but to improve the performance thereof: 
1. 
Radiation-generating devices for diagnosis under Article 37 of the Medical Service Act; 
2. 
Special medical equipment under Article 38 of the Medical Service Act;

3. 
Other medical devices determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety, whose safety and effectiveness are not affected by alteration or remodeling.

the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, such as matters to be stated by an audit

organization when issuing compliance certificates. 
(5) The Minister of Food and Drug Safety may conduct a regular or occasional investigation into
