(6) Except as provided in Paragraphs (1) through (5), details necessary for the procedures and 
methods for designating an audit organization, operation thereof, etc. shall be determined and 
publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
 
Article 49 (Standards for the Designation and Management of Medical Devices Subject to 
Tracking Management) (1) Medical devices subject to tracking management under the 
subparagraphs of Article 29 (1) of the Act shall be as follows: 
1. 
The following medical devices to be inserted into the human body for at least 1 year: 
(a) Implantable cardiac pacemakers; 
(b) Implantable cardiac pacemaker electrodes; 
(c) Composite artificial heart valves; 
(d) Biological artificial heart valves; 
(e) Non-biological artificial heart valves; 
(f) Implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs); 
(g) Electrically-powered implantable infusion pumps; 
(h) Other medical devices determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety as necessary to track the locations of such devices. 
2. 
The following medical devices for life support used in any place other than a medical 
institution: 
(a) Home care ventilators (limited to regular wearing); 
(b) Other medical devices determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety as necessary to track the locations of such devices. 
(2)  When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety permits the manufacture, import, etc. of 
medical devices subject to tracking management under Paragraph (1), he or she shall 
state in the license the phrase “Medical Device Subject to Tracking Management.” 
 
Article 49-2 (Criteria for Designation of Medical Devices Subject to Long-term Follow-up) (1) 
The Minister of Food and Drug Safety may designate medical devices subject to long-term follow-
up under Article 29 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as “medical devices subject to long-term 
follow-up”) by comprehensively reviewing the following matters: 
1. 
Whether adverse events associated with the use of the medical device occur at least once 
a year, thereby requiring continuous verification of the device’s safety; 
2. 
Whether the device is likely to cause serious adverse effects, such as death or non-curable 
conditions, after being implanted in the human body; 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
50 
 
3. 
Any other matters equivalent to those under subparagraphs 1 and 2, which the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety deems necessary for reviewing the designation of medical devices 
subject to long-term follow-up . 
(2)  When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety designates medical devices subject to long-term 
follow-up pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister shall publicly announce such designation. 
[Newly inserted on Aug. 1, 2025] 
 
Article 50 (Matters regarding Records on Medical Devices Subject to Tracking Management) 
(1) Manufacturers, importers, distributors, lessors, and repairers who handle medical devices under 
Article 30 (1) of the Act (hereinafter “handlers”) and the founders of medical institutions that 
handle medical devices subject to tracking management, and medical doctors, oriental medical 
doctors, dentists, etc. who work at medical institutions (hereinafter “users”) shall prepare records of 
the following matters: <Amended on Aug. 1, 2025> 
1. 
Records of handlers: 
(a) The quantity and date of manufacture or import (limited to manufacturers or 
importers) by product name (by item name, in the absence of the product name), by 
model name, and by manufacture unit; 
(b) The quantity and date of distribution or lease; the trade name and address of a 
distributor or lessor or the founder of a medical institution (excluding repairers) by 
product name (by item name, in the absence of the product name), by model name, 
and by manufacture unit; 
(c) The date of repair and the trade name and address of a requester (limited to repairers) 
by product name (by item name, in the absence of the product name), by model 
name, and by manufacture unit; 
(d) Other matters necessary to prevent harm to health and hygiene; 
2. 
Records of users: 
(a) The name and resident registration number of a patient who uses a medical device 
subject to tracking management; 
(b) The name and manufacturing number of a medical device subject to tracking 
management, and those in lieu thereof; 
(c) The date of use of a medical device subject to tracking management; 
(d) The name and location of a medical institution that uses a medical device subject to 
tracking management; 
(e) Other matters necessary to prevent harm to health and hygiene. 
(2) Handlers or users of medical devices subject to tracking management shall submit records and 
data related to the medical devices subject to tracking management to the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety according to the following classifications. In such cases, such handlers or users 
may submit such records and data using a computer program determined by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety: <Newly inserted on Jun. 15, 2016; Jun. 24, 2021; Aug. 1, 2025> 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
51 
 
1. 
Handlers: Handlers shall prepare records and data related to medical devices subject to 
tracking management every month and submit such records and data by the end of the 
following month as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety; 
2. 
Users: 
(a) In cases of business closure of a medical institution, users shall submit the entire 
record of use when filing a notification of business closure; 
(b) In cases of medical devices subject to tracking management publicly notified by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety that may cause death or are gravely life-
threatening, users shall submit data for each half year by the end of the following 
month of the end of the pertinent half year. Provided, however, that if data on real-
world use information (referring to real-world use information under Article 30 (3) 
of the Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) have been submitted pursuant to Article 
50-2 (2) and (3), the relevant data may be omitted from submission; 
(c) Upon receipt of a request by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety to submit records 
and data related to medical devices subject to tracking management, users shall 
submit such records and data within 10 days from the date of receipt of such request. 
(3) When handlers and users of medical devices subject to tracking management prepare records 
under Paragraph (1), they shall maintain confidentiality. 
(4) Records of medical devices subject to tracking management under Paragraph (1) shall be 
retained until the time determined by the following subparagraphs: 
1. 
When a medical device subject to tracking management is no longer used because of the 
death, etc. of a patient who has used such medical device; 
2. 
When the reasons to retain the previous records of a non-single-use medical device 
subject to tracking management cease to exist as the information thereon under Paragraph 
(1) 2 (a) or (c) is newly recorded; 
3. 
When the reasons to retain the relevant records cease to exist, as tracking management 
is no longer necessary or any other reason occurs. 
(5) The Minister of Food and Drug Safety may create and operate unique device identification 
(UDI) codes to be attached to or labeled on the containers, outer packages, or packages of 
medical devices subject to tracking management for efficient management of medical devices 
subject to tracking management. 
(6) Details regarding records by handlers or users of medical devices subject to tracking 
management under Paragraphs (1) and (2) and the submission of such records shall be 
determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. <Newly inserted on 
Jun. 24, 2021> 
 
Article 50-2 (Methods and Procedures for the Collection, Analysis, and Evaluation of Real-
World Use Information) (1) The head of the NIDS entrusted with the duties of collecting, 
analyzing, and evaluating real-world use information pursuant to Article 44 (2) of the Act may 
recruit users to participate in long-term follow-up (hereinafter referred to as “participants”) in order 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
52 
 
to collect, analyze, and evaluate real-world use information pursuant to Article 30 (3) of the Act. 
(2)  The data submitted by participants who respond to the recruitment under paragraph (1) to the 
head of the NIDS pursuant to Article 30 (3) of the Act shall consist of the following real-world 
use information generated in the process of using medical devices subject to long-term follow-
up: 
1. 
The name and resident registration number of the patient using the medical device subject 
to long-term follow-up; 
2. 
The name and manufacturing number of the medical device subject to long-term follow-
up, or information in lieu thereof; 
3. 
The date and time of use of the medical device subject to long-term follow-up, and the 
details of such use; 
4. 
The date and time of occurrence of any adverse event and its details; 
5. 
The name and location of the medical institution where the device is used; 
6. 
Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety for long-term 
follow-up and publicly notified by the Minister. 
(3)  When submitting data on real-world use information under paragraph (2) to the head of the 
NIDS, participants may do so using a computerized program designated by the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety. 
(4)  The head of the NIDS shall analyze and evaluate the data on real-world use information 
submitted by participants pursuant to paragraphs (2) and (3) on a semiannual basis and report 
the results to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety by the end of the month following the end 
of each half-year. However, in any of the following cases, the results of the analysis and 
evaluation shall be reported without delay: 
1. 
Where the frequency of adverse events significantly differs from that in previously 
reported analysis and evaluation results; 
2. 
Where the details of the adverse event fall under any of the subparagraphs of Article 51 
(1); 
3. 
Any other case equivalent to subparagraphs 1 and 2, where the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety considers it necessary to analyze and evaluate the adverse event without delay and 
requests such analysis and evaluation. 
(5)  In addition to the matters prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), detailed matters concerning 
the methods and procedures for the collection, analysis, and evaluation of real-world use 
information shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
[Newly inserted on Aug. 1, 2025] 
 
Article 51 (Reporting on Side Effects) (1) A person who intends to file a report on the side effects 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
53 
 
of a medical device under Article 31 (1) of the Act shall do so as prescribed in the following 
subparagraphs and retain the relevant data for two years: 
1. 
Within 7 days, when a medical device causes death or life-threatening side effects. In 
such cases, the details thereof shall be additionally reported within eight days from the 
date of the first report; 
2. 
Within 15 days, when the following side effects are caused or adverse events occur: 
(a) When admission to a hospital or the extension of an admission period is required; 
(b) When recovery is impossible or a serious disability or impaired function occurs; 
(c) When congenital malformations or abnormalities are caused. 
(2) The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall notify the founder of a medical institution of the 
side effects, a recall plan, etc. under Article 31 (4) of the Act by means of visit, mail, telephone, 
email, fax, etc. 
(3) The founder of a medical institution who has notified patients of the side effects, recall plan, 
etc. under Article 31 (5) of the Act shall prepare a written confirmation of notice to the patients 
in Form 42 and submit it to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. <Amended on Jun. 14, 
2018> 
(4) Except as provided in Paragraphs (1) through (3), details regarding the reporting and 
management of side effects shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food 
and Drug Safety. 
 
Article 52 (Standards and Procedures for the Recall of Harmful Medical Devices) (1) With 
respect to any medical device that has caused, or is likely to cause, harm to the human body among 
the medical devices repaired, distributed, or leased (hereinafter “medical device subject to recall”), 
the relevant medical device repairer, distributor, or lessor shall immediately cease repairing, 
distributing, or leasing such medical device following Article 31 (2) of the Act and notify such fact 
to the manufacturer or importer of such medical device (hereinafter “person responsible for recall”). 
(2) Following Article 31 (2) of the Act, with respect to medical devices that a person responsible 
for recall has distributed or leased after manufacturing or importing such devices, such person 
responsible for recall shall verify whether any medical device suspected to be subject to recall 
or any medical device notified under Paragraph (1) falls under any of the following: 
1. 
A medical device of which use causes grave irreversible side effects or death, or a 
medical device that is likely to cause such side effects or death; 
2. 
A medical device of which use causes reversible temporary or medical side effects, or 
a medical device that is likely to cause such side effects; 
3. 
A medical device which, when used, rarely causes side effects, but is problematic in 
terms of safety and effectiveness for failing to satisfy the standard specifications referred 
to in Article 19 of the Act. 
(3) With respect to any medical device found to be falling under any subparagraph of Paragraph (2) 
based on the results of verification under Paragraph (2), a person responsible for recall 
shall take measures, such as immediately ceasing the distribution of the relevant medical 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
54 
 
device, and submit a recall plan in Form 43 (including a plan in electronic form) to the 
Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety having jurisdiction over 
the location of the person responsible for recall business within 5 days from the date of 
verification under Paragraph (2). In such cases, the person responsible for recall may submit 
a recall plan using a computer program determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
<Amended on Dec. 31, 2018; Dec. 23, 2019>

Deleted. <Dec. 31, 2018>

Article 53 (Publication of Recall Plans) (1) Upon receipt of an order to publish a recall plan from 
the Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety following Article 31 (3) of the 
Act, a person responsible for recall shall publish such recall plan according to the following 
classifications: 
1. 
Medical devices falling under Article 52 (2) 1: Public announcement of the recall plan 
through broadcasting defined in Subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act; 
daily newspapers (referring to all the copies of the relevant newspapers printed and 
distributed for a day] that are distributed nationwide and registered under Article 9 (1) of 
the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, Etc.; or mass media at least equivalent thereto 
(including such media as may be recognized by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
considering the intended uses, utilization methods, etc. of medical devices subject to 
recall); 
2. 
Medical devices falling under Article 52 (2) 2: Public announcement of the recall plan in 
medical journals or medical engineering journals or media at least equivalent thereto; 
3. 
Medical devices falling under Article 52 (2) 3: Public announcement of the recall plan on 
the website of a person responsible for recall or media at least equivalent thereto. 
(2) The Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety may post the trade name of 
a person responsible for recall; the name, manufacturing number, date of manufacturing, use-
by date, and expiration date of a product; and the reason for recall on the website of the 
regional office of food and drug safety. 
(3) A person responsible for recall shall notify a recall plan to a repairer, distributer, lessor, or 
founder of a medical institution that handles medical devices subject to recall (hereinafter 
“handler of medical devices subject to recall”) via visit, mail, telephone, telegram, email, fax, 
public announcement through media, etc. and retain data evidencing such notice for two years 
from the date of the completion of recall. 
(4) A handler of medical devices subject to recall notified of a recall plan under Paragraph (3) 
shall take measures, such as returning a medical device subject to recall, and prepare a written 
confirmation of recall in Form 44 and send it to the person responsible for the recall of such 
medical device subject to recall. 
(5) Deleted. <Jun. 14, 2018> 
(6) The Minister of Food and Drug Safety may establish and operate a computer program that 
provides information on medical devices subject to recall, etc. and recommend that a handler 
of medical devices subject to recall, etc. install such program. 
(7) Except as provided in Paragraphs (1) through (6), details regarding the method and period for 
the publication of recall plans, notice of such plans, etc. shall be determined and publicly 
notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. <Newly inserted on Dec. 31, 2018> 
[Paragraph (5) of this Article shall be effective until May 10, 2016, following Article 2 of the 
Addenda to the Ordinance of the Prime Minister No. 1181 promulgated on Jul. 29, 2015.]

Article 54-3 (Operation of UDI System) (1) The information to be registered (including

Article 54-4 (Standards, Targets, and Procedures for Reporting Foreign Substances) (1) The 
scope of foreign substances to be reported to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety by a medical 
device handler following Article 31-5 (1) of the Act (hereinafter “foreign substances”) shall be as 
follows: 
1. 
A substance that is not a normal material used for medical devices, such as metal, plastic, 
or debris generated during manufacturing processes and that may cause direct or indirect 
harm or damage to the human body during the use of the medical devices; 
2. 
A substance related to living things such as insects and their eggs, parasites and their eggs, 
and animal carcasses that may cause direct or indirect harm or damage to the human body 
during the use of medical devices; 
3. 
Other substances determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety to prevent harm caused by the use of medical devices among the substances 
equivalent to those falling under Subparagraph 1 or 2. 
(2) Medical device handlers who intend to report the discovery of foreign substances following 
Article 31-5 (1) of the Act shall submit a foreign substance discovery report in Form 48-3 
(including a report in electronic form), along with evidentiary data to the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety. <Amended on Oct. 22, 2019> 
(3) Upon receipt of a report on the discovery of foreign substances following Paragraph (2), the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall notify the details thereof to the Commissioner of the 
Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety without delay. 
(4) Upon receipt of notice under Paragraph (3), the Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food 
and Drug Safety shall conduct an investigation into the cause of inclusion of the foreign 
substances without delay following Article 31-5 (2) of the Act. In such cases, the 
Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety may request necessary 
cooperation from the relevant central administrative agencies, local governments, public 
institutions, corporations, organizations, experts, etc. to investigate the cause of inclusion of 
the foreign substances. 
(5) Where the Commissioner of a Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety has completed an 
investigation into the cause of foreign substance contamination pursuant to paragraph (4), he or 
she shall report the investigation results and an action plan to the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety, and, taking into comprehensive consideration the contents of the investigation results, 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
59 
 
the safety of the medical device, and the necessity of preventing harm, shall, without delay, 
take the measures specified in each of the following subparagraphs. <Amended on Jan. 21, 
2022; Mar. 8, 2024> 
1. 
An order to conduct an inspection following Article 33 of the Act; 
2. 
An order of recall, destruction, or any other treatment or the publication thereof following 
Article 34 of the Act; 
3. 
An order of necessary measures such as suspension of use or repair following Article 35 
of the Act. 
(6) Except as provided in Paragraphs (1) through (5), details necessary for the procedures and 
methods for reporting the discovery of foreign substances and for an investigation into the 
inclusion of foreign substances, and relevant measures shall be determined and publicly 
notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
[Newly inserted on Jun. 12, 2019] 
[Renumbered from the previous Article 54-3 on Oct. 22, 2019] 
 
Article 54-5 (Public Announcement of Foreign Substance Findings, etc.) (1) Where any of the 
investigation results reported pursuant to Article 54-4 (5) falls under any of the following 
subparagraphs, the Minister of Food and Drug Safety may, pursuant to Article 31-5 (3) of the Act, 
publicly announce on the website of the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety the fact that foreign 
substances were found, the investigation results, and the action plan. 
1. 
Where it is recognized that harm to public health has occurred or is likely to occur due to 
the use of medical devices contaminated with foreign substances 
2. 
Where foreign substances are found at a location where they may directly or indirectly 
come into contact with the human body, or where it is otherwise necessary to promptly 
notify the public of such findings to prevent harm to public health 
(2)  In addition to the matters prescribed in paragraph (1), detailed matters necessary for the public 
announcement of foreign substance findings, etc. shall be determined and publicly notified by 
the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
[Newly Inserted on Mar. 8, 2024]

on-site inspection is refused), the Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall notify the results of 
the inspection and provide opinions on the necessary measures to the Commissioner of the 
Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety within 30 days from the completion date of the on-
site inspection. 
(3) The Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety notified of the results of an 
on-site inspection under Paragraph (2) may take the following measures following Article 
32-2 (2) of the Act. In such cases, with respect to the relevant measure taken, the 
Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety shall notify the matters 
pertaining to the details of, reasons for, and date of such measure, etc. in writing (including 
electronic documents) to the medical device manufacturer, the medical device importer, the 
manager of an overseas manufacturing site, or the government of an exporting country: 
<Amended on Jan. 21, 2022> 
1. 
Suspension of import; 
2. 
An order of recall, destruction, or any other measure or the publication thereof following 
Article 34 of the Act; 
3. 
An order of necessary measures, such as suspension of use or repair, following Article 35 
of the Act. 
(4) When any measure is canceled following Article 32-2 (3) of the Act, such as suspension of 
import, the Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety shall notify the 
matters pertaining to the details of, reasons for, and date of the cancellation, etc. in writing 
(including electronic documents) to the medical device manufacturer, the medical device 
importer, the manager of an overseas manufacturing site, or the government of an exporting 
country.

Article 59-3 (Designation of Medical Device Safety Information Monitoring Centers) (1) A 
person who intends to obtain designation as a monitoring center (hereinafter “monitoring center”) 
on medical device safety information under Article 43 (1) 7 (hereinafter “medical device safety 
information”) for an institution following Article 43 (3) shall submit an application for

regarding the following matters: 
1. 
A business progress plan of a monitoring center; 
2. 
Budget for a business progress plan of a monitoring center; 
3.

4. 
Performance regarding collection and analysis of medical device safety information 
within the last 3 years (only when applicable); 
5. 
Other matters similar to documents under Subparagraphs 1 through 4 which are 
deemed necessary by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
(2) Upon receipt of an application under Paragraph (1), the Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall 
verify a license for opening a medical institution through administrative data matching under 
Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That when an applicant does not 
consent to the verification of the license for opening a medical institution, such applicant 
shall attach a copy thereof. 
(3) When deemed necessary for designation as a monitoring center under Article 43 (3) by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety, he or she may conduct a fact-finding survey on the facility 
and personnel of such center. 
(4) When deemed necessary for effective operation of monitoring centers under Article 43 (3) by 
the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, he or she may designate monitoring centers by 
distributing them across regions or districts as determined by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety. 
(5) When the Minister of Food and Drug Safety designates a monitoring center under Article 43 
(3), he or she shall issue the applicant with a certificate of designation as a monitoring center in 
Form 50-5. 
(6) Except as provided in Paragraphs (1) through (5), details necessary for procedures and 
methods for designation as a monitoring center shall be determined and publicly notified by 
the Minister of Food and Drug Safety.

Article 59-4 (Business Scope and Operation of Monitoring Centers) (1) The scope of business 
of a monitoring center shall be as follows: 
1. 
Collection of side effects or safety information regarding medical devices; 
2. 
Analysis and research on side effects of medical devices; 
3. 
Exchange and cooperation with other medical institutions regarding medical device safety 
information; 
4. 
Education and campaigns regarding medical device safety information; 
5. 
Business similar to the matters under Subparagraphs 1 through 4 which is deemed 
necessary by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
(2) A monitoring center shall report through the NIDS every year to the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety on matters regarding a business operation plan, budget plan, results of business 
and budget execution, etc., as determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
(3) A monitoring center shall notify the NIDS every month of matters on side effects or safety 
information as determined by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety for supporting medical 
device safety information businesses: Provided, That in cases of matters regarding information 
with grave effects on public health, etc., the monitoring center shall report such matters to the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety and the NIDS without delay. 
(4) When deemed necessary for securement of appropriate business operations or budget 
operations of a monitoring center by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, he or she may 
order relevant measures, including the complementation or improvement of the relevant 
monitoring center. 
(5) When deemed necessary for facilitation of the operation of a monitoring center by the Minister 
of Food and Drug Safety, he or she shall fully or partially support operational expenses of 
such center within a set budget. 
(6) Except as provided in Paragraphs (1) through (5), details necessary for the business, operation, 
and supervision of a monitoring center shall be determined and publicly notified by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
[Newly inserted on Dec. 4, 2020]

Article 61-2 (Qualifications, Scope of Duties, and Identifications of Investigators of Causal 
Relationship) (1) An investigator of causal relationship under Article 43-5 (1) of the Act 
(hereinafter “investigator of causal relationship”) shall be appointed or commissioned from among

1. 
An employee of the NIDS responsible for investigating and identifying the causal

2.

3. 
A medical doctor, dentist, oriental medical doctor, or nurse referred to in Article 2 (1) of 
the Medical Service Act; 
4. 
Other persons with abundant expertise and experience in fields related to medical devices. 
(2) The head of the NIDS may pay allowances and travel expenses to a commissioned 
investigator of causal relationship within a set budget. 
(3) An investigator of causal relationship may investigate and identify the causal relationship 
between medical devices and the side effects in any of the following cases: 
1. 
When side effects falling under Article 51 (1) 1 or 2 have occurred or are suspected of 
having occurred during the use of medical devices; 
2. 
When unintended syndromes, symptoms, or diseases have occurred in large numbers 
to patients who have used the medical devices at a specific region or in a specific period 
of time; 
3. 
Other cases where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety deems it necessary to 
investigate and identify the causal relationship between medical devices and the side 
effects. 
(4) An identification indicating the authority of an investigator of causal relationship referred to in 
the latter part of Article 43-5 (3) of the Act shall be as prepared in Form 50-4. 
(5) “Relevant documents” in the latter part of Article 43-5 (3) of the Act refers to documents 
including the following matters: 
1. 
The purpose, duration, scope, and contents of the investigation; 
2. 
The name and position of a person responsible for the investigation; 
3. 
The list of submitted data; 
4. 
The statutes and regulations serving as a legal basis for the investigation; 
5. 
The details of administrative dispositions, penalties, etc. for the refusal, obstruction, 
evasion, etc. of the investigation and statutes and regulations used as a legal basis therefor;

manufacturing approval, etc. under the main text of Article 49 (1) (hereinafter “manufacturing 
approval, etc.”) does not apply to any of the following medical devices following the proviso of

Article 62-2 (Renewal of Manufacturing Approval) Standards for manufacturing approval, etc. 
under Article 49 (3) of the Act shall be as follows: 
1. 
Any serious problem shall not exist regarding safety or effectiveness of medical devices; 
2. 
Data necessary for renewal of manufacturing approval, etc. shall be faithfully submitted; 
3. 
Production or import performance data shall exist regarding the relevant medical device; 
4. 
Statues and regulations related to medical devices shall be faithfully observed; 
5. 
Other standards similar to the ones under Subparagraphs 1 through 4 determined and 
publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall be satisfied. 
(2) A person who intends to have manufacturing approval, etc. renewed under Article 49 (3) of the 
Act shall submit an application for the renewal of manufacturing (import) approval in Form 51, 
an application for renewal of manufacturing (import) certification in Form 51-2, or an 
application for notification of the renewal of manufacturing (import) notification in Form 51-3 
(including an application in electronic form) to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety [limited 
to manufacturing (import) renewal; hereinafter the same shall apply] or to the NIDS [limited to 
manufacturing (import) certification or notification renewal; hereinafter the same shall apply], 
along with the following documents (including electronic documents): 
1. 
Original copy of a manufacturing (import) license or manufacturing (import) certificate of 
the relevant medical device; 
2. 
Data evidencing that safety and effectiveness of the relevant medical device has been 
maintained over the previous validity period; 
3. 
Data regarding production or import performance of the relevant medical device for the 
previous validity period; 
4. 
Other cases similar to data under Subparagraphs 1 through 3, which are deemed 
necessary by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety for the renewal of manufacturing 
approval, etc.

such fees as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety.

Medical Devices Act (Ordinance of the Prime Minister No. 1081) enters into force, an in vitro 
diagnostic medical device referred to in this Rule shall be deemed cited in lieu thereof.

Standards and Procedures for Medical Device Classification and Designation of Classes 
(Related to Article 2) 
 
1. 
Standards for the Classification of Medical Devices 
A. The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall classify medical devices into any of the 
following four classes through deliberation by the Medical Device Committee 
according to the purpose of use and the degree of potential risk to human body. In 
such case, if a medical device falls under two or more of the following classes, it 
shall be classified into the class of the highest risk: 
1) 
Class I: Medical devices with little potential risk; 
2) 
Class II: Medical devices with low potential risk; 
3) 
Class III: Medical devices with moderate potential risk; 
4) 
Class IV: Medical devices with high risk. 
B. 
The standard for deciding the degree of potential risk of Item A are as follows: 
1) 
Duration of contact with human body; 
2) 
Degree of invasiveness; 
3) 
Whether a device delivers medicine or energy to the patient; 
4) 
Whether a device has biological impact on the patient. 
C. 
Deleted. <May 1, 2020> 
D. Deleted. <May 1, 2020> 
E. 
Detailed standards for the purpose and use and potential risk under Items A and B 
shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
 
2. 
Procedures for Designation of Class 
 
The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall classify medical devices into Section, 
Division, or Group according to the classification of the following items. In such case, 
items classified as Section and Division shall be publicly notified, and items classified as 
Group shall be publicly notified by assigning classification to each item: 
A. Section: Classification of medical devices into each instrument/machine, device, or material; 
B. 
Division: Classification of each Section into product groups with similar raw 
material, manufacturing process, and quality control system: 
C. 
Group: Classification of each Division into each item where functions are 
demonstrated independently. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
85 
 
3. 
Application for Class Re-Designation and Designation Procedures 
A. The Minister of Food and Drug Safety may re-designate the class of each item 
through deliberation by the Medical Device Committee when there is an application 
for re-designation from the party concerned, etc., or when it is deemed there is a 
need for such re-designation. 
B. 
In cases of re-designation, the degree of potential risk and validity of such re-
designation under the following standards shall be examined: 
1) 
Whether the description of each item and purpose, use, principle, feature, 
function, etc. of the relevant medical device correspond to similar items; 
2) 
Whether safety and performance of each item are fully secured compared to the 
items already classified to be designated, and managed. 
C. 
A person who intends to apply for class re-designation shall submit an application in 
Form 54 to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, along with the following data: 
1) 
Data on technical document, etc.; 
2) 
Data 
on 
comparative 
analysis 
of 
technical 
characteristics 
including 
structure/operational principle, performance, purpose of use, methods of use, etc. 
with other devices that are similar to medical devices subject to class re-
designation. 
D. Upon receiving an application for class re-designation under the provisions of Item C, 
The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall review and decide within 90 days and 
notify the applicant of the result, and notify the public thereof.

Standards for Facilities and Manufacturing and Quality Management Systems 
(Related to Article 8) 
 
1. 
Facility Standards 
A. Facility of Manufacturing Site 
1) 
A person who intends to obtain a manufacturing approval for medical devices 
(excluding software medical devices) or a manufacturer shall prepare and 
maintain the following facilities and equipment at a manufacturing site and 
shall inspect them periodically to prevent any trouble in manufacturing and 
quality management of medical devices: 
a) 
Production area where manufacturing processes are conducted; 
b) 
Laboratory where the quality management of raw materials, materials, and 
products are conducted; 
c) 
Storage area where raw materials, materials, and products are stored; 
d) 
Facilities and equipment required for manufacturing and quality management. 
2) 
A person who intends to obtain a manufacturing approval for software medical 
devices or a manufacturer shall prepare and maintain premises, facilities, and 
equipment for establishing and implementing a quality management system (QMS) 
under items 2 A and B at a manufacturing site and shall inspect them 
periodically to prevent any trouble in manufacturing and quality management 
of software medical devices. 
B. 
Standards for Manufacturing Site Facility 
 
A Production area and a storage area under items A 1) a) and b) shall satisfy 
the following standards: 
1) 
Production area 
a) 
A production area shall have facilities capable of preventing mice, harmful 
insects, dust, etc. 
b) 
The ceiling of a production area where products requiring sterilization are 
manufactured shall be finished to prevent dust from falling, and its 
floor and walls shall be maintained smooth so that dust or dirt can be 
easily removed, and the surface of its ceiling, floor, and walls shall be made 
to be resistant to cleaning processes using disinfecting sprays. 
c) 
A workbench shall be placed in a production area; In cases of 
manufacturing products requiring sterilization, sterilization facilities shall be 
placed. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
87 
 
2) 
A storage area shall be equipped so as to store raw materials, materials, and 
products hygienically and safely. 
C. 
Entrustment of Manufacturing Process and Testing 
 
A person who intends to obtain a manufacturing business approval or a manufacturer 
may entrust manufacturing processes of medical devices or testing for quality 
management to a medical device testing and inspection institution, a non-clinical trial 
institution, or a manufacturer that has obtained certification of conformity under 
subparagraph 2. 
D. Management Responsibility of Manufacturer for Trustee Entrusted with Manufacturing 
Processes or Testing A manufacturer who has entrusted any manufacturing process 
or testing shall thoroughly manage and supervise the trustee according to the 
following items so that the manufacturing process or testing may be performed 
appropriately: 
1) 
Shall prepare a device master record for quality management, provide it to the 
trustee, and have the trustee record matters concerning manufacturing process 
and quality management for each product based on the device master record; 
2) 
Shall have the trustee submit records on the manufacturing process and quality 
management of each product under item A, and retain them until one year 
from the expiration date of the product; Provided, That in cases of a product 
with no expiration date established, such records shall be preserved for a period 
corresponding to the life span of the product. 
 
2. 
Standards for Manufacturing and Quality Management System 
A. Quality Management System 
 
A manufacturer shall establish a quality management system (QMS) to efficiently 
manage the organization, responsibilities, procedures, processes, resources, etc. for the 
manufacturing and quality management and prepare documents related to the system 
in writing in forms of a quality manual, etc. 
B. 
Documentation and Implementation of QMS 
 
A manufacturer shall document the details of a QMS, such as procedures and 
methods for the following matters, and implement the QMS accordingly: 
1) 
Quality policy; 
2) 
Contract review; 
3) 
Design management; 
4) 
Document and data management; 
5) 
Purchase management; 
6) 
Product identification and tracking management; 
7) 
Manufacturing process management; 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
88 
 
8) 
Testing and inspection of purchases and products; 
9) 
Management of non-conforming products; 
10) Management of measuring equipment; 
11) Corrective and preventive actions; 
12) Matters concerning product handling, storage, packaging, preservation, and 
delivery; 
13) Education and training; 
14) Other matters necessary for manufacturing and quality management, such as 
product validation, etc. 
C. 
Responsibilities and Authorities 
 
A manufacturer shall define and document the responsibilities and authorities of 
each person, and relationship among these persons who may affect the quality of 
products. 
D. Management of Quality Records 
1) 
A manufacturer shall document and manage the procedures for identification, 
collection, indexing, perusal, storage, maintenance, and disposal of various records 
necessary for manufacturing and quality management. 
2) 
All quality records shall be stored in a facility where any damage, loss, or 
deterioration can be prevented in a manner that enables quick searching for 
necessary data. 
E. 
Quality Inspection, Etc. 
1) 
Internal Quality Inspection 
 
A manufacturer shall, to conform with these standards, document the procedures for 
planning and conducting internal quality inspections, conduct such inspections 
periodically, and use the results for manufacturing and quality management. 
2) 
External Quality Inspection 
 
According to Article 27 (1) 11 of the Rule, a manufacturer shall receive a periodical 
external inspection on conformity with these good manufacturing practices every 
three years as prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety. 
F. 
Certification of Conformity 
1) 
A person who intends to obtain certification for conformity with these standards or 
receive a periodic inspection shall apply to the head of a quality management 
examination agency under Article 28 of the Act as prescribed by the Minister of 
Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. 
2) 
Upon receipt of an application under 1), the head of a quality management 
examination agency shall conduct a document review and a fact-finding survey 
of the manufacturing site of the applicant as prescribed and publicly notified 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
89 
 
by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety: Provided, That this fact-finding survey 
may not be required if approved by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
3) 
Where, as a result of the document review and on-site inspection under subparagraph 
2, it is deemed to conform to the Medical Device Good Manufacturing Practices 
(GMP) prescribed by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, the head of a quality 
management examination agency shall issue a Certificate of Conformity with the 
Medical Device Good Manufacturing Practices and shall notify the results to the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety or the Commissioner of the Regional Office of 
Food and Drug Safety 
4) 
The Minister of Food and Drug Safety or the Commissioner of the Regional 
Office of Food and Drug Safety shall take administrative measures following 
relevant regulations according to the inspection results reported by the quality 
management examination agency. 
5) 
A person who intends to obtain a certification for conformity with the Standards or 
receive a periodic inspection on such compliance shall pay all or part of the 
expenses incurred for the process. 
G. Detailed Standards 
 
Details of manufacturing and quality management processes and matters not specified in 
the Standards shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety.
