ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT [Annex 3]  
<Amended on Jun. 24, 2021> 
 
Good Clinical Practice for Medical Devices  
(Related to Article 24 (1)) 
 
1. 
Purpose 
 
The purpose of this Good Clinical Practice (GCP) is to obtain accurate and reliable data and 
results and ensure that the protection of the rights and interests of the subjects and the 
guarantee of confidentiality are appropriately achieved during any clinical trial, by 
specifying standards for planning, implementing, monitoring, inspecting, data recording 
and analysis, preparing the clinical study report necessary for conducting such a clinical 
trial, etc. 
 
2. 
Definitions 
 
The terms used in this GCP are defined as follows: 
a. 
The term “clinical trial/study” refers to a test or research on human subjects to 
evidence the safety and effectiveness of a medical device used in clinical trials. 
b. 
The term “multicenter trial” refers to a clinical trial conducted at 2 or more 
clinical trial institutions under 1 clinical trial protocol. 
c. 
The term “non-clinical study” refers to a biomedical study not performed on 
human subjects. 
d. 
The term “clinical trial protocol (hereinafter, “protocol“)” refers to a document 
describing the purpose, subject, test (research) method, statistical considerations, 
relevant organizations, etc. of a clinical trial to provide the background or grounds for 
the relevant clinical trial. 
e. 
The term “protocol amendment” refers to a document stating changes in the content 
of a clinical trial protocol or clearly restating the ambiguous parts of the initial 
clinical trial protocol. 
f. 
The term “case report form” (CRF) refers to a document printed or electronically stored 
for recording information requested in a clinical trial protocol for each subject and 
delivering it to the sponsor of the clinical trial (hereinafter, “sponsor”). 
g. 
The term “clinical trial/study report (hereinafter, “CSR“)” refers to a document that 
describes the results obtained from a clinical trial which are integrated in clinical 
and statistical aspects. 
h. 
The term “interim clinical trial/study report” (hereinafter, “interim report”) refers to a 
document reporting interim results based on analyses conducted during a clinical 
trial. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
91 
 
i. 
The term “investigational device” refers to a study device and comparator used in a 
clinical trial. 
j. 
The term “study device” refers to a medical device excluding comparator among 
investigational devices. 
k. 
The term “comparator” refers to a mock product or a medical device under 
development or on the market, which is used in a clinical trial for being compared 
with a study device. 
l. 
The term “adverse event (AE)” refers to any unintended sign (including abnormal 
laboratory test results, etc.), symptom, or disease that occurs in a subject during a 
clinical trial, which does not necessarily has a causal relationship with the relevant 
investigational device. 
m. The term “adverse device effect (ADE)” refers to any harmful and unintended 
reactions arising out of use of an investigational device, where the causal relationship 
between these reactions and the device cannot be denied. 
n. 
The term “serious AE/ADE” refers to any of the following cases among adverse events 
or adverse device effects resulting from the medical device used in a clinical trial: 
1) 
Resulting in death or is life-threatening; 
2) 
Causing a subject to be hospitalized or extending the hospitalization of a 
subject; 
3) 
Resulting in a permanent or significant disability or decrease in function; 
4) 
Resulting deformity or abnormality in a fetus. 
o. 
The term “unexpected adverse device effect” refers to deviation from the aspect of 
adverse device effects or the degree of harm considering the available medical-device-
related information such as investigators’ brochure or medical device package inserts. 
p. 
The term “subject/trial subject” (hereinafter, “subject”) refers to a person who 
participates in a clinical trial by being subject to the application of investigational devices 
or being included in a control group. 
q. 
The term “vulnerable subjects” refer to subjects whose voluntary decision to 
participate in a clinical trial may be affected by their expectation of benefits related 
to their participation, or their fear of disadvantages from their superiors in the 
organizational hierarchy in cases of refusing to participate (e.g. students at medical 
colleges, oriental medicine colleges, pharmaceutical colleges, dental colleges, and nursing 
colleges; workers at medical institutions and research institutes; employees at 
manufacturing companies; military personnel; prisoners, etc.), patients suffering from 
incurable diseases, people housed in any of group facilities under Article 22, the 
unemployed, the poor, patients faced with emergencies, racial minorities, vagrants, the 
homeless, refugees, minors, or other subjects unable to give consent of their free will. 
r. 
The term “well-being of the trial subjects” refers to physical and mental well-being 
of subjects participating in a clinical trial. 
s. 
The term “subject identification code” refers to a unique identifier assigned to 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
92 
 
each subject by the principal investigator to protect the identity of the subject, 
which is used instead of the name of the subject when the principal investigator 
reports adverse events or other data related to the clinical trial. 
t. 
The term “investigators” collectively refer to a principal investigator, a subinvestigator or 
a coordinating investigator of a clinical trial. 
u. 
The term “coordinating committee” refers to a committee organized by the sponsor to 
coordinate the implementation of a multicenter trial. 
v. 
The term “coordinating investigator” refers to a principal investigator from each 
clinical trial institution with the authority and duty to coordinate opinions among 
investigators participating in a multicenter trial. 
w. The term “subject information sheet” refers to a document provided to subjects by a 
principal investigator that includes any information related to a clinical trial in order 
to obtain consent of the subjects on their participation in the trial. 
x. 
The term “subject’s representative” refers to a person with parental authority, spouse, 
or guardian of a subject, who can make a decision regarding the subject‘s participation 
in a clinical trial on behalf of the subject. 
y. 
The term “source data” refers to any information contained in an original document or an 
official copy of an original document stating relevant clinical findings, observations, 
other actions, etc. necessary to reproduce or evaluate a clinical trial. 
z. 
The term “source document” refers to any document (including electronic documents), 
data, and records that contain source data, such as hospital records, medical records, 
subject records, notes, pathology test results, subjects’ diaries, evaluation checklists, 
medical device dispensing records, data recorded on automated test equipment, test 
certificates and official copies thereof, microfiches (pieces of film containing 
microphotographs of each page of a book), microfilm, radiological test data, magnetic 
tapes, pathology laboratory records, etc. 
aa. The term “essential document” refers to any document (including electronic 
documents) used for the individual or general evaluation of the implementation of a 
clinical trial and the quality of data obtained therefrom. 
bb. The term “standard operating procedure” (SOP) refers to a document that describes 
in detail the relevant procedures and methods of implementing a specific task for 
consistent implementation of such a task according to a standardized method. 
cc. The term “investigator’s brochure” refers to a compilation of clinical and non-clinical 
data related to investigational devices, which is provided to subjects of a clinical trial. 
dd. The term “quality assurance for clinical trial (hereinafter, “quality assurance”)” refers to 
a systematic confirmation conducted according to a plan prepared in advance to 
ensure whether all matters related to a clinical trial, data collection, recording and 
document preparation, reporting, etc. comply with this GCP, Article 24 of the 
Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act, and other related statues and 
regulations. 
ee. The term “quality control for clinical trial data (hereinafter, “quality control“)” refers 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
93 
 
to an action or a technique thereof of verifying in detail that all actions or 
activities related to a clinical trial are being implemented at an appropriate level 
according to a quality assurance system. 
ff. 
The term “blinding/masking” refers to a procedure that prevents a person or a 
department participating in a clinical trial from finding out about the assigned treatment 
method. 
gg. The term “randomization” refers to assignment of subjects of a clinical trial to each 
treatment group according to the principle of probability in order to reduce bias that 
may occur during the trial. 
 
3. 
Basic Principles of Clinical Trial 
a. 
Clinical trials shall be conducted according to the ethical principles under the 
Declaration of Helsinki, this GCP, Article 24, and other related statues and regulations. 
b. 
Clinical trials shall be conducted only where the benefits that can be obtained from 
the trial for subjects themselves and the society exceed the risk, or the risk can be 
justified, in full consideration of the risks and inconveniences expected from the clinical 
trial. 
c. 
Rights, safety, and welfare of subjects shall be prioritized over the interests of 
science and the society. 
d. 
Clinical and non-clinical information on investigational devices shall be adequate for a 
clinical trial to be conducted. 
e. 
Clinical trials shall be scientifically appropriate, and protocols shall be prepared clearly 
and minutely. 
f. 
Clinical trials shall be conducted under a clinical trial protocol approved by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
g. 
Medical procedure or decision to be performed on subjects shall be made under 
responsibility of a physician, a dentist, or a doctor of oriental medicine. 
h. 
All people participating in a clinical trial shall receive appropriate education and 
training for their duties and have relevant experiences. 
i. 
Vonluntary consent to participation to a clinical trial shall be obtained before such 
participation. 
j. 
All information related to a clinical trial shall be recorded, handled, and restored so as 
to be accurately reported, interpreted, and checked. 
k. 
All records related to the identity of subjects shall be handled under related statues 
and regulations to ensure confidentiality. 
l. 
Investigational devices shall be managed according to the standards for facilities and 
manufacturing and quality management systems in Annex 2 and used according to a 
clinical trial protocol approved by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. 
m. Clinical trials shall be conducted under a system where quality assurance may be achieved. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
94 
 
4. 
Scope of Application 
 
This GCP shall apply to clinical trials on medical devices conducted under Article 10 of 
the Act. 
 
5. 
Clinical Trial Contracts and Clinical Trial Institutions 
a. 
Clinical trial contracts 
1) 
A sponsor shall conclude a clinical trial contract with the head of a clinical trial 
institution in writing, and if he/she intends to conduct a multicenter clinical trial, 
the sponsor may collectively conclude the contract with the head of 1 
institution. 
2) 
A clinical trial contract shall include matters concerning finances of a clinical 
trial, such as the scale and payment method of research expenses, return of 
unused research expenses for premature discontinuation and suspension of the 
trial; matters concerning the delegation and division of duties; and matters 
concerning obligations of the sponsor and the head of the clinical trial 
institution. 
b. 
Head of clinical trial institutions 
1) 
The head of clinical trial institutions shall establish an institutional review board 
(hereinafter “IRB”) according to subparagraph 6 in the clinical trial institution for 
reviewing the implementation of clinical trials, etc.; appoint members of the IRB; 
and establish regulations on administrative procedures, etc. necessary for the 
implementation of the clinical trial. 
2) 
The head of the institution shall ensure that the IRB may be operated independently. 
3) 
The head of the institution shall prepare a standard operating procedure (hereinafter, 
“SOP of the institution”) that outlines the following matters for the 
implementation of the IRB’s duties: 
a) 
Matters concerning the composition of the IRB such as the list of the 
names and qualifications of its members; 
b) 
Authority of the IRB; 
c) 
Methods of convening, scheduling, and conducting meetings; 
d) 
Methods of reviewing clinical trials and review deadline; 
e) 
Matters concerning determination of a review cycle under the latter part of 
subparagraph 6 (a) 4); 
f) 
Approval on expedited review under subparagraph 6 (a) 10) and minor changes 
of a clinical trial protocol under subparagraph 6 (a) 10) d); 
g) 
 Prohibition of subjects’ participation in a clinical trial prior to the 
approval of the protocol and the protocol amendment; 
h) 
Prohibition of implementation of a clinical trial prior to the approval of the 
protocol amendment, where any change has been made in the original 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
95 
 
clinical trial protocol; Provided, That the cases where it is required to 
eliminate immediate risk factors occurred to subjects or where the changes 
in the clinical trial protocol are minor under subparagraph 6 (a) 10) d) shall 
be excluded; 
i) 
Reporting procedures and handling method on the matters falling under any 
of the following that a principal investigator shall promptly report to the 
IRB: 
(1) Matters concerning a clinical trial conducted differently from the 
protocol to eliminate immediate risk factors occurred to subjects under 
the proviso of item h); 
(2) Matters concerning changes that may increase the risk for subjects or may 
have significant impact on the implementation of the relevant clinical 
trial; 
(3) Matters concerning an unexpected serious adverse device effect; 
(4) Matters concerning new information that may adversely affect the 
safety of subjects or the implementation of clinical trials. 
j) 
Matters concerning any of the following that the IRB shall promptly 
notify the principal investigator in writing: 
(1) Decisions and opinions on the relevant trial and the grounds for such 
decisions and opinions, and notification procedures; 
(2) Procedures for filing an objection against the decisions of the IRB. 
k) 
Qualifications of the principal investigator, subinvestigator, and coordinating 
investigator; 
l) 
Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the IRB other 
than the matters prescribed in items a) through k). 
4) 
The head of the institution shall secure clinical laboratories, facilities, and 
specialized personnel required for conducting a clinical trial, along with the 
facilities and personnel to take necessary measures in case of an emergency. 
5) 
The head of the institution shall require the IRB to provide active cooperation 
where the sponsor of the relevant clinical trial or the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety requests a perusal of the SOP of the institution concerning the operation of 
the IRB or submission of the list of IRB members and documents on their 
qualifications. 
6) 
Upon receipt of a notification of monitoring under subparagraph 8 (e-2), a 
notification of inspection under Subparagraph 8 (f-2), or a request for any 
perusal under Subparagraph 7 (i) 7), the head of the institution shall require the 
relevant principal investigators and departments to provide active cooperation. 
7) 
The head of the institution shall designate a manager among the personnel of 
the institution for proper management of investigational devices, and in cases of 
a multicenter clinical trial, each clinical trial institution concerned shall designate 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
96 
 
a manager: Provided, That upon the request of the principal investigator 
depending on the characteristics of the relevant clinical trial, the head may have 
the principal investigator or subinvestigators manage investigational devices through 
consultations with the IRB. 
8) 
The head of the institution shall designate a person in charge of retaining 
records and data transferred from the IRB and the principal investigator according 
to subparagraph 6 (a) 12) and subparagraph 7 (i) 
6) in order to store such records and data: Provided, That if there are other statues 
and regulations regarding the storage of records and data, the relevant statues 
and regulations shall be applied. 
9) 
Where the IRB has decided on the premature discontinuation or suspension of a 
clinical trial, the head of the institution shall immediately notify the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety of the decision and submit a detailed statement of reasons for 
the premature discontinuation or suspension. 
10) The head of the institution shall submit clinical trial management data, including 
data concerning the IRB, personnel related to clinical trials, clinical trial 
implementation status, etc. by the end of February every year as decided by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
 
6. 
Institutional Review Board (IRB) 
a. 
Duties of the IRB 
1) 
The IRB shall protect the rights, safety, and welfare of subjects and review 
whether it is justifiable to have vulnerable subjects participate in a clinical trial. 
2) 
The IRB shall review the documents submitted related to the clinical trial by 
the principal investigator under subparagraph 7 (d) 3) within a deadline 
specified in the SOP of the institution, and shall record and store the title 
of the clinical trial, reviewed documents, review date, and opinions of 
reviewers according to the following classification, and shall notify the 
principal investigator of the review results: 
a) 
Approved or approved with correction required; 
b) 
Supplementation required; 
c) 
Disapproved; 
d) 
Discontinuance or suspension of clinical trial. 
3) 
The IRB shall review whether the principal investigator has appropriate experience 
and qualifications to conduct the relevant clinical trial based on his/her career 
and other experiences. 
4) 
The IRB shall conduct a review of ongoing clinical trials at least once a year. 
In such cases, the frequency of such review is determined by the IRB in 
consideration of the degree of risk that may be posed to the subjects. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
97 
 
5) 
The IRB may request the head of the institution or the principal investigator to 
suspend an ongoing clinical trial if it is conducted differently from the IRB’s 
requirements or decisions, or when an unexpected serious risk is posed to the 
subjects. 
6) 
If it is deemed necessary to protect the rights, safety, and welfare of subjects, the 
IRB may request the sponsor to provide additional information in addition to 
the information under subparagraph 7 (h) 10) to the subjects. 
7) 
Where a clinical trial is identified in its protocol as one that prior consent 
from the subjects or their representatives is unobtainable, such as a trial 
conducted on emergency patients, the IRB shall review whether the submitted 
protocol and other related documents, etc. take full account of the ethical aspects 
of the clinical trial. 
8) 
If a monetary reward is provided to subjects for participating in a clinical trial, 
the IRB shall review the amount of the reward and payment methods, and 
whether it has an unreasonable influence on the subjects’ participation in the 
clinical trial. In such cases, the IRB shall review whether it is appropriate to 
offer the reward concerning the subjects’ degree and period of participation in 
the clinical trial and whether the reward is provided under the condition that the 
subjects participate in the clinical trial until it is completed. 
9) 
If a monetary reward is provided to subjects for participating in a clinical trial, 
the IRB shall confirm whether information of the reward such as the method, 
amount, and schedule of payment, etc. is clearly stated in the subject 
information sheet or other documents provided to the subject. In such cases, the 
IRB shall examine whether there is a measure for providing a reward to the 
subjects who failed to complete the clinical trial. 
10) The IRB shall conduct an expedited review in any of the following cases: 
a) 
Measures against adverse events reported under subparagraph 8 (d); 
b) 
Processing regarding reports on the completion of clinical trials under Article 
24 (2); 
c) 
Processing regarding corrections of a clinical trial protocol (including an 
amendment protocol) approved by the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety; 
d) 
Approval of minor changes in a clinical trial protocol such as changes in 
administrative procedures including change of monitors, subinvestigators, 
emergency contact numbers, etc., or additions and deletions of test items that 
do not affect the efficacy and safety of the clinical trial; 
e) 
Review of a clinical trial protocol supplemented and submitted according 
to the results of the review by the IRB; 
f) 
Processing of other matters deemed as requiring an expedited review regarding 
the implementation of the clinical trial as specified in the SOP of the 
institution. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
98 
 
11) If there is any request from a sponsor or the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety for a perusal of the SOP of the institution or the 
submission of the list of IRB members and documents on their 
qualifications, the IRB shall accept such a request. 
12) The IRB shall retain the list of its members, review records, and other related data 
or documents: Provided, That upon receiving a report on the completion of a 
clinical trial (including a premature discontinuation report) from the principal 
investigator under subparagraph 7 (m), the IRB shall transfer the relevant data 
and documents to the person in charge of keeping them under subparagraph 5 
(b) 8). 
b. 
Composition, function, and operation of the IRB 
1) 
The IRB shall consist of 5 or more members with experience and qualifications 
suitable for reviewing and evaluating the ethical, scientific, and medical aspects 
of a clinical trial, who are appointed by the head of the clinical trial institution. 
In such cases, the members shall include at least 1 person who has not majored 
in medicine, dentistry, oriental medicine, pharmacy, nursing, or biomedical 
engineering, and at least 1 person who has no personal stake in the relevant 
clinical trial institution. 
2) 
The chairman of the IRB shall be elected from among its members, and anyone who 
has relation with the investigator and sponsor of the clinical trial shall not be 
allowed to participate in the decision-making process or present their opinions for 
the clinical trial. 
3) 
The IRB shall establish and retain the list of its members and documents 
regarding their qualifications. 
4) 
The IRB shall perform all its duties according to the SOP of the institution, 
prepare and keep minute records of all its activities and meetings, and comply 
with this GCP, Article 24, and other related statues and regulations. 
5) 
All decisions of the IRB shall be made at a previously notified meeting which 
satisfies the quorum for voting as specified in the SOP of the institution, and the 
chairperson shall inform the members of the meeting agenda, meeting date, etc. in 
advance. 
6) 
Only members who have participated in the review process for a clinical trial 
shall be entitled to participate in the decision-making process or present their 
opinions for the trial. 
7) 
The principal investigator may provide information to the IRB on all matters of 
the relevant clinical trial, but shall not exert influence on the IRB members 
or participate in the decision-making process of matters related to the clinical 
trial. 
8) 
The IRB may seek advice from a person with expertise in the relevant field to 
facilitate the review process. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
99 
 
c. 
Operation of the IRB 
 
IRBs shall comply with the SOP of the institution for operation of the IRB. 
d. 
IRB in multicenter clinical trials 
1) 
Where a clinical trial is conducted by multiple clinical trial institutions, a meeting of 
the IRBs shall be jointly held (hereinafter, “joint IRB”) through the agreement 
between the heads of the clinical trial institutions for conducting a review or 
decision, or the IRBs of the individual institutions shall approve the results of 
review or decision by the IRB of another institution by making a decision. 
2) 
Items a through c shall apply mutatis mutandis to the duties, organization, and 
operation of a joint IRB. 
3) 
Matters reviewed and decided by a joint IRB or matters reviewed and decided by 
the IRB of another clinical trial institution and approved by the IRBs of the 
individual institutions shall be deemed to have been reviewed and decided by 
the IRBs of the individual clinical trial institutions. 
e. 
Entrustment of review 
1) 
Where the relevant clinical trial institution does not have an IRB or it is deemed 
necessary by the IRB established in the institution, the head of the institution 
may entrust a review of a clinical trial protocol, etc. to an IRB of another 
clinical institution under Article 21 (1) 1 or 2 which is designated by the Minister 
of Food and Drug Safety (hereinafter, “designated IRB”). 
2) 
Items a through c and item f shall apply mutatis mutandis to the duties, organization, 
and operation of a designated IRB. 
3) 
Matters determined by a designated IRB shall be deemed to have been determined 
by the clinical trial institution that entrusted the review to the IRB. 
f. 
Records 
 
The IRB shall retain the records related to a clinical trial such as records on the 
implement of the trial, list of names, occupations, and affiliations of persons involved in 
the trial, documents submitted to the IRB, minutes of meetings, letters, etc. for the period 
specified in Article 24 (3), and the investigator and sponsor of the trial, and the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety may request the IRB to submit such clinical trial 
implementation records and the list of persons involved in the trial. 
 
7. 
Investigator 
a. 
Qualifications, etc. for investigators 
1) 
Investigators shall satisfy education, training, and experience requirements for 
conducting clinical trials according to the SOP of a clinical trial institution for 
the proper implementation of a clinical trial. 
2) 
Investigators shall have detailed knowledge of proper use investigational devices 
specified in clinical trial protocols, investigators’ brochures, and other medical-

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
100 
 
device-related information provided by a sponsor. 
3) 
Investigators shall be fully aware of and comply with this GCP, Article 24, and 
other related statues and regulations. 
4) 
The principal investigator of a clinical trial and the head of the clinical trial 
institution shall comply with the monitoring under Item s of subparagraph 8 and 
inspection under Item u of the said subparagraph at the request of the sponsor. 
5) 
Where an important task related to a clinical trial is entrusted to subinvestigators, the 
principal investigator shall secure and maintain a list of such subinvestigators. 
b. 
Securing of resources required for clinical trials 
1) 
A principal investigator shall properly evidence that subjects necessary for a 
clinical trial can be enrolled within the subject enrollment period agreed with the 
sponsor based on past medical records, etc., and shall provide the relevant 
evidencing data upon request from the sponsor. 
2) 
A principal investigator shall assign sufficient time to each subject to properly 
conduct and complete a clinical trial during the period agreed with the 
sponsor. 
3) 
A principal investigator shall secure an adequate number of subinvestigators, 
equipment, and facilities required to conduct a clinical trial properly and safely 
during the clinical trial period. 
4) 
A principal investigator shall ensure that the subinvestigators have detailed 
knowledge of the clinical trial protocol, information on investigational devices, 
and duties and tasks related to the clinical trial. 
c. 
Investigators’ duty to protect the subjects 
1) 
All medical decisions related to a clinical trial on subjects shall be made by the 
principal investigator or subinvestigators qualified as physicians, dentists, or doctors 
of oriental medicine. 
2) 
During or after a clinical trial, the principal investigator shall ensure that the 
subjects receive appropriate medical treatment for all adverse events that may 
occur in the clinical trial (including clinically significant abnormalities in 
laboratory test results), and shall inform the subject if the medical treatment is 
required for the subject’s intercurrent disease that the principal investigator 
becomes aware of. 
3) 
If a subject has a family doctor, the principal investigator may notify such 
family doctor of the subject’s participation in the clinical trial under the consent 
of the subject. 
4) 
A subject does not have to disclose the reason for his/her withdrawal from a 
clinical trial before its completion, but the principal investigator shall make 
efforts to ascertain the reason within the scope where the subject’s rights are not 
infringed. 
d. 
Information exchange between the IRBs and principal investigators 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
101 
 
1) 
Before conducting a clinical trial, the principal investigator shall have the IRB 
review various information provided to the subjects in writing such as a clinical 
trial protocol, a consent form (including an amended one), documents on methods 
for recruiting subjects (including advertisements, etc.), and a subject information 
sheet, and where the implementation of the clinical trial is approved by the IRB 
(including approvals with changes 
or 
deferred 
approval), 
the 
principal 
investigator shall report the content of the review notice to the head of the 
institution and provide it to the sponsor after obtaining confirmation in writing 
from the head of the institution. 
2) 
Where a principal investigator intends to obtain the IRB’s approval for a clinical 
trial protocol, he or she shall submit a copy of the latest investigator’s brochure 
to the IRB. If the investigator’s brochure is amended during the clinical trial, 
the principal investigator shall submit a copy thereof to the IRB. 
3) 
A principal investigator shall submit the following documents to the IRB before 
conducting a clinical trial and shall have the IRB review such documents: 
a) 
Clinical trial protocol (including a protocol amendment); 
b) 
Informed consent form; 
c) 
Information provided to subjects in writing (including a subject information 
sheet); 
d) 
Procedure for recruiting subjects (including advertisements, etc.); 
e) 
Investigator’s brochure; 
f) 
Safety information; 
g) 
Information on the rewards to be provided to subjects; 
h) 
Principal investigator’s career and experience. 
4) 
The principal investigator shall promptly report to the IRB on the matters 
specified in Subparagraph 5 (b) 3) i (1) through (4). 
5) 
The IRB shall promptly notify the principal investigator in writing of the 
matters specified in Subparagraph 5 (b) 3) j (1) and (2). 
e. 
Compliance with clinical trial protocols 
1) 
The investigator shall conduct a clinical trial in compliance with the clinical 
trial protocol agreed upon by the sponsor in writing and approved by the IRB 
and the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
2) 
The principal investigator shall not conduct a clinical trial differently from the 
protocol before obtaining prior consent from the sponsor and approval of change 
from the IRB and the Minister of Food and Drug Safety: Provided, That the 
foregoing shall not apply to the cases that fall under the proviso of 
subparagraph 5 (b) 3) h. 
3) 
The principal investigator or subinvestigator shall record all matters conducted 
differently from the approved clinical trial protocol and the reasons therefor. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
102 
 
4) 
With respect to the changes made by the principal investigator to eliminate an 
immediate risk factor to subjects under the proviso of 2) before the prior 
approval of a protocol amendment, the principal investigator shall submit 
documents on such changes of the clinical trial protocol, the reasons therefor, and 
the protocol amendment to the sponsor and IRB, and Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety and obtain their consent and approval, respectively, as soon as possible. 
f. 
Management of investigational devices 
1) 
The responsibility for the management of investigational devices shall be borne by 
the principal investigator and manager of a relevant clinical trial institution. 
2) 
The manager or the principal investigator or subinvestigator (hereinafter, 
“manager, etc.”) who is responsible for managing the investigational devices 
under the proviso of subparagraph 5 (b) 7) shall perform tasks such as accepting 
investigational devices, managing their inventory, administering such devices to 
each subject, returning such devices, etc., shall prepare records on the relevant 
matters, and shall report to the principal investigator on such matters periodically. 
3) 
The records under 2) shall be prepared for each subject, including the application 
period of medical devices, manufacturing number or serial number, use-by date or 
expiration date (only if applicable), identification code of the devices, and the 
subject’s identification code. 
4) 
Manager, etc. shall maintain medical records from which it can be confirmed 
that investigational devices are used on each subject according to the methods of 
use described in the clinical trial protocol and shall check confirm whether the 
inventory of investigational devices matches the use records. 
5) 
Investigational devices shall be stored according to the conditions specified by 
the sponsor and related statues and regulations. 
6) 
The principal investigator shall confirm whether investigational devices are used 
and managed according to the clinical trial protocol. 
7) 
The principal investigator, subinvestigator, or manager shall provide each subject 
with accurate instructions for the use of investigational devices and confirm 
whether the subjects are properly following the instructions. 
g. 
Randomization and unblinding 
1) 
If a randomization procedure is established in a clinical trial protocol, the principal 
investigator shall comply with such a procedure, and unblinding shall be 
conducted only according to the procedure specified in the protocol. 
2) 
Where unblinding is conducted accidentally or due to a serious adverse event 
during a binding clinical trial, the principal investigator shall record such fact 
and promptly inform the sponsor thereof. 
h. 
Subjects’ consent 
1) 
Subjects’ consent shall be obtained according to Article 24 (1) 4, the ethical 
principles under the Declaration of Helsinki, and this GCP, and the principal 
investigator shall obtain the IRB’s approval on documented information 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
103 
 
provided to the subjects, including a consent form, a subject’s information 
sheet, etc, prior to the initiation of the clinical trial. 
2) 
If new information regarding the clinical trial that may affect the subject’s consent is 
obtained, a consent form, a subject information sheet, and other documented 
information shall be modified accordingly and obtain approval from the IRB before 
being provided to the subjects. In such case, the principal investigator shall notify 
the subjects or their representatives promptly of such information and record 
the recipients, the corresponding date and time, and details of the notification. 
3) 
The principal investigator or the subinvestigator shall not coerce nor unduly 
influence a subject to participate in a clinical trial. 
4) 
A consent form and oral or written information regarding a clinical trial shall 
not include descriptions that restrict the rights of the subjects or their 
representatives, imply such restriction, or exempt the investigators, clinical trial 
institution, sponsor, or his/her representative from any responsibilities. 
5) 
The principal investigator or the person designated by the principal investigator shall 
fully inform the subjects of information on all aspects of the clinical trial 
including written information approved by the IRB. In such cases, if the subject is 
unable to give consent, his or representative shall be notified of such 
information. 
6) 
Terms used in a consent form and oral or written information regarding a 
clinical trial shall be simple and easy for subjects, their representatives, or 
witnesses to understand. 
7) 
Before obtaining a subject’s consent, the principal investigator or a physician, a 
dentist, or a doctor of oriental medicine designated by the principal investigator 
shall provide the subject or his/her representative with sufficient time and 
opportunity for asking questions about the details of the clinical trial, deciding 
on the participation, and shall sincerely answer all questions asked by the 
subject or his/her representative concerning the clinical trial. 
8) 
Before a subject participates in the clinical trial, a consent form shall be signed by 
the subject or his/her representative, the principal investigator who has obtained 
his/her consent, or a physician, a dentist, or a doctor of oriental medicine 
designated by the principal investigator, with the date of the signature written in 
their own handwriting. 
9) 
Where a subject or his/her representative is unable to read a consent form, a 
subject information sheet, or other documented information, the entire process of 
obtaining the subject’s consent shall be implemented in the presence of a witness. 
In such cases, the principal investigator or the person designated by the principal 
investigator shall read the consent form, the subject information sheet, and 
other documented information and explain the details of such documents to the 
subject or his/her representative, who then shall verbally consent to participation 
in the clinical trial, and if possible, shall sign and date the consent form in 
his/her own handwriting and the witness shall sign and date the consent form in 
his/her own handwriting as well, and ensure whether the details of the consent 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
104 
 
form, subject information sheet, and other documented information have been 
accurately explained to the subject or his/her representative before signing and 
dating it; whether he/she has understood them correctly; and whether the process 
of obtaining his/her consent has been implemented following his/her own will. 
10) The information, consent form, subject information sheet, and other documented 
information provided to a subject or his/her representative in the process of 
obtaining consent shall include the following: 
a) 
The fact that the clinical trial is conducted for research purposes; 
b) 
Purpose of the clinical trial; 
c) 
Information regarding investigational devices and probability of being 
randomized into a test or control group; 
d) 
Various tests or procedures to which subjects will be subjected during the 
clinical trial, including invasive procedures; 
e) 
Matters that subjects shall comply with; 
f) 
The fact that the clinical trial has not yet been validated; 
g) 
Risks or inconveniences expected to be incurred in subjects (including fetuses 
if subjects are pregnant, and infants if they are nursing women); 
h) 
The presence or absence of an expected benefit to the subjects; 
i) 
Other treatment methods or types that can be chosen by the subjects and 
potential risks and benefits of such treatments; 
j) 
Compensation or treatments to be given to subjects in case of damage related to 
the clinical trial incurred in the subjects; 
k) 
If there is monetary compensation to be provided to the subjects for 
participating in the clinical trial, the expected amount, and the fact that the 
amount will be adjusted according to the degree or period of participation in 
the clinical trial; 
l) 
Expected expenses to be borne by subjects by participating in the clinical 
trial; 
m) The fact that the subject’s decision to participate in the clinical trial shall 
be voluntary, and that he/she can refuse to participate or withdraw from 
participation at any time during the trial without losing the benefits to 
which he or she is entitled; 
n) 
The fact that a monitor under Subparagraph 8 (e-2), a person conducting 
inspections under Item 8 (Item 8), the IRB, and the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety may be granted access to medical records of subjects to verify 
the quality of the clinical trial implementation procedure and data 
according to relevant statues and regulations within the scope where the 
subject’s confidentiality is not infringed, and the fact that the subjects’ or 
their representatives’ signature on the consent form indicates their consent to 
such access to the data. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
105 
 
o) 
The fact that any record that can identify subjects shall be kept confidential, 
and that their identity will also be kept confidential in publications related to 
results of the clinical trial; 
p) 
The fact that subjects or their representatives will be promptly notified 
of newly obtained information that may affect the subject’s continued 
participation; 
q) 
Persons to be contacted when additional information is desired to be obtained 
regarding the clinical trial and the rights and interests of subjects or in case 
of damage related to the clinical trial; 
r) 
Cases where subject participation in the clinical trial is suspended during 
the trial and the reasons therefor; 
s) 
Expected participation period of subjects in the clinical trial; 
t) 
The approximate number of subjects participating in the clinical trial. 
11) The principal investigator and the subinvestigator shall give the subjects or their 
representatives a copy of the consent form and other documented information 
provided to them before they participate in the clinical trial, and if the consent 
form is modified during the clinical trial or if there is any change in the 
documented information, a copy of the modified consent form and the changed 
documents shall be given to them, respectively. 
12) In a clinical trial where subjects can participate only with the consent of a 
person with parental authority over them or their guardian, etc., because of 
the subjects’ lack of comprehension and expression ability under the proviso of 
Article 24 (1) 4, the principal investigator and subinvestigator shall provide the 
subjects with information regarding the clinical trial to the extent that they can 
understand, and if possible, have them sign and date the consent form in their 
own handwriting. 
13) In an emergency where it is impossible to obtain consent from a subject in 
advance, the consent of the subject’s representative shall be obtained, and if the 
subject’s representative is absent, written approval shall be obtained from the 
IRB. In such cases, the principal investigator and the subinvestigators shall 
notify the subject or the subject’s representative of the clinical trial as soon as 
possible and shall obtain consent to continuous participation in the trial. 
i. 
Records and reports 
1) 
The principal investigator shall ensure that any data included in the case 
report form or any other reports submitted to the sponsor are accurate, complete, 
easy to read, and timely. 
2) 
Data described in the case report form originating from the source document 
shall match the source document, and explanations shall be provided regarding any 
mismatching contents. 
3) 
The sponsor shall provide the principal investigator or the person designated by the 
principal investigator with guidelines on change or correction of the content in the 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
106 
 
case report form, and a monitor or other persons designated by the sponsor shall 
establish guidelines on the cases where the case report form shall be 
modified or corrected, methods of recording such changes, and the procedure for 
receiving confirmation from the principal investigator after such change or correction. 
4) 
Any person who modifies or corrects the content of the documented or digitalized 
case report form shall revise it in such a manner that the original content therein 
are identifiable according to the change guidelines prepared by the sponsor, and 
provide the change date and reasons for such change with his/her signature. 
5) 
The principal investigator shall keep records on any change or correction under 3). 
6) 
The principal investigator shall keep essential documents and other documents 
regarding the clinical trial (including electronic documents) prepared according to 
this GCP, Article 24, and other related statues and regulations following Article 9, 
Article 24, and other related statues and regulations. However, after the completion 
of the trial report, these documents shall be transferred to the person in charge 
of storage under subparagraph 5 (b) 8). 
7) 
The principal investigator or the head of the institution shall actively cooperate with 
a request for access to documents related to the clinical trial (including 
electronic documents) by a monitor under subparagraph 8 s), a person 
conducting inspections under subparagraph 8 t), the IRB, or the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety. 
j. 
Reporting on progress 
1) 
The principal investigator shall submit a summary of the clinical trial progress in 
writing to the IRB at least once a year and when there is a request by the IRB. 
2) 
The principal investigator shall promptly report in writing to the sponsor and the 
IRB when there is an increase in risks to the subjects or any change or 
modification that has a significant impact on the implementation of the 
clinical trial. 
k. 
Reporting related to safety of clinical trials 
1) 
The principal investigator shall submit an expedited adverse device effect 
report in the attached Form 55 to the sponsor for every serious adverse event 
(excluding those not required to be reported immediately in the clinical trial 
protocol or investigator’s brochure) within the period specified in the clinical 
trial protocol. In such cases, the principal investigator shall use subject 
identification codes instead of the subjects’ personal information including their 
name, resident registration number, and address, to keep their identity 
confidential, and if there are guidelines for reporting adverse events, the principal 
investigator shall follow such guidelines. 
2) 
The principal investigator shall report adverse events or abnormal laboratory test 
results, which are separately specified concerning safety evaluation in the clinical 
trial protocol, to the sponsor according to the reporting methods and within the 
period specified in the clinical trial protocol. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
107 
 
3) 
In cases of reporting death cases, the principal investigator shall submit additional 
data such as an autopsy report (limited to cases where an autopsy is performed), 
a death certificate, etc. to the sponsor and the IRB. 
l. 
Premature discontinuation or suspension of clinical trials 
1) 
If the principal investigator decides on the premature discontinuation or suspension 
of the clinical trial without prior agreement with the sponsor, he/she shall promptly 
notify the sponsor and the IRB and submit a detailed statement of the reasons for 
such premature discontinuation or suspension. 
2) 
If the sponsor decides on the premature discontinuation or suspension of the 
clinical trial, the principal investigator shall promptly notify the IRB and submit 
a detailed statement of the reasons for such premature discontinuation or suspension. 
3) 
If the IRB decides on the premature discontinuation or suspension of the 
clinical trial, the principal investigator shall promptly notify the sponsor and 
submit a detailed statement of the reasons for such premature discontinuation or 
suspension. 
4) 
For premature discontinuation or suspension of the clinical trial, as specified in 
the provisions of 1) to 3), the principal investigator shall notify the subjects 
of such fact and ensure that appropriate measures and follow-ups are carried 
out. 
m. Reporting on clinical trial completion 
 
When a clinical trial is completed (including premature discontinuation), the 
principal investigator shall report the completion of the trial to the IRB with the 
summary of the results of the clinical trial. 
 
8. 
Clinical trial sponsor 
a. 
Quality assurance of clinical trial and quality management of clinical trial data 
1) 
A sponsor shall establish an SOP regarding quality assurance of a clinical trial 
and quality management of clinical trial data (hereinafter, “SOP of sponsor”) 
so that data regarding clinical trial may be generated, recorded, and reported 
according to the clinical trial protocol, this GCP, and Article 24. 
2) 
A sponsor shall conduct quality management for clinical trial data in all stages of 
data processing to ensure the reliability and accuracy of such data. 
3) 
A sponsor shall obtain prior consent from persons involved in the clinical trial 
for clinical trial site visits and access to source data, source documents, and 
reports, with the clinical trial protocol or in a separate form of a written 
consent so that the monitoring under item s and inspections under item t can be 
conducted. 
b. 
Contract research organizations 
1) 
A sponsor may entrust all or part of his/her tasks related to the clinical trial to a 
contract research organization (CRO), but the sponsor shall take responsibility for 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
108 
 
managing the quality and accuracy of the clinical trial data. 
2) 
A contract research organization shall perform quality assurance and management of 
clinical trial data for the entrusted clinical trial. 
3) 
The entrustment under 1) shall be made in a written form that includes the 
details of the specific tasks to be entrusted. 
4) 
A contract research organization shall implement the entrusted tasks according to 
this GCP and as prescribed in Article 24 regarding the sponsor’s duties and 
tasks. 
c. 
Medical advice 
 
A sponsor may designate experts with medical knowledge and experience to seek 
advice on medical problems or inquiries related to clinical trials. 
d. 
Advice from relevant experts 
 
A sponsor may seek advice from relevant experts including a biostatistician, a 
medical device expert, a physician, or experts in other fields regarding any 
procedure of a clinical trial such as designing a clinical trial protocol and a case 
report form, establishing an analysis plan, analyzing collected data, and preparing an 
interim report and a trial report. 
e. 
Management of clinical trial 
1) 
A sponsor shall have a person with knowledge and experience in clinical 
trials supervise the overall implementation of the clinical trial and perform the tasks 
of data processing and verification, statistical analyses, and trial report 
preparation. 
2) 
A sponsor may establish a data monitoring committee for periodical evaluation of 
the progress of the clinical trial including safety-related data and important 
efficacy outcome variables and for advice on whether to proceed, modify, or 
discontinue the clinical trial, and the data monitoring committee shall establish an 
SOP necessary for the performance of its duties and prepare and keep the 
minutes of the meeting. 
3) 
Where a clinical development of investigational devices is discontinued, the 
sponsor shall report to the investigators, the clinical trial institution, and the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
f. 
Data processing 
1) 
A sponsor who intends to electronically process clinical trial data or use a 
remote computing system shall comply with the following: 
a) 
Verify whether the integrity, accuracy, reliability, and consistency of the system 
to electronically process clinical trial data and the remote computer system 
meet the requirements set by the sponsor and record details of such 
confirmation; 
b) 
Prescribe the methods of use, etc. of the system to electronically process 
clinical trial data and the remote computer system in the SOP of sponsor; 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
109 
 
c) 
Ensure that the data change method of the system to electronically process 
clinical trial data and the remote computer system is designed to record the 
process of data change is recorded and not delete previously entered data, and 
verify whether the systems meet these requirements; 
d) 
Prepare a security system able to prevent access to data from an unauthorized 
person; 
e) 
Prepare and maintain a list of persons authorized to modify data; 
f) 
Prepare and maintain backups of data; 
g) 
Maintain blinding/masking status throughout data input and processing 
processes if blinding/masking is required in a clinical trial. 
2) 
Where the form of data is changed in the data processing process, comparison 
between the original and modified data shall be enabled at all times. 
3) 
The sponsor shall use subject identification codes to identify data on each 
subject. 
g. 
Record keeping 
1) 
A sponsor shall keep essential documents and other data under Article 9 and 
other related laws: Provided, That the storage period shall be extended if ordered 
by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety or deemed necessary by the sponsor. 
2) 
A sponsor shall notify the investigators and the head of the institution in writing 
regarding the necessity and period of data storage; If the sponsor determines that 
data storage is no longer necessary, he or she shall inform the principal 
investigator and the head of the institution of such fact in writing. 
h. 
Selection of principal investigator 
1) 
A sponsor shall select, as the principal investigator of the trial, a person who 
meets the education and experience requirements for the clinical trial and has 
facilities and human resources for conducting the trial, and may establish a 
coordinating committee and select a coordinating investigator for the proper 
implementation of a multicenter clinical trial. 
2) 
Before concluding a contract with the head of a clinical trial institution regarding 
the implement of a clinical trial, the sponsor shall provide the principal 
investigator with the clinical trial protocol and the up-to-date investigator’s brochure, 
and secure sufficient time for the principal investigator to review the protocol 
and other information related to the trial received from the sponsor. 
3) 
A sponsor shall reach an agreement with the principal investigator and the head 
of the institution on the following matters, include such agreed matters in the clinical 
trial protocol or clinical trial contract, and have the principal investigator and the 
head of the institution sign the documents: 
a) 
A clinical trial shall be conducted according to this GCP, Article 24, other 
related statues and regulations, the clinical trial protocol, and matters approved 
by the IRB; 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
110 
 
b) 
Procedures for recording and reporting data shall be observed; 
c) 
Monitoring and inspections under items s and t shall be followed; 
d) 
Essential documents and other data related to the clinical trial shall be kept 
until the sponsor notifies in writing that the keeping is no longer needed. 
i. 
Assignment of duties 
 
Before conducting a clinical trial, the sponsor shall define all duties and roles related 
to the clinical trial and assign them appropriately to the persons involved in the trial. 
j. 
Compensation for subjects, etc. 
1) 
A sponsor shall establish a compensation procedure for damages incurred 
concerning clinical trials. 
2) 
Compensation for subjects shall be appropriately made according to the contents 
and methods of compensation prescribed in Subparagraph 7 (h) 10) j) and 
related statues and regulations. 
k. 
Approval of clinical trial protocols by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
 
Before conducting a clinical trial, a sponsor shall obtain approval of the clinical trial 
protocol from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety according to Article 10 of the 
Act. 
l. 
Confirmation of matters reviewed by the IRB 
 
A sponsor shall have the principal investigator submit the following documents to confirm 
the matters reviewed by the IRB: 
1) 
A list of IRM members and documents on their qualifications; 
2) 
Documents confirming that the IRB has been properly organized and 
operated according to this GCP; 
3) 
A notice of review from the IRB that the principal investigator has 
received according to subparagraph 6 (a) 2); 
4) 
Request for discontinuation of the clinical trial from the IRB under 
subparagraph 6 (a) 5); 
5) 
A certificate of confirmation from the head of the clinical trial institution 
under subparagraph 7 (d) 1). 
m. Providing information regarding investigational devices 
1) 
When planning a clinical trial, the sponsor shall secure information evidencing the 
safety and effectiveness of the clinical trial from the testing results of non-
clinical trials or other clinical trials. 
2) 
Based on the information obtained according to 1), the sponsor shall 
prepare an investigator’s brochure containing information on risks or adverse 
events expected in the clinical trial, information necessary for special 
examinations and observations, and other precautions, and provide it to the 
investigators. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
111 
 
3) 
If a sponsor has newly obtained important information on safety and effectiveness, 
the investigator’s brochure shall be amended accordingly. 
n. 
Manufacturing, packaging, labeling, and coding of investigational devices 
1) 
A sponsor shall identify electrical, mechanical, biological, and physicochemical 
properties of investigational devices in the development stage thereof, manufacture 
them according to the facility and manufacturing and quality management 
standards in the Annex 2, and label or code them to maintain blinding. 
2) 
A sponsor shall decide proper use methods, application periods, and validity 
periods (if applicable) of investigational devices and notify all persons involved 
in the clinical trial thereof. 
3) 
A sponsor shall pack investigational devices to prevent them from being damaged, 
contaminated, or deteriorated during transportation, keeping, or storage. 
4) 
Even in cases of coding investigational devices in order to conduct blinding tests, 
the sponsor shall ensure that their types can be easily identified in an emergency 
and the fact of unblinding can be immediately revealed. 
5) 
If there is any significant change in the design of medical devices being used a 
clinical trial, the sponsor shall secure additional research results to determine 
whether such change will bring significant changes to the safety and 
effectiveness of the medical devices. 
o. 
Supply and handling of investigational devices 
1) 
A sponsor shall supply investigational devices to the manager, etc. 
2) 
A sponsor shall not supply investigational devices to the manager, etc. before 
obtaining approval (including approval with changes or deferred approval) of 
the clinical trial protocol from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety and the 
IRB. 
3) 
A sponsor shall prepare guidelines on how to receive, handle, and store 
investigational devices, collect unused investigational devices from the subjects, and 
return them to the sponsor, and provide such guidelines to the principal 
investigator, manager, etc. 
4) 
A sponsor shall supply investigational devices promptly and prepare and keep 
records on the supply, receipt, return, and destruction of such investigational devices. 
5) 
A sponsor shall establish a procedure for cases where investigational devices shall 
be withdrawn due to problems such as failure of investigational devices, 
completion of the clinical trial (including premature discontinuation), and the 
expiration of use or validity periods of investigational devices, and shall record the 
details of such withdrawal of investigational devices. 
6) 
Where a sponsor intends to repackage unused medical devices and use them for the 
relevant clinical trial or other clinical trials, he or she shall prepare procedures 
for repackaging and use shall be prepared and record details of repackaging 
and use of unused medical devices. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
112 
 
7) 
A sponsor shall ensure the stability of investigational devices within the use or 
validity periods and keep related records. 
8) 
Matters not prescribed in this GCP shall be in accordance with the provisions 
on the manufacturing and management of medical devices in the relevant statues 
and regulations. 
p. 
Access to data regarding clinical trial 
1) 
A sponsor shall specify matters regarding access to clinical-trial–related data in 
the clinical trial protocol or other agreement documents. 
2) 
A sponsor shall confirm whether the subjects have consented to access the data 
related to the clinical trial. 
q. 
Matters related to the safety of investigational devices 
1) 
A sponsor shall constantly conduct evaluation on the safety of investigational 
devices. 
2) 
If a sponsor obtains information on the safety of investigational devices that 
threatens the safety of the subjects, affects the decision whether to conduct a clinical 
trial, or changes the decision of the IRB, he/she shall promptly report to the 
investigators and the Minister of Food and Drug Safety of such fact. 
r. 
Reporting on adverse device effects (ADEs) 
1) 
A sponsor shall report all serious and unexpected ADEs to the investigators, the 
IRB (limited to cases where the principal investigator has not reported them to 
the IRB or there is any need to change in the reported matters), and the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety within the periods classified as follows: 
a) 
ADEs likely to cause death or threaten life: Within 7 days from the 
date the sponsor is notified or becomes aware of the ADE. In such case, 
the sponsor shall additionally report detailed information on the ADE within 
8 days from the date of the initial report. 
b) 
Other serious and unexpected adverse device effects: Within 15 days from 
the date the sponsor is notified or becomes aware of the ADE. 
2) 
If there is additional information on the ADE reported according to 1), the 
sponsor shall report it until the ADE is resolved (meaning that the ADE 
disappears or follow-ups become infeasible). 
3) 
If a sponsor intends to report an ADE to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
according to 1), he or she shall submit an ADE report in Attached Form 56, 
along with the expedited ADE report submitted by the principal investigator 
according to subparagraph 7 (l) 1) in the attached Form 55. 
s. 
Monitoring 
1) 
The purposes of monitoring are as follows: 
a) 
To protect the rights and welfare of subjects; 
b) 
To confirm accuracy, completeness, and verifiability of data through 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
113 
 
comparison of source documents with data related to the clinical trial provided 
by the principal investigator; 
c) 
To confirm whether the clinical trial is conducted according to the clinical 
trial protocol approved by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety and the 
IRB, this GCP, and Article 24. 
2) 
Standards for selecting monitoring personnel and their qualifications are as 
follows: 
a) 
Monitors shall be selected by the sponsor; 
b) 
Monitors shall have scientific or clinical knowledge necessary for monitoring 
the relevant clinical trial and shall receive the training necessary for 
conducting monitoring, and the sponsor shall prepare a list of monitors 
and documents on their qualifications. 
c) 
Monitors shall have adequate knowledge of the relevant investigational devices, 
clinical trial protocol, consent forms, subject information sheet, and other 
written information provided to the subjects, SOP of sponsor, SOP of the 
institution, this GCP, Article 24, and other related statues and regulations. 
3) 
Sponsors shall determine the scope and type of monitoring in consideration of 
the purpose, implementation plan, complexity, blinding, number of subjects, 
outcome variables, etc. of the clinical trial and shall ensure that the monitoring is 
performed properly. 
4) 
Monitors shall confirm whether the clinical trial is properly conducted and whether 
relevant matters are recorded by performing the following tasks at the request 
of the sponsor: 
a) 
Delivering information between the sponsors and investigators; 
b) 
Confirming qualifications of the principal investigator and whether an 
appropriate number of subinvestigators, equipment, and facilities that meet 
the qualifications specified in the SOP of the clinical trial institution are 
secured; 
c) 
Confirming the following matters regarding investigational devices; 
(1) Whether the storage conditions, use-by date, and expiration date of 
investigational devices under guidelines in item o (3) are observed, 
and whether the number of investigational devices is sufficient to 
conduct the clinical trial; 
(2) Whether investigational devices are being used only for the subjects 
who satisfy the selection standards, according to the application period 
and operation or use methods specified in the clinical trial protocol; 
(3) Whether the subjects are properly provided with information on the use, 
keeping, and return of investigational devices; 
(4) Whether the clinical trial institution properly manages the receipt, use, 
and return of investigational devices and records the details thereof. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
114 
 
d) 
Confirming whether the investigator complies with the approved clinical 
trial protocol or protocol amendment; 
e) 
Confirming whether the subjects gave prior informed consent; 
f) 
Confirming whether the investigator has received other items including the 
up-to-date investigator’s brochure, related data, and investigational devices; 
g) 
Confirming whether the investigator has full knowledge of all aspects of the 
clinical trial; 
h) 
Confirming whether related functions of a certain clinical trial are 
commissioned or entrusted to an unauthorized person; 
i) 
Confirming whether the principal investigator allow only the subjects who meet 
the selection standards to participate in the clinical trial; 
j) 
Reporting of the enrollment rate of subjects; 
k) 
Confirming whether source documents and other records related to the clinical 
trial are accurate and complete, and whether they reflect up-to-date 
information related to the clinical trial; 
l) 
Confirming whether the investigators is providing reports, notifications, 
applications, etc. to persons involved in the clinical trial according to 
the clinical trial protocol, this GCP, Article 24, and other related statues and 
regulations; whether the documents are specific to the clinical trial; whether 
the documents are accurate, complete, and readable; and whether the 
documents are prepared in a timely manner and are dated; 
m) Confirming whether the case report form, source documents, and other 
documents related to the clinical trial (including electronic documents) are 
accurate, complete, and consistent, and confirming the following matters: 
(1) Whether the clinical trial data required in the clinical trial protocol are 
accurately recorded in the case report form and whether the data in 
the case report form match those in the source document; 
(2) Whether changes in matters such as application periods and operation 
or use methods for each subject are properly recorded; 
(3) Whether adverse events, combined therapy, and intercurrent diseases are 
recorded on the case report form according to the clinical trial protocol; 
(4) Whether the details of clinical trial tests that were omitted for each 
subject (referring to the non-visit of the subject and the non-conduct 
of the test or examination on the subject) are clearly recorded in 
the case report form; 
(5) Whether the details of and reasons for the suspension of medication or 
subjects’ withdrawal are recorded in the case report form; 
n) 
Confirming whether notification to the investigators related to errors, omissions, 
and unreadable parts of the case report form or corrections thereof or additions 
thereto are made properly. In such cases, it shall be confirmed whether 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
115 
 
the causes of such errors, the signature of the person having the authority to 
change the information (referring to the principal investigator or the 
subinvestigator who has the authority to change the information on the case 
report form), and the date of change are properly provided. 
o) 
Confirming whether all adverse events have been reported according to this 
GCP, Article 24, clinical trial protocol, reporting standards set by the 
IRB, and other related statues and regulations; 
p) 
Confirming whether the principal investigator keeps essential documents 
according to subparagraph 7 (i) 6) and subparagraph 9; 
q) 
Confirming whether the principal investigator has been informed of all 
violations of the clinical trial protocol, SOP of sponsor, SOP of the clinical 
trial institution, this GCP, and Article 24, and whether appropriate measures to 
prevent the recurrence of such violations have been taken. 
5) 
Monitors shall conduct monitoring according to the SOP of sponsor and as 
determined by the sponsor concerning the clinical trial procedure. 
6) 
Reporting of monitoring shall be performed as follows: 
a) 
Where a monitor visits the clinical trial institution or contacts a person related 
to the clinical trial via telephone, fax, or e-mail, he or she shall report the 
details of such visits or contacts to the sponsor in writing. 
b) 
The monitoring report shall include the following information: 
(1) Date and place of monitoring; 
(2) Name of the monitor and the name of the investigator or the contacted 
person; 
(3) Summary of matters confirmed by the monitor; 
(4) Clinically significant discovery or events; 
(5) Violations of the clinical trial protocol, SOP of sponsor, SOP of the 
clinical trial institution, this GCP, and Article 24, or problems in the 
clinical trial; 
(6) Conclusion; 
(7) Measures taken to prevent the recurrence of violations of the clinical 
trial protocol, SOP of sponsor, SOP of the clinical trial institution, 
this GCP, and Article 24, and matters requiring such measures. 
c) 
A sponsor shall record the result of monitoring report reviews and follow-
up measures. 
t. 
Audit 
1) 
A sponsor shall conduct an audit to confirm whether the clinical trial is conducted in 
compliance with the protocol, the SOP of sponsor, the SOP of the clinical trial 
institution, these criteria, Article 24, and other relevant statutes and regulations 
according to their purposes. In such cases, the sponsor’s audit shall be performed 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
116 
 
separately from ordinary monitoring or quality management. 
2) 
Selection standards and qualifications of an auditor are as follows: 
a) 
The sponsor shall designate a person who has no personal stake in the 
clinical trial as an auditor; 
b) 
The auditor shall have the necessary knowledge, receive the training required 
for performing an audit for the study, and the sponsor shall prepare and 
keep a list of auditors and documents related to their qualifications. 
3) 
The procedures for audit are as follows: 
a) 
The sponsor shall establish guidelines for the audit on the subject, method, 
and frequency of audit, the form of audit report, details to be specified in the 
audit report, etc.; 
b) 
The sponsor shall establish an audit plan and audit procedures in consideration 
of the issues already confirmed concerning the significance of the clinical 
trial, subject number, type and complexity of the clinical trial, potential 
risks to subjects, and implementation of the study; 
c) 
The sponsor shall document and keep the audit results; 
d) 
The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall request to the sponsor for 
submission of the audit report only if there is evidence that the clinical trial 
has seriously violated Article 24 and this GCP, or if there is a legal 
dispute regarding the trial, in order to ensure the independent and 
autonomous implementation of the audit; 
e) 
The Minister of Food and Drug Safety may request to the sponsor for 
submission of an audit certificate. 
u. 
Actions against violations 
1) 
If the investigator, the sponsor, the monitor, or the auditor is found to violate 
the clinical trial protocol, the SOP of sponsor, the SOP of the clinical trial 
institution, this GCP, Article 24, and other relevant statues and regulations, the 
sponsor shall promptly take corrective and preventive action. 
2) 
If the investigator’s continued violation or serious violation is confirmed through 
monitoring or audit, the sponsor shall suspend the participation in the clinical 
trial by the relevant clinical trial institution and inform the Minister of Food 
and Drug Safety of such fact. 
v. 
Report on premature discontinuation or suspension of the study 
 
In cases of the premature discontinuation or suspension of the clinical trial, the 
sponsor shall promptly report such fact and reasons therefor in written form to the 
principal investigator and the Minister of Food and Drug Safety; if the clinical 
trial has been designed as a multicenter study, such fact and reasons therefor shall be 
notified in writing to the principal investigators of other clinical trial institutions as 
well. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
117 
 
w. Matters to be confirmed for a multicenter study 
 
In cases of a multicenter trial, the sponsor shall confirm the following: 
1) 
Whether all principal investigators are conducting the clinical trial in compliance 
with the protocol agreed by the sponsor and approved by the IRB and the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety; 
2) 
Whether the case report form is designed to collect all the data to be collected by 
each institution. In such cases, the principal investigator who intends to collect 
additional data shall be provided with a case report form with an addition of 
the relevant content; 
3) 
Whether the obligations of the investigators are documented before starting the 
clinical trial; 
4) 
Whether all principal investigators have complied with the clinical trial protocol and 
the evaluation standards for clinical and laboratory tests and have received a 
guideline for the recording of the case report form; 
5) 
Whether communications between the investigators are amicable; 
 
9.  Essential documents storage, access, etc. 
a. 
In order to terminate a clinical trial, the monitor shall review the essential documents of 
the investigator and sponsor and confirm the status of storage thereof. 
b. 
If there is a request for an audit from the sponsor under subparagraph 8 (t), the 
investigator shall allow the sponsor or the auditor to access the essential documents. 
c. 
In addition to the matters prescribed in this GCP, specific types of essential documents, 
the storage methods therefor for each clinical phase, and keeping managers per each 
document shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and 
Drug Safety.

Standards for Facilities and Manufacturing and Quality Management Systems  
of Import Businesses (Related to Article 31 (1)) 
 
1. 
Facilities of Import Business 
 
A person who intends to obtain an import business license, or an importer shall hold and keep 
the facilities and equipment under the following items, and check them periodically to avoid 
causing any trouble in import and quality management of medical devices 
A. Place of business where import business is conducted 
B. 
Warehouse where products are stored. Provided, however, that this shall not apply where 
only software medical devices are imported. 
C. 
Laboratory if testing for quality management is required, or testing facilities necessary for 
the test. Provided, however, that this shall not apply where only software medical devices 
are imported. 
 
2. 
Criteria for Facilities of Import Business 
 
The facilities of import business shall comply with the standards set forth in each of the 
following items. Provided, however, that this shall not apply where only software medical 
devices are imported. 
A. Facilities capable of maintaining the conditions at the time of importing the product 
B. 
Cold storage or facilities for shielding light (only for the products that require cold 
storage or the products that may have trouble with functions if exposed to the light) 
C. 
In case of handling the product item in which the storage method is specified, the 
facilities capable of maintaining such condition. 
 
3. 
Conformity Accreditation of Manufacturing and Quality Management System on 
Manufacturing Site of Imported Medical Devices 
A. An importer shall secure conformity of manufacturing and quality management system on 
the manufacturing site of imported medical devices. 
B. 
An importer of class II/class III/class IV medical devices shall receive periodic 
inspection every three years on whether manufacturing and quality management system 
on the manufacturing site conforms to the criteria of Annex 2 subparagraph 2. 
C. 
Annex 2 subparagraph 2 F shall apply mutatis mutandis for the standards and procedures 
of conformity accreditation or periodic inspection pursuant to item A and item B. 
D. Detailed matters of manufacturing and quality management system that are not prescribed 
in the Standards shall be set forth and notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act
