ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT [Annex 5] 
 <Amended on May. 1, 2017> 
 
Standards for Facilities and Quality Management Systems of Repair Businesses 
(Related to Article 35 (4)) 
 
1. 
Facility Management 
 
A repairer shall secure facilities and equipment necessary for repairing and testing 
medical devices. 
 
2. 
Repair Management Record 
 
A repairer shall prepare a repair management record for each item, and such record 
shall include the following: 
a. 
Item name and model name of the relevant medical device; 
b. 
Manufacturer (importer) name and country of manufacture of the relevant medical 
device; 
c. 
Date of manufacture and date of repair; 
d. 
Report of inspection and confirmation; 
e. 
Description of major repairs undertaken; 
f. 
Records on the management of repair facilities. 
 
3. 
Appointment of Chief Engineer 
 
A repairer shall appoint a chief engineer who has proper qualifications in the field of 
medical devices to be repaired who is in charge of managing repair duties. 
 
4. 
Duties of Chief Engineer 
a. 
Preparation, maintenance, and utilization of repair management records; 
b. 
Examination and confirmation on whether the medical device is properly repaired after 
the repair; 
c. 
Inspection and verification of repair results for quality assurance and documentation and 
maintenance of such results. 
 
5. 
Corrective Measures 
 
When there is a complaint on the quality of a repaired medical device, the repairer shall 
establish a procedure that allows the chief engineer to identify the causes and take 
corrective measures, and implement such a procedure. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
120 
 
6. 
Records 
 
The following records shall be prepared and maintained: 
a. 
Records regrading repair and maintenance work; 
b. 
Records regarding repair facilities including testing and inspection equipment; 
c. 
Records regarding corrective measures taken; 
d. 
Other records regarding conducting duties according to these standards. 
 
7. 
Training 
 
To improve the qualification of the chief engineer and repair workers, a repairer shall 
establish a company training plan that includes the following topics and provide the 
employees with such training at least once per quarter, for a total of 12 hours a year: 
a. 
Responsibilities regarding medical device repair and related statues and regulations; 
b. 
Content and specifications of the medical devices to be repaired; 
c. 
Matters regarding the quality management of medical device repair.

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT [Annex 6]  
<Amended on Jan. 21, 2022> 
 
Distribution Quality Management Standards for Medical Devices 
(Related to Article 39 (4)) 
 
1. 
Definitions 
 
The terms used in the Standards are defined as follows: 
a. 
The term “separation” refers to a condition of being in different buildings or in 
spaces separated by walls within the same building. 
b. 
The term “partitioning” refers to a condition of being divided by partitions, etc., so 
as to manage medical devices to prevent contamination or mix-ups thereof. 
c. 
The term “division” refers to a condition of different medical devices distinguished from 
each other by drawing lines or placing spaces among them so as to manage such 
medical devices to prevent confusion thereamong. 
d. 
The term “distribution quality management standards” refer to detailed standards that a 
person who may distribute or lease medical devices shall observe concerning 
distribution of such medical devices. 
e. 
The term “medical device mail-order distributor” refers to a person who conducts only a 
mail order business under Article 2 (2) of the Act on the Consumer Protection in 
Electronic Commerce among those who filed a distribution business notification 
under Article 17 of the Act. 
 
2. 
Facilities and equipment 
 
The place where medical devices are stored in the process of distribution or lease 
(hereinafter “storage area”) shall meet the following standards: 
a. 
The building where medical devices are stored shall be separated from dirty areas, and 
the storage site shall have sufficient area and space; 
b. 
A storage area shall not be used for any purpose other than the distribution or lease of 
medical devices: Provided, That products, etc. other than medical devices may also 
be stored in the space if divided or partitioned from medical devices within the extent 
of not damaging supply and quality management of the medical devices; 
c. 
Medical devices shall not come in direct contact with the floor; 
d. 
A storage area shall have adequate lighting for handling medical devices and shall be 
well-ventilated; 
e. 
A storage area shall be equipped with facilities that maintain proper temperature and 
humidity to prevent the deterioration of medical devices and shall have air 
conditioning facilities if necessary; in cases of storing medical devices that need to be 
kept at a fixed temperature, separate freezing or refrigerating equipment with automatic 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
122 
 
temperature recording devices shall be installed; 
f. 
When using automatic equipment such as freezing or refrigerating equipment, such 
equipment shall be periodically inspected and maintained to ensure that the 
equipment functions properly all the time, and records of such inspection and 
maintenance shall be preserved for one year; 
g. 
A storage area shall be equipped with facilities for preventing harmful insects and mice 
and with a fire extinguishing system. 
 
3. 
Chief manager 
 
For the stable supply and quality control of medical devices, a chief manager shall be 
appointed to check and confirm the compliance of the implement of tasks with the Standards. 
In such cases, the representative may concurrently hold the post of chief manager. 
 
4. 
Quality management and environment and hygiene management 
a. 
When warehousing medical devices, information on each transaction statement and the 
supplier, model name, quantity, specifications, etc., of the warehoused products shall 
be confirmed and checked, and the exterior of the devices shall be inspected for 
damage, contamination, etc. 
b. 
Medical devices that need to be divided according to storage temperature shall be 
stored by being divided in a refrigerated or frozen area. 
c. 
Returned medical devices and defective medical devices shall be stored separately. 
d. 
When shipping medical devices, a worker shall be present to perform exterior inspection 
and confirm the supplier, model name, quantity, specifications, shelf life (expiry date), 
etc., of the devices before shipping; when supplying medical devices to a medical 
institution, or medical device distributor or lessor, details of such supply including the 
customer, model name, quantity, and specifications, etc., of the devices shall be recorded. 
e. 
Medical devices that need to be divided according to storage temperature shall be 
stored at an appropriate temperature which is maintained during transport. 
f. 
A storage area and related machinery, apparatus, and equipment shall be kept clean. 
g. 
When any complaint is raised about the distribution process of medical devices, a 
prompt investigation shall be implemented to take appropriate measures, and the 
details of such investigation and measures shall be recorded. 
h. 
If a lessor intends to lease medical devices contacting with the human body which 
require contamination management, he or she shall remove contamination by methods 
such as cleaning, disinfection etc. and record and maintain the records of such 
contamination management. 
 
5. 
Record keeping and management 
a. 
The following ledgers necessary for proper supply and safety management of medical 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
123 
 
devices shall be prepared and placed: 
1) 
Facility and equipment ledger: Facility and equipment inspection results 
under subparagraph 2; 
2) 
Shipment ledger: Details of medical device supply under the latter part of 
subparagraph 4 d; 
3) 
Complaint handling ledger: Receipt of complaints and measures taken under 
subparagraph 4 g. 
b. 
Except for the records specified in the relevant statues and regulations, records related to 
handling duties including various ledgers shall be preserved for two years. 
 
6. 
Training 
 
In order to improve the capability of workers, a company training plan shall be 
established on the following topics, and such training shall be provided at least once 
per quarter, for a total of 12 hours a year: 
a. 
Responsibilities related to handling medical devices; 
b. 
Details and specifications of medical devices; 
c. 
Handling and quality management of medical devices. 
d. 
Laws and regulations on medical devices; 
e. 
Other matters necessary to efficiently implement the Standards. 
 
7. 
Subparagraph 2, subparagraph 4 b, c, e and f, and subparagraph 5 (a) 1) shall not 
apply to a person who does not have a storage area as a mail-order distributor of 
medical devices.

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT [Annex 7] 
 
Scope of Prohibited Advertisements 
(Related to Article 45 (1)) 
 
1. 
Falsified or exaggerated advertisement related to name/manufacturing method/performance or 
efficacy and effect of medical devices or their modes 
2. 
Advertisements on name/manufacturing method/performance or efficacy and effect of medical 
devices that are not approved, certified or notified for pursuant to Article 6 (2) or Article 15 (2) 
of the Act 
3. 
Advertisements with expressions to entirely deny the adverse effects of medical devices or 
with expressions to unreasonably emphasize safety 
4. 
Advertisements that have falsely cited medical clinical results, clinical study report, related 
papers or academic data, or falsely indicated as if obtaining patent or certification concerning 
efficacy or effect of the medical devices that have obtained license or certification, or filed a 
report for 
5. 
Advertisement that have used articles that might be misinterpreted as guaranteeing 
performance or efficacy and effect of medical device by doctor, dentist, doctor of oriental 
medicine, veterinarian or other persons 
6. 
Advertisement containing details such as designating/certifying/recommending/instructing or 
using the medical device by doctor, dentist, doctor of oriental medicine, veterinarian or other 
persons. However, advertisement containing details of being used by designating for the 
purposes of national health by government, local government or other public organizations 
shall be excluded. 
7. 
Advertisement that might misinterpret foreign products and domestic products or domestic 
products as foreign products 
8. 
Advertisements using letter of appreciation or personal experience of the user, or using 
expressions such as purchases/orders are pouring in or other similar expressions 
9. 
Advertisements containing details such as “definitely guarantee this” when advertising 
efficacy/effect, or advertisement using absolute expressions such as “top” or “best” 
10. Advertisements that might make people misinterpret that the medical device is not a medical 
device 
11. Advertisements that suggest as if being recommended by medical institution, etc. by pointing 
out the name of specific medical institution, department and contact info, etc. 
12. Advertisements using articles, photographs, designs or other suggestive methods to 
suggest performance or efficacy and effect of the medical device 
13. Advertisements that indicate or suggest the result of use with the comparison before and after 
using when advertising efficacy or performance 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
125 
 
14. Advertisements that slander or that are suspected as slandering other products regardless 
of whether it is true or not 
15. Advertisements that suggest abortion related to medical devices, or using obscene documents 
or designs 
16. Advertisements that indicate disease symptoms or surgery scenes related to efficacy/effect 
or purpose of use of medical devices in a threatening way 
17. Advertisements that are not reviewed pursuant to Article 25 (1) of the Act or 
advertisement containing different contents from the reviewed contents 
18. Advertisements that have received re-review request as the result of the review pursuant to 
Article 25 (1) of the Act

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT [Annex 7-2]  
<Amended on Oct. 22, 2019> 
 
UDI (Unique Device Identification) Management Standards 
(Related to Article 54-3 (2)) 
 
1. 
 Registration of Medical Device Information, etc. 
(a)  Manufacturers or importers shall register medical device information, etc. for each 
model name in the UDI System in order to efficiently record and manage integrated 
information on medical devices from approval through manufacturing, import, 
distribution, and use. 
(b)  Manufacturers or importers shall register medical device information, etc. in the UDI 
System after obtaining approval, certification, or completing notification of the 
medical device, and before releasing the medical device from their facilities. 
(c)  Where registered medical device information, etc. is changed, the manufacturer or 
importer shall register such changes within ten days from the date of the change. 
(d)  Where changes to medical device information, etc. specified by the Minister of Food 
and Drug Safety—such as the instructions for use or precautions—necessitate 
assignment of a new unique identification code, the manufacturer or importer shall 
register the changed medical device information, etc. in the UDI System and shall also 
register the newly assigned identification code. 
(e)  Where the head of the National Institute of Medical Device Safety Information finds 
that the registered medical device information, etc. is inaccurate or does not comply 
with the requirements prescribed by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, he or she 
may request the manufacturer or importer to correct or amend such information. In 
such cases, the manufacturer or importer shall take necessary measures—such as 
registering accurate information or submitting supplementary documents—within 
twenty days from the date of the request. 
(f)  Where the manufacturer or importer fails to take the necessary measures under item 
(e), or where it is evident that the registered information is inconsistent with the facts, 
the head of the National Institute of Medical Device Safety Information (NIDS) may 
delete or amend the relevant information. In such cases, the head of the NIDS shall 
notify the manufacturer or importer concerned without delay. 
(g)  Manufacturers or importers shall not falsely register medical device information, etc. 
(including false registration of changes). 
 
2.  Management of Medical Device Information, etc. 
(a)  Manufacturers or importers shall keep the medical device information, etc. registered 
in the UDI System up to date. 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
127 
 
(b)  Manufacturers or importers shall retain and manage records related to the medical 
device information, etc. registered in the UDI System. 
(c)  Where the marketing of a medical device is discontinued due to withdrawal or 
revocation of its approval, certification, or notification, or for any other reason, the 
manufacturer or importer shall retain the records related to the medical device 
information, etc. for three years from the date on which the marketing was 
discontinued. 
(d)  Manufacturers or importers shall provide education and training to employees and 
other personnel to enhance their competency regarding the registration of UDI and the 
use of the UDI System. 
(e)  Manufacturers or importers shall comply with the detailed standards prescribed and 
publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, including the methods and 
procedures for registration (including registration of changes) in the UDI System. 
 
3.  UDI Management Officer 
 
Manufacturers or importers shall appoint a management officer in order to efficiently and 
systematically manage UDI, including medical device information, etc. In this case, the 
quality manager may concurrently serve as the management officer, and the management 
officer shall inspect and verify whether employees and other personnel are performing their 
duties in accordance with the UDI Management Standards. 
 
 
 
 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
128 
 
■ 
ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT [Annex 8]  
<Amended on Oct. 31, 2025> 
 
Standards for Administrative Dispositions 
(Related to Article 58 (1)) 
 
I. 
General Standards 
1. 
Standards for Administrative Disposition for 2 or More violations 
a. 
In cases of 2 or more violations, the standard for the severest administrative 
disposition shall be followed: Provided, That if all the disposition standards 
correspond to business suspension or suspension of a product or product category 
(hereinafter “product”), disposition may be imposed by adding or weighting up to 
1/2 of each the period of such suspension shall be aggravated by summing up the 
suspension period following the respective less severe standards to the suspension period 
following the severest criteria. In such cases, the maximum suspension period shall not 
exceed 12 months: Provided, That when two or more individual standards are 
applicable to the violation for the same case in the causal relation (insufficient test 
equipment and failure to conduct testing, etc.), only the severest standards shall apply 
without adding up or weighting disposition. 
b. 
In cases of 2 or more types of violations of which disposition corresponds to business 
suspension and product suspension, each suspension period shall be calculated 
according to the criteria standards in item a, and if the business suspension period is 
longer than or equal to the product suspension period, only the disposition of 
business suspension shall be ordered; if the business period is shorter than the 
product suspension period, disposition of both business suspension and product 
suspension for the period that exceeds the business period shall be concurrently 
imposed. 
 
2. 
Standards for Administrative Dispositions for Cumulative Violations 
a. 
Standards for administrative dispositions for cumulative violations shall apply when 
administrative disposition is imposed for cumulative violations prescribed in “II. 
Criteria by Case” within a year (within 2 years for quality non-conformity [including 
cases applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 15 (6) of the Act] or within 5 years 
for a violation of Article 18 (2) of the Act) from the date of the latest disposition. 
In addition, when issuing a warning pursuant to the standards by case, the competent 
authority shall notify the party concerned to make improvements within a specified period, 
and if the violation is not remedied within that period, the case shall be regarded as a 
second violation. In such cases, the period to which the standards apply shall be 
calculated based on the date when a disposition was imposed on the preceding violation 
(in case of imposing a fine in lieu of a business suspension disposition, the date 
when the fine was imposed) and date when the same violation was detected after the 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
129 
 
imposition of the disposition: Provided, That the foregoing does not apply for 
violations involving different products. 
b. 
If an additional aggravated disposition is ordered following item a, such a disposition 
shall be given an ordinal number subsequent to that of the disposition imposed right 
before the violation for which it is issued (in cases of 2 or more dispositions ordered 
within the period under item a, the disposition with the highest ordinal number). 
c. 
When the same violation is detected during the period wherein the procedure for a 
previously received administrative disposition is in progress, 1/2 of the period of the 
dispositions set by the standards for each of the newly detected violations shall be 
added to the disposition period. In such cases, when the maximum period of business 
suspension or product suspension exceeds 12 months, the relevant manufacturing or 
import business approval or the approval or certification of the relevant product shall 
be revoked, or the relevant repair shop or business place shall be closed. 
d. 
When a business suspension period or a product suspension period is calculated to 
decimal places, such decimal places shall be rounded off. 
 
3. 
When the same violation is repeated three3 times or more, the case shall be excluded 
from the subject of imposition of a fine, and if the violation is repeated 5 times or more, 
the disposition standards for the 4th violation shall be applied. 
 
4. 
When, among the standards for administrative dispositions, a violation involves an 
individual product that has already been permitted, certified, or notified, the administrative 
disposition for the violation shall be imposed in relation to the approval, certification, or 
notification of the product or relevant business activities; when a violation involves all 
products that have been permitted, certified, or notified, the administrative disposition 
shall be imposed in relation to the approval, certification, or notification of the products 
or relevant business activities. 
 
5. 
When a violation involving a permitted, certified, or notified product is a violation on an 
individual factory, the administrative disposition for the violation shall be imposed on the 
items manufactured by the factory. 
 
6. 
When an administrative disposition has been enforced for a violation, the same violations 
committed before the disposition shall be deemed as having been punished by the 
disposition so that the disposition shall not be imposed again: Provided, That when the 
same violation has been committed in relation to a different product, or when it is in 
violation of 2 of II. Standards by Cases, the foregoing shall not apply. 
 
7. 
If any of the following reasons apply to a violation of which standard for disposition 
corresponds to business suspension or product suspension, the period of such suspension 
may be reduced to the extent of 1/2 (2/3 in cases of falling under item (f)); in cases of 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
130 
 
a violation of which standard for disposition corresponds to the revocation of 
manufacturing or import business approval, revocation of approval or certification of the 
relevant product, prohibition of manufacturing or import of the relevant product, or the 
closure of the repair shop or business place, the disposition may be mitigated to 3 
months of business suspension or product suspension: 
a. 
If the disposition is deemed necessary for public health or supply and demand, and 
for public interest; 
b. 
If a medical device fails to meet the standards for performance, safety, etc., 
according to a result of quality inspection thereof, and the non-conformity is so 
minor that it is deemed not harmful to the human body; 
c. 
If a medical device it has been manufactured or imported and repaired but not in 
circulation; 
d. 
If the device manufacturer or importer receives the disposition of suspension of 
indictment from the prosecutor or suspension of sentence from the court for the 
relevant violation; 
e. 
If the device manufacturer or importer reports a recall plan according to the provisions in 
Articles 52 through 54, sincerely conducts the recall accordingly in good faith, and 
notifies the result of the recall; 
f. 
If a person who has provided economic benefits, etc., in violation of Article 13 (3) 
of the Act (including cases where such provision applies mutatis mutandis under 
Article 15 (6) of the Act) or Article 18 (2) of the Act voluntarily reports the 
violation to an investigation agency or supervisory office before the violation is 
detected, and gives statements or testimonies or relevant data in a related 
investigation, lawsuit, etc. 
 
8. 
Notwithstanding subparagraphs 1 through 6, an exemption from any administrative 
disposition may be permitted if the medical device recalled by the device manufacturer or 
importer under Articles 52 through 54 is found to have no adverse effect on public health, 
or there is no reason attributable to the device manufacturer or importer.

■ 
ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE MEDICAL DEVICES ACT [Annex 9]  
<Amended on Jan. 16, 2024> 
 
Standards for Administrative Dispositions 
(Related to Article 58 (2)) 
 
I. 
General Standards 
1. 
In cases of 2 or more violations, the standard for the severest administrative disposition 
shall be followed: Provided, That if all the disposition standards correspond to business 
suspension, disposition may be imposed by adding 1/2 of each remaining disposition 
standard to the severest disposition standard within the range of 6 months. 
 
2. 
When a violation falls under any of the following and the disposition standard thereof 
corresponds to business suspension, the period of suspension may be reduced by 1/2 of 
the period set by the disposition standard, and when the disposition standard corresponds 
to the revocation of designation, such disposition may be mitigated into the suspension of 
the business from 3 to 6 months: 
a. 
When the violation does not have a significant impact on the results or is deemed to 
be a simple mistake; 
b. 
When the clinical trial subject to the disposition does not directly affect the 
safety of the subjects. 
 
3. 
The standards for aggravated administrative dispositions for cumulative violations shall 
apply when a person receives administrative dispositions for the same type of violations for 
the last 3 years. In such cases, the period shall be calculated based on the date when an 
administrative disposition was ordered for a violation and the date when the same 
violation is detected again: Provided, That when the same violation is detected during the 
period wherein the procedure for a previously received administrative disposition is in 
progress, 1/2 of the period of the dispositions set by the standards for each of the 
newly detected violations shall be added to the disposition period. 
 
4. 
When an aggravated additional disposition is ordered following subparagraph 3, such 
disposition shall be given the ordinal number subsequent to that of the disposition 
imposed right before the violation (in cases of 2 or more dispositions ordered within the 
period under subparagraph 3, the disposition with the highest ordinal number). 
 
 

Enforcement Rule of the Medical Devices Act 
 
169

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
178 
 
 
Standards of Good Manufacturing Practice 
(GMP) for Medical Devices 
[Enforced on December 9, 2025]  
[Ministry of Food and Drug Safety Notice No. 2025-80; December 9, 2025; Partially Amended] 
Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (Medical Device Management Division) 
 
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this GMP is to prescribe the detailed requirements to be 
observed when manufacturing or importing in medical devices (including medical devices for 
investigational use) and matters necessary for the designation procedures and management methods 
for the audit organization and training organizations for quality managers pursuant to Articles 6, 6-
2, 10, 12, 13, 15, 28, and 45 of the Medical Device Act; Articles 8, 14, 15, 24, 26, 27, 31, 33, 34, 
and 48, Annex 2, and Annex 4 of the Enforcement Rule of the Medical Device Act; Article 24 of the 
Promotion of the Medical Device Industry and Support for Innovative Medical Devices; and Article 
15 of the Regulations on the Support and Management of Innovative Medical Devices. 
 
Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this GMP shall have the meanings defined in Annex 1. 
 
Article 3 (Scope of Application) (1) The scope of this GMP shall be as follows: 
1.  A person who intends to obtain approval or certification for manufacturing or import of 
medical devices, or to submit a notification for such manufacturing or import; 
2.  A person who intends to manufacture or import medical device for investigational use. 
3.  A medical device manufacturer or importer who applies for conformity recognition and 
periodic assessment (hereinafter referred to as the “conformity recognition assessment”). 
4.  A person who has been designated, or who intends to be designated, as audit 
organization. 
5.  A person who has been designated or who intends to be designated, as training 
organizations for quality managers. 
(2)  Notwithstanding subparagraphs 1 through 3 of paragraph (1), where any of the following 
applies, this GMP shall be followed; provided, however, that conformity recognition 
assessments may be excluded. 
1.  Where medical devices are manufactured for export (hereinafter referred to as “medical 
devices for export”). 
2.  Where a person intends to manufacture or import Class I medical devices. 
3.  Where a manufacturing site manufactures medical devices by undertaking manufacturing 
processes from the legal manufacturer under a contractual relationship, as referred to in 
subparagraph 57 of Annex 1, and all of the following subparagraphs apply: 
(a)  Where the legal manufacturer is changed or added. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
179 
 
(b)  Where the same or a different manufacturer or importer holds a valid conformity 
recognition certificate under this GMP for the same product group with respect to 
the relevant manufacturing site. Provided, however, that where such conformity 
recognition certificate has been issued through document review without an on-site 
inspection, a quality management system conformity recognition certificate issued 
by an assessment organization under the Medical Device Single Audit Program in 
accordance with subparagraph 70 of Annex 1 (limited to cases where it is valid 
based on an on-site inspection; hereinafter referred to as the “MDSAP conformity 
recognition certificate”) shall be submitted. 
 
Article 4 (Classification of Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) Conformity recognition 
under this GMP shall be conducted by classifying the assessments as follows: 
1.  The initial assessment that a manufacturing site must undergo to be recognized as 
conforming to this GMP (hereinafter referred to as the “initial assessment”); 
2.  The assessment newly required when a manufacturing site adds medical devices of 
another product group pursuant to Annex 3 (hereinafter referred to as the “additional 
assessment”); 
3.  The assessment that must be newly conducted to obtain conformity recognition due to a 
change in the location of a manufacturing site (hereinafter referred to as the “assessment 
for change”); provided, however, that changes to storage facilities or test laboratories are 
excluded. 
(2)  Each manufacturing site shall undergo one periodic assessment every three years for each 
product group listed in Annex 3, pursuant to subparagraph 2 (e) 2) of Annex 2 and 
subparagraph 3 (b) of Annex 4 of the Enforcement Rule of the Medical Device Act (hereinafter 
referred to as the “Enforcement Rule”), and paragraph (1) 2 (d) and (e) of Article 15 of the 
Regulations on the Support and Management of Innovative Medical Devices. 
(3)  Notwithstanding Article 3 (2) and Article 4 (2), a manufacturing site may be exempted from 
periodic assessments when it has obtained conformity recognition for the following medical 
devices: 
1.  Medical device for export; 
2.  Class I medical device: 
3.  Medical device for investigational use 
4.  Drugs or quasi-drugs combined with, or integrally incorporated into combination medical 
devices 
 
Article 5 (Criteria for Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) The criteria for conformity 
recognition assessments pursuant to Annex 2 and Annex 4 of the Enforcement Rule and Article 15 
of the Regulations on the Support and Management of Innovative Medical Devices shall be as 
specified in Annex 2. Provided, however, that in cases of combined assessments under 
subparagraph 72 of Annex 1, the assessment criteria and assessment tables prescribed in the detailed 
operating guidelines under Article 14 (2) shall apply. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
180 
 
(2)  Notwithstanding paragraph (1), only part of Annex 2 may be applied in the following cases of 
each subparagraph: 
1.  For a person who intends to manufacture or import medical devices for investigational 
use, Sections 7.1, 7.3, 7.4.3, 7.5, 7.6, 8.2.6, and 8.3 shall be applied. 
2.  For an assessment for change under Article 4 (1) 3, Sections 4.1, 4.2, 6.1, 6.3, 6.4, 7.5, 
7.6, 8.2.2, 8.2.3, 8.2.6, 8.3, and 8.5 shall be applied. 
3.  Notwithstanding Article 3 (2), where conformity recognition assessments under this GMP 
are sought for Class I medical devices, Sections 4.1, 4.2, 5.5, 6.4, 7.1, 7.4, 7.5, 7.6, 8.2.1, 
8.2.2, 8.2.3, 8.2.6, 8.3, and 8.5 shall be applied. 
 
Article 6 (Methods of Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) Conformity recognition 
assessments pursuant to subparagraph 2 (e) and (f) of Annex 2 and subparagraph 3 of Annex 4 of 
the Enforcement Rule, and Article 15 of the Regulations on the Support and Management of 
Innovative Medical Devices shall be conducted jointly by the Commissioner of the Regional Office 
of Food and Drug Safety (hereinafter referred to as the “Commissioner of Regional Office”) and the 
head of the audit organization through document review and on-site inspection for each product 
group of the manufacturing site. Where the manufacturing process is carried out under an 
outsourcing arrangement between the legal manufacturer and the manufacturer (hereinafter referred 
to as the “legal manufacturer-manufacturer”), document review and on-site inspection may also be 
conducted separately for each of them. In such cases, for manufacturing sites of combination 
medical devices (including cases of legal manufacturer–manufacturer), separate document review 
and on-site inspection may be conducted. In such cases, on-site inspections shall not be limited to 
the core products under Article 7 (2). 
(2)  Notwithstanding paragraph (1), pursuant to the proviso to subparagraph 2 (f) 2) of Annex 2 of 
the Enforcement Rule and Article 15 of the Regulations on the Support and Management of 
Innovative Medical Devices, only document review shall be conducted in the following 
subparagraphs: 
1.  Where an additional assessment is conducted under Article 4 (1) 2; 
2.  Where an assessment for change is conducted based on the submission of data under 
Article 7 (1) 2 (b) for a manufacturing site whose location has been changed pursuant to 
Article 4 (1) 3; 
3.  Where another medical device manufacturer or importer has undergone document review 
and on-site inspection for the manufacturing site and holds a valid conformity recognition 
certificate; 
4.  Where a person has two or more manufacturing sites subject to periodic assessments 
under Article 4 (2), remaining manufacturing sites other than those selected for on-site 
inspection; 
5.  Where another manufacturer or importer of in vitro diagnostic medical devices under the 
Act on In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices has undergone document review and on-site 
inspection for the manufacturing site under the Good Manufacturing Practice for In Vitro 
Diagnostic Medical Devices and holds a valid conformity recognition certificate; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
181 
 
6.  Where a manufacturer holds MDSAP certificate; 
7.  Where periodic assessments are conducted for Excellent Manufacturing Sites under 
subparagraph 71 of Annex 1. 
(3)  Notwithstanding paragraph (2), an on-site inspection shall be conducted in any of the 
following cases: 
1.  Deleted 
2.  Where a manufacturing site is deemed to present potential risks; 
3.  Where a manufacturer or importer is unable to submit the data required under Article 7 
(1) 2 for reasons such as trade secrets, and requests an on-site inspection; 
4.  Where a manufacturer holds an MDSAP conformity recognition certificate, in any of the 
following cases: 
(a)  A manufacturing site subjects to periodic assessments under Article 4 (2); 
(b)  A manufacturing site that the Minister of Food and Drug Safety recognizes as likely 
to affect public health, including cases where significant nonconformities are 
identified in quality management system conformity recognition assessments under 
the Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP); 
(c)  A manufacturing site that produces combination medical devices. 
(d)  A manufacturing site that produces medical devices containing human-derived 
components or using human-derived tissues. 
(4)  Notwithstanding Article 4, a new initial assessment shall be required in any of the following 
cases: 
1.  Where the expiration date of the conformity recognition certificate held by a 
manufacturing site for export, Class I devices, or medical devices for investigational use 
has expired, and reapplication for conformity recognition is made; 
2.  Where a manufacturing site holding conformity recognition for medical devices for 
export intends to manufacture products for domestic sale; 
3.  Where the legal manufacturer in a legal manufacturer–manufacturer relationship that has 
undergone conformity recognition assessments is changed or removed; 
4.  Where the location of a manufacturing site that has obtained conformity recognition for 
medical devices for investigational use pursuant to Article 5 (2) 1 is changed, or where 
medical devices for investigational use belonging to a different product group are added, 
or where such devices are intended to be manufactured or imported for the purpose of 
sale; 
5.  Where a manufacturing site that has obtained conformity recognition for Class I medical 
devices pursuant to Article 5 (2) 3 intends to manufacture or import Class II, Class III, or 
Class IV medical devices. 
(5)  The entities for conducting conformity recognition assessments under paragraphs (1) through 
(4) shall be as provided in Annex 4. 
(6)  Where an on-site inspection cannot be conducted at a manufacturing site that is subject to such 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
182 
 
inspection due to circumstances such as war, infectious disease, natural disasters, or other 
similar events, the on-site inspection may be temporarily suspended and only a document 
review shall be conducted. 
(7)  Manufacturers or importers for whom only document review was conducted under paragraph 
(6) shall submit test reports conforming to their self-quality control test specifications for each 
manufacturing or import unit to the Commissioner of Regional Office at each instance of 
manufacture or import. 
 
Article 7 (Application for Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) A person who falls under 
any subparagraph of Article 3 (1) 1 through 3 and seeks to undergo conformity recognition 
assessments under this GMP shall submit an application in Form 1, along with the following 
documents, to the head of the audit organization. In this case, the manufacturing site shall have 
quality control records for at least one manufacturing unit, and the preferred date for the on-site 
inspection shall be finalized and submitted at least 20 days before the inspection start date. 
1.  A copy of the manufacturing (import) business license for medical devices or a copy of 
the conditional manufacturing (import) business license for medical devices (excluding 
cases where no such initial assessment or license for manufacturing (importing) medical 
devices (conditional) for investigational use is held). 
2.  The following documents corresponding to each item: 
(a)  An overview of the manufacturing site (including the name of the site and the 
address of each facility; if there are multiple sites, all site names must be included), 
organizational chart, number of employees, and medical devices manufactured; 
(b)  A copy of the quality management system conformity certificate issued by the 
regulatory authority or an agency delegated by the regulatory authority (only 
applicable to Article 6 (2) and Article 6 (6)) and on-site inspection results (only 
applicable to Article 6 (2) 2 and Article 6 (6), including any follow-up actions taken 
in response to the inspection results); 
(c)  A description of facility conditions for each manufacturing site subject to 
assessment [including floor plans of work areas, test laboratories, and storage 
facilities, and lists of facilities and equipment], cleanroom procedures (if 
applicable), and procedures for monitoring and measurement equipment that 
specify monitoring cycles; 
(d)  The quality manual of the manufacturing site (including the quality policy); 
(e)  Procedures and test reports related to finished product testing (e.g., final release 
inspection) for the core product of the manufacturing site (including documentation 
demonstrating sterilization for sterile products); 
(f)  Purchasing and outsourcing procedures for the core product of the manufacturing 
site, names of major suppliers (including contracted suppliers), and scope of work; 
(g)  Device Master Records of the core product for the manufacturing site (including 
descriptions of specific manufacturing processes such as sterilization or software, 
as applicable), and procedures for validation of sterilization, where applicable; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
183 
 
(h)  Checklist for Annex 2 criteria of the manufacturing site; 
(i)  Declaration of conformity to Annex 2 criteria of the manufacturing site; 
(j)  Deleted 
3.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 2, when undergoing assessment using the conformity 
recognition results obtained under the Medical Device Single Audit Program, the 
documents in any of the following items, excluding the materials corresponding to 
subparagraph 2, shall be submitted: 
(a)  A copy of the MDSAP conformity recognition certificate and the accompanying 
assessment results (including, where nonconformities were identified, the 
nonconformity report issued by the audit organization and the corrective and 
preventive action plan or results submitted by the manufacturing site that have been 
confirmed by the organization as compliant). 
(b)  Device Master Records for the product belonging to the highest classification level 
within each product group of the manufacturing site.  Provided, however, that for 
such an assessment for change, the Device Master Record shall be that of the 
product which belongs to the highest classification level within the product group 
of the manufacturing site and has the highest manufacturing or import volume. 
(c)  The following documents demonstrating that the quality management system 
complies with the requirements prescribed in statutes related to medical devices: 
1)  Quality manual of the manufacturing site; 
2)  Procedures related to record management; 
3)  Procedures that define the scope of responsibilities of the quality manager; 
4)  Procedures for managing medical devices subject to traceability (where 
applicable); 
5)  Procedures for adverse event reporting and advisory notices. 
(d)  Documents demonstrating the correlation between the products covered by the 
MDSAP conformity recognition certificate and the products subject to conformity 
recognition assessments. 
4.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 2, where a manufacturing site qualifies as a Excellent 
Manufacturing Site and undergoes a periodic assessment, the following documents shall 
be submitted in lieu of the documents required under subparagraph 2: 
(a)  Documentation confirming that the manufacturing site falls under Annex 1, 
subparagraph 71 (d); 
(b)  The Device Master Record for the core product that belongs to the highest 
classification level within each product group of the manufacturing site and has the 
highest manufacturing or import volume; 
(c)  The following documents demonstrating the appropriateness of quality control over 
the past three years: 
1)  Procedures and test reports related to finished product testing (e.g., final 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
184 
 
release inspection) for the core product (including sterilization validation 
procedures and test reports for sterile products); 
2)  Documents on corrective and preventive actions taken in the last three years 
in accordance with the criteria set out in Annex 2; 
3)  Checklist under Annex 2 and declaration of conformity. 
(2)  The submission documents for the core product falling under Article 7 (1) 2 (e), (f), (g), and (j) 
shall be the documents for the products corresponding to each of the following subparagraphs. 
1.  Where two or more products are submitted, the product belonging to the highest 
classification level within each product group of the manufacturing site shall be selected; 
2.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 1, in the case of a periodic assessment under Article 4 (2), 
the product belonging to the highest classification level of the manufacturing site and 
having the highest manufacturing or import volume among the products under the 
assessment shall be selected; 
3.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 1, in the case of an assessment for change under Article 4 
(3), the product belonging to the highest classification level within each product group of 
the manufacturing site and having the highest manufacturing or import volume shall be 
selected. 
(3)  A medical device manufacturer and importer required to undergo a periodic assessment under 
Article 4 (2) shall apply for the periodic assessment to the head of the audit organization by 
submitting an application in Form 1, accompanied by the documents under Article 7 (1) 1 and 
2, no later than three months before the expiration date stated on the conformity recognition 
certificate. In such cases, the desired on-site inspection date shall be fixed and applied for no 
later than 20 days before the expiration date stated on the conformity recognition certificate, 
and if the desired on-site inspection date is not confirmed at the time of application 
submission, the applicant shall submit the desired date in writing no later than 20 days before 
the start date of the requested on-site inspection. 
(4)  Where a medical device manufacturer and importer has multiple manufacturing sites subject to 
periodic assessment under paragraph (3), a consolidated application for periodic assessment 
may be submitted. Provided, however, that manufacturing sites that received the conformity 
recognition certificate using the Medical Device Single Audit Program or those designated as 
Excellent Manufacturing Sites shall be excluded from periodic assessment consolidated 
applications. 
(5)  A person who intends to submit a consolidated periodic assessment application under 
paragraph (4) shall prepare the documents required under paragraph (3) and the manufacturing 
site summary sheet in Form 1, and submit them to the head of the audit organization. 
(6)  Where Article 6 (2) 3 applies because another manufacturer or importer holds a valid 
conformity recognition certificate for the relevant manufacturing site under this GMP, only the 
following documents among those required under paragraph (1) may be submitted along with 
the application in Form 1: 
1.  A copy of the manufacturing (import) business license for medical devices or a copy of 
the conditional manufacturing (import) business license for medical devices (excluding 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
185 
 
cases where no such initial assessment or license for manufacturing (importing) medical 
devices (conditional) for investigational use is held); 
2.  The documents under Article 7 (1) 2 (g) (excluding sterilization validation procedures) 
and (j); 
3.  The document of the manufacturing site demonstrating that the products are 
manufactured under the same system at the same manufacturing site. 
(7)  When any of the following circumstances occurs, an Excellent Manufacturing Site under 
Annex 1, subparagraph 71, or a manufacturer or importer that has been issued a conformity 
recognition certificate under Article 6 (6) shall submit an application in Form 1 to the head of 
the audit organization within 10 days from the date of occurrence. In such cases, the applicant 
may omit the supporting documents for Form 1. 
1.  Where an Excellent Manufacturing Site no longer satisfies any of the criteria listed in 
Annex 1, subparagraph 71; 
2.  Where the conditions at the location or region of a manufacturing site for which an on-
site inspection was deferred under Article 6 (6) have ended. 
(8)  Where a person required to apply for a periodic assessment fails to do so at least three months 
before the expiration date under paragraph (3), the head of the audit organization shall report 
the name of the company, its representative, and other relevant information to the 
Commissioner of Regional Office. 
(9)  For manufacturing sites subject to on-site inspection under Article 6 (5), the documents listed 
in Article 7 (1) 2 (b), (h), and (j) may be omitted. 
(10)  Where a person who intends to undergo conformity recognition assessments pursuant to 
paragraph (1) may apply for a combined assessment under subparagraph 72 of Annex 1 where 
the person also intends to undergo a quality management system conformity recognition 
assessment under the Medical Device Single Audit Program. 
(11)  Costs and other matters related to conformity recognition assessments shall be governed by 
Annex 2 of the Enforcement Rule. 
(12)  Where a person who intends to undergo conformity recognition assessments pursuant to 
paragraph (1) may apply to the head of the audit organization for a priority assessment 
(meaning an assessment conducted in priority over other applications for conformity 
recognition assessments) with respect to a manufacturing site that manufactures medical 
devices falling under any of the following subparagraphs: In such cases, documents 
demonstrating that the medical devices fall under any of the following subparagraphs shall be 
submitted. 
1.  Medical devices subject to reporting under Article 2 of the Notice on the Scope of 
Medical Devices Subject to Production/Import Suspension Reporting and Reporting 
Methods, and medical devices deemed by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety to pose a 
substantial risk of suspension of production or importation pursuant to Article 3 (6) 
thereof. 
2.  Newly developed medical devices pursuant to Article 8 (1) 1 of the Medical Device Act. 
3.  Medical devices designated as innovative medical devices pursuant to Article 21 of the 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
186 
 
Promotion of the Medical Device Industry and Support for Innovative Medical Devices 
(excluding cases where such designation has been revoked). 
4.  Medical devices designed to display labeling or provide information by means of braille, 
audio, or other methods for persons with visual or hearing impairments pursuant to 
Article 23 (1) (a) and (b) of the Medical Device Act. 
 
Article 8 (Procedures for Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) Upon receiving an 
application for conformity recognition and related assessments under Article 7, the head of the audit 
organization shall, in accordance with the following subparagraphs, report the receipt and request 
confirmation of whether an on-site inspection is required under Article 6 (3) from the Commissioner 
of Regional Office. Provided, however, that where the assessment entity is single-agency under 
Article 6 (5) and Annex 4, and Article 6 (6) does not apply, reporting the receipt to the 
Commissioner of Regional Office may be omitted. 
1.  The head shall verify within five days whether all required documents under Article 7 (1) 
through (7) have been submitted, and if complete, shall report and request within seven 
days after receipt. 
2.  If, as a result of confirming whether the supporting documents under subparagraph 1 
have been submitted, any deficiency such as missing supporting documents is identified, 
the applicant shall be requested to supplement them by setting a supplementation 
deadline for the submission of such documents in accordance with the Administrative 
Procedures Act. 
3.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 1, where an application additionally includes a confirmed 
desired on-site inspection date, the report and request shall be made no later than the day 
following the receipt of the application. 
(2)  Within ten days after receiving the report and request under paragraph (1), the Commissioner 
of Regional Office shall determine the need for on-site inspection under Article 6 (3), the 
assessment entity under Article 6 (5), and the assessment method, and shall notify the head of 
the audit organization, who shall in turn notify the applicant. 
(3)  The head of the audit organization shall notify the applicant in writing of the conformity 
recognition assessment results under Article 6 within 30 days from the date the application for 
conformity recognition was received. Provided, however, that if an on-site inspection is 
required under paragraph (2), the period from the date of notification to the applicant until the 
start of the on-site inspection under this paragraph shall not be included in the processing 
period. 
(4)  Where an on-site inspection is required under paragraph (2), the head of the audit organization 
shall conduct the on-site inspection in accordance with the following subparagraphs: 
1.  The assessment entity determined under paragraph (2) shall conduct the on-site 
inspection on the notified inspection date, and the head of the audit organization shall 
notify the applicant in writing of the results within seven days from the end of the 
inspection visit or within the processing period under paragraph (3). Provided, however, 
that if the results of the on-site inspection are determined to be nonconforming, the 
Commissioner of Regional Office shall be notified immediately. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
187 
 
2.  If an on-site inspection under subparagraph 1 cannot be conducted due to war, epidemics, 
natural disasters, or other similar circumstances during the inspection period, or if the 
inspection cannot proceed normally due to delayed or refused submission of inspection 
documents, the on-site inspection may be suspended. In such cases, the applicant shall be 
immediately notified in writing of the reasons for the suspension, and the Commissioner 
of Regional Office shall be notified accordingly. 
3.  When the reason for suspension under subparagraph 2 is confirmed to be resolved, the 
on-site inspection may resume, and the results shall be notified to the applicant in writing 
within seven days from the completion date of the resumed inspection or within the 
processing period under paragraph (3). 
(5)  Where the head of the audit organization is unable to notify the applicant of the conformity 
recognition assessment results within the processing period under paragraphs (3) and (4) due to 
unavoidable reasons such as natural disasters, the head shall notify the applicant in advance of 
the delay. 
(6)  Where the results of the conformity recognition assessments fall under Annex 2, Section 9.4 
(2) (a) 2, the head of the audit organization shall take the actions in any of the following 
subparagraphs: 
1.  Require the applicant to submit corrective documentation and a corrective action plan, 
and evaluate conformity within 15 days from the end of the conformity recognition 
assessment. 
2.  Review the documents submitted under subparagraph 1 and notify the applicant in 
writing of the results. 
3.  If the applicant fails to submit the required documents within 15 days or the submitted 
documents are not adequate, supplementary measures shall be taken in accordance with 
paragraph (7). 
4.  If the applicant fails to submit the implementation results of corrective actions under 
subparagraph 1 within three months or the submitted results are inadequate, the head of 
the audit organization shall immediately report to the Commissioner of Regional Office 
and notify the applicant in writing. 
(7)  Where matters requiring supplementation are identified, the head of the audit organization 
shall take the following actions with respect to the results of the conformity recognition 
assessment: 
1.  Supplementation procedures and deadlines shall be required in accordance with the Civil 
Petitions Treatment Act, and the assessment entity under paragraph (2) shall review the 
results submitted by the applicant and evaluate conformity. 
2.  If the applicant fails to submit the required documents within the deadline, the 
assessment entity shall determine as nonconforming. 
3.  Where an application is determined nonconforming under subparagraph 2, the fact shall 
be reported immediately to the Commissioner of Regional Office, and the applicant shall 
be notified in writing. 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
188 
 
(8)  The head of the audit organization shall prepare a result report in Form 3 and submit it to the 
Commissioner of Regional Office in accordance with the following subparagraphs. Provided, 
however, that submission may be omitted where the assessment entity is single-agency under 
Article 6 (5) and Annex 4, and the case does not fall under Article 6 (6). 
1.  Assessment results under paragraph (3) shall be submitted within the processing period 
prescribed in paragraph (3). 
2.  Assessment results under paragraph (4) 1 shall be submitted within seven days from the 
end of the on-site inspection. 
3.  Where the on-site inspection is resumed pursuant to paragraph (4) 3, the results shall be 
submitted within seven days from the end of the resumed inspection visit or within the 
processing period under paragraph (3). 
(9)  Where the results of conformity recognition assessments under Article 6 are conforming, the 
head of the audit organization shall issue the Conformity Recognition Certificate under the 
Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical Devices (Form 2 or Form 2-2, pursuant to Annex 5) 
(hereinafter referred to as the “conformity recognition certificate”) to the applicant. Provided, 
however, that the temporary certificate may be issued in any case of the following 
subparagraphs: 
1.  Where the conformity recognition assessment results fall under Annex 2, 9.4 (2) (a) 2, a 
conditional conformity recognition certificate may be issued on the condition that 
corrective actions are implemented within three months; 
2.  Where document review is deemed to conform under Article 6 (6), a temporary 
conformity recognition certificate may be issued. 
(10) Where an applicant objects to the assessment results under Article 6, the applicant may file an 
objection with the head of the relevant audit organization in accordance with the Civil Petitions 
Treatment Act. 
(11) When an objection is filed under paragraph (9), the head of the audit organization shall report 
both the content of the objection and the handling results to the head of the Commissioner of 
Regional Office. 
(12) Where multiple manufacturing sites are submitted as a consolidated periodic assessment 
application under Article 7 (4), the Commissioner of Regional Office and the head of the audit 
organization shall conduct an on-site inspection for one manufacturing site, selected by 
comprehensively considering the following criteria: 
1.  A manufacturing site that produces the product of the highest class; 
2.  A manufacturing site with high domestic production or import volume; 
3.  A manufacturing site that has not previously undergone an on-site inspection. 
(13) For manufacturing sites that apply for conformity recognition assessments under Article 7 (7), 
the head of the audit organization shall conduct an on-site inspection within 90 days from the 
date of application. 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
189 
 
Article 9 (Expiration Date of the Conformity Recognition Certificate) (1) The expiration date of 
a conformity recognition certificate issued following an initial assessment shall be three years from 
the date of issuance. 
(2)  When conformity recognition is granted following an additional assessment or an assessment 
for change, the existing expiration date shall remain unaffected. 
(3)  The expiration date of a conformity recognition certificate issued following a periodic 
assessment shall be three years from the day after the expiration date of the previous 
certificate. Provided, however, that where the certificate is issued after the previous expiration 
date, or where the periodic assessment was submitted as a consolidated application, the 
expiration date shall be three years from the issuance date. 
(4)  Where conformity recognition assessments have been conducted pursuant to Article 6 (2) 3, 
the expiration date for the relevant manufacturing site shall be set to match the expiration date 
of the manufacturer or importer that previously underwent conformity recognition 
assessments. 
(5)  Where conformity recognition assessments have been conducted pursuant to Article 6 (2) 5, 
the expiration date for the relevant manufacturing site shall be set to match the expiration date 
of the in vitro diagnostic medical device manufacturer or importer that previously underwent 
conformity recognition assessments. 
(6)  Where conformity recognition assessments have been conducted using the Medical Device 
Single Audit Program pursuant to Article 6 (2) 6, the expiration date for the relevant 
manufacturing site shall be set to match the expiration date of the MDSAP conformity 
recognition certificate. 
(7)  Where conformity recognition assessments have been conducted pursuant to Article 7 (10), 
notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (3), the expiration date of the conformity recognition 
certificate may, at the applicant’s request, be set at up to three years. 
(8)  Where conformity recognition assessments have been conducted only for the legal 
manufacturer pursuant to Article 3 (2) 3, the expiration date for the relevant legal 
manufacturer–manufacturer shall be set to match the expiration date of the conformity 
recognition certificate previously issued for the same product group. Provided, however, that 
where only document review has been conducted without an on-site inspection pursuant to the 
proviso to Article 3 (2) 3 (b), the expiration date shall be set to match the expiration date of the 
MDSAP conformity recognition certificate. 
 
Article 10 (Reissuance of the Conformity Recognition Certificate) (1) A manufacturer or 
importer who has been issued a conformity recognition certificate under Article 8 (9) may apply to 
the audit organization that issued the certificate for reissuance if the certificate is lost or otherwise 
needs to be reissued. 
(2)  Upon receiving an application for reissuance under paragraph (1), the head of the audit 
organization shall reissue the conformity recognition certificate in accordance with Annex 5. 
(3)  A medical device manufacturer or importer may either obtain reissuance of the conformity 
recognition certificate or record the changes in any of the following subparagraphs on the 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
190 
 
reverse side of the certificate for control purposes: 
1.  Change in the name of the place of manufacturing or importing business; 
2.  Change in the location of the manufacturing site (limited to changes under the proviso of 
Article 4 (1) 3); 
3.  Change in the location of an importing business; 
4.  Change in the trade name of the legal manufacturer or the manufacturer; 
5.  Change in the location of the legal manufacturer or the manufacturer (limited to changes 
under the proviso to Article 4 (1) 3). 
(4)  Where a medical device manufacturer or importer records changes on the reverse side of the 
conformity recognition certificate under paragraph (3), the date and details of the approval of 
change shall also be recorded. 
(5)  A manufacturer or importer who has been issued a conformity recognition certificate under 
Article 8 (9) 1 may apply to the issuing audit organization for replacement of the certificate 
only after corrective actions have been completed, and may receive a replacement certificate 
accordingly. 
 
Article 10-2 (Return of the Conformity Recognition Certificate) (1) A manufacturer or importer 
who has been issued a conformity recognition certificate under Article 8 (9) may return the 
certificate to the issuing audit organization, specifying the relevant reasons in detail, when any of 
the following circumstances occurs: 
1.  Where the manufacturing business license or import business license is revoked; 
2.  Where the manufacturing approval, import approval, manufacturing certification, or 
import certification is revoked; 
3.  Where any other reasons exist requiring the manufacturer or importer to return the 
conformity recognition certificate. 
(2)  In accordance with paragraph (1), the head of an audit organization who has received the 
return of the conformity recognition certificate shall, immediately upon receipt of the returned 
conformity recognition certificate, report the fact of its return to the Commissioner of Regional 
Office. 
 
Article 11 (Marking for Conformity Recognition Assessments) A medical device manufacturer 
and importer may affix the conformity recognition marking, as specified in Annex 6, to medical 
devices that belong to the same product group as the manufacturing site which has undergone 
conformity recognition assessments. 
 
Article 12 (Duties of the Audit Organization) The duties of the head of the audit organization 
shall be any of following subparagraphs: 
1.  Conducting conformity recognition assessments under the Good Manufacturing Practice 
for Medical Devices; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
191 
 
2.  Issuing conformity recognition certificates. 
3.  Compiling statistics and providing administrative support related to conformity 
recognition assessments. 
4.  Other matters necessary for conformity recognition assessments. 
 
Article 13 (Assessment for Designation of an Audit Organization) (1) Where the Minister of 
Food and Drug Safety receives an application for designation as an audit organization pursuant to 
Article 48 (1) of the Enforcement Rule, the Minister shall conduct a document review and an on-
site evaluation of the submitted materials, including the application. 
(2)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall establish a plan for the on-site evaluation under 
paragraph (1) and notify the applicant of the following matters at least seven days prior to the 
conduct of the on-site evaluation: 
1.  The site and schedule of the on-site evaluation 
2.  The composition of the on-site evaluation team; 
3.  Matters requiring cooperation in connection with the on-site evaluation. 
(3)  The assessment criteria for designation as an audit organization pursuant to paragraph (1) shall 
be as specified in Annex 7. 
 
Article 14 (Standards for Management and Operation of an Audit Organization) (1) The head 
of an audit organization shall establish detailed operating guidelines necessary for conducting 
conformity recognition assessments. 
(2)  Where the head of an audit organization establishes or amends the detailed operating 
guidelines pursuant to paragraph (1), approval from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall 
be obtained. 
(3)  An auditor of an audit organization shall maintain impartiality and integrity in conducting 
conformity recognition assessments. 
(4)  An auditor of an audit organization shall not disclose to any third party, or use for purposes 
other than official duties, any information acquired in connection with conformity recognition 
assessments. 
(5)  An entity subject to conformity recognition assessments may file a request for recusal of a 
specific auditor for special reasons that make it difficult to expect a fair audit. The head of the 
audit organization may replace the auditor if the recusal application is deemed justified. 
(6)  Other standards for management and operation to be observed by an audit organization shall be 
as specified in Annex 8. 
 
Article 15 (Reporting) (1) The head of the audit organization shall submit the quarterly report on 
the results of conformity recognition assessments for medical devices (Form 4) and the detailed list 
of such assessment results (Form 5) to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety and the Commissioner 
of Regional Office within 20 days after the end of each quarter. Provided, however, that where the 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
192 
 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety or the Commissioner of Regional Office requests separate data, 
the relevant data shall be submitted within seven days from the date of the request. 
(2)  Where there are personnel changes, such as transfers or resignations of assessors, the head of 
the audit organization shall report such changes to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
within seven days. 
 
Article 16 (Guidance and Inspection of Audit Organizations) (1) The Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety shall conduct annual guidance and inspections of audit organizations to determine whether 
conformity recognition assessments are being properly conducted and whether the organizations are 
being operated in compliance with the standards for management and operation. 
(2)  Where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety deems that there are improper conformity 
recognition assessments, issues with determinations, or problems in the performance of such 
assessments due to complaints or other reasons, the Minister may conduct guidance and 
inspections at any time. 
(3)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall establish detailed criteria for guidance and 
inspections to be conducted pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2). 
 
Article 17 (Application for Designation of Training Organizations for Quality Managers) (1) 
Where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety intends to additionally designate training 
organizations for quality managers, the Minister shall announce an application period during which 
institutions or organizations falling under Article 14 (1) of the Enforcement Rule may apply for 
designation as training organizations for quality managers. 
(2)  The specific criteria for the designation of a training organizations for quality managers 
pursuant to Article 14 (6) of the Enforcement Regulations shall be as per Annex 9. 
 
Article 18 (Assessment for Designation of Training Organizations for Quality Managers) (1) 
Where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety receives an application for designation as a training 
organization for quality managers pursuant to Article 17 (1), the Minister shall conduct a document 
review and an inspection of the submitted materials, including the application pursuant to Article 14 
(2) of the Enforcement Rule. 
(2)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall establish a plan for the inspection under paragraph 
(1) and notify the applicant of the following matters at least seven days before the inspection: 
1.  the site and schedule of the inspection; 
2.  the composition of the inspection team; 
3.  Matters requiring cooperation in connection with the inspection. 
 
Article 19 (Announcement of Designation of Training Organizations for Quality Managers) 
The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall publicly announce the training organizations for quality 
managers that comply with the Article 17.

Article 20 (Training Content) Pursuant to Article 13 (1) 4 of the Enforcement Rule, the head of a 
training organizations for quality managers shall establish a training plan to ensure that the 
curriculum includes the following training content: 
1.  Matters concerning the scope of duties of a quality manager pursuant to Article 12 of the 
Enforcement Rule; 
2.  Matters concerning safety related to the handling of hazardous substances, such as 
radiation; 
3.  Matters requiring scientific and technical training related to medical devices; 
4.  Other matters concerning the latest amendments in the laws and regulations on medical 
devices. 
 
Article 21 (Matters to Be Observed by the Head of a Training Organizations for Quality 
Managers, etc.) (1) Where the head of a training organizations for quality managers intends to 
amend the regulations on training implementation specified in Annex 9, approval from the Minister 
of Food and Drug Safety shall be obtained. 
(2)  Pursuant to Article 15 (2) of the Enforcement Rule, the head of a training organization for 
quality managers shall establish a training plan that includes the matters prescribed in Article 
20 and the following: 
1.  The trainees and the expected number of participants by category; 
2.  The training venue; 
3.  Tuition fees (including supporting documentation); 
4.  Training method (by target trainee, by region, etc.); 
5.  The curriculum; 
6.  Training subjects, hours, and content for each curriculum (including training materials); 
7.  Instructors; 
8.  An annual training schedule; 
9.  Other matters necessary for the implementation of the training. 
(3)  Where the training plan pursuant to paragraph (2) is to be amended, the revised plan shall be 
submitted to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety at least one month prior to the 
commencement of the training. 
(4)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety may review the training plan and related documents 
submitted pursuant to paragraph (2) and, if necessary, request corrective measures or 
supplementation. 
(5)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall approve the training plan submitted pursuant to 
Article 15 (2) of the Enforcement Rule within 15 days from the date of submission.

Article 22 (Guidance and Inspection of Training Organizations for Quality Manager) (1) The 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall conduct annual guidance and inspections of training 
organizations for quality manager to determine whether training is being properly conducted and 
whether such organizations are being operated in compliance with the training implementation 
rules. 
(2)  Where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety deems that there are problems in the performance 
of training activities due to improper training or the filing of complaints, the Minister may 
conduct guidance and inspections at any time. 
(3)  The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall establish detailed criteria for guidance and 
inspections to be conducted pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2). 
 
Article 23 (Review of Regulation) In accordance with Article 8 of the Framework Act on 
Administrative Regulations and the Regulation on the Issuance and Management of Directives and 
Guidelines, the validity of this Notice shall be reviewed every three years, starting from Jan. 1, 2014 
(until Dec. 31 of every third year), and necessary measures, including improvements, shall be taken.
