Documents 
shall be controlled in accordance with Section 4.2.5.  
(b) Procedures necessary to control the following shall be 
documented: 
1)  Review and approval of documents for adequacy prior to 
issuance; 
2)  Review, update, and re-approval of documents as 
necessary; 
3)  Ensure that changes to documents and the current revision 
status are identified; 
4)  Ensure that applicable versions of documents are available 
at points of use;  
5)  Ensure that documents remain legible and readily 
identifiable;  
6)  Ensure that documents of external origin determined by 
the organization to be necessary for the planning and 
operation of the quality management system are identified 
and their distribution controlled; 
7)  Prevent deterioration or loss of documents; 
8) Preventing the unintended use of obsolete documents and 
applying appropriate identification if they are retained for 
any purpose. 
(c) The organization shall ensure that document changes are 
reviewed and approved by the original approving authority or 
other authorized personnel who have access to the background 
information on which the organization’s decisions are based. 
(d) The organization shall retain at least one copy of obsolete 
controlled documents for a period corresponding to the 
product’s life cycle, which shall be no less than the retention 
period required for records. 
4.2.5 Control of 
Records 
(a) Records shall be established and maintained to demonstrate the 
effective operation of the quality management system and 
conformity to requirements.  
(b) The organization shall document procedures defining the 
controls needed for the identification, storage, security and 
integrity, retrieval, retention period, and disposition of records. 
(c) The organization shall establish and implement methods to 
protect personal health information contained in records in 
accordance with applicable statutory requirements. 
(d) All records shall be easily legible, readily identifiable, and 
retrievable. Any changes to records shall remain identifiable. 
(e) The organization shall retain records for a period 
corresponding to the product’s life cycle. This period shall be 
at least five years from the date of manufacture and at least 
two years after release to the market. 
 
 
 
 
 
5. Management 
Responsibility 
5.1 
Management 
Commitment 
Top management shall demonstrate its commitment to the 
development and implementation of the quality 
management system and to maintaining its effectiveness 
through the following:  
1)  Communicate the importance of fulfilling customer 
requirements and applicable statutory requirements with the 
organization; 
2)  Establish the quality policy; 
 
 
 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
240 
 
GMP Criteria  
Requirements  
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment Result 
Remarks 
A 
B 
C 
D 
3)  Ensure that quality objectives are established; 
4)  Conduct management reviews; 
5)  Ensure the availability of resources. 
5.2 Customer 
Focus 
Top management shall ensure that customer requirements 
and applicable statutory requirements are determined and 
fulfilled. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.3 Quality 
Policy 
Top management shall ensure that the quality policy: 
1)  Is appropriate to the purpose of the organization; 
2)  Includes a commitment to comply with requirements and to 
maintain the effectiveness of the quality management system; 
3)  Provides a framework for establishing and reviewing quality 
objectives; 
4)  Is communicated and understood within the organization; 
5)  Is reviewed for continuing suitability. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.4 Planning 
5.4.1 Quality 
Objectives 
(a) Top management shall ensure that the quality objectives 
include the necessary elements to meet applicable statutory 
requirements and product requirements, and that they are 
established at relevant functions and levels within the 
organization.  
(b) The quality objectives shall be measurable and shall be 
consistent with the quality policy. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.4.2 Planning 
of the Quality 
Management 
System 
Top management shall ensure the following: 
1)  The planning of the quality management system is carried out 
not only to achieve the quality objectives but also to meet the 
requirements of Section 4.1;  
2)  The integrity of the quality management system is maintained 
when changes to the quality management system are planned 
and implemented.  
 
 
 
 
 
5.5 
Responsibility, 
Authority, and 
Communication 
5.5.1 
Responsibility 
and Authority 
(a) Top management shall ensure that responsibilities and 
authorities within the organization are defined, documented, 
and communicated. 
(b) Top management shall document the interrelationships of all 
personnel who manage, perform, and verify work affecting 
quality, and shall ensure the authority and independence 
necessary to perform such work. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.5.2 Quality 
Manager 
Top management shall appoint a person within the 
organization who, irrespective of other responsibilities, has 
the authority and responsibility to perform the following: 
1)  Ensure that the processes necessary for the quality 
management system are documented; 
2)  Report to top management on the performance and 
effectiveness of the quality management system and on the 
need for improvement; 
3)  Ensure that awareness of applicable statutory requirements 
and quality management system requirements is promoted 
throughout the organization. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.5.3 Internal 
Communication 
Top management shall ensure that appropriate 
communication processes are established within the

241 
 
GMP Criteria  
Requirements  
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment Result 
Remarks 
A

organization and that communication regarding the 
effectiveness of the quality management system is carried 
out. 
5.6 
Management 
Review 
5.6.1 General 
Requirements 
(a) The organization shall document the procedure for 
management review.  
(b) Top management shall review the quality management system 
at documented planned intervals to ensure its continuing 
suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.  
(c) Management reviews shall include an evaluation of the need 
for changes and opportunities for improvement in the quality 
management system, including the quality policy and quality 
objectives. 
(d) Records of management reviews shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.6.2 Review 
Inputs 
The inputs to management review shall include, but not be 
limited to, the following: 
1)  Feedback; 
2)  Handling of complaints; 
3)  Reports to regulatory authorities; 
4)  Audits; 
5)  Monitoring and measurement of processes; 
6)  Monitoring and measurement of product; 
7)  Corrective action; 
8)  Preventive action; 
9)  Follow-up actions from previous management reviews; 
10) Changes that could affect the quality management system; 
11) Recommendations for improvement; 
12) New or revised applicable statutory requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.6.3 Review 
Outputs 
The outputs of management review shall be recorded and 
shall include decisions and actions related to the reviewed 
inputs and the following: 
1)  Improvements needed to maintain the suitability, adequacy, 
and effectiveness of the quality management system and its 
processes; 
2)  Improvement of product related to customer requirements; 
3)  Changes needed to meet new or revised applicable statutory 
requirements; 
4)  Resource needs. 
 
 
 
 
 
6. Resource 
Management 
6.1 Provision of 
Resources 
The organization shall determine and provide the resources 
needed for: 
1)  Implementing the quality management system and 
maintaining its effectiveness; 
2)  Meeting applicable regulatory requirements and customer 
requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
6.2 Human 
Resources 
(a) Personnel performing work affecting product quality shall be 
competent on the basis of appropriate education, training, 
skills, and experience.  
(b) The organization shall establish the competencies required of 
personnel, provide the necessary training, and establish and

document processes to ensure personnel awareness. 
(c) The organization shall perform the following:  
1)  Determine the competencies needed for personnel 
performing work that affects product quality;  
2)  Provide training or take other actions to achieve or 
maintain the necessary competencies;  
3)  Evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken; 
4) Ensure that personnel are aware of the relevance and 
importance of their activities and how they contribute to 
the achievement of quality objectives;  
5)  Maintain appropriate records of education, training, skills, 
and experience. 
6.3 
Infrastructure 
(a) The organization shall document the infrastructure 
requirements necessary to ensure conformity to product 
requirements, prevent product mix-ups, and ensure orderly 
handling. Where applicable, infrastructure includes: 
1)  Buildings, workspace, and associated facilities; 
2)  Process equipment (hardware and software); 
3)  Supporting services such as transport, communication, or 
information systems. 
(b) Where maintenance activities of infrastructure, or lack thereof, 
may affect product quality, the organization shall document 
the maintenance requirements, including maintenance 
intervals. Where applicable, these requirements shall apply to 
equipment used for manufacturing, work environment control, 
and monitoring and measurement. 
(c) Records of such maintenance activities shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
6.4 Work 
Environment 
and 
Contamination 
Control 
6.4.1 Work 
Environment 
(a) The organization shall document the requirements for the work 
environment necessary to ensure conformity to product 
requirements. 
(b) Where work environment conditions may have an adverse 
effect on product quality, the organization shall document the 
requirements for the work environment and procedures for 
monitoring and controlling such conditions. 
(c) The organization shall perform the following requirements: 
1)  Where personnel may come into contact with the product 
or the work environment in a manner that could affect the 
safety or performance of medical devices, requirements 
for personnel health, cleanliness, and clothing shall be 
documented. 
2)  All personnel who work temporarily under special 
environmental conditions shall be competent or shall be 
supervised by competent personnel. 
 
 
 
 
 
6.4.2 
Contamination 
Control 
(a) Where applicable, the organization shall plan and document 
methods for controlling products that are contaminated or 
potentially contaminated, in order to prevent contamination of 
the work environment, personnel, or products.  
(b) For sterilized medical devices, the organization shall document 
requirements for contamination control related to 
microorganisms or particulates and shall maintain the required 
cleanliness during assembly or packaging processes.

7. Production 
Realization 
7.1 Planning of 
Production 
Realization 
(a) The organization shall plan and develop the processes needed 
for production realization. Planning of production realization 
shall be consistent with the other process requirements of the 
quality management system. 
(b) The organization shall document one or more processes for 
risk management during production realization, and records of 
risk management activities shall be maintained.  
(c) Where applicable, the organization shall determine the 
following in planning production realization:  
1)  Quality objectives and requirements for the product; 
2)  The need to establish and document processes, and to 
ensure the availability of specific resources for the 
product, including infrastructure and work environment;  
3)  Specific verification, validation, monitoring, 
measurement, testing and inspection, handling, storage, 
distribution, and traceability activities required for the 
product, along with the criteria for product acceptance; 
4)  Records necessary to demonstrate that production 
realization processes and their outputs meet requirements. 
(d) The outputs of such planning shall be documented in a form 
appropriate to the organization’s method of operation. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.2 Customer-
Related 
Processes 
7.2.1 
Determination 
of 
Requirements 
Related to the 
Product 
The organization shall determine the following:  
1)  Requirements specified by the customer, including those 
related to delivery and post-delivery activities; 
2)  Requirements not stated by the customer but necessary for 
known specified or intended use;  
3) Applicable statutory requirements related to the product; 
4)  User training necessary to ensure stated performance and safe 
use of the medical device; 
5)  Any additional requirements determined by the organization. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.2.2 Review of 
Requirements 
Related to the 
Product 
(a) The organization shall review the requirements related to the 
product. This review shall be conducted prior to the 
organization’s commitment to supply the product to the 
customer.  
1)  The requirements for the product are defined and 
documented; 
2)  Any contract or order requirements differing from those 
previously expressed are resolved; 
3)  Applicable statutory requirements are met; 
4)  User training determined under Section 7.2.1 is feasible or 
planned to be feasible; 
5)  The organization has the capability to meet the defined 
requirements. 
(b) Records of the results of the review and any actions arising 
from the review shall be maintained. 
(c) Where the customer does not provide documented 
requirements, the organization shall confirm the customer 
requirements prior to acceptance.  
(d) When product requirements are changed, the organization shall 
amend the relevant documents and ensure that relevant 
personnel are made aware of the changed requirements.

7.2.3 
Communication 
(a) The organization shall plan and document the methods for 
communicating with customers regarding: 
1)  Product information; 
2)  Handling inquiries, including amendments, contracts, or 
orders; 
3)  Customer feedback, including complaints; 
4)  Advisory notices. 
(b) The organization shall communicate with regulatory 
authorities in accordance with applicable statutory 
requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3. Design and 
Development 
7.3.1 General  
The organization shall document procedures for design and 
development. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.2 Design 
and 
Development 
Planning 
(a) The organization shall plan and control the design and 
development of the product. Where applicable, the design and 
development plan shall be maintained and updated as design 
and development progress. 
(b) The organization shall document the following in the course of 
design and development planning:  
1)  The stages of design and development; 
2)  The reviews required at each stage of design and 
development;  
3)  The verification, validation, and design transfer activities 
appropriate to each stage of design and development; 
4)  The responsibilities and authorities for design and 
development; 
5)  The methods to ensure traceability between design and 
development inputs and outputs; 
6)  The necessary resources, including personnel competence. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.3 Design 
and 
Development 
Inputs 
(a) The organization shall determine and maintain records of 
inputs relating to product requirements. These inputs shall 
include:  
1)  Functional, performance, usability, and safety 
requirements necessary for the intended use; 
2)  Applicable statutory requirements and standards; 
3)  Applicable risk management outputs; 
4)  Information derived from previous similar designs, where 
applicable; 
5)  Other requirements essential for the design and 
development of the product and process. 
(b) Such inputs shall be reviewed and approved for adequacy.  
(c) Product requirements shall be clear, unambiguous, verifiable 
or validatable, and shall not conflict with other requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.4 Design 
and 
Development 
Outputs 
(a) The design and development outputs shall: 
1)  Meet the design and development input requirements; 
2)  Provide appropriate information for purchasing, 
production, and service provision; 
3)  Include or reference the criteria for product acceptance;   
4)  Specify the characteristics of the product that are essential

245

Requirements  
Assessment Criteria

A 
B 
C

for safe and proper use. 
(b) The outputs of the design and development process shall be 
provided in a form that enables verification against the design 
and development inputs and shall be approved prior to release.  
(c) Records of the design and development outputs shall be 
maintained. 
7.3.5 Design 
and 
Development 
Review 
(a) Systematic reviews of the design and development shall be 
conducted at appropriate stages in accordance with planned 
and documented methods for the purpose of:  
1)  Evaluating the ability of the design and development 
results to meet the requirements; 
2)  Identifying and proposing any necessary actions. 
(b) Personnel participating in such reviews shall include not only 
the persons responsible for the design and development stage 
under review, but also other relevant experts. 
(c) Records of the results of the reviews and any necessary actions 
shall be maintained and shall include identification of the 
design under review, the personnel participating in the review, 
and the dates of the review.  
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.6 Design 
and 
Development 
Verification 
(a) Design and development verification shall be performed in 
accordance with planned and documented methods to ensure 
that the design and development outputs meet the input 
requirements.  
(b) The organization shall document the verification plan, 
including the verification methods, acceptance criteria, and, 
where applicable, statistical techniques with justification for 
sample size. 
(c) If the intended use requires the medical device to be connected 
to or interfaced with another medical device, the verification 
shall include confirmation that the design outputs meet the 
design inputs when so connected or interfaced. 
(d) Records of the verification results, conclusions, and any 
necessary actions shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.7 Design 
and 
Development 
Validation 
(a) Design and development validation shall be performed, in 
accordance with planned and documented methods, to ensure 
that the resulting product meets the requirements for the 
intended use or specified application.  
(b) The organization shall document the validation plan, including 
the validation methods, acceptance criteria, and, where 
applicable, justification for sample size. 
(c) Design validation shall be performed on core product. Core 
product includes initial production units, batches, or their 
equivalents. The rationale for the selection of the product used 
for validation shall be recorded. 
(d) As part of design and development validation, the organization 
shall perform clinical evaluation in accordance with applicable 
statutory requirement. 
(e) Medical devices used for clinical evaluation shall not be 
considered as released for customer use. 
(f) If the intended use requires the medical device to be connected 
to or interfaced with another medical device, the validation 
shall include confirmation that the product requirements for 
the specified application or intended use are met when so

(g) Validation shall be completed prior to the product’s release for 
customer use.  
(h) Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, 
and any necessary actions shall be maintained. 
7.3.8 Design 
and 
Development 
Transfer 
(a) The organization shall document procedures for the transfer of 
design and development outputs to manufacturing. These 
procedures shall ensure that the design and development 
outputs have been verified as suitable for manufacturing 
before becoming the final production specifications and that 
manufacturing capability can meet product requirements.  
(b) Records of the results and conclusions of the transfer shall be 
maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.9 Control of 
Design and 
Development 
Changes 
(a) The organization shall document procedures for controlling 
design and development changes. The organization shall 
determine the significance of changes to the function, 
performance, usability, safety, applicable statutory 
requirements, and intended use of the medical device. 
(b) Design and development changes shall be identified. Prior to 
implementation, the changes shall be: 
1)  Reviewed;  
2)  Verified;  
3)  Validated, where applicable; 
4)  Approved. 
(c) The review of design and development changes shall include 
evaluation of the effects of the changes on constituent parts, 
products in manufacturing or already delivered, risk 
management inputs or outputs, and the production realization 
processes.  
(d) Records of the changes, the review of the changes, and any 
necessary actions shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.10 Design 
and 
Development 
File 
(a) The organization shall maintain a design and development file 
for each medical device model or product. 
(b) This file shall contain or reference the records generated to 
demonstrate conformity with the design and development 
requirements and the records of design and development 
changes. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.4. Purchasing 
7.4.1 
Purchasing 
Process 
(a) The organization shall document procedures to ensure that 
purchased product conforms to specified requirements. 
(b) The organization shall establish criteria for the evaluation and 
selection of suppliers. The criteria shall be based on: 
1)  The supplier’s ability to provide product that meets the 
organization’s requirements; 
2)  The supplier’s performance; 
3)  The effect of the purchased product on the quality of the 
medical device; 
4)  Proportionality to risks associated with the medical 
device. 
(c) The organization shall plan monitoring and re-evaluation of 
suppliers. The performance of suppliers in meeting purchased 
product requirements shall be monitored. The results of

Requirements  
Assessment Criteria

Remarks 
A 
B

monitoring shall be provided as input to the supplier re-
evaluation process.  
(d) Non-fulfillment of purchasing requirements shall be addressed 
with the supplier in proportion to the risks associated with the 
purchased product and compliance with applicable statutory 
requirements. 
(e) Records of the results of evaluation, selection, monitoring, and 
re-evaluation of suppliers and of any necessary actions arising 
from these activities shall be maintained. 
7.4.2 
Purchasing 
Information 
(a) Purchasing information shall describe or reference the product 
to be purchased, including, where appropriate:  
1)  Product specifications; 
2)  Requirements for product approval, procedures, processes, 
and equipment; 
3)  Requirements for the qualification of supplier personnel; 
4)  Quality management system requirements. 
(b) The organization shall ensure the adequacy of specified 
purchasing requirements prior to communication with the 
supplier. 
(c) Purchasing information shall include, where appropriate, a 
written agreement that the supplier notify the organization of 
any changes to the product prior to implementation if such 
changes may affect the ability of the product to meet specified 
purchasing requirements. 
(d) The organization shall maintain the relevant purchasing 
information as documents and records to the extent that 
traceability is required in accordance with Section 7.5.9. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.4.3 
Verification of 
Purchased 
Product 
(a) The organization shall establish and implement the inspection 
or other activities necessary to ensure that purchased product 
meets specified requirements. The extent of verification 
activities shall be based on the results of supplier evaluation 
and shall be proportional to the risks associated with the 
purchased product.  (b) When the organization becomes aware 
of any changes to the purchased product, it shall determine 
whether such changes affect the production realization 
processes or the medical device. 
(c) If the organization or its customer intends to verify the 
purchased product at the supplier’s premises, the organization 
shall specify in the purchasing information the intended 
verification arrangements and the method of product release.  
(d) Records of verification shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5 Production 
and Service 
Provision 
7.5.1 Control of 
Production and 
Service 
Provision 
(a) Production and service provision shall be planned, carried out, 
monitored, and controlled to ensure that product conforms to 
specifications. Where appropriate, production control shall 
include, but not be limited to: 
1)  Documentation of procedures and methods for production 
control; 
2)  Qualification of infrastructure; 
3)  Implementation of monitoring and measurement of 
process parameters and product characteristics; 
4)  Availability and use of monitoring and measuring 
equipment;

5)  Implementation of activities specified for labeling and

6)  Implementation of product release, delivery, and post-

(b) The organization shall provide traceability to the extent 
required in accordance with Section 7.5.9 and shall establish 
and maintain records by medical device or by medical device 
batch that enable identification of the quantity produced and 
approved for distribution. These records shall be verified and 
approved. 
7.5.2 
Cleanliness of 
Product 
The organization shall document requirements for 
cleanliness of product or contamination control of product 
in the following cases. Provided, however, that where the 
product is cleaned in accordance with 1) or 2), the 
requirements of 6.4.1 do not apply prior to the cleaning 
process. 
1)  Product that is cleaned by the organization prior to 
sterilization or use; 
2)  Product supplied non-sterile that requires a cleaning process 
prior to sterilization or use; 
3)  Product that cannot be cleaned prior to sterilization or use and 
for which cleanliness is of significant importance for use; 
4)  Product supplied non-sterile for which cleanliness is of 
significant importance for use; 
5)  Removal of process agents used during manufacturing from 
the product. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.3 
Installation 
Activities 
(a) Where applicable, the organization shall document the 
acceptance criteria for installation of the medical device and 
for installation verification. 
(b) Where installation by parties other than the organization or the 
supplier is permitted by the customer, the organization shall 
provide documented requirements for installation of the 
medical device and for installation verification.  
(c) Records of installation of the medical device and of 
installation verification performed by the organization or the 
supplier shall be maintained.  
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.4 Servicing 
Activities 
(a) Where servicing of the medical device is a specified 
requirement, the organization shall document, where 
necessary, servicing procedures, reference materials, and 
reference measurements for performing servicing activities 
and for verifying that the specified requirements are met.  
(b) The organization shall analyze records of servicing activities 
performed by the organization or the supplier for the purpose 
of: 
1)  Determining whether the information should be handled 
as a complaint; 
2)  Providing, where applicable, input to the improvement 
processes. 
(c) Records of servicing activities performed by the organization 
or the supplier shall be maintained.

The organization shall maintain records of the parameters of the 
sterilization process used for each sterilization batch. Sterilization

7.5.6 Validation 
of Processes for 
Production and 
Service 
Provision 
(a) The organization shall validate any processes for production 
and service provision where the resulting output cannot be 
verified by subsequent monitoring or measurement. Validation 
shall include all processes where deficiencies become apparent 
only after the product is used or the service is delivered.  
(b) Validation shall demonstrate the ability of the processes to 
achieve the planned results consistently.  
(c) The organization shall document procedures for process 
validation that include:  
1)  Defined criteria for review and approval of the processes; 
2)  the suitability of equipment and personnel; 
3)  the use of specific methods, procedures, and acceptance 
criteria; 
4)  Statistical techniques, where applicable, including 
justification for sample size; 
5)  Requirements for records; 
6)  Revalidation, including the criteria for revalidation; 
7)  Approval of changes to the process. 
(d) The organization shall document procedures for validation of 
the application of computer software used in production and 
service provision. Such software applications shall be 
validated prior to initial use and, where appropriate, validated 
after changes or software applications have been made. The 
specific approach and activities related to software validation 
and revalidation shall be proportionate to the risks associated 
with the use of the software, including the impact on product 
specifications and product performance.  
(e) Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, 
and any necessary actions resulting from the validation shall 
be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.7 Specific 
Requirements 
for Validation 
of Sterilization 
and Sterile 
Packaging 
Processes 
(a) The organization shall document procedures for validation of 
the sterilization processes and the sterile barrier systems. 
(b) The sterilization processes and the sterile barrier systems shall 
be validated prior to initial use and, where applicable, prior to 
changes to the product or the process. 
(c) Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, 
and any necessary actions resulting from the validation shall 
be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.8 
Identification 
(a) The organization shall document procedures for product 
identification and shall identify the product by suitable means 
throughout production realization. 
(b) The organization shall identify the status of the product with 
respect to monitoring and measurement requirements 
throughout production realization. The organization shall 
maintain identification of product status to ensure that only 
product that has passed the required tests and inspections, or 
that has been released under an approved concession, is 
dispatched, used, or installed during all phases of production,

storage, installation, and servicing. 
(c) Where required by applicable statutory requirements, the 
organization shall document a system for assigning a unique 
device identification (UDI) to the medical device. 
(d) The organization shall document procedures to ensure that 
medical devices returned to the organization are identified and 
distinguished from conforming product. 
7.5.9 
Traceability 
7.5.9.1 General 
Requirements 
The organization shall document procedures for traceability. 
These procedures shall define the scope of traceability and 
the records to be maintained in accordance with applicable 
statutory requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.9.2 Specific 
Requirements 
for Medical 
Devices 
Subject to 
Traceability 
(a) Where components, materials, or working environment 
conditions used could cause the medical device not to meet 
specified safety and performance requirements, records 
required for traceability shall include records of the 
components, materials, and working environment conditions 
used. 
(b) The organization shall require distributors or retailers to 
maintain records of sales of the medical device and to make 
such records available for investigation to ensure product 
traceability.  
(c) The organization shall maintain records of the name and 
address of the consignee for released product.   
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.10 
Customer 
Property 
Where customer property provided for use or incorporation 
into the product is under the manufacturer’s control or is 
being used by the manufacturer, the organization shall 
identify, verify, protect, and safeguard such property. If 
customer property is lost, damaged, or found to be 
unsuitable for use, this shall be reported to the customer and 
records shall be maintained.  
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.11 
Preservation of 
Product 
(a) The organization shall document procedures to preserve 
product conformity to requirements during processing, 
storage, handling, and distribution. 
(b) Preservation shall also apply to components of the medical 
device. 
(c) When exposed to expected conditions and hazards during 
processing, storage, handling, and distribution, the 
organization shall protect the product from alteration, 
contamination, or damage by the following means: 
1)  Designing and constructing appropriate packaging and 
transportation containers; 
2)  Documenting requirements for any special conditions 
needed where packaging alone does not provide 
preservation. 
(d) Where special conditions are necessary, such conditions shall 
be controlled and recorded.  
 
 
 
 
 
7.6 Control of 
Monitoring and 
Measuring 
Equipment 
(a) The organization shall determine the monitoring and 
measurement activities to be performed, and the monitoring 
and measuring equipment required, to demonstrate that the 
product meets specified requirements. 
(b) The organization shall document procedures to ensure that 
 
 
 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
251 
 
GMP Criteria  
Requirements  
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment Result 
Remarks 
A 
B 
C 
D 
monitoring and measurement activities are carried out in a 
manner consistent with the monitoring and measurement 
requirements. 
(c) Where necessary to ensure valid results, measuring equipment 
shall: 
1)  Be calibrated or verified, or both, at specified intervals or 
prior to use, against measurement standards traceable to 
international or national measurement standards; Where 
no such standards exist, the basis used for calibration or 
verification shall be recorded. 
2)  Be adjusted or re-adjusted as necessary. Such adjustment 
or re-adjustment shall be recorded.  
3)  Be identified to enable the calibration status to be 
determined;  
4)  Be safeguarded from adjustments that would invalidate 
the measurement result;  
5)  Be protected from damage and deterioration during 
handling, maintenance, and storage. 
(d) The organization shall calibrate or verify the equipment in 
accordance with documented procedures.  
(e) When equipment is found not to conform to requirements, the 
organization shall assess the validity of previous measurement 
results. The organization shall take appropriate action 
regarding the equipment and any product affected. Records of 
the results of calibration and verification shall be maintained. 
(f)  When computer software is used in monitoring or measuring 
the requirements specified, the organization shall document 
procedures for validation of the application of computer 
software. The software shall be validated prior to initial use 
and, where appropriate, revalidated after changes to the 
software or its application. The specific approach and 
activities related to software validation and revalidation shall 
be proportionate to the risks associated with the use of the 
software, including the impact on product specifications and 
product performance.   
(g) Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, 
and any necessary actions resulting from the validation shall 
be maintained. 
8. 
Measurement, 
Analysis and 
Improvement 
8.1 General 
Requirements 
(a) The organization shall plan and implement the monitoring, 
measurement, analysis, and improvement processes needed: 
1)  To demonstrate conformity of the product; 
2)  To ensure conformity of the quality management system; 
3)  To maintain the effectiveness of the quality management 
system. 
(b) This shall include determination of the methods, including 
statistical techniques, and the extent of their use.  
 
 
 
 
 
8.2 Monitoring 
and 
Measurement 
8.2.1 Feedback 
(a) As one of the measurements of the effectiveness of the quality 
management system, the organization shall collect and 
monitor information relating to whether customer 
requirements have been met.  
(b) The methods for obtaining and using this information shall be 
documented. 
(c) The organization shall document procedures for the feedback 
 
 
 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
252 
 
GMP Criteria  
Requirements  
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment Result 
Remarks 
A 
B 
C 
D 
process. The feedback process shall include provisions for 
gathering data from production as well as post-production 
activities.  
(d) Information gathered in the feedback process shall be used as 
potential input to risk management in order to monitor and 
maintain the product requirements and the production 
realization or improvement processes. 
(e) Where applicable statutory requirements require the 
organization to collect information from post-production 
activities, review of that information shall be part of the 
feedback process. 
8.2.2 Handling 
of Complaints 
(a) The organization shall document procedures for timely 
handling of complaints in accordance with applicable statutory 
requirements. These procedures shall include, at a minimum, 
the following requirements and responsibilities: 
1)  Receiving and recording information; 
2)  Evaluating information to determine whether feedback 
constitutes a complaint; 
3)  Investigating complaints; 
4)  Determining whether the information must be reported to 
the appropriate regulatory authorities;  
5)  Handling complaint-related product; 
6)  Determining the need for correction or corrective action. 
(b) If any complaint is not investigated, the justification for not 
conducting the investigation shall be documented. All results 
of corrections and corrective actions arising from the 
complaint handling process shall be documented. 
(c) Where an investigation determines that activities external to 
the organization caused the complaint, relevant information 
shall be exchanged between the organization and the external 
parties.  
(e) Records of complaint handling shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.2.3 Reporting 
to Regulatory 
Authorities 
(a) Where complaints are subject to adverse event reporting or 
advisory notice reporting in accordance with applicable 
statutory requirements, the organization shall document 
procedures for reporting such complaints to the regulatory 
authorities.  
(b) Records of reports submitted to regulatory authorities shall be 
maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.2.4 Internal 
Audit 
(a) The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned 
intervals to determine whether the quality management 
system: 
1)  Conforms to the planned and documented (established, 
implemented, and maintained) arrangements, the 
requirements of this GMP, the quality management system 
requirements established by the organization, and the 
applicable statutory requirements; 
2)  Is effectively implemented and maintained. 
(b) The organization shall document procedures that define the 
responsibilities and requirements for planning and conducting 
audits, and for recording and reporting audit results. 
(c) The audit program shall be planned, taking into consideration

253 
 
GMP Criteria  
Requirements  
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment Result 
Remarks 
A 
B 
C 
D 
the status and importance of the processes and areas to be 
audited, as well as the results of previous audits. The audit 
criteria, scope, frequency, and methods shall be defined and 
recorded. Auditors shall be selected and audits conducted to 
ensure objectivity and impartiality of the audit process. 
Auditors shall not audit their own work. Records of the audit 
and audit results, including the processes and areas audited 
and the conclusions reached, shall be maintained. 
(d) Management responsible for the areas being audited shall 
ensure that necessary corrections and corrective actions are 
taken without undue delay to eliminate detected 
nonconformities and their causes. Follow-up activities shall 
include the verification of the actions taken and the reporting 
of the results of verification. 
8.2.5 
Monitoring and 
Measurement 
of Processes 
The organization shall apply suitable methods for 
monitoring and, where applicable, measurement of the 
quality management system processes. These methods shall 
demonstrate the ability of the processes to achieve the 
planned results. When the planned results are not achieved, 
appropriate correction and corrective action shall be taken to 
ensure conformity of the product.  
 
 
 
 
 
8.2.6 
Monitoring and 
Measurement 
of Product 
(a) The organization shall monitor and measure the characteristics 
of the product to verify that product requirements have been 
met. This shall be carried out at appropriate stages of the 
production realization process in accordance with the planned 
and documented arrangements and documented procedures. 
(b) Records demonstrating conformity with the acceptance criteria 
shall be maintained. The identity of the person authorizing 
product release shall be recorded. Where applicable, the test 
equipment used for measurement activities shall be identified 
and recorded. 
(c) Product shall not be released, nor shall service be provided, 
until the planned and documented activities have been 
satisfactorily completed. 
(d) For medical devices subject to traceability, the organization 
shall identify and record the identity of personnel performing 
all inspections or tests. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.3 Control of 
Nonconforming 
Product 
8.3.1 General 
(a) The organization shall ensure that nonconforming product is 
identified and controlled to prevent its unintended use or 
delivery. The organization shall document procedures that 
define the controls and related responsibilities and authorities 
for dealing with nonconforming product, including 
identification, documentation, segregation, evaluation, and 
disposition. 
(b) Evaluation of nonconformities shall include investigation into 
any external party responsible for the nonconformity and 
determination of whether notification is required. 
(c) Records of the nonconformity, including the evaluation, 
investigation, the basis for the decisions made, and all actions 
taken in response, shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.3.2 Actions in 
Response to 
Nonconforming 
(a) The organization shall deal with nonconforming product in one 
or more of the following ways:  
1)  Taking action to eliminate the detected nonconformity;

Detected Prior

2)  Taking action to preclude its original intended use or 
application; 
3)  Authorizing its use, release, or acceptance under 
concession. 
(b) The organization shall ensure that concessions are granted only 
when justified, approved, and compliant with applicable 
statutory requirements. Records shall be maintained to identify 
acceptance under concession and the personnel authorizing the 
concession. 
8.3.3 Actions in 
Response to 
Nonconforming 
Product 
Detected After 
Delivery 
(a) When nonconforming product is detected after delivery or use, 
the organization shall take appropriate action regarding the 
effects or potential effects of the nonconformity. Records of 
the actions taken shall be maintained. 
(b) The organization shall document procedures for issuing 
advisory notices in accordance with applicable statutory 
requirements. These procedures shall be capable of being 
implemented at any time. Records of the actions related to 
advisory notices shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.3.4 Rework 
(a) The organization shall perform rework in accordance with 
documented procedures that take into account any potential 
adverse effects on the product. These procedures shall be 
subject to the same review and approval as the original 
procedures.  
(b) After completion of the rework, the product shall be verified to 
ensure that it meets the applicable acceptance criteria and 
statutory requirements.  
(c) Records of the rework shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.4 Analysis of 
Data 
(a) The organization shall document procedures to determine, 
collect, and analyze appropriate data to demonstrate the 
suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the quality 
management system. These procedures shall include the 
determination of appropriate methods, including statistical 
techniques and the extent of their application. 
(b) Analysis of data shall include data generated from the results 
of monitoring and measurement and from other relevant 
sources, and shall include, at a minimum, the following inputs: 
1)  Feedback;  
2)  Conformity to product requirements;  
3)  Process and product characteristics and trends, including 
opportunities for improvement; 
4)  Suppliers; 
5)  Audits; 
6)  Service reports, where applicable. 
(c) Where analysis of data shows that the quality management 
system is not suitable, adequate, or effective, the organization 
shall use this analysis as input for improvement as required in 
8.5.  
(d) Records of the results of data analysis shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.5 
Improvement 
8.5.1 General 
The organization shall identify and implement any changes 
necessary to ensure and maintain the ongoing suitability, 
adequacy, and effectiveness of the quality management 
system, as well as the safety and performance of medical

devices, through the use of the quality policy, quality

analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and management

8.5.2 
Corrective 
Action 
(a) The organization shall take action to eliminate the causes of 
nonconformities in order to prevent their recurrence. 
(b) Corrective actions required shall be taken without undue delay. 
Corrective actions shall be proportionate to the effects of the 
nonconformities encountered. 
(c) Documented procedures shall define requirements for: 
1)  Reviewing nonconformities (including customer 
complaints); 
2)  Determining the causes of nonconformities; 
3)  Evaluating the need for action to ensure that 
nonconformities do not recur; 
4)  Planning and documenting the required actions and 
implementing them, including document changes where 
applicable;  
5)  Verifying that corrective actions do not adversely affect 
the safety and performance of the medical device or 
compliance with applicable statutory requirements; 
6)  Reviewing the effectiveness of the corrective actions 
taken. 
(d) Records of all investigation results and actions taken shall be 
maintained.  
 
 
 
 
 
8.5.3 
Preventive 
Action 
(a) The organization shall determine preventive actions to 
eliminate the causes of potential nonconformities in order to 
prevent their occurrence. Preventive actions shall be 
proportionate to the potential impacts of such issues.  
(b) Documented procedures shall define requirements for:  
1)  Determining potential nonconformities and their causes; 
2)  Evaluating the need for action to prevent the occurrence of 
nonconformities; 
3)  Planning and documenting the required actions and 
determining and implementing such actions, including 
document changes where applicable; 
4)  Verifying that preventive actions do not adversely affect 
the safety and performance of the medical device or 
compliance with applicable statutory requirements; 
5)  Reviewing the effectiveness of preventive actions taken, 
where applicable. 
(c) Records of the results of all investigations and actions taken 
shall be maintained.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
256 
 
1.  Assessment Sheet 
(a)  “A (Conforming)” means that the requirements prescribed in the Good Manufacturing 
Practice (GMP) are recognized as being met. 
(b)  “B (Additional action required)” means that the requirements prescribed in the Good 
Manufacturing Practice (GMP) are not being fully met, or that although the 
requirements are being met, the evidence of conformance, feasibility of implementation, 
or adequacy of documentation is insufficient, thereby requiring improvement or 
supplementary actions. 
(c)  “C (Nonconforming)” means that no action has been taken in response to “Additional 
action required,” or that a violation of statutes related to medical devices has occurred. 
(d)  “D (Not applicable)” means that the requirement prescribed in the Good Manufacturing 
Practice (GMP) does not apply. 
 
2.  Determination Criteria 
(a)  Conforming 
1)  Where all items under each review criterion are rated “A (Conforming).” 
2)  Where all other items under each review criterion are rated “A (Conforming),” and 
certain sections—specifically Sections 4.1 through 6.3 (excluding Section 4.2.3) 
and Section 8.2.4—are rated “B (Additional action required).” Provided, however, 
that this shall not apply where the same item was rated “B (Additional action 
required)” or “C (Nonconforming)” in the previous assessment. 
(b)  Additional action required 
 
Where all other items under each assessment criterion are rated “A (Conforming),” and 
some items are rated “B (Additional action required)” (provided, however, that this does 
not apply to cases under item (a) 2)). 
(c)  Nonconforming 
1)  Where the required actions have not been submitted or have not been completed. 
2)  Where one or more items are rated “C (Nonconforming)” in the evaluation sheet.

[Annex 4] 
 
Entities for Conformity Recognition Assessments 
(Related to Article 6 and 8) 
 
1.  Conformity recognition assessments shall, pursuant to Article 4, be classified into initial 
assessments, additional assessments, assessments for change, and periodic assessments. 
 
2.  ‘Single-agency (assessment)’ means an assessment conducted solely by the head of audit 
organization, and “joint (assessment)” means a conformity recognition assessment conducted 
jointly by the Commissioner of Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety (hereinafter referred 
to as the “Commissioner of Regional Office”) and the head of audit organization. 
   
3.  The head of the audit organization shall conduct the conformity recognition assessments as a 
“single-agency assessment” under subparagraph 1 for manufacturing sites of Class I, Class II, 
and Class III domestically manufactured or imported medical devices, as well as 
manufacturing sites for medical devices for export. 
   
4.  The Commissioner of Regional Office and the head of the audit organization may conduct the 
conformity recognition assessments as a “joint assessment” under subparagraph 1 for 
manufacturing sites of Class IV domestically manufactured or imported medical devices. 
Provided, however, that assessments for change and periodic assessments (limited to document 
review) for such Class IV manufacturing sites, as well as combined assessments under 
subparagraph 72 of Annex 1, shall be conducted as a single-agency assessment by the audit 
organization. 
 
5.  Notwithstanding subparagraphs 3 and 4, where a manufacturing site for domestically 
manufactured or imported medical devices is deemed to be a Manufacturing Site of Potential 
Risks, the Commissioner of Regional Office and the head of the audit organization may 
conduct a joint on-site inspection as part of the conformity recognition assessments under 
subparagraph 1.

(a)  The mark for conformity recognition assessment shall be applied based on the size and 
color specified in item (a), and may be used in various sizes (with the same proportions) 
and colors suitable for the characteristics of the product and its packaging materials; 
provided that the design of the mark shall not be altered. 
(b)  The method of the conformity recognition assessment marking in item (a) may follow the 
labeling requirements under Articles 20 through 22 of the Medical Device Act, and the 
mark may be affixed to one or more of the following: the container, outer packaging, 
external package, or package insert.

[Annex 7] 
 
Evaluation Criteria for Medical Device Audit Organizations 
(Related to Article 13) 
 
1.  Scope of Application  
 
Organizations seeking new designation as a medical device audit organization 
 
2.  Composition of the Evaluation Team 
 
The evaluation team shall consist of at least two officials of the Ministry of Food and Drug 
Safety, and external experts shall account for a majority of the committee members. 
 
3.  Evaluation Items 
(a)  Compliance with the standards for management and operation for medical device Audit 
Organizations (90%) 
(b)  Capability to perform conformity recognition assessments activities (10%) 
 
4.  Designation Criteria 
 
An absolute evaluation shall be conducted based on a total score of 100 points, and 
organization scoring 80 points or higher shall be designated.  
 
5.  Evaluation Procedure 
 
The evaluation team shall review and verify the evaluation report, supporting evidence, and 
other relevant materials of the audit organization, and shall assign scores for each evaluation 
item. 
 
6.  Designation Evaluation Report for Audit Organizations 
 
Audit Organization 
Requirements 
(Points) 
Evaluation Items

1.  Audit Organization 
Requirements 
(a) General 
Requirements  
(4 points) 
(1) The policies, procedures, and operation of the audit 
organization in performing its duties shall be fair. 
 
(2) The audit organization shall be accessible to all applicants and 
shall not impose any unfair monetary or other conditions.

(3) The audit organization shall perform the duties prescribed by

(4) The criteria for conformity recognition with respect to an

(b) Organizational 
Structure  
(6 points) 
The organizational structure of the audit organization shall be 
capable of ensuring the reliability of assessment activities and 
shall meet the following requirements: 
(1) In performing assessment activities, the audit organization 
shall ensure independence and fairness and shall be 
accountable for its decisions. 
 
(2) The head of the audit organization shall designate an operating 
manager or a committee with overall responsibility for the 
following duties: 
(a) Supervision of the implementation of assessment activities 
prescribed under this GMP 
(b) Establishment and implementation of the operational 
policies for the audit organization 
(3) The audit organization shall have a documented organizational 
structure that ensures the fairness of its operations. Such 
organizational structure shall be designed to allow the 
participation of interested parties in establishing policies and 
principles related to the performance of assessment activities.  
(4) The audit organization shall establish internal procedures to 
fulfill its responsibilities and obligations in relation to its 
operation and the performance of assessment activities. Such 
procedures shall clearly define policies and procedures to 
ensure the continuity of assessment activities in cases where 
continued performance becomes difficult, including 
suspension of the organization’s operations, and the 
organization shall have in place appropriate means or 
arrangements to cover liabilities, such as compensation 
responsibilities, arising from its operations and activities.  
(5) The audit organization shall secure the financial resources and 
other resources necessary for stable operation and shall 
maintain an independent organization composed of personnel 
with the professional knowledge and experience required to 
perform assessment activities.  
(6) Personnel of the organization performing assessment activities

shall not engage in other duties that may impair the 
professionalism, fairness, or independence of assessments.  
(7) To ensure the reliability of operational capability related to

(8) The activities of the audit organization shall be conducted in a

(d) Offering or providing information on benefits such as cost

are received from a specific organization 
 
(9) It shall be ensured that the operating manager and all personnel 
of the audit organization are free from any commercial, 
financial, or other pressures that may influence, or have the 
potential to influence, the assessment process or assessment 
results.  
(c) Quality 
Management 
System  
(10 points) 
(1) The head of the audit organization shall establish and 
document a quality policy that includes quality objectives and 
a commitment to implementation, and shall maintain and 
manage the policy so that it is understood and implemented at 
all levels of the organization.  
 
(2) The head of the audit organization shall establish and 
document a quality management system appropriate to the 
types and volume of tasks to be performed in accordance with 
this GMP, and shall ensure that such system is available for use 
by the personnel of the audit organization. The head of the 
audit organization shall demonstrate that the documented 
quality manual, procedures, and guidelines are being 
effectively implemented, and shall designate a quality manager 
vested with authority over the following matters:  
(a) Establishment, implementation, and maintenance of the quality 
management system in accordance with this GMP 
(b) Reporting operational performance to the head of the audit

manufacturing technologies, the scope of medical devices 
manufactured, and post-market surveillance.

the identified findings.

under the Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical Devices

Supplementation shall specify the items to be supplemented by 
the applicant.

[Annex 8] 
 
Standards for Management and Operation for  
Medical Device Audit Organizations 
(Related to Article 14) 
 
1.  Requirements for Audit Organizations 
(a)  General Requirements 
1)  The policies, procedures, and operation of the audit organization in performing its 
duties shall be fair.  
2)  The audit organization shall be accessible to all applicants for conformity 
recognition assessments (hereinafter referred to as the “applicants”) and shall not 
impose any unjust monetary or other conditions.  
3)  The audit organization shall perform the duties prescribed by the Minister of Food 
and Drug Safety. 
4)  Conformity recognition assessments with respect to an applicants’ compliance with 
Good Manufacturing Practice shall be conducted in accordance with the Good 
Manufacturing Practice for Medical Devices. Where a separate interpretation of this 
GMP is required, approval shall be obtained from the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety. 
 
(b)  Organizational Structure 
 
The organizational structure of the audit organization shall be capable of ensuring the 
reliability of conformity recognition assessments activities and shall meet the following 
requirements: 
1)  In performing duties such as conformity recognition assessments, the audit 
organization shall ensure independence and fairness and shall be accountable for its 
decisions. 
2)  The head of the audit organization shall designate an operating manager or a 
committee with overall responsibility for the following duties: 
(a)  Supervision of the implementation of assessment activities in accordance with 
this GMP 
(b)  Establishment and implementation of the operational policies for the audit 
organization 
3)  The audit organization shall have a documented organizational structure that 
ensures the fairness of its operations. Such organizational structure shall be 
designed to allow the participation of interested parties in establishing policies and 
principles related to the performance of assessment activities. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
276 
 
4)  The audit organization shall establish internal procedures to fulfill its 
responsibilities and obligations in relation to its operation and the performance of 
assessment activities. Such procedures shall clearly define policies and procedures 
to ensure the continuity of assessment activities in cases where continued 
performance becomes difficult, including suspension of the organization’s 
operations, and the organization shall have in place appropriate means or 
arrangements to cover liabilities, such as compensation responsibilities, arising 
from its operations and activities. 
5)  The audit organization shall secure the financial resources and other resources 
necessary for stable operation, and shall maintain an independent organization 
composed of personnel with the professional knowledge and experience required to 
perform assessment activities. 
6)  Personnel of the organization performing assessment activities shall not engage in 
other duties that may impair the professionalism, fairness, or independence of 
assessments. 
7)  To ensure the reliability of operational capability related to assessment activities, 
the audit organization shall establish a quality management system as referred to in 
item (c). 
8)  The activities of the audit organization shall be conducted in a manner that ensures 
they do not affect the confidentiality, objectivity, or fairness of assessments, and the 
organization shall not directly or indirectly propose or promote any of the following 
to applicants: 
(a)  Provision of consultancy services for obtaining or maintaining conformity 
recognition 
(b)  Recommendation or referral to receive consultancy services from a specific 
organization 
(c)  Consultancy services related to the design, implementation, or maintenance of 
a quality management system 
(d)  Offering or providing information on benefits such as cost reductions or time 
savings in cases where consultancy services are received from a specific 
organization 
9)  It shall be ensured that the operating manager and all personnel of the audit 
organization are free from any commercial, financial, or other pressures that may 
influence, or have the potential to influence, the assessment process or assessment 
results. 
 
(c)  Quality Management System 
1)  The head of the audit organization shall establish and document a quality policy 
that includes quality objectives and a commitment to implementation, and shall 
maintain and manage the policy so that it is understood and implemented at all 
levels of the organization. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
277 
 
2)  The head of the audit organization shall establish and document a quality 
management system appropriate to the types and volume of tasks to be performed 
in accordance with this GMP, and shall ensure that such system is available for use 
by the personnel of the audit organization. The head of the audit organization shall 
demonstrate that the documented quality manual, procedures, and guidelines are 
being effectively implemented, and shall designate a quality manager vested with 
authority over the following matters: 
(a)  Establishment, implementation, and maintenance of the quality management 
system in accordance with this GMP 
(b)  Reporting operational performance to the head of the audit organization for 
the review and improvement of the quality management system 
3)  The quality management system shall be documented in the form of a quality 
manual, relevant procedures, guidelines, and other related documents, and the 
quality manual shall include the following matters: 
(a)  The quality policy 
(b)  Matters concerning the statutory status of the audit organization 
(c)  Qualifications, experience, and authority of the operating manager and 
personnel belonging to the audit organization that may affect assessment 
activities 
(d)  An organizational chart showing the lines of authority, responsibility, and 
division of duties centered on the head of the audit organization (The 
organizational chart shall indicate the relationship between the person 
responsible for assessments and the person responsible for conformity 
recognition decisions) 
(e)  Matters concerning the organization of the audit organization (in this case, 
details regarding the operating manager or committee in accordance with item 
(b) (2), including its composition, allocation of duties, and rules of operation, 
shall be included.) 
(f)  Policies and procedures for conducting internal audits and quality 
management system reviews 
(g)  Operational procedures, including control of documents 
(h)  Responsibilities and authority of personnel in charge of operational and 
functional tasks related to assessment activities 
(i)  Education and training plans for personnel of the audit organization, including 
quality auditors 
(j)  Procedures for handling nonconformities identified after assessments and for 
ensuring the validity of corrective actions taken 
(k)  Other policies and procedures necessary for the performance of assessment 
activities, including the issuance of conformity recognition certificates, 
conformity assessment of applicants’ compliance with Good Manufacturing 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
278 
 
Practice, and post-assessment follow-up management (including follow-up 
actions after guidance and inspections pursuant to Article 16) 
(l)  Policies and procedures for handling appeals, complaints, and disputes 
 
(d)  Conditions for Approval of Conformity Recognition 
1)  The head of the audit organization shall establish the conditions for approval of 
conformity recognition, etc., and shall require applicants to notify the audit 
organization in cases where the applicant changes its quality management system to 
an extent that may affect conformity.  
2)  The audit organization shall establish procedures for performing conformity 
recognition assessments. 
 
(e)  Internal Audit and Review of the Quality Management System 
1)  The head of the audit organization shall conduct internal audits at least once a year, 
in a systematic manner, covering all procedures related to assessment activities, in 
order to verify the implementation and validity of the quality management system, 
and shall ensure the following: 
(a)  Notification and reporting of audit results to the personnel of the audited 
organization and to the head of the audit organization 
(b)  Implementation of corrective actions in a timely manner 
(c)  Recording and maintenance of audit and corrective action results 
2)  The head of the audit organization shall conduct a review of the quality 
management system at least once a year in order to satisfy the requirements of this 
GMP, the quality policy, and quality objectives, and to continuously maintain 
conformity and validity, and shall retain records thereof. 
 
(f)  Documentation 
1)  The head of the audit organization shall prepare and manage documents covering

(a)  The basis for performing assessment activities; 
(b)  Criteria and procedures for approval of conformity recognition; 
(c)  Guidelines and procedures, including assessment guidelines; 
(d)  Matters related to assessment fees; 
(e)  Procedures for handling appeals, complaints, and disputes; 
(f)  A list of entities that have been granted conformity recognition. 
2)  The head of the audit organization shall establish procedures for controlling all 
documents and related materials pertaining to assessment activities, and shall

maintain a document list that enables identification of the current version and

issuance by a person vested with delegated authority. 
 
(g)  Records 
1)  The head of the audit organization shall retain documents related to assessment 
activities for five years, and shall establish policies and procedures for their proper 
retention. 
2)  Documents related to assessment activities shall be maintained in a manner that 
ensures traceability, and shall be securely stored with appropriate security measures 
in place. 
 
(h)  Confidentiality 
 
The head of the audit organization shall establish documented procedures to ensure the 
confidentiality of information concerning applicants collected in the course of performing 
duties, and shall not disclose such information to any third party without the applicant’s 
written consent, except where specifically required under this GMP. 
 
2.  Composition of Personnel and Assessment Teams of the Audit Organization 
(a)  General Requirements 
1)  Personnel of the organization performing assessment activities shall have the 
competence required for their respective duties, and the organization shall secure at 
least one senior quality auditor and two or more quality auditors. 
2)  The organization shall maintain and manage up-to-date records of the 
qualifications, education and training, and experience of personnel performing 
assessment activities, and shall maintain guidelines that clearly describe each 
individual’s duties and responsibilities. 
 
(b)  Qualification and Criteria for Qualification Maintenance for Quality Auditors, Senior 
Quality Auditors, and Technical Experts 
1)  A quality auditor shall be a person who has obtained a bachelor’s degree or higher 
by majoring in a field of natural sciences, engineering, or medicine as prescribed in 
Article 2 (9) of the Regulation on the Establishment and Operation of Universities, 
at a school specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 of the Higher Education Act 
(excluding junior colleges), and shall meet one of the following requirements:  
(a)  A certified auditor for quality management system 
(b)  A person who has obtained the qualification of assistant quality management 
system auditor and has engaged for at least one year in the field of medical 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
280 
 
device quality management (including GMP assessments, testing and 
inspection, and technical documentation review) 
(c)  A certified auditor in the medical device field pursuant to Article 15 of the 
Enforcement Rule of the Industrial Standardization Act 
(d)  A person who has performed related work in medical device manufacturing 
and quality management for at least two years and has completed the quality 
auditor training course for the Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical 
Device designated by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
2)  A senior quality auditor shall be a person who meets the qualifications under 1) and 
has at least six years of experience in conducting conformity recognition 
assessments under the Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical Device at a 
regulatory authority or an organization delegated by a regulatory authority. 
3)  In order to maintain the qualifications of a senior quality auditor and a quality 
auditor, one of the following requirements shall be satisfied: 
(a)  Maintenance of the qualification as a certified quality management system 
auditor and completion of at least eight hours per year of a quality auditor 
qualification maintenance training course designated by the Minister of Food 
and Drug Safety 
(b)  Conducting five or more assessments per year (with at least 12 assessment 
days) of conformity recognition assessments under the Good Manufacturing 
Practice for Medical Device (on-site assessments), and completion of at least 
24 hours of technical development activities (including at least eight hours per 
year of a quality auditor qualification maintenance training course designated 
by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, and including education related to 
the Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical Device, performance of 
research, acquisition of qualifications, etc.) 
4)  A technical expert is not required to meet the qualification requirements for a 
quality auditor, but shall meet one of the following requirements: 
(a) A person who has directly conducted research, planning, or implementation of 
relevant work in the medical device field for at least ten years at a research 
institute, public institution, organization, or company 
(b)  A person who holds a professional engineer license or a doctoral degree in the 
medical device field 
 
(c)  Composition of Assessment Teams 
1)  Assessment teams shall be organized in accordance with the provisions determined 
by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. Provided, however, that, where necessary, 
technical experts related to the medical devices subject to assessment may be 
included in the assessment team, and such technical experts may provide advice to 
the assessment team under the supervision of quality auditors. 
2)  Assessment teams shall have knowledge of the applicable relevant statutes, 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
281 
 
assessment criteria, and requirements, and shall possess sufficient experience and 
competence in medical device quality management as specified below, and shall be 
able to communicate effectively both in writing and orally. 
(a)  Evaluation of applicants’ compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice and 
determination of the effectiveness of their implementation 
(b)  Understanding of specific standards and criteria applied to the evaluation of 
applicants’ compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice 
(c)  Assessment of the intended use and risks related to the medical devices 
subject to assessment 
(d)  Evaluation of design, manufacturing processes, and related technologies 
 
(d)  Records on Quality Auditors and Technical Experts 
1)  The head of the audit organization shall maintain and manage up-to-date records on 
quality auditors and technical experts with respect to the following matters: 
(a)  Name and address 
(b)  Position and title 
(c)  Evidence of educational background and professional technical qualifications 
(d)  Scope of assessment activities and grounds for assignment, practical 
experience, and education and training 
(e)  Date of last qualification renewal 
(f)  A statement that consultancy services will not be provided to applicants 
(2)  The head of the audit organization shall maintain and manage records that enable 
confirmation that quality auditors and technical experts satisfy the requirements of 
this GMP. 
 
3.  Assessment Procedures 
 
Where matters are not specified under this GMP, the audit organization shall conduct 
assessment activities in accordance with the detailed operating rules approved by the Minister 
of Food and Drug Safety. 
(a)  Assessment Preparation 
1)  The audit organization shall evaluate the Application for Conformity Recognition 
of Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical Device submitted by the applicant, 
together with the required supporting documents, and shall designate the quality 
auditors who will conduct the assessment and, where necessary, technical experts 
related to the medical devices subject to assessment.  
2)  In selecting specific quality auditors and technical experts, the audit organization 
shall provide an advance notice period taking into account the possibility of 
objections by the applicant, and shall notify the applicant of the list of quality 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
282 
 
auditors and technical experts who will conduct the assessment. 
3)  The audit organization shall consult with the applicant regarding the assessment 
plan and schedule. 
4)  For the preparation of on-site assessments, the assessment team shall review the 
required documents and relevant regulations and shall maintain appropriate 
confidentiality in handling such materials. 
5)  The audit organization shall provide the assessment team with all documents and 
information received from the applicant. 
 
(b)  Assessment 
1)  Based on all requirements related to the Good Manufacturing Practice, the 
assessment team shall review documents and records extracted from all stages of 
the applicant’s quality management system. Such extracted documents and records 
shall reflect information relevant to risks associated with the intended use of the 
medical device, the complexity of manufacturing technologies, the scope of 
medical devices manufactured, and post-market surveillance. 
2)  The assessment team shall collect and verify objective evidence through interviews, 
document reviews, and observation of activities and conditions in relevant areas. 
3)  Findings shall be recorded as follows: 
(a)  In a clear and concise manner; 
(b)  Supported by objective evidence; 
(c)  Indicating the specific requirements that have not been met. 
4)  The assessment team (including technical experts) shall not provide consultancy to 
the applicant during the assessment process.  
 
(c)  Notification of Assessment Results 
1)  Prior to leaving the assessment site, the assessment team shall hold a meeting with 
the applicant’s management and relevant responsible personnel. At the meeting, the 
assessment team shall notify the applicant of the results of the evaluation of the 
applicant’s compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice, provide the applicant 
with an opportunity to ask questions regarding the findings identified by the 
assessment team and the grounds therefor, and obtain management’s agreement on 
the identified findings. 
2)  The assessment team shall submit a results report on the conformity assessment of 
the applicant’s compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice to the audit 
organization. 
3)  Based on the results report, the audit organization shall issue to the applicant either 
a Conformity Recognition Certificate under the Good Manufacturing Practice for 
Medical Devices or a Request for Supplementation, and the Request for 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
283 
 
Supplementation shall specify the items to be supplemented by the applicant. 
 
4.  Procedures for Handling Appeals, Complaints, and Disputes 
 
The head of the audit organization shall establish procedures for handling appeals, complaints, 
and disputes raised by applicants or other relevant parties, and shall record the following 
matters: 
1)  All appeals, complaints, and disputes related to assessment activities and the actions 
taken in response thereto 
2)  Appropriate corrective and preventive actions 
3)  Documentation of corrective actions taken and evaluation of their validity
