Criteria for Designation of Training Organizations  
for Quality Manager 
(Related to Article 17) 
 
1.  Training Facilities and Equipment 
(a)  A training organization shall either own training facilities or continuously lease such 
facilities for the duration of the training period. 
(b)  Training facilities shall include lecture rooms, rest areas, restrooms (with separate 
facilities for men and women), parking areas, and other necessary facilities.  
(c)  There shall be at least one lecture room with a floor area of 150 m² or more (where the 
expected number of trainees exceeds 100, an additional 1.5 m² per excess trainee shall be 
secured). 
(d)  Lecture rooms shall be equipped with a sufficient number of chairs and desks to 
accommodate trainees, and shall be fitted with screens, audio systems, and other facilities 
enabling audiovisual instruction, as well as appropriate ventilation and lighting facilities. 
(e)  The training institution shall be equipped with equipment necessary for training, such as 
portable computers and beam projectors. 
 
2.  Training Personnel and Curriculum 
(a)  Training Administrator 
1)  A training organization shall designate at least one training administrator to 
supervise overall operations. 
(b)  Training instructors shall satisfy one of the following requirements: 
1)  A person who has graduated from a junior college or higher educational institution 
under the Higher Education Act with a major related to the training curriculum 
(including graduates of relevant majors who possess academic qualifications 
equivalent to or higher than those prescribed under other statutes) and has at least 
five years of practical experience in a relevant field 
2)  A person who has at least 50 hours of teaching experience over the past five years 
in education or training related to the Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical 
Device, conducted by a government authority or a government-designated 
institution 
3)  Any other person recognized by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety as having 
qualifications equivalent to those of a training instructor 
(c)  The curriculum. 
1)  A training organization shall establish and operate training programs to enable 
quality managers to develop fundamental competencies. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Medical Devices 
 
 
 
285 
 
2)  A training organization shall establish and conduct training programs tailored to the 
characteristics of each training demand area of quality managers. 
 
3.  Training Implementation Rules  
A training organization shall establish and operate training implementation rules that include 
the following matters in order to ensure efficient implementation of training: 
(a)  Training objectives; 
(b)  Training subjects and methods for the preparation of training materials; 
(c)  Matters related to the conduct of training; 
(d)  Matters related to instructors and tuition fees; 
(e)  Matters related to the curriculum; 
(f)  Measures concerning class cancellations; 
(g)  Various forms related to training, including the register for issuance of certificates of 
completion 
(h)  Other matters necessary for the implementation of training

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
299 
 
Standards of Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for 
In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
[Enforced on August 12, 2025] 
[Ministry of Food and Drug Safety Notice No. 2025-51; August 12, 2025; Partially Amended] 
Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (Innovative and Diagnostic Medical Devices Policy Division) 
 
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this GMP is to prescribe the detailed requirements to be 
observed when manufacturing or importing in vitro diagnostic medical devices (including in vitro 
diagnostic medical devices for clinical performance studies) pursuant to Article 4, Article 5 (5), 
Article 7 (2), Article 10 (1), and Article 11 (4) of the Act on In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices, 
Article 6 (1) 1, Article 10 (1), Article 11, Article 13 (1) 2, Article 26 (1) 2, and Article 27 of the 
Enforcement Rule of the same Act, Article 13 (1), Article 15 (4) and (6), Article 28, and Article 45 
of the Medical Device Act, Article 27 (1) 10 and 11, Article 33 (1) 15, Article 48, Annex 2, and 
Annex 4 of the Enforcement Rule of the Medical Device Act, Article 24 (9) of the Act on the 
Promotion of the Medical Device Industry and Support for Innovative Medical Devices, and Article 
15 of the Regulations on the Support and Management of Innovative Medical Devices. 
 
Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this GMP shall have the meanings defined in Annex 1. 
 
Article 3 (Scope) (1) The scope of this GMP shall be as follows: 
1.  A person who intends to obtain approval or certification for manufacturing or import of in 
vitro diagnostic medical devices, or to submit a notification for such manufacturing or 
import; 
2.  A person who intends to manufacture or import in vitro diagnostic medical devices for 
clinical performance studies; 
3.  A holder of a manufacturing business license (“manufacturer”) or a holder of an import 
business license (hereinafter referred to as the “importer”) who applies for conformity 
recognition and periodic assessment (hereinafter referred to as the “conformity 
recognition assessment”). 
(2)  Notwithstanding subparagraphs 1 through 3 of paragraph (1), a person who intends to 
manufacture in vitro diagnostic medical devices for export (hereinafter referred to as the “in 
vitro diagnostic medical devices for export”) or a person who intends to manufacture or import 
Class I in vitro diagnostic medical devices shall comply with this GMP, but may be exempted 
from the conformity recognition assessment. 
 
Article 4 (Types of Conformity Recognition Assessment) (1) Conformity recognition under this 
GMP shall be conducted by classifying it as follows: 
1.  The initial assessment that a manufacturing site must undergo to be recognized as 
conforming to this GMP (hereinafter referred to as the “initial assessment”); 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
300 
 
2.  The assessment newly required when a manufacturing site adds in vitro diagnostic 
medical devices of another product group pursuant to Annex 3 (hereinafter referred to as 
the “additional assessment”); 
3.  The assessment that must be newly conducted to obtain conformity recognition due to a 
change in the location of a manufacturing site (hereinafter referred to as the “assessment 
for change”); provided, however, that changes to storage facilities or test laboratories that 
have little relevance to product quality, or changes to the location of in vitro diagnostic 
software manufacturing sites, are excluded. 
(2)  Each manufacturing site shall undergo one periodic assessment every three years for each 
product group listed in Annex 3. 
(3)  Notwithstanding Article 3 (2) and Article 4 (2), a manufacturing site may be exempted from 
periodic assessments when it has obtained conformity recognition for the following in vitro 
diagnostic medical devices: 
1.  In vitro diagnostic medical devices for export; 
2.  Class I in vitro diagnostic medical devices; 
3.  In vitro diagnostic medical devices for clinical performance studies. 
 
Article 5 (Criteria for Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) The criteria for conformity 
recognition assessments shall be as specified in Annex 2. 
(2)  Notwithstanding paragraph (1), only part of Annex 2 may be applied in the following cases of 
each subparagraph: 
1.  For a person who intends to manufacture or import in vitro diagnostic medical devices for 
clinical performance studies, Sections 7.1, 7.3, 7.4.3, 7.5, 7.6, 8.2.6, and 8.3 shall be 
applied; 
2.  For an assessment for change under Article 4 (1) 3, Sections 4.1, 4.2, 6.1, 6.3, 6.4, 7.5, 
7.6, 8.2.2, 8.2.3, 8.2.6, 8.3, and 8.5 shall be applied; 
3.  Notwithstanding Article 3 (2), where conformity recognition assessments under this GMP 
are sought for Class I in vitro diagnostic medical devices, Sections 4.1, 4.2, 5.5, 6.4, 7.1, 
7.4, 7.5, 7.6, 8.2.1, 8.2.2, 8.2.3, 8.2.6, 8.3, and 8.5 shall be applied. 
 
Article 6 (Methods of Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) Conformity recognition 
assessments shall be conducted jointly by the Commissioner of the Regional Office of Food and 
Drug Safety (hereinafter referred to as the “Commissioner of Regional Office”) and the head of the 
audit organization through document review and on-site inspection for each product group of the 
manufacturing site. Where the manufacturing process is carried out under an outsourcing 
arrangement between the legal manufacturer and the manufacturer (hereinafter referred to as the 
“legal manufacturer-manufacturer”), document review and on-site inspection may also be 
conducted separately for each of them. In such cases, on-site inspections shall not be limited to the 
core products under Article 7 (2). 
(2)  Notwithstanding paragraph (1), only document review shall be conducted in the following 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
301 
 
subparagraphs: 
1.  Where an additional assessment is conducted under Article 4 (1) 2; 
2.  Where an assessment for change is conducted based on the submission of data under 
Article 7 (1) 2 (b) for a manufacturing site whose location has been changed under Article 
4 (1) 3; 
3.  Where another manufacturer or importer has undergone document review and on-site 
inspection for the relevant manufacturing site under this GMP and holds a valid 
conformity recognition certificate; 
4.  Where a person has two or more manufacturing sites subject to periodic assessments 
under Article 4 (2), remaining manufacturing sites other than those selected for on-site 
inspection; 
5.  Where a medical device manufacturer or importer under the Medical Device Act has 
undergone document review and on-site inspection for the manufacturing site under the 
Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical Devices and holds a valid conformity 
recognition certificate; 
6.  Where a manufacturer holds a quality management system conformity recognition 
certificate (hereinafter referred to as the “MDSAP conformity recognition certificate”) 
issued through an on-site inspection by an audit organization pursuant to the Medical 
Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP) under subparagraph 68 of Annex 1; 
7.  Where periodic assessments are conducted for Excellent Manufacturing Sites under 
subparagraph 69 of Annex 1. 
(3)  Notwithstanding paragraph (2), on-site inspection shall be conducted in any of the following cases: 
1.  Where a manufacturing site is deemed to present potential risks; 
2.  Where a manufacturer or importer is unable to submit the data required under Article 7 
(1) 2 for reasons such as trade secrets, and requests an on-site inspection; 
3.  Where a manufacturer holds a MDSAP conformity recognition certificate, in any of the 
following cases: 
(a)  A manufacturing sites subject to periodic assessments under Article 4 (2); 
(b)  A manufacturing site that the Minister of Food and Drug Safety recognizes as likely 
to affect public health, including cases where significant nonconformities are 
identified in conformity recognition assessments under the Medical Device Single 
Audit Program (MDSAP); 
(c)  A manufacturing site that produces in vitro diagnostic medical devices containing 
human-derived components or using human-derived tissues. 
(4)  Notwithstanding Article 4, a new initial assessment shall be required in any of the following cases: 
1.  Where the expiration date of the conformity recognition certificate held by a 
manufacturing site for export, Class I devices, or in vitro diagnostic medical devices for 
clinical performance studies has expired, and reapplication for conformity recognition is 
made; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
302 
 
2.  Where a manufacturing site holding conformity recognition for in vitro diagnostic 
medical devices for export intends to manufacture products for domestic sale; 
3.  Where the legal manufacturer in a legal manufacturer-manufacturer relationship that has 
undergone conformity recognition assessments is changed or removed; 
4.  Where the location of a manufacturing site that has obtained conformity recognition for in 
vitro diagnostic medical devices for clinical performance studies pursuant to Article 5 (2) 
1 is changed, or where in vitro diagnostic medical devices for clinical performance studies 
belonging to a different product group are added, or where such devices are intended to be 
manufactured or imported for the purpose of sale; 
5.  Where a manufacturing site that has obtained conformity recognition for Class I in vitro 
diagnostic medical devices pursuant to Article 5 (2) 3 intends to manufacture or import 
Class II, Class III, or Class IV in vitro diagnostic medical devices. 
(5)  The entities and methods for conducting conformity recognition assessments under paragraphs 
(1) through (4) shall be as provided in Annex 4. 
(6)  Where an on-site inspection cannot be conducted at a manufacturing site that is subject to such 
inspection due to circumstances such as war, infectious disease, natural disasters, or other 
similar events, the on-site inspection may be temporarily suspended and only a document 
review shall be conducted. 
(7)  Manufacturers or importers for whom only document review was conducted under paragraph 
(6) shall submit test reports conforming to their self-quality control test specifications for each 
manufacturing or import unit to the Commissioner of Regional Office at each instance of 
manufacture or import. 
(8)  In Article 11 (1) 1 and Article 27 (2) 2 of the Enforcement Rule of the Act on In Vitro 
Diagnostic Medical Devices (hereinafter referred to as the “Enforcement Rule”), the term “ a 
person prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety” means a 
manufacturer or a medical device manufacturer who has been recognized as conforming to the 
GMP system requirements pursuant to the texts of Article 5 (5) of the Act and Article 6 (4) of 
the Medical Device Act. 
(9)  Where tests or manufacturing processes for quality control are outsourced under Article 11 (2) 
of the Enforcement Rule, the consignor and the consignee shall faithfully fulfill their 
respective responsibilities and obligations as prescribed in any of the following subparagraphs: 
1.  The consignor shall provide the consignee with the GMP standards to be observed. 
2.  The consignee shall record manufacturing and quality control information for each product in 
accordance with the standards referred to in subparagraph 1. 
3.  The consignor shall receive the records referred to in subparagraph 2 from the consignee and 
retain them for one year from the date of expiration of the product’s shelf life (provided, 
however, that where no shelf life is specified, the records shall be retained for a period 
corresponding to the product’s service life). 
 
Article 7 (Application for Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) A person who falls under 
any subparagraph of Article 3 (1) and seeks to undergo conformity recognition assessments under 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
303 
 
this GMP shall submit an application in Form 1, along with the following documents, to the head of 
the audit organization. In this case, the manufacturing site shall have quality control records for at 
least one manufacturing unit, and the preferred date for the on-site inspection shall be finalized and 
submitted at least 20 days before the inspection start date. 
1.  A copy of the manufacturing (import) business license for in vitro diagnostic medical 
devices or a copy of the conditional manufacturing (import) business license for in vitro 
diagnostic medical devices (excluding cases where no such initial assessment or license 
for manufacturing (importing) in vitro diagnostic medical devices (conditional) for 
clinical performance study is held). 
2.  The following documents corresponding to each item: 
(a)  An overview of the manufacturing site (including the name of the site and the 
address of each facility; if there are multiple sites, all site names must be included), 
organizational chart, number of employees, and in vitro diagnostic medical devices 
manufactured; 
(b)  A copy of the quality management system conformity certificate issued by the 
regulatory authority or an agency delegated by the regulatory authority (only 
applicable to Article 6 (2) and Article 6 (6)) and on-site inspection results (only 
applicable to Article 6 (2) 2 and Article 6 (6), including any follow-up actions taken 
in response to the inspection results); 
(c)  A description of facility conditions for each manufacturing site subject to assessment 
[including floor plans of work areas, test laboratories, and storage facilities (for 
software manufacturing sites, only if such work areas, test laboratories, or storage 
facilities exist), and lists of facilities and equipment], cleanroom procedures (if 
applicable), and procedures for monitoring and measurement equipment that specify 
monitoring cycles; 
(d)  The quality manual of the manufacturing site (including the quality policy); 
(e)  Procedures and test reports related to finished product testing (e.g., final release 
inspection) for the core product of the manufacturing site (including documentation 
demonstrating sterilization for sterile products); 
(f)  Purchasing and outsourcing procedures for the core product of the manufacturing 
site, names of major suppliers (including contracted suppliers), and scope of work; 
(g)  Device Master Records of the core product for the manufacturing site (including 
descriptions of specific manufacturing processes such as sterilization or software, as 
applicable), and procedures for validation of sterilization, where applicable; 
(h)  Checklist for Annex 2 criteria of the manufacturing site; 
(i)  Declaration of conformity to Annex 2 criteria of the manufacturing site; 
(j)  The designation certificate for the core innovative medical device. 
3.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 2, when undergoing assessment using the conformity 
recognition results obtained under the Medical Device Single Audit Program under Annex 
1, subparagraph 68 (hereinafter referred to as the “use of the Medical Device Single Audit 
Program”), the documents in any of the following items shall be submitted: 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
304 
 
(a)  A copy of the MDSAP conformity recognition certificate and the accompanying 
assessment results (including, where nonconformities were identified, the 
nonconformity report issued by the audit organization and the corrective and 
preventive action plan or results submitted by the manufacturing site that have been 
confirmed by the organization as compliant). 
(b)  Device Master Records for the product belonging to the highest classification level 
within each product group of the manufacturing site. 
 
Provided, however, that for an assessment for change, the Device Master Record 
shall be that of the product belonging to the highest classification level within the 
product group of the manufacturing site and having the highest manufacturing or 
import volume. 
(c)  The following documents related to the quality management system: 
1)  Quality manual of the manufacturing site; 
2)  Procedures related to record management; 
3)  Procedures that define the scope of responsibilities of the quality manager; 
4)  Procedures for managing medical devices subject to traceability (where 
applicable); 
5)  Procedures for adverse event reporting and advisory notices. 
(d)  Documents demonstrating the correlation between the products covered by the 
MDSAP conformity recognition certificate and the products subject to conformity 
recognition assessments. 
4.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 2, where a manufacturing site qualifies as an Excellent 
Manufacturing Site and undergoes a periodic assessment, the following documents shall 
be submitted in lieu of the documents required under subparagraph 2: 
(a)  Documentation confirming that the site falls under Annex 1, subparagraph 69 (d); 
(b)  The Device Master Record for the core product that belongs to the highest 
classification level within each product group of the manufacturing site and has the 
highest manufacturing or import volume; 
(c)  The following documents demonstrating the appropriateness of quality control over 
the past three years: 
1)  Procedures and test reports related to finished product testing (e.g., final release 
inspection) for the core product (including sterilization validation procedures and test 
reports for sterile products); 
2)  Documents on corrective and preventive actions taken in the last three years in 
accordance with the criteria set out in Annex 2; 
3)  Checklist under Annex 2 and declaration of conformity. 
(2)  The submission documents for the core product falling under Article 7 (1) 2 (e), (f), (g), and 
(h) shall be the documents for the products corresponding to each of the following 
subparagraphs. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
305 
 
1.  Where two or more products are submitted, the product belonging to the highest 
classification level within each product group of the manufacturing site shall be selected. 
2.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 1, in the case of a periodic assessment under Article 4 (2), 
the product belonging to the highest classification level of the manufacturing site and 
having the highest manufacturing or import volume among the products under the 
assessment shall be selected. 
3.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 1, in the case of an assessment for change under Article 4 
(3), the product belonging to the highest classification level within each product group of 
the manufacturing site and having the highest manufacturing or import volume shall be 
selected. 
(3)  A manufacturer or importer required to undergo a periodic assessment under Article 4 (2) shall 
apply for the periodic assessment to the head of the audit organization by submitting an 
application in Form 1, accompanied by the documents under Article 7 (1) 1 and 2, no later than 
three months before the expiration date stated on the conformity recognition certificate. In such 
cases, the desired on-site inspection date shall be fixed and applied for no later than 20 days 
before the expiration date stated on the conformity recognition certificate, and if the desired 
on-site inspection date is not confirmed at the time of application submission, the applicant 
shall submit the desired date in writing no later than 20 days before the start date of the 
requested on-site inspection. 
(4)  Where a manufacturer or importer has multiple manufacturing sites subject to periodic 
assessment under paragraph (3), a consolidated application for periodic assessment may be 
submitted. Provided, however, that manufacturing sites that received the conformity 
recognition certificate using the Medical Device Single Audit Program or those designated as 
Excellent Manufacturing Sites shall be excluded from periodic assessment consolidated 
applications. 
(5)  A person who intends to submit a consolidated periodic assessment application under 
paragraph (4) shall prepare the documents required under paragraph (3) and the manufacturing 
site summary sheet in Form 1, and submit them to the head of the audit organization. 
(6)  Where Article 6 (2) 3 applies because another manufacturer or importer holds a valid 
conformity recognition certificate for the relevant manufacturing site under this GMP, only the 
following documents among those required under paragraph (1) may be submitted along with 
the application in Form 1: 
1.  A copy of the manufacturing (import) business license for in vitro diagnostic medical 
devices or a copy of the conditional manufacturing (import) business license for in vitro 
diagnostic medical devices (excluding cases where no such initial assessment or license 
for manufacturing (importing) in vitro diagnostic medical devices (conditional) for 
clinical performance study is held). 
2.  The documents under Article 7 (1) 2 (g) (excluding sterilization validation procedures) 
and (h); 
3.  The document of the manufacturing site demonstrating that the products are manufactured 
under the same system at the same manufacturing site. 
(7)  When any of the following circumstances occurs, an Excellent Manufacturing Site under 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
306 
 
Annex 1, subparagraph 69, or a manufacturer or importer that has been issued a conformity 
recognition certificate under Article 6 (6) shall submit an application in Form 1 to the head of 
the audit organization within 10 days from the date of occurrence. In such cases, the applicant 
may omit the supporting documents for Form 1. 
1.  Where an Excellent Manufacturing Site no longer satisfies any of the criteria listed in 
Annex 1, subparagraph 69; 
2.  Where the conditions at the location or region of a manufacturing site for which an on-site 
inspection was deferred under Article 6 (6) have ended. 
(8)  If a person required to apply for a periodic assessment fails to do so at least three months 
before the expiration date under paragraph (3), the head of the audit organization shall report 
the name of the company, its representative, and other relevant information to the 
Commissioner of Regional Office. 
(9)  For manufacturing sites subject to on-site inspection under Article 6 (5), the documents listed 
in Article 7 (1) 2 (b), (h), and (i) may be omitted. 
(10) Costs and other matters related to conformity recognition assessments shall be governed by 
Annex 2 of the Enforcement Rule of the Medical Device Act. 
 
Article 8 (Procedures for Conformity Recognition Assessments) (1) Upon receiving an 
application for conformity recognition and related assessments under Article 7, the head of the audit 
organization shall, in accordance with the following subparagraphs, report the receipt and request 
confirmation of whether an on-site inspection is required under Article 6 (3) from the Commissioner 
of Regional Office. Provided, however, that where the assessment entity is single-agency under 
Article 6 (5) and Annex 4, and Article 6 (6) does not apply, reporting the receipt to the 
Commissioner of Regional Office may be omitted. 
1.  The head shall verify within five days whether all required documents under Article 7 (1) 
through (6) have been submitted, and if complete, shall report and request within seven 
days after receipt. 
2.  If, as a result of confirming whether the supporting documents under subparagraph 1 have 
been submitted, any deficiency such as missing supporting documents is identified, the 
applicant shall be requested to supplement them by setting a supplementation deadline for 
the submission of such documents in accordance with the Administrative Procedures Act. 
3.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 1, where an application additionally includes a confirmed 
desired on-site inspection date, the report and request shall be made no later than the day 
following the receipt of the application. 
(2)  Within ten days after receiving the report and request under paragraph (1), the Commissioner 
of Regional Office shall determine the need for on-site inspection under Article 6 (3), the 
assessment entity under Article 6 (5), and the assessment method, and shall notify the head of 
the audit organization, who shall in turn notify the applicant. 
(3)  The head of the audit organization shall notify the applicant in writing of the conformity 
recognition assessment results under Article 6 within 30 days from the date the application for 
conformity recognition was received. Provided, however, that if an on-site inspection is required 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
307 
 
under paragraph (2), the period from the date of notification to the applicant until the start of the 
on-site inspection under this paragraph shall not be included in the processing period. 
(4)  Where an on-site inspection is required under paragraph (2), the head of the audit organization 
shall conduct the on-site inspection in accordance with the following subparagraphs: 
1.  The assessment entity determined under paragraph (2) shall conduct the on-site inspection 
on the notified inspection date, and the head of the audit organization shall notify the 
applicant in writing of the results within seven days from the end of the inspection visit or 
within the processing period under paragraph (3). Provided, however, that if the results of 
the on-site inspection are determined to be nonconforming, the Commissioner of Regional 
Office shall be notified immediately. 
2.  If an on-site inspection under subparagraph 1 cannot be conducted due to war, epidemics, 
natural disasters, or other similar circumstances during the inspection period, or if the 
inspection cannot proceed normally due to delayed or refused submission of inspection 
documents, the on-site inspection may be suspended. In such cases, the applicant shall be 
immediately notified in writing of the reasons for the suspension, and the Commissioner 
of Regional Office shall be notified accordingly. 
3.  When the reason for suspension under subparagraph 2 is confirmed to be resolved, the on-
site inspection may resume, and the results shall be notified to the applicant in writing 
within seven days from the completion date of the resumed inspection or within the 
processing period under paragraph (3). 
(5)  Where the head of the audit organization is unable to notify the applicant of the conformity 
recognition assessment results within the processing period under paragraphs (3) and (4) due to 
unavoidable reasons such as natural disasters, the head shall notify the applicant in advance of 
the delay. 
(6)  Where the results of the conformity recognition assessments fall under Annex 2, Section 9.4 (2) 
(a) 2, the head of the audit organization shall take the actions in any of the following 
subparagraphs: 
1.  Require the applicant to submit corrective documentation and a corrective action plan, 
and evaluate conformity within 15 days from the end of the conformity recognition 
assessment. 
2.  Review the documents submitted under subparagraph 1 and notify the applicant in writing 
of the results. 
3.  If the applicant fails to submit the required documents within 15 days or the submitted 
documents are not adequate, supplementary measures shall be taken in accordance with 
paragraph (7). 
4.  If the applicant fails to submit the implementation results of corrective actions under 
subparagraph 1 within three months or the submitted results are inadequate, the head of 
the audit organization shall immediately report to the Commissioner of Regional Office 
and notify the applicant in writing. 
(6)  Where matters requiring supplementation are identified, the head of the audit organization shall 
take the following actions with respect to the results of the conformity recognition assessment: 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
308 
 
1.  Supplementation procedures and deadlines shall be required in accordance with the Civil 
Petitions Treatment Act, and the assessment entity under paragraph (2) shall review the 
results submitted by the applicant and evaluate conformity. 
2.  If the applicant fails to submit the required documents within the deadline, the assessment 
entity shall determine as nonconforming. 
3.  Where an application is determined nonconforming under subparagraph 2, the fact shall 
be reported immediately to the Commissioner of Regional Office, and the applicant shall 
be notified in writing. 
(8)  The head of the audit organization shall prepare a result report in Form 3 and submit it to the 
Commissioner of Regional Office in accordance with the following subparagraphs. Provided, 
however, that submission may be omitted where the assessment entity is single-agency under 
Article 6 (5) and Annex 4, and the case does not fall under Article 6 (6). 
1.  Assessment results under paragraph (3) shall be submitted within the processing period 
prescribed in paragraph (3). 
2.  Assessment results under paragraph (4) 1 shall be submitted within seven days from the 
end of the on-site inspection. 
3.  Where the on-site inspection is resumed pursuant to paragraph (4) 3, the results shall be 
submitted within seven days from the end of the resumed inspection visit or within the 
processing period under paragraph (3). 
(9)  Where the results of conformity recognition assessments under Article 6 are conforming, the 
head of the audit organization shall issue the Certificate of GMP (Form 2 or Form 2-2, 
pursuant to Annex 5) (hereinafter referred to as the “certificate of conformity”) to the applicant. 
Provided, however, that the certificate may be issued in any case of the following 
subparagraphs: 
1.  Where the conformity recognition assessment results fall under Annex 2, 9.4 (2) (a) 2, a 
conditional certificate of conformity may be issued on the condition that corrective 
actions are implemented within three months; 
2.  Where document review is deemed to conform under Article 6 (6), a temporary certificate 
of conformity may be issued. 
(10) Where an applicant objects to the assessment results under Article 6, the applicant may file an 
objection with the head of the relevant audit organization in accordance with the Civil Petitions 
Treatment Act. 
(11) When an objection is filed under paragraph (9), the head of the audit organization shall report 
both the content of the objection and the handling results to the head of the Commissioner of 
Regional Office. 
(12) Where multiple manufacturing sites are submitted as a consolidated periodic assessment 
application under Article 7 (4), the Commissioner of Regional Office and the head of the audit 
organization shall conduct an on-site inspection for one manufacturing site, selected by 
comprehensively considering the following criteria: 
1.  A manufacturing site that produces the product of the highest class; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
309 
 
2.  A manufacturing site with high domestic production or import volume; 
3.  A manufacturing site that has not previously undergone an on-site inspection. 
(13) For manufacturing sites that apply for conformity recognition assessments under Article 7 (7), 
the head of the audit organization shall conduct an on-site inspection within three months from 
the date of application. 
 
Article 9 (Expiration Date of the Certificate of Conformity) (1) The expiration date of a 
certificate of conformity issued following an initial assessment shall be three years from the date of 
issuance. Provided, however, that the Minister of Food and Drug Safety may extend this period 
where deemed necessary. 
(2)  When conformity recognition is granted following an additional assessment or an assessment 
for change, the existing expiration date shall remain unaffected. 
(3)  The expiration date of a certificate of conformity issued following a periodic assessment shall 
be three years from the day after the expiration date of the previous certificate. Provided, 
however, that where the certificate is issued after the previous expiration date, or where the 
periodic assessment was submitted as a consolidated application, the expiration date shall be 
three years from the issuance date. Where conformity recognition assessments have been 
conducted pursuant to Article 6 (2) 3 or 5, the expiration date for the relevant manufacturing 
site shall be set to match the expiration date of the manufacturer or importer that previously 
underwent conformity recognition assessments. Where conformity recognition assessments 
have been conducted based on the documents under Article 7 (1) 3, the expiration date for the 
relevant manufacturing site shall be set to be identical to that of the MDSAP conformity 
recognition certificate. 
 
Article 10 (Reissuance of the Certificate of Conformity) (1) A manufacturer or importer who has 
been issued a certificate of conformity under Article 8 (9) may apply to the audit organization that 
issued the certificate for reissuance if the certificate is lost or otherwise needs to be reissued. 
(2)  Upon receiving an application for reissuance under paragraph (1), the head of the audit 
organization shall reissue the certificate of conformity in accordance with Annex 5. 
(3)  A manufacturer or importer may either obtain reissuance of the certificate of conformity or 
record the changes in any of the following subparagraphs on the reverse side of the certificate 
for control purposes: 
1.  Change in the name of the manufacturing or importing business; 
2.  Change in the location of the manufacturing site (limited to changes under the proviso of 
Article 4 (1) 3); 
3.  Change in the location of an importing business; 
4.  Change in the trade name of the legal manufacturer 
5.  Change in the location of the legal manufacturer (limited to changes under the proviso of 
Article 4 (1) 3); 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
310 
 
6.  Change in the manufacturer’s trade name; 
7.  Change in the manufacturer’s location (limited to changes under the proviso of Article 4 
(1) 3). 
(4)  Where a manufacturer or importer records changes on the reverse side of the certificate of 
conformity under paragraph (3), the date and details of the approval of change shall also be 
recorded. 
(5)  A manufacturer or importer who has been issued a certificate of conformity under Article 8 (9) 
1 may apply to the issuing audit organization for replacement of the certificate only after 
corrective actions have been completed, and may receive a replacement certificate accordingly. 
 
Article 11 (Return of the Certificate of Conformity) (1) A manufacturer or importer who has 
been issued a certificate of conformity under Article 8 (9) may return the certificate to the issuing 
audit organization, specifying the relevant reasons in detail, when any of the following 
circumstances occurs: 
1.  Where the manufacturing business license or import business license is revoked; 
2.  Where the manufacturing approval, import approval, manufacturing certification, or 
import certification is revoked; 
3.  Where any other reasons exist requiring the manufacturer or importer to return the 
certificate of conformity. 
(2)  In accordance with paragraph (1), the head of a quality management examination agency, etc. 
who has received the return of the certificate of conformity shall, immediately upon receipt of 
the returned certificate of conformity, report the fact of its return to the Commissioner of 
Regional Office. 
 
Article 12 (Marking for Conformity Recognition Assessments) A manufacturer or importer may 
affix the conformity recognition marking, as specified in Annex 6, to in vitro diagnostic medical 
devices that belong to the same product group as the manufacturing site which has undergone 
conformity recognition assessments. 
 
Article 13 (Duties of the Audit Organization) The duties of the audit organization under Article 4 
of the Act on In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices and Article 48 of the Enforcement Rule of the 
Medical Device Act shall be as follows: 
1.  Conducting conformity recognition assessments under the Good Manufacturing Practice 
for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices; 
2.  Issuing certificates of conformity; 
3.  Compiling statistics and providing administrative support related to conformity 
recognition assessments; 
4.  Other matters necessary for conformity recognition assessments. 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
311 
 
Article 14 (Reporting) (1) The head of the audit organization shall submit the quarterly report on 
the results of conformity recognition assessments for in vitro diagnostic medical devices (Form 4) 
and the detailed list of such assessment results (Form 5) to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
and the Commissioner of Regional Office within 20 days after the end of each quarter. Provided, 
however, that where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety or the Commissioner of Regional Office 
requests separate data, the relevant data shall be submitted within seven days from the date of the 
request. 
(2)  Where there are personnel changes, such as transfers or resignations of assessors, the head of 
the audit organization shall report such changes to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
within seven days. 
 
Article 15 (Review of Regulation) Pursuant to Article 8 of the Framework Act on Administrative 
Regulations, the validity of this GMP shall be reviewed every three years as of July 1, 2020 (that is, 
by June 30 of every third year), and necessary improvements shall be made. 
 
Article 16 (Review Deadline) The Minister of Food and Drug Safety shall review the validity of 
this Notice every three years as of January 1, 2024 (that is, by December 31 of every third year), 
pursuant to the Regulation on the Issuance and Management of Directives and Established Rules, 
and shall take necessary measures for improvement.

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices
