[Annex 1] 
Definitions 
(Related to Article 2) 
 
1.  “Audit” means a systematic and independent verification activity conducted to determine 
whether quality-related work and its associated results conform to planned arrangements and 
whether such arrangements have been effectively implemented and are suitable for achieving 
the intended objectives. 
2.  “Verification” means confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence (data 
demonstrating the existence of something or substantiating a fact) and testing, that specified 
requirements have been fulfilled.  
3.  “Review” means an activity conducted to determine the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness 
of a subject in order to achieve established objectives. 
4.  “Management Review” means an activity conducted by top management at planned intervals 
to evaluate the need for changes to, and the potential for improvement of, the quality 
management system, including the quality policy and quality objectives, in order to ensure its 
continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness. 
5.  “Customer” means a collective term for purchasers and users (patients and healthcare 
professionals).  
6.  “Customer Property” means assets owned by the customer, which include each of the 
following items: 
(a)  Raw materials or components (including packaging materials) provided for inclusion in 
the product;  
(b)  Products supplied for repair, maintenance, or upgrading; 
(c)  Products supplied for additional processes (such as packaging, sterilization, or testing 
using customer-provided materials); 
(d)  Services provided on behalf of the customer (e.g., transportation of customer property to a 
third party); 
(e)  Customer intellectual property (e.g., specifications, drawings, and asset information). 
7.  “Supplier” means an individual or organization that provides all or part of components, 
processes, or services. 
8.  “Calibration” means the operation that confirms that a specific device or instrument produces 
results within the prescribed limits when measured against measurement standards recognized 
under international or national standards. 
9.  “Advisory notice” means a communication issued by the manufacturing site after delivery of 
an in vitro diagnostic medical device for the purpose of providing additional information or 
recommending actions regarding the use, change, return, or disposal of the in vitro diagnostic 
medical device. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
313 
 
10.  “Record” means a document that states achieved results or provides evidence of activities 
performed.  
11.  “Infrastructure” means the system of facilities, equipment, and services required for the 
operation of an organization. 
12.  “Single-agency Assessment” means conducting an on-site inspection for conformity 
recognition assessments solely by the audit organization. 
13.  “Sterilization” means a process that uses physical or chemical methods to destroy all types of 
microorganisms, including spores. 
14.  “Sterile Barrier System” means the minimum packaging that prevents microbial ingress and 
ensures that the product is presented sterile at the point of use. 
15.  “Sterilized Device” means an in vitro diagnostic medical device that undergoes a sterilization 
process during manufacturing process and is labeled as sterilized on the product container or 
packaging with indications such as the word “sterile,” the sterilization method, and the 
expiration date. 
16.  “Document” means criteria or procedures that are specified or created prior to performing an 
activity. 
17.  “Batch” means a specified quantity of products produced during a defined manufacturing 
cycle, intended to have uniform characteristics and quality. 
18.  “Complaint” means any written, electronic, or oral communication alleging defects related to 
the identification, quality, durability, reliability, usability, safety, or performance of an in vitro 
diagnostic medical device after it has left the organization’s control, or alleging defects in 
services that affect the performance of such devices. 
19.  “Service” means an intangible output of an organization involving activities that necessarily 
occur between the organization and the customer, such as decision-making, relationship-
maintenance activities, repair, transportation, and information delivery. 
20.  “Senior Quality Auditor” means a person who is affiliated with the audit organization 
designated by the Minister of Food and Drug Safety and who oversees conformity recognition 
assessment activities. 
21.  “Design and Development” means a set of processes that transforms requirements into 
specified characteristics or into the specifications of a product, process, or system.  
22.  “Installation” means the activities of placing a product at the site of use and enabling it to 
operate in accordance with its intended purpose, including arrangements such as piping and 
waste disposal. 
23.  “Performance Evaluation” means the assessment and data analysis conducted to identify or 
verify the ability of an in vitro diagnostic medical device to achieve its intended use. 
24.  “Cleaning” means a chemical or physical method used to remove contaminants or 
microorganisms from surfaces. 
25.  “Life Cycle” means all stages of the life of an in vitro diagnostic medical device, from initial 
conception to final disposal and processing. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
314 
 
26.  “Correction” means an action taken to eliminate a detected nonconformity. 
27.  “Corrective Action” means an action taken to eliminate the cause of a detected nonconformity 
or other undesirable situation. 
28.  “Identification” means the activities performed at all stages—including raw materials, 
materials, in-process products, and finished products—to ensure product traceability and 
proper transfer to the next process or shipment. 
29.  “Safety” means the property of being free from hazards or the risk of malfunction, and of 
ensuring safe performance. 
30.  “Preventive Action” means an action taken to eliminate the cause of a potential nonconformity 
or other undesirable situation to prevent its occurrence. 
31.  “Requirement” means an expressed need or expectation, generally one that is implicit or 
obligatory.  
32.  “Manufacturing Site of Potential Concern” means a manufacturing site that falls under any of 
the following cases: 
(a)  If the applicant manufacturing site has failed a GMP assessment within the past three 
years; 
(b)  If the product group subject to the application has been found noncompliant in quality 
based on sampling inspection results within the past three years; 
(c)  If the product subject to the application has been subject to compulsory recall, suspension 
of use, suspension of manufacturing, or similar regulatory actions by domestic or foreign 
government authorities within the past three years. 
33.  “Risk Management” means an advanced safety management system that analyzes and 
evaluates all risks that may arise throughout the entire lifecycle of an in vitro diagnostic 
medical device—including design, production, distribution, and use—and manages those risks 
to an acceptable level.  
34.  “Validation” means the act of verifying and documenting that methods of manufacturing and 
quality control—including the structure and facilities of the manufacturing site, manufacturing 
processes, and systems—achieve the intended results. 
35.  “Revalidation” means validation activities that are conducted either periodically or in response 
to changes to raw materials, manufacturing processes, machinery and equipment, or 
manufacturing systems that may have an impact on product quality. 
36.  Deleted 
37.  “Rework” means an operation performed to bring a nonconforming product into conformity 
with quality standards by applying a method different from the established manufacturing 
process. 
38.  “Conformity Recognition Assessments” means assessments conducted to determine whether 
an in vitro diagnostic medical device can be consistently manufactured with a high level of 
assurance of safety, effectiveness, and quality appropriate for its intended use. 
39.  “Procedure” means an established method for performing an activity or process.  

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
315 
 
40.  “Manufacturing” means all operations required to produce in vitro diagnostic medical device, 
including design, packaging, and labeling. 
41.  “Manufacturing Process” means the activities related to the design and development, 
procurement of raw materials, incoming inspection, production, in-process inspection, finished 
product inspection, packaging, labeling, shipment, and storage for the manufacture of in vitro 
diagnostic medical device. 
42.  “Manufacturing Unit” or “Lot” means a unit of finished products, components, or raw 
materials manufactured under the same manufacturing conditions and having uniform 
characteristics and quality. 
43.  “Legal Manufacturer” means a person who, under a contractual relationship, entrusts all or the 
principal manufacturing processes of an in vitro diagnostic medical device falling under any of 
the following items to a manufacturer under subparagraph 44 and bears statutory responsibility 
therefor.  
(a)  An in vitro diagnostic medical device that has obtained, or intends to obtain, authorization 
or certification from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety; 
(b)  An in vitro diagnostic medical device that has submitted, or intends to submit, a 
notification to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety. 
44.  “Manufacturer” means a person who performs all operations necessary to produce an in vitro 
diagnostic medical device, or a person who, under a contractual relationship, is entrusted by 
the legal manufacturer with the principal manufacturing processes of the product.  
45.  “Product” means the output of a process and includes each of the following items: 
(a)  Hardware; 
(b)  Software; 
(c)  Processed materials; 
(d)  Services. 
46.  “Production Realization” means the combined sequence of processes and detailed processes 
required to achieve a product. 
47.  “Device Master Record (DMR)” means a document that contains detailed information on all 
manufacturing processes—from product design to shipment (installation)—including 
specifications, manufacturing processes, manufacturing criteria, and installation, for each in 
vitro diagnostic medical device item or model. 
48.  “Organization” means a group of personnel and facilities with an established arrangement of 
responsibilities, authorities, and interrelationships. 
49.  “Critical/Core Process” means a process in which an intermediate product at a particular stage 
acquires the form of a finished in vitro diagnostic medical device and, even after further 
processing, its configuration or performance remains unchanged. 
50.  “Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Digital Medical Devices” means 
a quality management system that prescribes the requirements to be observed to ensure the 
quality of in vitro diagnostic medical devices throughout all processes—from development and 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
316 
 
procurement of raw materials to manufacturing, testing, packaging, installation, storage, 
shipment, and the handling of complaints or returns—so that products of consistently high 
quality may be supplied.  
51.  “Traceability” means identifying and managing the sources of raw materials and components 
of an in vitro diagnostic medical device, its quality control history, and information on its 
distributors and users (locations). 
52.  “Measuring Equipment” means measuring instruments, software, measurement standards, 
reference materials, auxiliary devices, or combinations thereof required to carry out a 
measurement process. 
53.  “Concession” means written approval to use or release a specific product that has minor 
nonconformities not directly related to safety or effectiveness, provided that statutory 
requirements are met. 
54.  “Product Group” means a set of products that share similar raw materials, manufacturing 
processes, and quality control systems. 
55.  “Quality” means the degree to which a set of inherent characteristics fulfills requirements. 
56.  “Quality Management System” means a management system for efficiently managing the 
organization, responsibilities, procedures, processes, and resources for product quality 
management. 
57.  “Quality Control (QC)” means the part of quality management that focuses on fulfilling quality 
requirements. 
58.  “Quality Manual” means a document that defines the manufacturer’s quality management 
system and describes the details or requirements appropriate to the scale and complexity of the 
organization. 
59.  “Quality Objective” means a target or objective that is pursued with respect to quality. 
60.  “Quality Policy” means the overall intentions and direction of an organization related to 
quality, as formally expressed by top management.  
61.  “Quality Nonconformity” means a case in which an in vitro diagnostic medical device 
manufactured or imported for the purpose of sale by an in vitro diagnostic medical device 
manufacturer or importer is found to be nonconforming as a result of inspection under Article 
32 or Article 33 of the Medical Device Act. 
62.  “Quality Auditor” means a person affiliated with the audit organization designated by the 
Minister of Food and Drug Safety who conducts conformity recognition assessment activities. 
63.  “Process” means a set of interrelated or interacting activities that transforms inputs into 
outputs. 
64.  “Joint” means that the on-site inspection for conformity recognition assessments is conducted 
jointly by the MFDS and an audit organization, or by the Regional Office of Food and Drug 
Safety and an audit organization. 
65.  ‘Innovative Medical Device Software’ means medical device software designated as an 
innovative medical device and developed and manufactured as stand-alone software. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
317 
 
66.  “Effectiveness” means the extent to which planned activities are realized and planned results 
are achieved. 
67.  “Efficiency” means the ratio or relationship between the results achieved and the resources 
used. 
68.  “Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP)” means a system in which the results of 
conformity recognition and related audits conducted by audit organizations (AO) jointly 
designated and operated by participating jurisdictions, including the United States and Japan, 
are mutually recognized by multiple countries. 
69.  “Excellent Manufacturing Site” means a manufacturing site that satisfies all of the following 
items: 
(a)  It is not classified as a Manufacturing Site of Potential Concern under subparagraph 32; 
(b)  It has not been subject to administrative dispositions under the Act on In Vitro Diagnostic 
Medical Devices or the Medical Device Act within the past three years; 
(c)  During the most recent periodic assessment, an on-site inspection was conducted and the 
result was ‘conforming’; 
(d)  For imported in vitro diagnostic medical devices, where the applicant holds a valid 
certificate of conformity to the quality management system issued by the regulatory 
authority or an organization delegated by the regulatory authority, and can demonstrate 
that all corrective actions for any nonconformities identified in the certificate have been 
completed. 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
318 
 
[Annex 2] 
Criteria for Conformity Recognition Assessments of In Vitro 
Diagnostic Medical Devices 
(Related to Article 5 and 6) 
 
1.  Purpose 
 
The purpose of the Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical 
Devices is to specify the requirements of the quality management system applied to the design 
and development, production, installation, and servicing of in vitro diagnostic medical devices 
by manufacturers or by manufacturing sites of imported in vitro diagnostic medical devices 
(hereinafter referred to as the “organization”). 
 
2.  Scope of Application 
 
Where, due to the activities performed by the organization or the characteristics of in vitro 
medical devices to which this GMP apply, any requirement under Chapter 6 (Resource 
Management), Chapter 7 (Production Realization), or Chapter 8 (Measurement, Analysis, and 
Improvement) is not applicable, the organization may exclude such requirement from its 
quality management system. Provided, however, that the organization shall document the 
justification for each excluded requirement in accordance with Section 4.2.2. 
 
3.  Definitions  
(a)  With respect to the requirements in this GMP that are limited to those “where applicable,” 
the organization shall be deemed applicable unless it otherwise provides reasonable 
justification. 
(b)  Where a requirement in this GMP is stated as “shall document,” it also includes the 
requirement to establish, implement, and maintain the corresponding content. 
(c)  In applying this GMP, the definitions of other terms shall be in accordance with Annex 1. 
 
4. 
Quality Management System 
4.1  General Requirements 
4.1.1 (a) The organization shall document its quality management system in accordance with the 
requirements of this GMP and applicable statutory requirements, and shall maintain the 
effectiveness of the quality management system.  
(b)  The organization shall establish, implement, and maintain specific requirements, 
procedures, activities, or methods of operation that must be documented pursuant to this 
GMP and applicable statutory requirements.  
(c)  The organization shall document the roles required to perform in accordance with 
applicable statutory requirements. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
319 
 
4.1.2 The organization shall implement the following: 
1)  Determine the processes necessary for the quality management system, taking into 
account the roles performed by the organization, and apply those processes throughout the 
organization; 
2)  Apply a risk-based approach to the appropriate management of processes required for the 
quality management system; 
3)  Determine the sequence and interaction of those processes. 
 
4.1.3 For the processes of the quality management system, the organization shall perform the 
following: 
1)  Determine the criteria and methods necessary to ensure the effective operation and control 
of the processes; 
2)  Ensure the availability of information and resources necessary to support the operation 
and monitoring of the processes; 
3)  Take necessary actions to achieve planned results and maintain the effectiveness of the 
processes; 
4)  Monitor such processes and, where applicable, measure and analyze them; 
5)  Prepare and maintain the records necessary to demonstrate conformity with this GMP and 
compliance with applicable statutory requirements. 
 
4.1.4 The organization shall control quality management system processes in conformity with this 
GMP and applicable statutory requirements. Where such processes are to be changed, the 
organization shall perform the following: 
1)  Evaluate whether the change to the process affects the quality management system; 
2)  Evaluate whether the change to the process affects the in vitro diagnostic medical devices 
produced under the quality management system; 
3)  Control such matters in accordance with this GMP and applicable statutory requirements. 
 
4.1.5 (a) Where the organization outsources any process that affects product conformity 
requirements, it shall ensure that such processes are monitored and controlled.  
(b)  The organization shall retain responsibility for ensuring compliance with this GMP, 
customer requirements, and applicable statutory requirements for outsourced processes. 
(c)  Control of outsourced processes shall be proportionate to the associated risks and to the 
capability of the contracted supplier to meet the requirements under paragraph 7.4, and 
shall include a written quality agreement. 
 
4.1.6 (a) The organization shall document procedures for the validation of computer software used 
in the quality management system.  

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
320 
 
(b)  Such software shall be validated prior to initial use, and where applicable, shall also be 
validated following any changes to the software or its application. 
(c)  Specific approaches and activities related to software validation and revalidation shall be 
proportionate to the risks associated with the use of the software.  
(d)  Records of these activities shall be maintained.  
 
4.2  Documentation Requirements 
4.2.1 General Requirements 
 
Documentation of the quality management system shall include the following: 
1)  Documented quality policy and quality objectives; 
2)  Quality Manual; 
3)  Documented procedures and records required by this GMP; 
4)  Documents, including records, determined by the organization to be necessary to ensure 
the effective planning, operation, and control of its processes; 
5)  Any additional documentation required by applicable statutory requirements. 
 
4.2.2 Quality Manual 
(a)  The organization shall document a quality manual that includes the following: 
1)  The scope of the quality management system, including details of any exclusions or 
non-applications and their justification; 
2)  Documented procedures established for the quality management system and 
reference to such documents; 
3)  A description of the interactions between processes of the quality management 
system. 
(b)  The quality manual shall briefly specify the structure of the documents used in the quality 
management system. 
 
4.2.3 In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Device File 
(a)  For each in vitro diagnostic medical device model or item, the organization shall establish 
and maintain one or more files containing or referencing documents generated to 
demonstrate conformity with this GMP and compliance with applicable statutory 
requirements. 
(b)  The contents of the in vitro diagnostic medical device file shall include, but not be limited 
to, the following:  
1)  A general description of the in vitro diagnostic medical device, including its intended 
use/purpose and all instructions for use; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
321 
 
2)  Product specifications; 
3)  Specifications and procedures for manufacturing, packaging, storage, handling, and 
distribution; 
4)  Measurement and monitoring procedures; 
5)  Installation requirements, where applicable; 
6)  Servicing procedures, where applicable. 
 
4.2.4 Control of Documents 
(a)  Documents required by the quality management system shall be controlled. Records are a 
special type of document and shall be controlled in accordance with Section 4.2.5.  
(b)  Procedures necessary to control the following shall be documented: 
1)  Review and approval of documents for adequacy prior to issuance; 
2)  Review, update, and re-approval of documents as necessary; 
3)  Ensure that changes to documents and the current revision status are identified; 
4)  Ensure that applicable versions of documents are available at points of use;  
5)  Ensure that documents remain legible and readily identifiable;  
6)  Ensure that documents of external origin determined by the organization to be 
necessary for the planning and operation of the quality management system are 
identified and their distribution controlled; 
7)  Prevent deterioration or loss of documents; 
8)  Preventing the unintended use of obsolete documents and applying appropriate 
identification if they are retained for any purpose. 
(c)  The organization shall ensure that document changes are reviewed and approved by the 
original approving authority or another designated authority with access to background 
information on which the organization’s decisions are based. 
(d)  The organization shall retain at least one copy of obsolete controlled documents for a 
period corresponding to the product’s life cycle, which shall be no less than the retention 
period required for records. 
 
4.2.5 Control of Records 
(a)  Records shall be established and maintained to demonstrate the effective operation of the 
quality management system and conformity to requirements.  
(b)  The organization shall document procedures defining the controls needed for the 
identification, storage, security and integrity, retrieval, retention period, and disposition of 
records.  
(c)  The organization shall establish and implement methods to protect personal health 
information contained in records in accordance with applicable statutory requirements. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
322 
 
(d)  All records shall be easily legible, readily identifiable, and retrievable. Any changes to 
records shall remain identifiable. 
(e)  The organization shall retain records for a period corresponding to the product’s life 
cycle. This period shall be at least five years from the date of manufacture and at least two 
years after release to the market. 
 
5.  Management Responsibility 
5.1  Management Commitment 
 
Top management shall demonstrate its commitment to the development and implementation of 
the quality management system and to maintaining its effectiveness through the following:  
1)  Communicate the importance of fulfilling customer requirements and applicable statutory 
requirements with the organization; 
2)  Establish the quality policy; 
3)  Ensure that quality objectives are established; 
4)  Conduct management reviews; 
5)  Ensure the availability of resources. 
 
5.2  Customer Focus 
 
Top management shall ensure that customer requirements and applicable statutory 
requirements are determined and fulfilled. 
 
5.3  Quality Policy 
 
Top management shall ensure that the quality policy: 
1)  Is appropriate to the purpose of the organization; 
2)  Includes a commitment to comply with requirements and to maintain the effectiveness of 
the quality management system; 
3)  Provides a framework for establishing and reviewing quality objectives; 
4)  Is communicated and understood within the organization; 
5)  Is reviewed for continuing suitability. 
 
5.4  Planning 
5.4.1 Quality Objectives 
(a)  Top management shall ensure that the quality objectives include the necessary elements to 
meet applicable statutory requirements and product requirements, and that they are 
established at relevant functions and levels within the organization.  
(b)  The quality objectives shall be measurable and shall be consistent with the quality policy. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
323 
 
5.4.2 Planning of the Quality Management System 
 
Top management shall ensure the following: 
1)  The planning of the quality management system is carried out not only to achieve the 
quality objectives but also to meet the requirements of Section 4.1;  
2)  The integrity of the quality management system is maintained when changes to the 
quality management system are planned and implemented.  
 
5.5  Responsibility, Authority, and Communication 
5.5.1 Responsibility and Authority 
(a)  Top management shall ensure that responsibilities and authorities within the organization 
are defined, documented, and communicated. 
(b)  Top management shall document the interrelationships of all personnel who manage, 
perform, and verify work affecting quality, and shall ensure the authority and 
independence necessary to perform such work. 
 
5.5.2 Quality Manager 
 
Top management shall appoint a person within the organization who, irrespective of other 
responsibilities, has the authority and responsibility to perform the following: 
1)  Ensure that the processes necessary for the quality management system are documented; 
2)  Report to top management on the performance and effectiveness of the quality 
management system and on the need for improvement; 
3)  Ensure that awareness of applicable statutory requirements and quality management 
system requirements is promoted throughout the organization. 
 
5.5.3 Internal Communication 
 
Top management shall ensure that appropriate communication processes are established within 
the organization and that communication regarding the effectiveness of the quality 
management system is carried out. 
 
5.6  Management Review 
5.6.1 General Requirements 
(a)  The organization shall document the procedure for management review.  
(b)  Top management shall review the quality management system at documented planned 
intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.  
(c)  Management reviews shall evaluate the need for changes to the quality management 
system, including the quality policy and quality objectives, and shall identify 
opportunities for improvement. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
324 
 
(d)  Records of management reviews shall be maintained. 
 
5.6.2 Review Inputs 
 
The inputs to management review shall include, but not be limited to, the following: 
1)  Feedback; 
2)  Handling of complaints; 
3)  Reports to regulatory authorities; 
4)  Audits; 
5)  Monitoring and measurement of processes; 
6)  Monitoring and measurement of product; 
7)  Corrective action; 
8)  Preventive action; 
9)  Follow-up actions from previous management reviews; 
10)  Changes that could affect the quality management system; 
11)  Recommendations for improvement; 
12)  New or revised applicable statutory requirements. 
 
5.6.3 Review Outputs 
 
The outputs of management review shall be recorded and shall include decisions and actions 
related to the reviewed inputs and the following: 
1)  Improvements needed to maintain the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the 
quality management system and its processes; 
2)  Improvement of product related to customer requirements; 
3)  Changes needed to meet new or revised applicable statutory requirements; 
4)  Resource needs. 
 
6.  Resource Management 
6.1  Provision of Resources 
 
The organization shall determine and provide the resources needed for: 
1)  Implementing the quality management system and maintaining its effectiveness; 
2)  Meeting applicable regulatory requirements and customer requirements. 
 
6.2  Human Resources 
(a)  Personnel performing work affecting product quality shall be competent on the basis of 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
325 
 
appropriate education, training, skills, and experience.  
(b)  The organization shall establish the competencies required of personnel, provide the 
necessary training, and establish and document processes to ensure personnel awareness. 
(c)  The organization shall perform the following:  
1)  Determine the competencies needed for personnel performing work that affects 
product quality;  
2)  Provide training or take other actions to achieve or maintain the necessary 
competencies;  
3)  Evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken; 
4)  Ensure that personnel are aware of the relevance and importance of their activities 
and how they contribute to the achievement of quality objectives;  
5)  Maintain appropriate records of education, training, skills, and experience. 
 
6.3. Infrastructure 
(a)  The organization shall document the infrastructure requirements necessary to ensure 
conformity to product requirements, prevent product mix-ups, and ensure orderly 
handling. Where applicable, infrastructure includes: 
1)  Buildings, workspace, and associated facilities; 
2)  Process equipment (hardware and software); 
3)  Supporting services such as transport, communication, or information systems. 
(b)  Where maintenance activities of infrastructure, or lack thereof, may affect product quality, 
the organization shall document the maintenance requirements, including maintenance 
intervals. Where applicable, these requirements shall apply to equipment used for 
manufacturing, work environment control, and monitoring and measurement. 
(c)  Records of such maintenance activities shall be maintained. 
 
6.4  Work Environment and Contamination Control 
6.4.1 Work Environment 
(a)  The organization shall document the requirements for the work environment necessary to 
ensure conformity to product requirements. 
(b)  Where work environment conditions may have an adverse effect on product quality, the 
organization shall document the requirements for the work environment and procedures 
for monitoring and controlling such conditions. 
(c)  The organization shall perform the following requirements: 
1)  Where personnel may come into contact with the product or the work environment in 
a manner that could affect the safety or performance of in vitro diagnostic medical 
devices, requirements for personnel health, cleanliness, and clothing shall be 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
326 
 
documented. 
2)  All personnel who work temporarily under special environmental conditions shall be 
competent or shall be supervised by competent personnel. 
 
6.4.2 Contamination Control 
(a)  Where applicable, the organization shall plan and document methods for controlling 
products that are contaminated or potentially contaminated, in order to prevent 
contamination of the work environment, personnel, or products.  
(b)  For sterilized in vitro diagnostic medical devices, the organization shall document 
requirements for contamination control related to microorganisms or particulates and shall 
maintain the required cleanliness during assembly or packaging processes. 
 
7.  Production Realization 
7.1  Planning of Production Realization 
(a)  The organization shall plan and develop the processes needed for production realization. 
Planning of production realization shall be consistent with the other process requirements 
of the quality management system. 
(b)  The organization shall document one or more processes for risk management during 
production realization, and records of risk management activities shall be maintained.  
(c)  Where applicable, the organization shall determine the following in planning production 
realization:  
1)  Quality objectives and requirements for the product; 
2)  The need to establish and document processes, and to provide specific resources for 
the product, including infrastructure and work environment; 
3)  Specific verification, validation, monitoring, measurement, testing and inspection, 
handling, storage, distribution, and traceability activities required for the product, 
along with the criteria for product acceptance; 
4)  Records necessary to demonstrate that production realization processes and their 
outputs meet requirements. 
(d)  The outputs of such planning shall be documented in a form appropriate to the 
organization’s method of operation. 
 
7.2  Customer-Related Processes 
7.2.1 Determination of Requirements Related to the Product 
 
The organization shall determine the following:  
1)  Requirements specified by the customer, including those related to delivery and post-
delivery activities; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
327 
 
2)  Requirements not stated by the customer but necessary for known specified or intended 
use;  
3)  Applicable statutory requirements related to the product; 
4)  User training necessary to ensure stated performance and safe use of the in vitro 
diagnostic medical device; 
5)  Any additional requirements determined by the organization. 
 
7.2.2 Review of Requirements Related to the Product 
(a)  The organization shall review the requirements related to the product. This review shall 
be conducted prior to the organization’s commitment to supply the product to the 
customer.  
1)  The requirements for the product are defined and documented; 
2)  Any contract or order requirements differing from those previously expressed are 
resolved; 
3)  Applicable statutory requirements are met; 
4)  User training determined under Section 7.2.1 is feasible or planned to be feasible; 
5)  The organization has the capability to meet the defined requirements. 
(b)  Records of the results of the review and any actions arising from the review shall be 
maintained. 
(c)  Where the customer does not provide documented requirements, the organization shall 
confirm the customer requirements prior to acceptance.  
(d)  When product requirements are changed, the organization shall amend the relevant 
documents and ensure that relevant personnel are made aware of the changed 
requirements.  
 
7.2.3 Communication 
(a)  The organization shall plan and document the methods for communicating with customers 
regarding: 
1)  Product information; 
2)  Handling inquiries, including amendments, contracts, or orders; 
3)  Customer feedback, including complaints; 
4)  Advisory notices. 
(b)  The organization shall communicate with regulatory authorities in accordance with 
applicable statutory requirements. 
 
7.3. Design and Development 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
328 
 
7.3.1 General  
 
The organization shall document procedures for design and development.  
7.3.2 Design and Development Planning 
(a)  The organization shall plan and control the design and development of the product. Where 
applicable, the design and development plan shall be maintained and updated as design 
and development progress. 
(b)  The organization shall document the following in the course of design and development 
planning:  
1)  The stages of design and development; 
2)  The reviews required at each stage of design and development;  
3)  The verification, validation, and design transfer activities appropriate to each stage 
of design and development; 
4)  The responsibilities and authorities for design and development; 
5)  The methods to ensure traceability between design and development inputs and 
outputs; 
6)  The necessary resources, including personnel competence. 
 
7.3.3 Design and Development Inputs 
(a)  The organization shall determine and maintain records of inputs relating to product 
requirements. These inputs shall include:  
1)  Functional, performance, usability, and safety requirements necessary for the 
intended use; 
2)  Applicable statutory requirements and standards; 
3)  Applicable risk management outputs; 
4)  Information derived from previous similar designs, where applicable; 
5)  Other requirements essential for the design and development of the product and 
process. 
(b)  Such inputs shall be reviewed and approved for adequacy.  
(c)  Product requirements shall be clear, unambiguous, verifiable or validatable, and shall not 
conflict with other requirements. 
 
7.3.4 Design and Development Outputs 
(a)  The design and development outputs shall: 
1)  Meet the design and development input requirements; 
2)  Provide appropriate information for purchasing, production, and service provision; 
3)  Include or reference the criteria for product acceptance;  

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
329 
 
4)  Specify the characteristics of the product that are essential for safe and proper use. 
(b)  The outputs of the design and development process shall be provided in a form that 
enables verification against the design and development inputs and shall be approved 
prior to release.  
(c)  Records of the design and development outputs shall be maintained. 
 
7.3.5 Design and Development Review 
(a)  Systematic reviews of the design and development shall be conducted at appropriate 
stages in accordance with planned and documented methods for the purpose of:  
1)  Evaluating the ability of the design and development results to meet the 
requirements; 
2)  Identifying and proposing any necessary actions. 
(b)  Personnel participating in such reviews shall include not only the persons responsible for 
the design and development stage under review, but also other relevant experts. 
(c)  Records of the results of the reviews and any necessary actions shall be maintained and 
shall include identification of the design under review, the personnel participating in the 
review, and the dates of the review.  
 
7.3.6 Design and Development Verification  
(a)  Design and development verification shall be performed in accordance with planned and 
documented methods to ensure that the design and development outputs meet the input 
requirements.  
(b)  The organization shall document the verification plan, including the verification methods, 
acceptance criteria, and, where applicable, statistical techniques with justification for 
sample size. 
(c)  If the intended use requires the in vitro diagnostic medical device to be connected to or 
interfaced with another in vitro diagnostic medical device, the verification shall include 
confirmation that the design outputs meet the design inputs when so connected or 
interfaced. 
(d)  Records of the verification results, conclusions, and any necessary actions shall be 
maintained.  
 
7.3.7 Design and Development Validation 
(a)  Design and development validation shall be performed, in accordance with planned and 
documented methods, to ensure that the resulting product meets the requirements for the 
intended use or specified application.  
(b)  The organization shall document the validation plan, including the validation methods, 
acceptance criteria, and, where applicable, justification for sample size. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
330 
 
(c)  Design validation shall be performed on core product. Core product includes initial 
production units, batches, or their equivalents. The rationale for the selection of the 
product used for validation shall be recorded. 
(d)  As part of design and development validation, the organization shall perform clinical 
performance studies in accordance with applicable statutory requirements. 
(e)  In vitro diagnostic medical devices used for clinical performance studies shall not be 
considered as released for customer use. 
(f)  If the intended use requires the in vitro diagnostic medical device to be connected to or 
interfaced with another in vitro diagnostic medical device, the validation shall include 
confirmation that the product requirements for the specified application or intended use 
are met when so connected or interfaced.  
(g)  Validation shall be completed prior to the product’s release for customer use.  
(h)  Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, and any necessary actions 
shall be maintained. 
 
7.3.8 Design and Development Transfer 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for the transfer of design and development 
outputs to manufacturing. These procedures shall ensure that the design and development 
outputs have been verified as suitable for manufacturing before becoming the final 
production specifications and that manufacturing capability can meet product 
requirements.  
(b)  Records of the results and conclusions of the transfer shall be maintained. 
 
7.3.9 Control of Design and Development Changes 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for controlling design and development 
changes. The organization shall determine the significance of changes to the function, 
performance, usability, safety, applicable statutory requirements, and intended use of the 
in vitro diagnostic medical device. 
(b)  Design and development changes shall be identified. Prior to implementation, the changes 
shall be: 
1)  Reviewed;  
2)  Verified;  
3)  Validated, where applicable; 
4)  Approved. 
(c)  The review of design and development changes shall include evaluation of the effects of 
the changes on constituent parts, products in manufacturing or already delivered, risk 
management inputs or outputs, and the production realization processes.  
(d)  Records of the changes, the review of the changes, and any necessary actions shall be 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
331 
 
maintained. 
 
7.3.10 Design and Development File 
(a)  The organization shall maintain a design and development file for each in vitro diagnostic 
medical device model or item. 
(b)  This file shall contain or reference the records generated to demonstrate conformity with 
the design and development requirements and the records of design and development 
changes. 
 
7.4.  Purchasing 
7.4.1 Purchasing Process 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures to ensure that purchased product conforms to 
specified requirements. 
(b)  The organization shall establish criteria for the evaluation and selection of suppliers. The 
criteria shall be based on: 
1)  The supplier’s ability to provide product that meets the organization’s requirements; 
2)  The supplier’s performance; 
3)  The effect of the purchased product on the quality of the in vitro diagnostic medical 
device; 
4)  Proportionate to the risks associated with the in vitro diagnostic medical device. 
(c)  The organization shall plan monitoring and re-evaluation of suppliers. The performance 
of suppliers in meeting purchased product requirements shall be monitored. The results of 
monitoring shall be provided as input to the supplier re-evaluation process.  
(d)  Non-fulfillment of purchasing requirements shall be addressed with the supplier in 
proportion to the risks associated with the purchased product and compliance with 
applicable statutory requirements. 
(e)  Records of the results of evaluation, selection, monitoring, and re-evaluation of suppliers 
and of any necessary actions arising from these activities shall be maintained. 
 
7.4.2 Purchasing Information 
(a)  Purchasing information shall describe or reference the product to be purchased, including, 
where appropriate:  
1)  Product specifications; 
2)  Requirements for product approval, procedures, processes, and equipment; 
3)  Requirements for the qualification of supplier personnel; 
4)  Quality management system requirements. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
332 
 
(b)  The organization shall ensure the adequacy of specified purchasing requirements prior to 
communication with the supplier. 
(c)  Purchasing information shall include, where appropriate, a written agreement that the 
supplier notify the organization of any changes to the product prior to implementation if 
such changes may affect the ability of the product to meet specified purchasing 
requirements. 
(d)  The organization shall maintain the relevant purchasing information as documents and 
records to the extent that traceability is required in accordance with Section 7.5.9. 
 
7.4.3 Verification of Purchased Product 
(a)  The organization shall establish and implement the inspection or other activities necessary 
to ensure that purchased product meets specified requirements. The extent of verification 
activities shall be based on the results of supplier evaluation and shall be proportional to 
the risks associated with the purchased product.  
(b)  When the organization becomes aware of any changes to the purchased product, it shall 
determine whether such changes affect the production realization processes or the in vitro 
diagnostic medical device. 
(c)  If the organization or its customer intends to verify the purchased product at the supplier’s 
premises, the organization shall specify in the purchasing information the intended 
verification arrangements and the method of product release.  
(d)  Records of verification shall be maintained. 
 
7.5  Production and Service Provision 
7.5.1 Control of Production and Service Provision 
(a)  Production and service provision shall be planned, carried out, monitored, and controlled 
to ensure that product conforms to specifications. Where appropriate, production control 
shall include, but not be limited to: 
1)  Documentation of procedures and methods for production control; 
2)  Qualification of infrastructure; 
3)  Implementation of monitoring and measurement of process parameters and product 
characteristics; 
4)  Availability and use of monitoring and measuring equipment; 
5)  Implementation of activities specified for labeling and packaging operations; 
6)  Implementation of product release, delivery, and post-delivery activities. 
(b)  The organization shall provide traceability to the extent required in accordance with 
Section 7.5.9 and shall establish and maintain records by in vitro diagnostic medical 
device or by in vitro diagnostic medical device batch that enable identification of the 
quantity produced and approved for distribution. These records shall be verified and 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
333 
 
approved. 
 
7.5.2 Cleanliness of Product 
 
The organization shall document requirements for cleanliness of product or contamination 
control of product in the following cases. Provided, however, that where the product is cleaned 
in accordance with 1) or 2), the requirements of 6.4.1 do not apply prior to the cleaning 
process. 
1)  Product that is cleaned by the organization prior to sterilization or use; 
2)  Product supplied non-sterile that requires a cleaning process prior to sterilization or use; 
3)  Product that cannot be cleaned prior to sterilization or use and for which cleanliness is of 
significant importance for use; 
4)  Product supplied non-sterile for which cleanliness is of significant importance for use; 
5)  Removal of process agents used during manufacturing from the product. 
 
7.5.3 Installation Activities 
(a)  Where applicable, the organization shall document the acceptance criteria for installation 
of the in vitro diagnostic medical device and for its installation verification. 
(b)  Where installation by parties other than the organization or the supplier is permitted by 
the customer, the organization shall provide documented requirements for installation of 
the in vitro diagnostic medical device and for installation verification.  
(c)  Records of installation of the in vitro diagnostic medical device and of installation 
verification performed by the organization or the supplier shall be maintained.  
 
7.5.4 Servicing Activities 
(a)  Where servicing of the in vitro diagnostic medical device is a specified requirement, the 
organization shall document servicing procedures, reference materials, and reference 
measurements, where necessary, for performing servicing activities and for verifying that 
the specified requirements are met.  
(b)  The organization shall analyze records of servicing activities performed by the 
organization or the supplier for the purpose of: 
1)  Determining whether the information should be handled as a complaint; 
2)  Providing, where applicable, input to the improvement processes. 
(c)  Records of servicing activities performed by the organization or the supplier shall be 
maintained.  
 
7.5.5 Particular Requirements for Sterile In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
The organization shall maintain records of the parameters of the sterilization process used for 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
334 
 
each sterilization batch. Sterilization records shall be traceable to each production batch of the 
in vitro diagnostic medical device. 
 
7.5.6 Validation of Processes for Production and Service Provision 
(a)  The organization shall validate any processes for production and service provision where 
the resulting output cannot be verified by subsequent monitoring or measurement. 
Validation shall include all processes where deficiencies become apparent only after the 
product is used or the service is delivered.  
(b)  Validation shall demonstrate the ability of the processes to achieve the planned results 
consistently.  
(c)  The organization shall document procedures for process validation that include:  
1)  Defined criteria for review and approval of the processes; 
2)  Qualification of equipment and personnel; 
3)  Use of specific methods, procedures, and acceptance criteria; 
4)  Statistical techniques, where applicable, including justification for sample size; 
5)  Requirements for records; 
6)  Revalidation, including the criteria for revalidation; 
7)  Approval of changes to the process. 
(d)  The organization shall document procedures for validation of the application of computer 
software used in production and service provision. Such software applications shall be 
validated prior to initial use and, where appropriate, validated after changes or software 
applications have been made. The specific approach and activities related to software 
validation and revalidation shall be proportionate to the risks associated with the use of 
the software, including the impact on product specifications and product performance.  
(e)  Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, and any necessary actions 
resulting from the validation shall be maintained. 
 
7.5.7 Specific Requirements for Validation of Sterilization and Sterile Packaging Processes 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for validation of the sterilization processes 
and the sterile barrier systems. 
(b)  The sterilization processes and the sterile barrier systems shall be validated prior to initial 
use and, where applicable, prior to changes to the product or the process. 
(c)  Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, and any necessary actions 
resulting from the validation shall be maintained. 
 
7.5.8 Identification 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for product identification and shall identify 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
335 
 
the product by suitable means throughout production realization. 
(b)  The organization shall identify the status of product with respect to monitoring and 
measurement requirements throughout production realization. The organization shall 
maintain identification of the status of product to ensure that only product that has passed 
the required tests and inspections, or that has been released under an approved 
concession, is dispatched, used, or installed during all phases of production, storage, 
installation, and servicing. 
(c)  Where required by applicable statutory requirements, the organization shall document a 
system for assigning a unique device identification (UDI) to the in vitro diagnostic 
medical device. 
(d)  The organization shall document procedures to ensure that in vitro diagnostic medical 
devices returned to the organization are identified and distinguished from conforming 
product. 
 
7.5.9 Traceability 
7.5.9.1 General Requirements 
 
The organization shall document procedures for traceability. These procedures shall define the 
scope of traceability and the records to be maintained in accordance with applicable statutory 
requirements. 
 
7.5.9.2 Particular Requirements for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Subject to 
Traceability 
(a)  Where components, materials, or working environment conditions used could cause the in 
vitro diagnostic medical device not to meet specified safety and performance 
requirements, records required for traceability shall include records of the components, 
materials, and working environment conditions used. 
(b)  The organization shall require distributors or retailers to maintain records of sales of the 
in vitro diagnostic medical device and to make such records available for investigation to 
ensure product traceability.  
(c)  The organization shall maintain records of the name and address of the consignee for 
shipped product.  
 
7.5.10 Customer Property 
 
Where customer property provided for use or incorporation into the product is under the 
manufacturer’s control or is being used by the manufacturer, the organization shall identify, 
verify, protect, and safeguard such property. If customer property is lost, damaged, or found to 
be unsuitable for use, this shall be reported to the customer and records shall be maintained. 
  
7.5.11 Preservation of Product 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
336 
 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures to preserve product conformity to 
requirements during processing, storage, handling, and distribution. 
(b)  Preservation shall also apply to components of the in vitro diagnostic medical device. 
(c)  When exposed to expected conditions and hazards during processing, storage, handling, 
and distribution, the organization shall protect the product from alteration, contamination, 
or damage by the following means: 
1)  Designing and constructing appropriate packaging and transportation containers; 
2)  Documenting requirements for any special conditions needed where packaging alone 
does not provide preservation. 
(d)  Where special conditions are necessary, such conditions shall be controlled and recorded.  
 
7.6. Control of Monitoring and Measuring Equipment 
(a)  The organization shall determine the monitoring and measurement activities to be 
performed, and the monitoring and measuring equipment required, to demonstrate that the 
product meets specified requirements. 
(b)  The organization shall document procedures to ensure that monitoring and measurement 
activities are carried out in a manner consistent with the monitoring and measurement 
requirements. 
(c)  Where necessary to ensure valid results, measuring equipment shall: 
1)  Be calibrated or verified, or both, at specified intervals or prior to use, against 
measurement standards traceable to international or national measurement standards. 
Where no such standards exist, the basis used for calibration or verification shall be 
recorded. 
2)  Be adjusted or re-adjusted as necessary. Such adjustments or re-adjustments shall be 
recorded. 
3)  Be identified to enable the calibration status to be determined.  
4)  Be safeguarded from adjustments that would invalidate the measurement result.  
5)  Be protected from damage and deterioration during handling, maintenance, and 
storage. 
(d)  The organization shall calibrate or verify the equipment in accordance with documented 
procedures.  
(e)  When equipment is found not to conform to requirements, the organization shall assess 
the validity of previous measurement results. The organization shall take appropriate 
action regarding the equipment and any product affected. Records of the results of 
calibration and verification shall be maintained. 
(f)  When computer software is used in monitoring or measuring the requirements specified, 
the organization shall document procedures for validation of the application of computer 
software. The software shall be validated prior to initial use and, where appropriate, 
revalidated after changes to the software or its application. The specific approach and 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
337 
 
activities related to software validation and revalidation shall be proportionate to the risks 
associated with the use of the software, including the impact on product specifications and 
product performance.  
(g)  Records of the results of validation, the conclusions reached, and any necessary actions 
resulting from the validation shall be maintained. 
 
8.  Measurement, Analysis and Improvement 
8.1  General Requirements 
(a)  The organization shall plan and implement the monitoring, measurement, analysis, and 
improvement processes needed: 
1)  To demonstrate conformity of the product; 
2)  To ensure conformity of the quality management system; 
3)  To maintain the effectiveness of the quality management system. 
(b)  This shall include determination of the methods, including statistical techniques, and the 
extent of their use.  
 
8.2 Monitoring and Measurement 
8.2.1 Feedback 
(a)  As one of the measurements of the effectiveness of the quality management system, the 
organization shall collect and monitor information relating to whether customer 
requirements have been met.  
(b)  The methods for obtaining and using this information shall be documented. 
(c)  The organization shall document procedures for the feedback process. The feedback 
process shall include provisions for gathering data from production as well as post-
production activities.  
(d)  Information gathered in the feedback process shall be used as potential input to risk 
management in order to monitor and maintain the product requirements and the 
production realization or improvement processes. 
(e)  Where applicable statutory requirements require the organization to collect information 
from post-production activities, review of that information shall be part of the feedback 
process. 
 
8.2.2 Handling of Complaints 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for timely handling of complaints in 
accordance with applicable statutory requirements. These procedures shall include, at a 
minimum, the following requirements and responsibilities: 
1)  Receiving and recording information; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
338 
 
2)  Evaluating information to determine whether feedback constitutes a complaint; 
3)  Investigating complaints; 
4)  Determining whether the information must be reported to the appropriate regulatory 
authorities;  
5)  Handling complaint-related product; 
6)  Determining the need for correction or corrective action. 
(b)  If any complaint is not investigated, the justification for not conducting the investigation 
shall be documented. All results of corrections and corrective actions arising from the 
complaint handling process shall be documented. 
(c)  Where an investigation determines that activities external to the organization caused the 
complaint, relevant information shall be exchanged between the organization and the 
external parties.  
(e)  Records of complaint handling shall be maintained. 
 
8.2.3 Reporting to Regulatory Authorities 
(a)  Where complaints are subject to adverse event reporting or advisory notice reporting in 
accordance with applicable statutory requirements, the organization shall document 
procedures for reporting such complaints to the regulatory authorities.  
(b)  Records of reports submitted to regulatory authorities shall be maintained. 
 
8.2.4 Internal Audit 
(a)  The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to determine whether 
the quality management system: 
1)  Conforms to the planned and documented arrangements, the requirements of this 
GMP, the quality management system requirements established by the organization, 
and the applicable statutory requirements; 
2)  Is effectively implemented and maintained. 
(b)  The organization shall document procedures that define the responsibilities and 
requirements for planning and conducting audits, and for recording and reporting audit 
results. 
(c)  The audit program shall be planned, taking into consideration the status and importance of 
the processes and areas to be audited, as well as the results of previous audits. The audit 
criteria, scope, frequency, and methods shall be defined and recorded. Auditors shall be 
selected and audits conducted to ensure objectivity and impartiality of the audit process. 
Auditors shall not audit their own work. Records of the audit and audit results, including 
the processes and areas audited and the conclusions reached, shall be maintained. 
(d)  Management responsible for the areas being audited shall ensure that necessary 
corrections and corrective actions are taken without undue delay to eliminate detected 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
339 
 
nonconformities and their causes. Follow-up activities shall include the verification of the 
actions taken and the reporting of the results of verification.  
 
8.2.5 Monitoring and Measurement of Processes 
 
The organization shall apply suitable methods for monitoring and, where applicable, 
measurement of the quality management system processes. These methods shall demonstrate 
the ability of the processes to achieve the planned results. When the planned results are not 
achieved, appropriate correction and corrective action shall be taken to ensure conformity of 
the product.  
 
8.2.6 Monitoring and Measurement of Product 
(a)  The organization shall monitor and measure the characteristics of the product to verify 
that product requirements have been met. This shall be carried out at appropriate stages of 
the production realization process in accordance with the planned and documented 
arrangements and documented procedures. 
(b)  Records demonstrating conformity with the acceptance criteria shall be maintained. The 
identity of the person authorizing product release shall be recorded. Where applicable, the 
test equipment used for measurement activities shall be identified and recorded. 
(c)  Product shall not be released, nor shall service be provided, until the planned and 
documented activities have been satisfactorily completed. 
(d)  For in vitro diagnostic medical devices subject to traceability, the organization shall 
identify and record the identity of personnel performing all inspections or tests. 
 
8.3  Control of Nonconforming Product 
8.3.1 General 
(a)  The organization shall ensure that nonconforming product is identified and controlled to 
prevent its unintended use or delivery. The organization shall document procedures that 
define the controls and related responsibilities and authorities for dealing with 
nonconforming product, including identification, documentation, segregation, evaluation, 
and disposition. 
(b)  Evaluation of nonconformities shall include investigation into any external party 
responsible for the nonconformity and determination of whether notification is required. 
(c)  Records of the nonconformity, including the evaluation, investigation, the basis for the 
decisions made, and all actions taken in response, shall be maintained. 
 
8.3.2 Actions in Response to Nonconforming Product Detected Prior to Delivery 
(a)  The organization shall deal with nonconforming product in one or more of the following 
ways:  

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
340 
 
1)  Taking action to eliminate the detected nonconformity; 
2)  Taking action to preclude its original intended use or application; 
3)  Authorizing its use, release, or acceptance under concession. 
(b)  The organization shall ensure that concessions are granted only when justified, approved, 
and compliant with applicable statutory requirements. Records shall be maintained to 
identify acceptance under concession and the personnel authorizing the concession. 
 
8.3.3 Actions in Response to Nonconforming Product Detected After Delivery 
(a)  When nonconforming product is detected after delivery or use, the organization shall take 
appropriate action regarding the effects or potential effects of the nonconformity. Records 
of the actions taken shall be maintained. 
(b)  The organization shall document procedures for issuing advisory notices in accordance 
with applicable statutory requirements. These procedures shall be capable of being 
implemented at any time. Records of the actions related to advisory notices shall be 
maintained. 
 
8.3.4 Rework 
(a)  The organization shall perform rework in accordance with documented procedures that 
consider the potential adverse effects of the rework on the product. These procedures shall 
be subject to the same review and approval as the original procedures.  
(b)  After completion of the rework, the product shall be verified to ensure that it meets the 
applicable acceptance criteria and statutory requirements.  
(c)  Records of the rework shall be maintained. 
 
8.4 Analysis of Data 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures to determine, collect, and analyze 
appropriate data to demonstrate the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the quality 
management system. These procedures shall include the determination of appropriate 
methods, including statistical techniques and the extent of their application. 
(b)  Analysis of data shall include data generated from the results of monitoring and 
measurement and from other relevant sources, and shall include, at a minimum, the 
following inputs: 
1)  Feedback;  
2)  Conformity to product requirements;  
3)  Process and product characteristics and trends, including opportunities for 
improvement; 
4)  Suppliers; 
5)  Audits; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
341 
 
6)  Service reports, where applicable. 
(c)  Where analysis of data shows that the quality management system is not suitable, 
adequate, or effective, the organization shall use this analysis as input for improvement as 
required in 8.5.  
(d)  Records of the results of data analysis shall be maintained.  
 
8.5 Improvement 
8.5.1 General Requirements 
 
The organization shall identify and implement any changes necessary to ensure and maintain 
the ongoing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the quality management system, as well 
as the safety and performance of in vitro diagnostic medical devices, through the use of the 
quality policy, quality objectives, audit results, post-marketing surveillance, data analysis, 
corrective and preventive actions, and management review.  
 
8.5.2 Corrective Action 
(a)  The organization shall take action to eliminate the causes of nonconformities in order to 
prevent their recurrence. 
(b)  Corrective actions required shall be taken without undue delay. Corrective actions shall be 
proportionate to the effects of the nonconformities encountered. 
(c)  Documented procedures shall define requirements for:  
1)  Reviewing nonconformities (including customer complaints); 
2)  Determining the causes of nonconformities; 
3)  Evaluating the need for action to ensure that nonconformities do not recur; 
4)  Planning and documenting the required actions and implementing them, including 
document changes where applicable;  
5)  Verifying that corrective actions do not adversely affect the safety and performance 
of the in vitro diagnostic medical device or compliance with applicable statutory 
requirements;  
6)  Reviewing the effectiveness of the corrective actions taken. 
(d)  Records of all investigation results and actions taken shall be maintained.  
 
8.5.3 Preventive Action 
(a)  The organization shall determine preventive actions to eliminate the causes of potential 
nonconformities in order to prevent their occurrence. Preventive actions shall be 
proportionate to the potential impacts of such issues.  
(b)  Documented procedures shall define requirements for:  
1)  Determining potential nonconformities and their causes; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
342 
 
2)  Evaluating the need for action to prevent the occurrence of nonconformities; 
3)  Planning and documenting the required actions and determining and implementing 
such actions, including document changes where applicable; 
4)  Verifying that preventive actions do not adversely affect the safety and performance 
of the in vitro diagnostic medical device or compliance with applicable statutory 
requirements;  
5)  Reviewing the effectiveness of preventive actions taken, where applicable. 
(c)  Records of the results of all investigations and actions taken shall be maintained.  
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices

4.  Quality 
Management 
System 
4.1  General 
Requirements 
4.1.1 
(a)  The organization shall document its quality 
management system in accordance with the 
requirements of this GMP and applicable 
statutory requirements, and shall maintain the 
effectiveness of the quality management 
system. 
(b)  The organization shall establish, implement, 
and maintain specific requirements, procedures, 
activities, or methods of operation that must be 
documented pursuant to this GMP and 
applicable statutory requirements. 
(c)  The organization shall document the roles 
required to perform in accordance with 
applicable statutory requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
4.1.2 
The organization shall implement the following: 
1)  Determine the processes necessary for the 
quality management system, taking into 
account the roles performed by the 
organization, and apply those processes 
throughout the organization; 
2)  Apply a risk-based approach to the appropriate 
management of processes required for the 
quality management system; 
3)  Determine the sequence and interaction of 
those processes. 
 
 
 
 
 
4.1.3 
For each processes of the quality management 
system, the organization shall perform the 
following: 
1)  Determine the criteria and methods necessary 
to ensure the effective operation and control of 
the processes; 
2)  Ensure the availability of information and 
resources necessary to support the operation 
and monitoring of the processes; 
3)  Take necessary actions to achieve planned 
results and maintain the effectiveness of the 
processes; 
4)  Monitor such processes and, where applicable, 
measure and analyze them; 
5)  Prepare and maintain the records necessary to

requirements. 
4.1.4 
The organization shall control quality management 
system processes in conformity with this GMP and 
applicable statutory requirements. Where such 
processes are to be changed, the organization shall 
perform the following: 
1)  Evaluate whether the change to the process 
affects the quality management system; 
2)  Evaluate whether the change to the process 
affects the in vitro diagnostic medical devices 
produced under the quality management 
system; 
3)  Control such matters in accordance with this 
GMP and applicable statutory requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
4.1.5 
(a)  Where the organization outsources any process 
that affects product conformity requirements, it 
shall ensure that such processes are monitored 
and controlled. 
(b)  The organization shall retain responsibility for 
ensuring compliance with this GMP, customer 
requirements, and applicable statutory 
requirements for outsourced processes. 
(c)  Control of outsourced processes shall be 
proportionate to the associated risks and to the 
capability of the contracted supplier to meet the 
requirements under paragraph 7.4, and shall 
include a written quality agreement.

5)  Installation requirements, where applicable; 
6)  Servicing procedures, where applicable. 
4.2.4 Control of 
Documents 
(a)  Documents required by the quality 
management system shall be controlled. 
Records are a special type of document and 
shall be controlled in accordance with Section 
4.2.5. 
(b)  Procedures necessary to control the following 
shall be documented: 
1)  Review and approval of documents for 
adequacy prior to issuance; 
2)  Review, update, and re-approval of documents 
as necessary; 
3)  Ensure that changes to documents and the 
current revision status are identified; 
4)  Ensure that applicable versions of documents 
are available at points of use; 
5)  Ensure that documents remain legible and 
readily identifiable; 
6)  Ensure that documents of external origin 
determined by the organization to be necessary 
for the planning and operation of the quality 
management system are identified and their 
distribution controlled; 
7)  Prevent deterioration or loss of documents; 
8)  Preventing the unintended use of obsolete 
documents and applying appropriate 
identification if they are retained for any 
purpose. 
(c)  The organization shall ensure that document 
changes are reviewed and approved by the 
original approving authority or other authorized 
personnel who have access to the background 
information on which the organization’s 
decisions are based. 
(d)  The organization shall retain at least one copy 
of obsolete controlled documents for a period 
corresponding to the product’s life cycle, which 
shall be no less than the retention period

required for records. 
4.2.5 Control of 
Records 
(a)  Records shall be established and maintained to 
demonstrate the effective operation of the 
quality management system and conformity to 
requirements. 
(b)  The organization shall document procedures 
defining the controls needed for the 
identification, storage, security and integrity, 
retrieval, retention period, and disposition of 
records. 
(c)  The organization shall establish and implement 
methods to protect personal health information 
contained in records in accordance with 
applicable statutory requirements. 
(d)  All records shall be easily legible, readily 
identifiable, and retrievable. Any changes to 
records shall remain identifiable. 
(e)  The organization shall retain records for a 
period corresponding to the product’s life cycle. 
This period shall be at least five years from the 
date of manufacture and at least two years after 
release to the market. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.  Management 
Responsibility 
5.1  Management 
Commitment 
Top management shall demonstrate its commitment 
to the development and implementation of the 
quality management system and to maintaining its 
effectiveness through the following: 
1)  Communicate the importance of fulfilling 
customer requirements and applicable statutory 
requirements with the organization; 
2)  Establish the quality policy; 
3)  Ensure that quality objectives are established; 
4)  Conduct management reviews; 
5)  Ensure the availability of resources. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.2  Customer Focus 
Top management shall ensure that customer 
requirements and applicable statutory requirements 
are determined and fulfilled. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.3  Quality Policy 
Top management shall ensure that the quality policy: 
1)  Is appropriate to the purpose of the 
organization; 
2)  Includes a commitment to comply with 
requirements and to maintain the effectiveness
