of the quality management system; 
3)  Provides a framework for establishing and 
reviewing quality objectives; 
4)  Is communicated and understood within the 
organization; 
5)  Is reviewed for continuing suitability. 
5.4  Planning 
5.4.1 Quality 
Objectives 
(a)  Top management shall ensure that the quality 
objectives include the necessary elements to 
meet applicable statutory requirements and 
product requirements, and that they are 
established at relevant functions and levels 
within the organization. 
(b)  The quality objectives shall be measurable and 
shall be consistent with the quality policy. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.4.2 Planning of the 
Quality 
Management 
System 
Top management shall ensure the following: 
1)  The planning of the quality management 
system is carried out not only to achieve the 
quality objectives but also to meet the 
requirements of Section 4.1; 
2)  The integrity of the quality management system 
is maintained when changes to the quality 
management system are planned and 
implemented. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.5  Responsibility, 
Authority, and 
Communication 
5.5.1 Responsibility 
and Authority 
(a)  Top management shall ensure that 
responsibilities and authorities within the 
organization are defined, documented, and 
communicated. 
(b)  Top management shall document the 
interrelationships of all personnel who manage, 
perform, and verify work affecting quality, and 
shall ensure the authority and independence 
necessary to perform such work. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.5.2 Quality Manager 
Top management shall appoint a person within the 
organization who, irrespective of other 
responsibilities, has the authority and responsibility 
to perform the following: 
1)  Ensure that the processes necessary for the 
quality management system are documented; 
2)  Report to top management on the performance 
and effectiveness of the quality management 
system and on the need for improvement;

5.5.3 Internal

Top management shall ensure that appropriate 
communication processes are established within the 
organization and that communication regarding the 
effectiveness of the quality management system is 
carried out. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.6  Management 
Review 
5.6.1 General 
Requirements 
(a)  The organization shall document the procedure 
for management review. 
(b)  Top management shall review the quality 
management system at documented planned 
intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, 
adequacy, and effectiveness. 
(c)  Management reviews shall include an 
evaluation of the need for changes and 
opportunities for improvement in the quality 
management system, including the quality 
policy and quality objectives. 
(d)  Records of management reviews shall be 
maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
5.6.2 Review Inputs 
The inputs to management review shall include, but

1)  Feedback; 
2)  Handling of complaints; 
3)  Reports to regulatory authorities; 
4)  Audits; 
5)  Monitoring and measurement of processes; 
6)  Monitoring and measurement of product; 
7)  Corrective action; 
8)  Preventive action; 
9)  Follow-up actions from previous management 
reviews; 
10)  Changes that could affect the quality 
management system; 
11)  Recommendations for improvement; 
12)  New or revised applicable statutory 
requirements.

6.  Resource 
Management 
6.1 Provision of 
Resources 
The organization shall determine and provide the 
resources needed for: 
1)  Implementing the quality management system 
and maintaining its effectiveness; 
2)  Meeting applicable regulatory requirements 
and customer requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
6.2  Human 
Resources 
(a)  Personnel performing work affecting product 
quality shall be competent on the basis of 
appropriate education, training, skills, and 
experience. 
(b)  The organization shall establish the 
competencies required of personnel, provide 
the necessary training, and establish and 
document processes to ensure personnel 
awareness. 
(c)  The organization shall perform the following: 
1)  Determine the competencies needed for 
personnel performing work that affects product 
quality; 
2)  Provide training or take other actions to achieve 
or maintain the necessary competencies; 
3)  Evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken; 
4)  Ensure that personnel are aware of the 
relevance and importance of their activities and 
how they contribute to the achievement of 
quality objectives; 
5)  Maintain appropriate records of education, 
training, skills, and experience. 
 
 
 
 
 
6.3  Infrastructure 
(a)  The organization shall document the 
infrastructure requirements necessary to ensure 
conformity to product requirements, prevent

7.  Production 
Realization 
7.1  Planning of 
Production 
Realization 
(a)  The organization shall plan and develop the 
processes needed for production realization. 
Planning of production realization shall be 
consistent with the other process requirements 
of the quality management system. 
(b)  The organization shall document one or more 
processes for risk management during 
production realization, and records of risk 
management activities shall be maintained. 
(c)  Where applicable, the organization shall 
determine the following in planning production 
realization: 
1)  Quality objectives and requirements for the 
product; 
2)  The need to establish and document processes, 
and to ensure the availability of specific 
resources for the product, including 
infrastructure and work environment; 
3)  Specific verification, validation, monitoring, 
measurement, testing and inspection, handling, 
storage, distribution, and traceability activities 
required for the product, along with the criteria 
for product acceptance; 
4)  Records necessary to demonstrate that 
production realization processes and their 
outputs meet requirements. 
(d)  The outputs of such planning shall be 
documented in a form appropriate to the 
organization’s method of operation.

7.3. Design and 
Development 
7.3.1 General 
The organization shall document procedures for 
design and development. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.2 Design and 
Development 
Planning 
(a)  The organization shall plan and control the 
design and development of the product. Where 
applicable, the design and development plan 
shall be maintained and updated as design and 
development progress. 
(b)  The organization shall document the following 
in the course of design and development 
planning: 
1)  The stages of design and development; 
2)  The reviews required at each stage of design 
and development; 
3)  The verification, validation, and design transfer 
activities appropriate to each stage of design 
and development; 
4)  The responsibilities and authorities for design 
and development; 
5)  The methods to ensure traceability between 
design and development inputs and outputs; 
6)  The necessary resources, including personnel 
competence. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.3 Design and 
Development 
Inputs 
(a)  The organization shall determine and maintain 
records of inputs relating to product 
requirements. These inputs shall include: 
1)  Functional, performance, usability, and safety 
requirements necessary for the intended use; 
2)  Applicable statutory requirements and 
standards; 
3)  Applicable risk management outputs; 
4)  Information derived from previous similar 
designs, where applicable; 
5)  Other requirements essential for the design and 
development of the product and process. 
(b)  Such inputs shall be reviewed and approved for 
adequacy. 
(c)  Product requirements shall be clear,

7.3.4 Design and

Outputs 
(a)  The design and development outputs shall: 
1)  Meet the design and development input 
requirements; 
2)  Provide appropriate information for purchasing, 
production, and service provision; 
3)  Include or reference the criteria for product 
acceptance; 
4)  Specify the characteristics of the product that 
are essential for safe and proper use. 
(b)  The outputs of the design and development 
process shall be provided in a form that enables 
verification against the design and development 
inputs and shall be approved prior to release. 
(c)  Records of the design and development outputs 
shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.5 Design and 
Development 
Review 
(a)  Systematic reviews of the design and 
development shall be conducted at appropriate 
stages in accordance with planned and 
documented methods for the purpose of: 
1)  Evaluating the ability of the design and 
development results to meet the requirements; 
2)  Identifying and proposing any necessary 
actions. 
(b)  Personnel participating in such reviews shall 
include not only the persons responsible for the 
design and development stage under review, 
but also other relevant experts. 
(c)  Records of the results of the reviews and any 
necessary actions shall be maintained and shall 
include identification of the design under 
review, the personnel participating in the 
review, and the dates of the review. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.3.6 Design and 
Development 
Verification 
(a)  Design and development verification shall be 
performed in accordance with planned and

and development outputs meet the input 
requirements.

(e)  In vitro diagnostic medical devices used for

7.3.9 Control of 
Design and 
Development 
Changes 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for 
controlling design and development changes. 
The organization shall determine the 
significance of changes to the function, 
performance, usability, safety, applicable 
statutory requirements, and intended use of the 
in vitro diagnostic medical device. 
(b)  Design and development changes shall be 
identified. Prior to implementation, the changes 
shall be: 
1)  Reviewed; 
2)  Verified; 
3)  Validated, where applicable; 
4)  Approved. 
(c)  The review of design and development changes 
shall include evaluation of the effects of the 
changes on constituent parts, products in 
manufacturing or already delivered, risk 
management inputs or outputs, and the 
production realization processes. 
(d)  Records of the changes, the review of the 
changes, and any necessary actions shall be 
maintained.

Development File

7.4. Purchasing 
7.4.1 Purchasing 
Process 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures to 
ensure that purchased product conforms to 
specified requirements. 
(b)  The organization shall establish criteria for the 
evaluation and selection of suppliers. The 
criteria shall be based on: 
1)  The supplier’s ability to provide product that 
meets the organization’s requirements; 
2)  The supplier’s performance; 
3)  The effect of the purchased product on the 
quality of the in vitro diagnostic medical 
device; 
4)  Proportionate to the risks associated with the in 
vitro diagnostic medical device. 
(c)  The organization shall plan monitoring and re-
evaluation of suppliers. The performance of 
suppliers in meeting purchased product 
requirements shall be monitored. The results of 
monitoring shall be provided as input to the 
supplier re-evaluation process. 
(d)  Non-fulfillment of purchasing requirements 
shall be addressed with the supplier in 
proportion to the risks associated with the 
purchased product and compliance with 
applicable statutory requirements. 
(e)  Records of the results of evaluation, selection, 
monitoring, and re-evaluation of suppliers and 
of any necessary actions arising from these 
activities shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.4.2 Purchasing 
Information 
(a)  Purchasing information shall describe or 
reference the product to be purchased, 
including, where appropriate: 
1)  Product specifications; 
2)  Requirements for product approval, procedures, 
processes, and equipment; 
3)  Requirements for the qualification of supplier 
personnel; 
4)  Quality management system requirements. 
(b)  The organization shall ensure the adequacy of 
 
 
 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices 
 
364 
 
GMP Criteria 
Requirements 
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment 
Result 
Remarks 
A B C D 
specified purchasing requirements prior to 
communication with the supplier. 
(c)  Purchasing information shall include, where 
appropriate, a written agreement that the 
supplier notify the organization of any changes 
to the product prior to implementation if such 
changes may affect the ability of the product to 
meet specified purchasing requirements. 
(d)  The organization shall maintain the relevant 
purchasing information as documents and 
records to the extent that traceability is required 
in accordance with Section 7.5.9. 
7.4.3 Verification of 
Purchased 
Product 
(a)  The organization shall establish and implement 
the inspection or other activities necessary to 
ensure that purchased product meets specified 
requirements. The extent of verification 
activities shall be based on the results of 
supplier evaluation and shall be proportional to 
the risks associated with the purchased product. 
(b) When the organization becomes aware of 
any changes to the purchased product, it shall 
determine whether such changes affect the 
production realization processes or the in vitro 
diagnostic medical device. 
(c)  If the organization or its customer intends to 
verify the purchased product at the supplier’s 
premises, the organization shall specify in the 
purchasing information the intended 
verification arrangements and the method of 
product release. 
(d)  Records of verification shall be maintained.

(a)  Production and service provision shall be

7.5.2 Cleanliness of 
Product 
The organization shall document requirements for 
cleanliness of product or contamination control of 
product in the following cases. Provided, however, 
that where the product is cleaned in accordance with 
1) or 2), the requirements of 6.4.1 do not apply prior 
to the cleaning process. 
1)  Product that is cleaned by the organization 
prior to sterilization or use; 
2)  Product supplied non-sterile that requires a 
cleaning process prior to sterilization or use; 
3)  Product that cannot be cleaned prior to 
sterilization or use and for which cleanliness is 
of significant importance for use; 
4)  Product supplied non-sterile for which 
cleanliness is of significant importance for use; 
5)  Removal of process agents used during 
manufacturing from the product.

7.5.4 Servicing 
Activities 
(a)  Where servicing of the in vitro diagnostic 
medical device is a specified requirement, the

(b)  The organization shall analyze records of

2)  Providing, where applicable, input to the

(c)  Records of servicing activities performed by 
the organization or the supplier shall be 
maintained.

The organization shall maintain records of the

sterilization batch. Sterilization records shall be 
traceable to each production batch of the in vitro 
diagnostic medical device. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.6 Validation of 
Processes for 
Production and

(a)  The organization shall validate any processes 
for production and service provision where the 
resulting output cannot be verified by 
subsequent monitoring or measurement. 
Validation shall include all processes where 
deficiencies become apparent only after the 
product is used or the service is delivered. 
(b)  Validation shall demonstrate the ability of the 
processes to achieve the planned results 
consistently. 
(c)  The organization shall document procedures for 
process validation that include: 
1)  Defined criteria for review and approval of the 
processes;

2)  the suitability of equipment and personnel;

4)  Statistical techniques, where applicable, 
including justification for sample size; 
5)  Requirements for records; 
6)  Revalidation, including the criteria for 
revalidation; 
7)  Approval of changes to the process. 
(d)  The organization shall document procedures for 
validation of the application of computer 
software used in production and service

validated prior to initial use and, where

(e)  Records of the results of validation, the 
conclusions reached, and any necessary actions 
resulting from the validation shall be 
maintained.

(a)  The organization shall document procedures for

(b)  The sterilization processes and the sterile 
barrier systems shall be validated prior to initial 
use and, where applicable, prior to changes to 
the product or the process. 
(c)  Records of the results of validation, the 
conclusions reached, and any necessary actions 
resulting from the validation shall be 
maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.8 Identification 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for 
product identification and shall identify the 
product by suitable means throughout 
production realization.

(b)  The organization shall identify the status of 
product with respect to monitoring and

production realization. The organization shall 
maintain identification of the status of product 
to ensure that only product that has passed the 
required tests and inspections, or that has been 
released under an approved concession, is 
dispatched, used, or installed during all phases

(c)  Where required by applicable statutory

(d)  The organization shall document procedures to 
ensure that in vitro diagnostic medical devices 
returned to the organization are identified and 
distinguished from conforming product. 
7.5.9 Traceability 
7.5.9.1 General 
Requirements 
The organization shall document procedures for 
traceability. These procedures shall define the scope 
of traceability and the records to be maintained in 
accordance with applicable statutory requirements. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.5.9.2 Particular 
Requirements for 
In Vitro 
Diagnostic 
Medical Devices 
Subject to 
Traceability 
(a)  Where components, materials, or working 
environment conditions used could cause the in 
vitro diagnostic medical device not to meet 
specified safety and performance requirements, 
records required for traceability shall include 
records of the components, materials, and 
working environment conditions used. 
(b)  The organization shall require distributors or 
retailers to maintain records of sales of the in 
vitro diagnostic medical device and to make 
such records available for investigation to 
ensure product traceability. 
(c)  The organization shall maintain records of the 
name and address of the consignee for shipped 
product.

Property 
Where customer property provided for use or 
incorporation into the product is under the

manufacturer’s control or is being used by the

protect, and safeguard such property. If customer 
property is lost, damaged, or found to be unsuitable 
for use, this shall be reported to the customer and 
records shall be maintained. 
7.5.11 Preservation of 
Product 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures to 
preserve product conformity to requirements 
during processing, storage, handling, and 
distribution. 
(b)  Preservation shall also apply to components of 
the in vitro diagnostic medical device. 
(c)  When exposed to expected conditions and 
hazards during processing, storage, handling, 
and distribution, the organization shall protect 
the product from alteration, contamination, or 
damage by the following means: 
1)  Designing and constructing appropriate 
packaging and transportation containers; 
2)  Documenting requirements for any special 
conditions needed where packaging alone does 
not provide preservation. 
(d)  Where special conditions are necessary, such 
conditions shall be controlled and recorded. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.6  Control of 
Monitoring and 
Measuring 
Equipment 
(a)  The organization shall determine the 
monitoring and measurement activities to be 
performed, and the monitoring and measuring 
equipment required, to demonstrate that the 
product meets specified requirements. 
(b)  The organization shall document procedures to 
ensure that monitoring and measurement 
activities are carried out in a manner consistent 
with the monitoring and measurement 
requirements. 
(c)  Where necessary to ensure valid results, 
measuring equipment shall: 
1)  Be calibrated or verified, or both, at specified 
intervals or prior to use, against measurement 
standards traceable to international or national 
measurement standards; Where no such 
standards exist, the basis used for calibration or

GMP Criteria

verification shall be recorded; 
2)  Be adjusted or re-adjusted as necessary. Such 
adjustments or re-adjustments shall be 
recorded; 
3)  Be identified to enable the calibration status to 
be determined; 
4)  Be safeguarded from adjustments that would 
invalidate the measurement result; 
5)  Be protected from damage and deterioration 
during handling, maintenance, and storage. 
(d)  The organization shall calibrate or verify the 
equipment in accordance with documented 
procedures. 
(e)  When equipment is found not to conform to 
requirements, the organization shall assess the

organization shall take appropriate action 
regarding the equipment and any product 
affected. Records of the results of calibration 
and verification shall be maintained. 
(f)  When computer software is used in monitoring 
or measuring the requirements specified, the

software. The software shall be validated prior 
to initial use and, where appropriate, 
revalidated after changes to the software or its 
application. The specific approach and 
activities related to software validation and 
revalidation shall be proportionate to the risks 
associated with the use of the software, 
including the impact on product specifications 
and product performance. 
(g)  Records of the results of validation, the 
conclusions reached, and any necessary actions 
resulting from the validation shall be 
maintained.

1)  To demonstrate conformity of the product;

8.2  Monitoring and 
Measurement 
8.2.1 Feedback 
(a)  As one of the measurements of the 
effectiveness of the quality management 
system, the organization shall collect and 
monitor information relating to whether 
customer requirements have been met. 
(b)  The methods for obtaining and using this 
information shall be documented. 
(c)  The organization shall document procedures for 
the feedback process. The feedback process 
shall include provisions for gathering data from 
production as well as post-production activities. 
(d)  Information gathered in the feedback process 
shall be used as potential input to risk 
management in order to monitor and maintain 
the product requirements and the production 
realization or improvement processes. 
(e)  Where applicable statutory requirements 
require the organization to collect information 
from post-production activities, review of that 
information shall be part of the feedback 
process. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.2.2 Handling of 
Complaints 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for 
timely handling of complaints in accordance 
with applicable statutory requirements. These 
procedures shall include, at a minimum, the 
following requirements and responsibilities: 
1)  Receiving and recording information; 
2)  Evaluating information to determine whether 
feedback constitutes a complaint; 
3)  Investigating complaints; 
4)  Determining whether the information must be 
reported to the appropriate regulatory 
authorities; 
5)  Handling complaint-related product; 
6)  Determining the need for correction or

(b)  If any complaint is not investigated, the

of corrections and corrective actions arising 
from the complaint handling process shall be 
documented. 
(c)  Where an investigation determines that 
activities external to the organization caused 
the complaint, relevant information shall be 
exchanged between the organization and the 
external parties. 
(e)  Records of complaint handling shall be 
maintained. 
8.2.3 Reporting to 
Regulatory 
Authorities 
(a)  Where complaints are subject to adverse event 
reporting or advisory notice reporting in 
accordance with applicable statutory 
requirements, the organization shall document 
procedures for reporting such complaints to the 
regulatory authorities. 
(b)  Records of reports submitted to regulatory 
authorities shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.2.4 Internal Audit 
(a)  The organization shall conduct internal audits 
at planned intervals to determine whether the 
quality management system: 
1)  Conforms to the planned and documented 
(established, implemented, and maintained) 
arrangements, the requirements of this GMP, 
the quality management system requirements 
established by the organization, and the 
applicable statutory requirements; 
2)  Is effectively implemented and maintained. 
(b)  The organization shall document procedures 
that define the responsibilities and requirements 
for planning and conducting audits, and for 
recording and reporting audit results. 
(c)  The audit program shall be planned, taking into 
consideration the status and importance of the 
processes and areas to be audited, as well as the 
results of previous audits. The audit criteria, 
scope, frequency, and methods shall be defined

not audit their own work. Records of the audit

be maintained. 
(d)  Management responsible for the areas being

and corrective actions are taken without undue 
delay to eliminate detected nonconformities 
and their causes. Follow-up activities shall 
include the verification of the actions taken and 
the reporting of the results of verification. 
8.2.5 Monitoring and

The organization shall apply suitable methods for 
monitoring and, where applicable, measurement of 
the quality management system processes. These 
methods shall demonstrate the ability of the 
processes to achieve the planned results. When the 
planned results are not achieved, appropriate 
correction and corrective action shall be taken to 
ensure conformity of the product. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.2.6 Monitoring and 
Measurement of 
Product 
(a)  The organization shall monitor and measure the 
characteristics of the product to verify that 
product requirements have been met. This shall 
be carried out at appropriate stages of the 
production realization process in accordance 
with the planned and documented arrangements 
and documented procedures. 
(b)  Records demonstrating conformity with the 
acceptance criteria shall be maintained. The 
identity of the person authorizing product 
release shall be recorded. Where applicable, the 
test equipment used for measurement activities 
shall be identified and recorded. 
(c)  Product shall not be released, nor shall service 
be provided, until the planned and documented 
activities have been satisfactorily completed. 
(d)  For in vitro diagnostic medical devices subject 
to traceability, the organization shall identify 
and record the identity of personnel performing

8.3  Control of 
Nonconforming 
Product 
8.3.1 General 
(a)  The organization shall ensure that 
nonconforming product is identified and 
controlled to prevent its unintended use or 
delivery. The organization shall document 
procedures that define the controls and related 
responsibilities and authorities for dealing with 
nonconforming product, including 
identification, documentation, segregation, 
evaluation, and disposition. 
(b)  Evaluation of nonconformities shall include 
investigation into any external party 
responsible for the nonconformity and 
determination of whether notification is 
required. 
(c)  Records of the nonconformity, including the 
evaluation, investigation, the basis for the 
decisions made, and all actions taken in 
response, shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.3.2 Actions in 
Response to 
Nonconforming 
Product Detected 
Prior to Delivery 
(a)  The organization shall deal with 
nonconforming product in one or more of the 
following ways: 
1)  Taking action to eliminate the detected 
nonconformity; 
2)  Taking action to preclude its original intended 
use or application; 
3)  Authorizing its use, release, or acceptance 
under concession. 
(b)  The organization shall ensure that concessions 
are granted only when justified, approved, and 
compliant with applicable statutory 
requirements. Records shall be maintained to 
identify acceptance under concession and the 
personnel authorizing the concession. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.3.3 Actions in 
Response to 
Nonconforming 
Product Detected 
After Delivery 
(a)  When nonconforming product is detected after 
delivery or use, the organization shall take 
appropriate action regarding the effects or 
potential effects of the nonconformity. Records 
of the actions taken shall be maintained. 
(b)  The organization shall document procedures for 
issuing advisory notices in accordance with

Requirements 
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment 
Result

applicable statutory requirements. These 
procedures shall be capable of being 
implemented at any time. Records of the 
actions related to advisory notices shall be 
maintained. 
8.3.4 Rework 
(a)  The organization shall perform rework in 
accordance with documented procedures that 
take into account any potential adverse effects 
on the product. These procedures shall be 
subject to the same review and approval as the 
original procedures. 
(b)  After completion of the rework, the product 
shall be verified to ensure that it meets the 
applicable acceptance criteria and statutory 
requirements. 
(c)  Records of the rework shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.4  Analysis of Data 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures to 
determine, collect, and analyze appropriate data 
to demonstrate the suitability, adequacy, and 
effectiveness of the quality management 
system. These procedures shall include the 
determination of appropriate methods, 
including statistical techniques and the extent 
of their application. 
(b)  Analysis of data shall include data generated 
from the results of monitoring and 
measurement and from other relevant sources, 
and shall include, at a minimum, the following 
inputs: 
1)  Feedback; 
2)  Conformity to product requirements; 
3)  Process and product characteristics and trends, 
including opportunities for improvement; 
4)  Suppliers; 
5)  Audits; 
6)  Service reports, where applicable. 
(c)  Where analysis of data shows that the quality 
management system is not suitable, adequate, 
or effective, the organization shall use this 
analysis as input for improvement as required 
in 8.5.

8.5  Improvement 
8.5.1 General 
Requirements 
The organization shall identify and implement any 
changes necessary to ensure and maintain the 
ongoing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of 
the quality management system, as well as the safety 
and performance of in vitro diagnostic medical 
devices, through the use of the quality policy, 
quality objectives, audit results, post-marketing 
surveillance, data analysis, corrective and preventive 
actions, and management review. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.5.2 Corrective 
Action 
(a)  The organization shall take action to eliminate 
the causes of nonconformities in order to 
prevent their recurrence. 
(b)  Corrective actions required shall be taken 
without undue delay. Corrective actions shall 
be proportionate to the effects of the 
nonconformities encountered. 
(c)  Documented procedures shall define 
requirements for: 
1)  Reviewing nonconformities (including 
customer complaints); 
2)  Determining the causes of nonconformities; 
3)  Evaluating the need for action to ensure that 
nonconformities do not recur; 
4)  Planning and documenting the required actions 
and implementing them, including document 
changes where applicable; 
5)  Verifying that corrective actions do not 
adversely affect the safety and performance of 
the in vitro diagnostic medical device or 
compliance with applicable statutory 
requirements; 
6)  Reviewing the effectiveness of the corrective 
actions taken. 
(d)  Records of all investigation results and actions 
taken shall be maintained. 
 
 
 
 
 
8.5.3 Preventive 
Action 
(a)  The organization shall determine preventive 
actions to eliminate the causes of potential 
nonconformities in order to prevent their 
occurrence. Preventive actions shall be

GMP Criteria 
Requirements 
Assessment Criteria 
Assessment 
Result 
Remarks 
A B C D 
proportionate to the potential impacts of such 
issues. 
(b)  Documented procedures shall define 
requirements for: 
1)  Determining potential nonconformities and 
their causes; 
2)  Evaluating the need for action to prevent the 
occurrence of nonconformities; 
3)  Planning and documenting the required actions 
and determining and implementing such 
actions, including document changes where 
applicable; 
4)  Verifying that preventive actions do not 
adversely affect the safety and performance of 
the in vitro diagnostic medical device or 
compliance with applicable statutory 
requirements; 
5)  Reviewing the effectiveness of preventive 
actions taken, where applicable. 
(c)  Records of the results of all investigations and 
actions taken shall be maintained. 
 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices

1.  Assessment Sheet 
(a)  “A (Conforming)” means that the requirements prescribed in the Good Manufacturing 
Practice (GMP) are recognized as being met. 
(b)  “B (Additional action required)” means that the requirements prescribed in the Good 
Manufacturing Practice (GMP) are not being fully met, or that although the requirements 
are being met, the evidence of conformance, feasibility of implementation, or adequacy 
of documentation is insufficient, thereby requiring improvement or supplementary 
actions. 
(c)  “C (Nonconforming)” means that no action has been taken in response to “Additional 
action required,” or that a violation of statutes related to in vitro diagnostic medical 
devices has occurred. 
(d)  “D (Not applicable)” means that the requirement prescribed in the Good Manufacturing 
Practice (GMP) does not apply. 
 
2.  Determination Criteria 
(a)  Conforming 
1)  Where all items under each review criterion are rated “A (Conforming).” 
2)  Where all other items under each review criterion are rated “A (Conforming),” and 
certain sections—specifically Sections 4.1 through 6.3 (excluding Section 4.2.3) 
and Section 8.2.4—are rated “B (Additional action required).” Provided, however, 
that this shall not apply where the same item was rated “B (Additional action 
required)” or “C (Nonconforming)” in the previous assessment. 
(b)  Additional action required 
 
Where all other items under each assessment criterion are rated “A (Conforming),” and 
some items are rated “B (Additional action required)” (provided, however, that this does 
not apply to cases under item (a) 2)). 
(c)  Nonconforming 
1)  Where the required actions have not been submitted or have not been completed. 
2)  Where one or more items are rated “C (Nonconforming)” in the evaluation sheet.

Marking of Conformity Recognition Assessment 
(Related to Article 11) 
 
1.  Design of the conformity recognition assessment mark 
(a)  Design 
 
(b)  Size ratio: Width × Height = 1 × 0.83 
(c)  Color code: Pantone 2736CVC 
 
2.  Methods and standards for marking 
(a)  The mark for conformity recognition assessment shall be applied based on the size and 
color specified in item (a), and may be used in various sizes (with the same proportions) 
and colors suitable for the characteristics of the product and its packaging materials; 
provided that the design of the mark shall not be altered. 
(b)  The method of the conformity recognition assessment marking in item (a) may follow the 
labeling requirements under Articles 13 through 15 of the Act on In Vitro Diagnostic 
Medical Devices, and the mark may be affixed to one or more of the following: the 
container, outer packaging, external package, or package insert.

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
397 
 
 
Standards of Good Manufacturing Practice 
(GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
[Enforced on April 21, 2025] 
 [Ministry of Food and Drug Safety Notice No. 2025-28; Apr. 21, 2025; Enacted] 
Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (Medical Device Policy Division)  
 
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this GMP is to prescribe the specific requirements to be 
observed for the manufacture or import of digital medical devices pursuant to Articles 5 (1), 8 (4), 9 
(3), 11 (1), 12 (3), and 24, 25, and 48 of the Digital Medical Products Act, and Articles 12, 14, 19, 
24, 25, 27, 34, 35, and 54 of the Enforcement Rule of the same Act. 
 
Article 2 (Definitions) The definitions of terms used in this GMP shall be as specified in Annex 1. 
 
Article 3 (Scope of Application) (1) The scope of this GMP shall be as follows: 
1.  A person who intends to obtain manufacturing/import approval or manufacturing/import 
certification for digital medical devices, or who intends to submit a manufacturing/import 
notification; 
2.  A person who intends to manufacture or import medical device hardware for 
investigational use; 
3.  A person who has been granted a manufacturing business license (hereinafter referred to 
as the “manufacturer”) or a person who has been granted an import business license 
(hereinafter referred to as the “importer”) and who intends to undergo the assessment 
falling under each of the following subparagraphs (hereinafter referred to as “conformity 
determination assessment”). 
(a)  Conformity recognition and periodic assessment of the manufacturing and quality 
management system pursuant to the text of Article 8 (4) and the text of Article 12 (3) 
of the Digital Medical Products Act, and Article 12 (1) of the Enforcement Rule of 
the same Act 
(b)  Conformity determination (including conformity determination for changes) and 
periodic assessments under Article 24 of the Digital Medical Products Act 
(2)  Notwithstanding subparagraphs 1 through 3 of paragraph (1), A person who intends to 
manufacture digital medical devices solely for export (hereinafter referred to as “digital 
medical devices for export”), or A person who intends to manufacture or import Class I digital 
medical devices, shall comply with this GMP, but may be exempted from the conformity 
determination assessment. 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
398 
 
Article 4 (Classification of Conformity Determination Assessment) (1) Conformity 
determination assessment under this GMP shall be conducted by classifying them into the following 
categories: 
1.  The assessment that must be initially undergone under any of the following items in order 
to be determined as conforming to this GMP (hereinafter referred to as the “initial 
assessment”) 
(a)  The assessment to be undergone by a manufacturer or a manufacturing site of 
standalone software that is not combined with hardware (such as electronic or 
mechanical equipment), operates in an environment equivalent to a general-purpose 
computer, and functions independently as a digital medical device (hereinafter 
referred to as “standalone digital medical device software”) 
(b)  The assessment to be undergone by a manufacturer or manufacturing site of software 
that is installed in a digital medical device or connected to it, either wired or 
wirelessly, and is used for controlling or operating the digital medical device, or for 
storing data, processing signals, or processing images generated by the digital 
medical device (hereinafter referred to as “embedded digital medical device 
software”) 
(c)  The assessment to be undergone by a manufacturer or manufacturing site of medical 
device hardware under Article 2 subparagraph 2 of the Regulation on the 
Classification and Designation of Class of Digital Medical Products (hereinafter 
referred to as “medical device hardware”) 
2.  The assessment to be newly undergone when changes falling under the following items 
occur after having been determined as conforming to this GMP (hereinafter referred to as 
the “assessment for change”): 
(a)  Where a manufacturer or a manufacturing site of digital medical device software 
adds artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) functions pursuant to 
Annex 5; 
(b)  Where a manufacturing site of medical device hardware seeks to add another product 
group pursuant to Annex 5; 
(c)  Where a manufacturer or a manufacturing site of digital medical devices has no 
history of conformity determination under this GMP with respect to whether all or 
part of the manufacturing processes and services are outsourced; 
(d)  Where the location of a medical device hardware manufacturing site is changed or 
added. Provided, however, that changes to storage facilities or laboratories with 
minimal relevance to product quality shall be excluded; 
(e)  Where a medical device hardware manufacturer or a manufacturing site has changed 
the manufacturer or manufacturing site of the embedded digital medical device 
software; 
(f)  Where a manufacturer or a manufacturing site of embedded digital medical device 
software has changed the manufacturer or manufacturing site of medical device 
hardware. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
399 
 
(2)  Notwithstanding paragraph (1) 2, a manufacturer or a manufacturing site may undergo the 
assessment under paragraph (1) 1. In such cases, it shall be deemed to have undergone a 
periodic assessment under paragraph (3).  
(3)  A manufacturer and manufacturing site that has been determined as conforming pursuant to 
paragraph (1) shall undergo one periodic assessment every three years, as prescribed in each of 
the following subparagraphs: 
1.  A manufacturer or a manufacturing sites of digital medical device software; 
2.  A manufacturing site or a manufacturer of medical device hardware. 
(4)  Notwithstanding Article 3 (2) and (3), periodic assessments may be exempted in the following 
cases of each subparagraph: 
1.  Digital medical device for export; 
2.  Class I medical device hardware; 
3.  Medical device hardware for investigational use. 
(5)  Where an assessment received in substitution for the assessments under paragraphs (1) through 
(3) pursuant to Article 6 (2) (hereinafter referred to as the “alternate assessment”) has been 
conducted, it shall be deemed that the conformity determination assessment under this Notice 
has been undergone.  
 
Article 5 (Standards for Conformity Determination Assessment) (1) The standards for 
conformity determination assessment of digital medical devices shall be as prescribed in each of the 
following subparagraphs: 
1.  Annex 2 shall apply to medical device hardware. 
2.  Annexes 2 and 3 shall apply to digital medical device software. 
3.  Where artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) functions are incorporated, 
Annexes 2 through 4 shall apply. 
(2)  Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where any of the following subparagraphs applies, only part of 
Annexes 2 through 4 may be applied. In such cases, the applicant shall secure clear 
justification therefor. 
1.  Where the requirements pertain only to digital medical device software or only to medical 
device hardware; 
2.  In the case of an assessment for change under the text of Article 4 (1) 2 (d); 
3.  Notwithstanding Article 3 (2), where a conformity determination assessment under this 
GMP is applied for in relation to a Class I digital medical device; 
4.  Where a person intends to manufacture or import medical device hardware for 
investigational use. 
 
Article 6 (Methods of Conformity Determination Assessment) (1) The head of a quality 
management audit organization pursuant to Article 28 (2) of the Medical Device Act, which applies 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
400 
 
mutatis mutandis under Article 5 of the Digital Medical Products Act (hereinafter referred to as the 
“audit organization”), and the head of an agency designated to perform certification-related duties 
pursuant to Article 48 of the Digital Medical Products Act (hereinafter referred to as the “agency 
entrusted with certification-related duties”) (collectively referred to as the “heads of the audit 
organizations”) shall jointly conduct a document inspection and an on-site inspection in accordance 
with the following subparagraphs. In such cases, the audit organization and the agency entrusted 
with certification-related duties (hereinafter referred to as the “audit organizations”) may conduct a 
conformity determination assessment together with experts in the relevant field, and, in the case of 
digital medical device software, may conduct a remote inspection upon the applicant’s request. 
1.  An assessment shall be conducted by product group under Annex 5 for manufacturers and 
manufacturing sites of digital medical device software.  
2.  Where the entire manufacturing process of digital medical device software or medical 
device hardware is performed under a contractual manufacturing arrangement between 
the legal manufacturer and the manufacturer (hereinafter collectively referred to as the 
“legal manufacturer and manufacturer”), each shall be subject to a separate assessment. 
3.  Where an outsourced entity (hereinafter referred to as the “supplier”) is entrusted with 
part of the manufacturing process or related services, each such supplier shall be subject 
to a separate assessment. In such cases, only part of Annexes 2 through 4 shall be applied 
within the scope of the outsourced work. 
(2)  Notwithstanding paragraph (1), in any of the following subparagraphs, the conformity 
determination assessment may be substituted.  
1.  Where another manufacturer or importer submits a valid certificate of conformity 
determination under this GMP for the relevant manufacturing site or manufacturer; 
2.  Where a manufacturer or importer of medical devices (including in vitro diagnostic 
medical devices) under the Medical Device Act or the Act on In Vitro Diagnostic Medical 
Devices submits a valid conformity recognition certificate issued under the Good 
Manufacturing Practice for Medical Devices or the Good Manufacturing Practice for In 
Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices for the relevant manufacturing site or manufacturing 
site operator (limited to medical device hardware and digital medical device software 
without artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) functions); 
3.  Where a relevant manufacturing site has obtained a valid conformity certificate under the 
Good Manufacturing Practice for Medical Devices or the Good Manufacturing Practice 
for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices pursuant to Article 4 (1) 2 (b), and submits a 
conformity recognition certificate (limited to valid certificates) whose item group falls 
under the product group of Annex 5 (limited to medical device hardware); 
4.  Where a manufacturer submits a copy of a quality management system conformity 
recognition certificate and on-site inspection results (including follow-up actions based on 
such results), issued by a regulatory authority or an institution delegated by the regulatory 
authority for a manufacturing site whose location has been changed pursuant to the text of 
Article 4 (1) 2 (d) (limited to medical device hardware); 
5.  Where a manufacturer submits a quality management system conformity recognition 
certificate (hereinafter referred to as the “MDSAP conformity recognition certificate”) 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
401 
 
and the on-site inspection results (including any follow-up actions), issued by an audit 
organization under item 58 of Annex 1 pursuant to the Medical Device Single Audit 
Program (MDSAP) (limited to medical device hardware). 
(3)  Notwithstanding paragraph (2), an on-site inspection shall be conducted for digital medical 
devices in any of the following subparagraphs: 
1.  Where the materials under paragraph (2) 2 through 5 cannot be submitted due to trade 
secrets or similar reasons, and an on-site inspection is requested; 
2.  Where the materials under Article 7 (1) cannot be submitted due to trade secrets or similar 
reasons, and an on-site inspection is requested; 
3.  Where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety recognizes that public health may otherwise 
be affected. 
(4)  Notwithstanding Article 4, digital medical devices shall undergo a new initial assessment in 
any of the following subparagraphs: 
1.  Where the expiration date of a certificate of conformity determination issued to a 
manufacturing site or manufacturer of digital medical devices for export, Class I digital 
medical devices, or medical device hardware for investigational use has expired and 
conformity determination assessment are applied for again; 
2.  Where the legal manufacturer in a legal manufacturer–manufacturer relationship that has 
undergone a conformity determination assessment is changed or removed; 
3.  Where a manufacturing site that has undergone conformity determination assessment for 
Class I digital medical devices under Article 5 (2) 3 intends to manufacture or import 
Class II, III, or IV digital medical devices; 
4.  Where the location of a manufacturing site that has undergone conformity determination 
assessment for medical device hardware for investigational use under Article 5 (2) 4 is 
changed, another item group of medical device hardware for investigational use is added, 
or the hardware is intended to be manufactured or imported for commercial sale. 
(5)  A manufacturing site or manufacturer for which only a document inspection has been 
conducted pursuant to Article 35 (1) of the Enforcement Rule of the Digital Medical Products 
Act shall, for each manufacturing or import unit, submit test reports prepared in accordance 
with its in-house quality control test specifications to the head of the relevant agency entrusted 
with certification-related duties.  
 
Article 7 (Application for Conformity Determination Assessment) (1) Any person falling under 
any of the subparagraphs of Article 3 (1) who intends to undergo conformity determination 
assessment under this GMP shall submit the application form with Form 1, along with the following 
documents of each subparagraph, to the head of the agency entrusted with certification-related 
duties. In such cases, except for digital medical device software, the relevant manufacturer and 
manufacturing site shall have quality management performance for at least one manufacturing unit, 
and the desired on-site inspection date shall be fixed and applied for at least 20 days prior to the 
start of the inspection. 
1.  For digital medical device software, the following documents of each item shall be 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
402 
 
submitted: 
(a)  Documents under Article 34 (1) 1 through 6 of the Enforcement Rule of the Digital 
Medical Products Act;  
(b)  Process flow diagrams, purchasing and outsourcing procedures, names of suppliers 
(including contracted suppliers), and scope of work for the core products of each 
product group under Annexes 5 and 6 for a manufacturer or manufacturing site; 
(c)  Device Master Records for core products of each product group under Annexes 5 
and 6, and procedures related to cybersecurity against electronic intrusion for a 
manufacturer or manufacturing site. 
2.  For medical device hardware, the documents under Article 7 (1) of the Good 
Manufacturing Practice for Medical Devices or the documents under Article 7 (1) of the 
Good Manufacturing Practice for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices, together with 
process flow diagrams, shall be submitted. 
3.  Pursuant to Article 4 (5), in the case of an alternative assessment, the required materials 
shall consist of the process flow diagrams for core products by product group under 
Annexes 5 and 6 for a manufacturer or manufacturing site; and the applicable materials 
under each item of Article 6 (2). 
(2)  A manufacturer or importer who must undergo a periodic assessment under Article 4 (3) shall, 
no later than three months before the expiration date stated on the certificate of conformity 
determination, submit the application form with Form 1 together with the documents specified 
in paragraph (1) to the head of the agency entrusted with certification-related duties to apply 
for the periodic assessment. In such cases, the desired on-site inspection date shall be fixed and 
applied for no later than 20 days before the expiration date stated on the certificate of 
conformity determination, and if the desired on-site inspection date is not confirmed at the 
time of application submission, the applicant shall submit the desired date in writing no later 
than 20 days before the start date of the requested on-site inspection.  
(3)  Upon receiving an application for conformity determination assessment under paragraph (1) or 
(2), the head of the agency entrusted with certification-related duties shall forward the 
application and related documents to the head of the audit organization.  
(4)  If a manufacturer or importer required to apply for a periodic assessment under Article 4 (3) 
fails to apply by three months before the expiration date under paragraph (2), the head of the 
agency entrusted with certification-related duties shall report the business name, 
representative, and other relevant information to the Commissioner of Regional Office of Food 
and Drug Safety. 
 
Article 8 (Procedures for Conformity Determination Assessment) (1) Upon receiving an 
application for conformity determination assessment under Article 7 (1), the head of the audit 
organization shall comply with each of the following subparagraphs: 
1.  The submission of the supporting documents under Article 7 (1) shall be verified within 
five days, and where no deficiencies are identified, the application shall be accepted. 
2.  If, as a result of confirming whether the supporting documents under subparagraph 1 have 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
403 
 
been submitted, any deficiency such as missing supporting documents is identified, the 
applicant shall be requested to supplement them by setting a supplementation deadline for 
the submission of such documents in accordance with the Administrative Procedures Act. 
3.  Notwithstanding subparagraph 1, where an application additionally includes a confirmed 
desired on-site inspection date, the request shall be made no later than the day following 
the receipt of the application. 
(2)  The head of the audit organizations shall, within 10 days from the date of acceptance under 
paragraph (1) 1, notify the applicant of whether experts in the relevant field will attend and of 
other matters related to the assessment. 
(3)  The head of the audit organization shall notify the applicant in writing of the assessment 
results under Article 7 within 30 days from the date on which the application for conformity 
determination assessment was received. Provided, however, that where an on-site inspection or 
a remote inspection (hereinafter referred to as “on-site inspection, etc.”) is conducted under 
Article 6 (1), the period from the date on which the applicant is notified to the start date of the 
on-site inspection, etc. under paragraph (3) shall not be counted toward the processing period.  
(4)  Where an on-site inspection, etc. is conducted under Article 6 (1), the heads of the audit 
organizations shall conduct the inspection in accordance with the following subparagraphs: 
1.  The on-site inspection, etc. shall be conducted in accordance with the matters notified to 
the applicant under paragraph (2), and the results shall be notified to the applicant in 
writing within seven days from the completion date of the on-site inspection, etc., or 
within the processing period under paragraph (3). Provided, however, that if the results of 
the on-site inspection, etc. are determined to be nonconforming, the Commissioner of 
Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety shall be notified immediately. 
2.  If an on-site inspection cannot be conducted due to war, epidemics, natural disasters, or 
other similar circumstances during the inspection period, or if the inspection cannot 
proceed normally due to delayed or refused submission of inspection documents, the on-
site inspection may be suspended. In such cases, the applicant shall be immediately 
notified in writing of the reasons for the suspension, and the Commissioner of Regional 
Office of Food and Drug Safety shall be notified accordingly. 
3.  When the reason for suspension under subparagraph 2 is confirmed to be resolved, the on-
site inspection may resume, and the results shall be notified to the applicant in writing 
within seven days from the completion date of the resumed inspection or within the 
processing period under paragraph (3). 
(5)  Where the head of the audit organization is unable to notify the applicant of the conformity 
determination assessment results within the processing period under paragraphs (3) and (4) due 
to unavoidable reasons such as natural disasters, the head shall notify the applicant in advance 
of the delay. In such cases, this shall apply only where the on-site inspection is conducted 
pursuant to the text of Article 6 (1). 
(6)  Where matters requiring supplementation are identified, the head of the audit organization 
shall take the following actions with respect to the results of the conformity determination 
assessment: 
1.  The applicant shall be requested to make supplementation, including the supplementation 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
404 
 
procedure and deadline, in accordance with the Civil Petitions Treatment Act. After 
reviewing the applicant’s submissions in response to the supplementation request, the 
conformity shall be evaluated.  
2.  Where the applicant, pursuant to the first part of subparagraph 1, is unable to submit the 
required documents due to trade secrets or similar reasons and requests an on-site 
inspection, an on-site inspection, etc. may be conducted. In such cases, the related 
expenses may be charged to the applicant by applying mutatis mutandis the provisions 
governing on-site inspections under the text of Article 6 (1), and, in the case of a remote 
inspection, the applicant shall prepare the necessary remote inspection platforms and 
tools. 
3.  If the applicant fails to submit the required documents within the supplementation 
deadline, the application shall be determined nonconforming. 
4.  Where an application is determined to be nonconforming under subparagraph 3, the 
Commissioner of Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety shall be notified immediately, 
and the application shall be determined nonconforming. 
(7)  The head of the audit organization shall prepare and retain the result report in Form 3 
regarding the assessment results. 
(8)  Where the results of the conformity determination assessment under Article 6 are found to be 
conforming, the head of the audit organization shall issue to the applicant the certificate of 
conformity determination under the Good Manufacturing Practice for Digital Medical Devices, 
in Form 2 and in accordance with Annex 7.  
(9)  If the applicant objects to the assessment results under Article 6, an objection may be filed in 
accordance with the Civil Petitions Treatment Act. 
(10) Upon receiving an objection under paragraph (9), the head of the audit organization shall 
prepare and retain the results of the disposition made in response to the objection. 
 
Article 9 (Expiration Date of the Certificate of Conformity Determination) (1) The expiration 
date of a certificate of conformity determination issued following an initial assessment shall be 
three years from the date of issuance. 
(2)  Where conformity determination is granted based on an assessment for change, it shall not 
affect the existing expiration date. 
(3)  Notwithstanding paragraph (2), where an assessment is conducted pursuant to the text of 
Article 4 (2), paragraph (4) shall apply. 
(4)  The expiration date of a certificate of conformity determination issued following a periodic 
assessment shall be three years from the day after the expiration date of the previous certificate 
of conformity determination. Provided, however, that where the date of issuance of the 
certificate of conformity determination is later than the expiration date of the previous 
certificate, the expiration date shall be three years from the date of issuance. 
(5)  Where a conformity determination assessment is conducted pursuant to Article 6 (2) 1, the 
expiration date for the relevant manufacturer and manufacturing site shall be calculated to 
coincide with the expiration date of the manufacturer or importer that previously underwent 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
405 
 
the conformity determination assessment. 
(6)  Where a conformity determination assessment is conducted pursuant to Article 6 (2) 2, the 
expiration date for the relevant manufacturer, manufacturing entity, or manufacturing site, shall 
be calculated to coincide with the expiration date of the manufacturer or importer that 
previously underwent the conformity determination assessment. 
(7)  Where the expiration date of the certificate of conformity determination for embedded digital 
medical device software differs from that of the conformity recognition certificate for medical 
device hardware, the expiration date shall be determined based on the certificate with the 
longer remaining validity.  
(8)  For medical device hardware for which conformity recognition assessments have been 
conducted under the Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP), the expiration date for 
the relevant manufacturing site shall be set to be identical to the expiration date of the MDSAP 
conformity recognition certificate.

(1) A manufacturer or importer that has received a certificate of conformity determination pursuant 
to Article 8 (8) may apply to the head of the audit organization for reissuance if reissuance is

(2)  Where the head of the audit organization receives an application for reissuance under

with Annex 7. 
(3)  A manufacturer or importer may either obtain reissuance of the certificate of conformity 
determination or record the changes in any of the following subparagraphs on the reverse side 
of the certificate for control purposes: 
1.  Change in the name of the manufacturing or importing business; 
2.  Change in the location of a manufacturing site (limited to cases under the proviso of 
Article 4 (1) 2 (d) and to digital medical device software); 
3.  Change in the location of an importing business; 
4.  Change in the trade name of the legal manufacturer or the manufacturer; 
5.  Change in the location of the legal manufacturer or the manufacturer (limited to cases 
under the proviso of Article 4 (1) 2 (d) and to digital medical device software); 
6.  Change in location due to administrative district reorganization. 
(4)  Where a manufacturer or importer records the changes on the reverse side of the certificate 
pursuant to paragraph (3), the manufacturer or importer shall also record the date and details of 
the approval of change, certification of change, or notification of change.

Article 11 (Return of the Certificate of Conformity Determination) (1) Where any of the 
following subparagraphs occur, a manufacturer or importer that has received a certificate of 
conformity determination pursuant to Article 8 (8) may return the certificate to the head of the audit 
organization that issued it, specifying the reasons therefor in detail. 
1.  Where the manufacturing business license or import business license is revoked; 
2.  Where the manufacturing approval, import approval, manufacturing certification, or 
import certification is revoked; 
3.  Where any other reasons exist requiring the manufacturer or importer to return the 
certificate of conformity determination. 
(2)  In accordance with paragraph (1), the head of an audit organization, etc. who has received the 
return of the certificate of conformity determination shall, immediately upon receipt of the 
returned conformity recognition certificate, report the fact of its return to the Commissioner of 
the Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety. 
 
Article 12 (Marking of Conformity Determination Assessment) A manufacturer or importer that 
has received a certificate of conformity determination pursuant to Article 8 (8) may affix the 
marking for conformity determination assessment, as prescribed in Annex 8, to digital medical 
devices that belong to the same product group as the manufacturing sites and manufacturers that 
underwent such assessments. 
 
Article 13 (Duties of the Audit Organization) The duties of the head of the audit organization 
shall be any of following subparagraphs: 
1.  Conduct a conformity determination assessment under the Good Manufacturing Practice 
for Digital Medical Devices; 
2.  Issuance of certificates of conformity determination; 
3.  Statistics and support related to conformity determination assessment; 
4.  Other matters necessary for conformity determination assessment. 
 
Article 14 (Reporting) (1) The head of the audit organization shall submit the quarterly report on 
the results of conformity determination assessment for digital medical devices, prepared in Form 4, 
and the detailed list of assessment results, prepared in Form 5, to the Minister of Food and Drug 
Safety and the Commissioner of Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety within 20 days after the 
end of each quarter. Provided, that where the Minister of Food and Drug Safety or the 
Commissioner of Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety requests separate data, the relevant data 
shall be submitted within seven days from the date of the request. 
(2)  Where there are personnel changes, such as transfers or resignations of auditors, the head of 
the audit organization shall report such changes to the Minister of Food and Drug Safety 
within seven days.
