[Annex 3] 
Criteria for Assessment of Digital Medical Device Software  
(Related to Article 5) 
1.  Software Development Process 
1.1  Planning 
1.1.1 Planning for Design and Development of Digital Medical Device Software 
(a)  The organization shall establish a design and development plan to conduct design and 
development process activities appropriate to the scope, scale, and software safety class of 
the software system of the digital medical device to be developed. This plan shall define 
or reference all development life cycle models and shall be maintained and updated as 
design and development progress. 
(b)  The organization shall document the following in the course of design and development 
planning:  
1)  The processes used for design and development, including standards, methods, and 
tools; 
2)  The responsibilities and authorities for design and development; 
3)  Outputs of activities and tasks (including documentation); 
4)  Traceability among customer requirements, software system requirements, software 
item requirements, tests, and the risk control measures implemented in the digital 
medical device; 
5)  Software 
configuration 
management 
and 
change 
management, 
including 
configuration items such as software of unknown provenance (SOUP) and 
development support software; 
6)  Methods for resolving issues identified in the outputs and activities of each life cycle 
phase; 
7)  Methods to ensure traceability between design and development inputs and outputs; 
8)  The necessary resources, including personnel competence. 
1.1.2 Verification Planning for Digital Medical Device Software 
(a)  The organization shall include or reference the following verification information in the 
digital medical device software development plan: 
1)  Outputs required for verification; 
2) 
Verification activities required for each life cycle activity; 
3)  Milestones indicating which outputs are to be verified; 
4)  Acceptance criteria for verification of outputs. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
441 
 
(b)  The organization shall include or reference a plan for integrating software items of the 
digital medical device (including SOUP) and performing tests during the integration 
process in the digital medical device development plan. 
1.1.3 Validation Planning for Digital Medical Device Software 
The organization shall establish and document a validation plan for design and development. 
The validation plan shall include the following: 
(a)  The scope of validation, related activities, and any existing constraints; 
(b)  Validation criteria and validation methods; 
(c)  The environment and tools for performing validation; 
(d)  Qualifications of personnel performing validation and the required prerequisite training. 
1.1.4 Establishment of Maintenance Plan for Digital Medical Device Software 
The organization shall establish a maintenance plan to perform the activities and tasks of the 
maintenance process. This plan shall include the following: 
(a)  Procedures for receiving, documenting, evaluating, resolving, and tracking feedback 
arising after release of the digital medical device; 
(b)  Criteria for determining which feedback requires action; 
(c)  Use of the risk management process; 
(d)  Use of the problem-resolution process for analyzing and resolving issues that arise after 
distribution of the digital medical device; 
(e)  Use of the digital medical device configuration management process to control changes to 
the existing digital medical device software system; 
(f)  Procedures for evaluating and implementing upgrades, bug fixes, patches, and 
obsolescence-related updates of software of unknown provenance (SOUP). 
1.2  Requirements Analysis 
1.2.1 Definition and Documentation of Software System Requirements 
(a)  The manufacturer shall define and document the software system requirements for each 
software system of the digital medical device. 
(b)  Where applicable, the manufacturer shall include the following in the software system 
requirements: 
1)  Customer-specified requirements; 
2)  Requirements necessary for the stated or intended use, even if not specified by the 
customer; 
3)  Functional and performance requirements; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
442 
 
4)  Inputs to and outputs from the software system; 
5)  Interfaces between the software system and other systems; 
6)  Software-based alarms, warnings, and operational messages; 
7)  Security requirements; 
8)  User interface requirements implemented in the software; 
9)  Data definitions and database requirements; 
10)  Installation and acceptance requirements for software deployed to operational and 
maintenance organizations; 
11)  Requirements related to operation and maintenance methods; 
12)  IT-network-related requirements; 
13)  User maintenance requirements; 
14)  Deployment requirements; 
15)  Regulatory requirements; 
16)  Any additional requirements determined by the organization. 
17)  Risk control measures. 
(c)  Where the customer does not provide documented requirements, the organization shall 
confirm the customer requirements prior to acceptance.  
1.2.2 Updating Software System Requirements 
(a)  When software system requirements are changed, the organization shall update the related 
documents and ensure that the relevant personnel are made aware of the changed 
requirements. 
(b)  When updating existing requirements, including software system requirements, the 
organization shall use the risk management process to re-evaluate activities such as risk 
analysis and risk control. 
(c)  When updating existing requirements, including software system requirements, the 
organization shall ensure that they are appropriately re-evaluated and updated through 
requirements analysis activities. 
1.2.3 Verification of Software System Requirements 
(a)  Prior to committing to supply the device to the customer, the organization shall perform 
requirements verification and shall ensure the following: 
1)  Device requirements are defined and documented; 
2)  Any contract or order requirements differing from those previously expressed are 
resolved; 
3)  Applicable statutory requirements are met; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
443 
 
4)  User training is possible or planned to be made possible; 
5) 
The organization has the capability to meet the specified requirements. 
(b)  The organization shall verify and document the software system requirements, including 
the following: 
1)  Whether risk control elements are included when implementing the requirements; 
2)  Whether any conflicts exist between requirements; 
3)  Whether clear terminology has been used; 
4)  Whether test results and criteria are described using recognized terminology; 
5)  Whether unique identifiers are used; 
6)  Whether traceability to system requirements or other sources is ensured. 
(c)  Records of verification results and any actions taken based on the verification shall be 
maintained. 
1.3  Design and Development 
1.3.1 Software Design and Development Inputs 
(a)  When preparing the software development plan, the organization shall refer to the 
software system requirements as inputs for development. 
(b)  The organization shall determine and maintain records of inputs related to software 
requirements. These inputs shall include the following:  
1)  Functional, performance, usability, and safety requirements necessary for the 
intended use; 
2)  Applicable statutory requirements and standards; 
3)  Applicable risk management outputs; 
4)  Information derived from previous similar designs, where applicable; 
5)  Other requirements essential to the design and development of the digital medical 
device and processes. 
(c)  Inputs to the design and development process shall be reviewed for appropriateness and 
approved. 
1.3.2 Software Design and Development Outputs 
(a)  The organization shall determine and maintain records of outputs related to software 
requirements. These outputs shall include the following:  
1)  Meet the design and development input requirements; 
2)  Provide appropriate information for purchasing, production, and service provision; 
3)  Include or reference the acceptance criteria for the digital medical device;  

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
444 
 
4)  Specifying the characteristics of the device essential for safe and proper use. 
(b)  Outputs of the design and development process shall be provided in a form that enables 
verification against the design and development inputs and shall be approved prior to 
release.  
1.3.3 Software Architecture Design 
(a)  The organization shall describe the architecture of the software system or software items 
and shall document the software system requirements using the architecture. 
(b)  The organization shall develop and document the architecture of interfaces between 
software items and external components (both software and hardware), as well as between 
software items. 
(c)  Where software items include software of unknown provenance (SOUP), the organization 
shall specify the functional and performance requirements essential to the intended use of 
the SOUP, as well as the hardware and software requirements. 
(d)  The organization shall identify the separations between software items that are essential 
for risk control and shall describe the methods used to ensure that such separations are 
effective. 
(e)  The organization shall evaluate the capability of the architectural design to meet the 
requirements and shall identify and specify any necessary actions. 
(f)  The organization shall verify and document the architecture of the software system and 
software items, including the requirements of 1.3.1 and the following. Personnel 
participating in verification shall include not only those responsible for the design but also 
other experts. 
1)  Whether the software system or software item requirements, including those related 
to risk control, are implemented using the software system or software item 
architecture; 
2)  Whether the architecture of the software system or software items can support 
interfaces between software items and between software items and hardware; 
3)  Whether the architecture of the software system or software items can support the 
operation of software of unknown provenance (SOUP). 
(g)  The organization shall maintain records of verification, including the verification 
methods, acceptance criteria, and justification for sample size, along with any statistical 
techniques used. The records shall identify the design under review, the personnel 
involved in the verification, and the date of verification. 
1.3.4 Detailed Software Design 
(a)  The organization shall decompose the software system or software items into software 
units. 
(b)  Where applicable, the organization shall include the following additional acceptance 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
445 
 
criteria for software units in the design: 
1)  Proper event sequencing; 
2)  Data and control flow; 
3)  Planned resource allocation; 
4)  Fault handling (fault definition, detection, and recovery); 
5)  Initialization of variables 
6)  Self-diagnostics; 
7)  Memory management and memory overflow; 
8)  Boundary conditions. 
(c)  The organization shall verify and document the detailed design, including the 
requirements of 1.3.1 and 1.3.2, and the following, to enable implementation of each 
software unit. Personnel participating in the verification shall include not only those 
responsible for the design but also other experts. 
1)  Whether the software architecture has been implemented using the detailed design; 
2)  Whether interfaces between software units and interfaces between software units and 
external components (hardware or software) are implemented using the detailed 
design; 
3)  Whether the detailed design is consistent with the software architecture. 
(d)  The organization shall maintain records of verification, including the verification 
methods, acceptance criteria, and justification for sample size, along with any statistical 
techniques used. The records shall identify the design under review, the personnel 
involved in the verification, and the date of verification. 
1.3.5 Implementation of Software Units 
(a)  The organization shall implement each software unit. 
(b)  Before integrating software units into larger software items, the organization shall 
establish acceptance criteria and ensure that the software units meet those criteria. 
(c)  The organization shall establish strategies, methods, and procedures for verifying 
software units. Where verification is performed by testing, the organization shall evaluate 
the adequacy of the test procedures. 
(d)  The organization shall verify the software units and document the results. Personnel 
participating in verification shall include not only those responsible for the design but also 
other experts. 
(e)  The organization shall maintain records of verification, including the verification 
methods, acceptance criteria, and justification for sample size, along with any statistical 
techniques used. The records shall identify the design under review, the personnel 
involved in the verification, and the date of verification. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
446 
 
1.3.6 Design and Development Transfer 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for the transfer of design and development 
outputs to manufacturing. These procedures shall ensure that the design and development 
outputs have been verified as suitable for manufacturing before becoming the final 
production specifications and that manufacturing capability can meet device 
requirements.  
(b)  Records of the results and conclusions of the transfer shall be maintained. 
1.3.7 Control of Design and Development Changes 
(a)  The organization shall document procedures for controlling design and development 
changes. The organization shall determine the significance of changes to the function, 
performance, usability, safety, applicable statutory requirements, and intended use of the 
medical device. 
(b)  Design and development changes shall be identified. Prior to implementation, the changes 
shall be reviewed, verified, and approved. Validation shall be included where applicable. 
(c)  Review of design and development changes shall include evaluation of the impact on 
components, devices in manufacturing or already delivered, risk management inputs or 
outputs, and the requirements of 1.1.1.  
(d)  Records of the changes, the review of the changes, and any necessary actions shall be 
maintained. 
1.4  Testing 
1.4.1 Software Integration 
(a)  The organization shall integrate software units in accordance with the integration plan. 
(b)  The organization shall verify and document the process and results of integrating software 
units into the software system or software items in accordance with the integration plan. 
Personnel participating in the verification shall include not only those responsible for the 
design but also other experts. 
(c)  The organization shall maintain records of verification, including verification methods, 
acceptance criteria, and justification for sample size, along with any statistical techniques 
used. The records shall identify the personnel involved and the verification date. 
1.4.2 Software Integration Testing 
(a)  The organization shall evaluate the adequacy of the integration test procedures. 
(b)  The organization shall test the software system or software items resulting from 
integration of the software units in accordance with the integration plan and shall 
document the results. 
(c)  Through integration testing, the organization shall confirm that the software system or 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
447 
 
software items resulting from integration of the software units function as intended. 
(d)  When integrating software units, the organization shall perform appropriate regression 
testing to demonstrate that defects have not been introduced into previously integrated 
software systems or software items. 
(e)  The organization shall maintain integration test records, including test results 
(conformity/nonconformity, list of deviations), records for repeated testing, and the 
identity of the tester. The records shall identify the personnel involved in the verification 
and the verification date. 
(f)  The organization shall feed anomalies identified during software integration and 
integration testing into the software problem-resolution process. 
1.4.3 Software System Testing 
(a)  The organization shall evaluate the adequacy of the verification strategy and test 
procedures. 
(b)  The organization shall establish and perform test configurations—expressed as input 
values, expected outputs, pass/fail criteria, and procedures—in software system testing to 
address all digital medical device requirements. 
(c)  The organization shall feed anomalies identified during software system testing into the 
software problem-resolution process. 
(d)  For changes that arise during software system testing, the organization shall: 
1)  Repeat testing as appropriate and perform revised or additional tests to verify that the 
changes made to resolve issues are effective. 
2)  Perform tests to demonstrate that no unintended side effects have been introduced. 
3)  Perform risk-management activities for the change. 
(e)  The organization shall evaluate software system test results, including the following: 
1)  Verification that all digital medical device requirements have been tested, or 
confirmation that untested requirements have been addressed. 
2)  Records demonstrating traceability between digital medical device requirements and 
tests or other verification activities. 
3)  Confirmation that test results meet the required pass/fail criteria. 
(f)  The organization shall maintain software system test records, including the following: 
1)  References to test-case procedures showing the required functions and expected 
results; 
2)  Test results (pass/fail, list of nonconformities); 
3)  Version of the software tested; 
4)  Appropriate hardware and software test setup; 
5)  Appropriate test tools; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
448 
 
6)  Date of testing; 
7)  Identification of personnel responsible for conducting the test and recording the 
results. 
1.4.4 Validation 
(a)  Validation shall be performed according to planned and documented methods to ensure 
that the resulting device meets the requirements for its intended use or specified 
application.  
(b)  The organization shall document a validation plan that includes the validation methods, 
acceptance criteria, and, where applicable, the rationale for sample size. 
(c)  Design validation shall be performed on representative devices. Representative devices 
include initial production units, batches, or equivalent devices. The rationale for selecting 
devices used for validation shall be documented. 
(d)  As part of design and development validation, the organization shall conduct a clinical 
evaluation in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. 
(e)  A digital medical device used for clinical evaluation shall not be considered as shipped for 
customer use. 
(f)  If, in its intended use, the digital medical device is required to be connected or interfaced 
with another medical device or digital medical device, validation shall include 
confirmation that the device requirements for the specified application or intended use are 
met when so connected or interfaced.  
(g)  Validation shall be completed before the device is released for customer use.  
(h)  Records of the validation results, conclusions, and any necessary actions shall be 
maintained. 
1.5  Distribution 
1.5.1 Software Distribution for System-Level Use 
(a)  The organization shall complete all verification activities and evaluate their results before 
distributing the digital medical device software. 
(b)  The organization shall document all known residual risks. 
(c)  The organization shall assess all known residual risks to ensure that they do not contribute 
to unacceptable risk. 
(d)  The organization shall document the version of the digital medical device software being 
distributed. 
(e)  The organization shall document the procedures and environment used to prepare the 
digital medical device software for distribution. 
(f)  The organization shall ensure that all digital medical device software development plan 
(or maintenance plan) activities and tasks are completed in accordance with the relevant 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
449 
 
documentation. 
1.5.2 Software Record Retention 
(a)  The organization shall record and retain the following: 
1)  Software and configuration items 
2)  Documentation 
(b)  The retention period shall be the longer of the digital medical device software lifetime 
defined by the organization or the period specified by applicable regulatory requirements. 
(c)  The organization shall establish procedures to verify that the digital medical device 
software has been reliably distributed without alteration or unauthorized change. Such 
procedures shall take into account the production and handling of media containing the 
software, including duplication, media labeling, packaging, protection, storage space, and 
distribution. 
1.6  Maintenance  
1.6.1 Establishment of Maintenance Plan 
The organization shall establish a maintenance plan that includes the following items to 
conduct maintenance process activities and tasks.  
(a)  Procedures for receiving, documenting, evaluating, resolving, and tracking feedback; 
(b)  Criteria for determining which feedback requires action; 
(c)  Use of the risk management process; 
(d)  Use of the problem-resolution process for analyzing and resolving issues that occur after 
distribution of the digital medical device software; 
(e)  Use of the configuration management process for managing changes to the digital medical 
device software; 
(f)  Procedures for evaluating and implementing updates, defect corrections, patches, and 
retirement of software of unknown provenance (SOUP).  
1.6.2 Documentation and Evaluation of Feedback 
(a)  The organization shall monitor feedback on distributed digital medical device software. 
(b)  The organization shall document and evaluate feedback to determine whether any 
problems exist in the distributed digital medical device software. All identified problems 
shall be recorded in a problem report. A problem report shall include actual or potential 
adverse events and deviations from specifications. 
(c)  The organization shall evaluate each problem report to determine its impact on the safety 
of the distributed digital medical device software and to identify the changes necessary 
for problem resolution. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
450 
 
1.6.3 Use of Software Problem Resolution Process 
The organization shall use Section 2.4 to address problem reports. 
2.  Life Cycle Support Processes 
2.1  Risk Management 
2.1.1 Software Risk Management Plan 
(a)  The organization shall document one or more processes for risk management during 
realization of digital medical device software, and records of risk management activities 
shall be maintained.  
(b)  The organization shall include or reference in the digital medical device development plan 
the planning necessary to perform the activities and tasks required under the risk 
management process for software items of the digital medical device, including SOUP. 
(c)  Where applicable, the organization shall include the following procedures in the risk 
management plan: 
1)  Identification of defect categories that may be introduced based on the programming 
techniques adopted for the software system or item; 
2)  Documentation of evidence demonstrating that the identified defects do not 
contribute to unacceptable risk. 
2.1.2 Software Risk Analysis and Evaluation 
(a)  The organization shall identify hazards related to the software system or item that were 
identified during the medical device risk analysis activities under ISO 14971. 
(b)  The organization shall identify potential hazardous situations associated with the software 
system or item that contribute to hazardous situations and, where applicable, shall 
consider potential hazardous situations including the following: 
1)  Incorrect or incomplete functional specifications; 
2)  Software defects in the identified software system or item functions; 
3)  Failures or unexpected outcomes caused by software of unknown provenance 
(SOUP); 
4)  Hardware failures or other software defects that may cause unexpected software 
behavior; 
5)  Reasonably foreseeable misuse. 
(c)  Where failures or unexpected outcomes caused by software of unknown provenance 
(SOUP) constitute potential hazards that may contribute to a hazardous situation, the 
organization shall, at a minimum, evaluate the list of all known issues for the SOUP 
components used in the digital medical device to determine whether such issues could 
initiate a sequence of events leading to a hazardous situation. This evaluation shall be 
based on the list of issues provided by the software of unknown provenance (SOUP) 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
451 
 
supplier. 
(d)  The organization shall document in the risk management file the potential hazardous 
situations of the software system or item that affect hazardous situations. 
(e)  The organization shall analyze changes to software within the digital medical device, 
including software of unknown provenance (SOUP), to determine: 
1)  Whether additional potential hazardous situations are found to contribute to 
hazardous situations; 
2)  Whether additional software systems or items require risk control measures. 
(f)  The organization shall analyze changes to the software system or item, including software 
of unknown provenance (SOUP), to determine whether such changes may affect existing 
risk control measures. 
2.1.3 Software Risk Control 
(a)  Where a software system or item can affect a hazardous situation, the organization shall 
define and document risk control measures for each software system or item as 
documented in the risk management file. 
(b)  Where risk control measures are implemented as part of the functions of a software 
system or item, the organization shall perform the following: 
1)  Include the risk control measures in the software requirements of the digital medical 
device; 
2)  Assign a software safety classification, based on the risk controlled by the risk 
control measure, to each software system or item that contributes to implementation 
of the risk control measure; 
3)  Develop the software items in accordance with subparagraph 1). 
(c)  The organization shall verify the implementation of each documented risk control 
measure and shall document the verification. 
(d)  The organization shall determine whether new hazardous situations have arisen and shall 
review the risk control measures. 
2.1.4 Ensuring Traceability for Software Risk Management 
The organization shall adequately document the traceability of hazards related to the software 
system or item, including the following: 
(a)  From the hazardous situation to the software item; 
(b)  From the software system or item to the specific software cause; 
(c)  From the software cause to the risk control measure; 
(d)  From the risk control measure to the verification of the risk control measure. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
452 
 
2.1.5 Performance of Software Risk Management 
The organization shall perform the risk management activities defined in Sections 2.1.1, 2.1.3, 
and 2.1.4 based on Section 2.1.2. 
2.1.6 Performance of Risk Management for Legacy Software 
(a)  Legacy software shall either comply with Annex 3 or demonstrate conformity as 
presented in Section 2.1.6. 
(b)  When legacy software is used, the organization shall evaluate all feedback—internal or 
from users—related to incidents or events associated with the legacy software, including 
post-production information, and shall comply with a risk management process in 
accordance with ISO 14971. 
(c)  The organization shall perform risk management activities related to the continued use of 
legacy software by considering the following elements: 
1)  Integration of the legacy software into the overall medical device architecture; 
2)  Continued effectiveness of risk control measures implemented as part of the legacy 
software; 
3)  Identification of hazardous situations associated with continued use of the legacy 
software; 
4)  Identification of potential causes in the legacy software that contribute to hazardous 
situations; 
5)  Definition of risk control measures for each potential cause in the legacy software 
that contributes to hazardous situations. 
(d)  For legacy software, the manufacturer shall perform a gap analysis of valid outputs. 
1)  The organization shall assess the continued validity of the valid outputs. 
2)  Where gaps are identified, the organization shall evaluate whether the risks arising 
from missing activities and outputs can be reduced. 
3)  Based on this evaluation, the organization shall determine the activities to be 
performed and the outputs to be generated, and shall produce, at a minimum, 
software system test records. 
(e)  Gap closure activities 
1)  The organization shall establish and execute a plan to generate the identified outputs. 
Where possible, the organization may generate the required outputs using objective 
evidence. 
2)  The plan shall use the problem-resolution process under Section 2.4 to address issues 
identified in the legacy software and its outputs. 
3)  Changes to the legacy software shall be performed in accordance with Section 1.6. 
(f)  The organization shall document the version of the legacy software together with the 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
453 
 
justification for its continued use. 
2.2  Control of Outsourced Processes 
2.2.1 Outsourcing Management Process 
(a)  Where the organization outsources devices that affect the conformity requirements of the 
digital medical device, the organization shall ensure that the outsourced devices are 
monitored and controlled. 
(b)  The organization shall retain responsibility for compliance with this GMP, customer 
requirements, and applicable statutory requirements for outsourced devices. 
(c)  Control of outsourced devices shall be proportionate to the associated risks and to the 
capability of the contracted supplier to meet the requirements of the purchasing process, 
and shall include a written quality agreement. 
(d)  The organization shall plan monitoring and re-evaluation of suppliers. 
(e)  The organization shall establish criteria for evaluating and selecting suppliers, and such 
criteria shall be based on: 
1)  The supplier’s capability to provide devices that meet the organization’s 
requirements; 
2)  The supplier’s performance; 
3)  The effect of the outsourced device on the quality of the software; 
4)  Proportionality to the risks associated with the software. 
(f)  The organization shall plan monitoring and re-evaluation of suppliers. The organization 
shall monitor the performance of suppliers that provide outsourced devices to ensure that 
the requirements for the outsourced devices are met. The results of monitoring shall be 
provided as inputs to the supplier re-evaluation process.  
(g)  Non-fulfillment of outsourcing requirements shall be addressed with the supplier, 
proportionate to the risks associated with the outsourced device and compliance with 
applicable regulatory requirements. 
(h)  Records of the results of evaluation, selection, monitoring, and re-evaluation of suppliers 
and of any necessary actions arising from these activities shall be maintained. 
2.2.2 Outsourcing Information 
(a)  Where applicable, the organization shall describe or reference outsourcing information, 
including:  
1)  Device specifications; 
2)  Requirements for device approval, procedures, processes, and equipment; 
3)  Requirements for the qualification of supplier personnel; 
4)  Software quality management system requirements. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
454 
 
(b)  Before communicating with the supplier, the organization shall ensure the adequacy of the 
specified outsourcing requirements. 
(c)  Where applicable, the organization shall include a written agreement requiring the 
supplier to notify the organization of changes to devices that meet the organization’s 
outsourcing requirements, prior to implementing changes that may affect the functionality 
of the outsourced device. 
(d)  The organization shall maintain documentation and records of relevant outsourcing 
information to the extent required for traceability. 
2.2.3 Verification of Outsourced Devices 
(a)  The organization shall establish and perform inspections or other activities necessary to 
ensure that outsourced devices conform to specified requirements. The extent of 
verification activities shall be proportionate to the risks associated with the outsourced 
device, based on the results of supplier evaluation.  
(b)  When the organization becomes aware of any changes to the outsourced device, it shall 
determine whether such changes affect the device realization process or the software. 
(c)  Where the organization or its customer intends to verify outsourced devices at the 
supplier’s premises, it shall specify the intended verification activities and the release 
arrangements for the devices within the outsourcing information.  
(d)  Records of verification shall be maintained. 
2.3  Configuration Management 
2.3.1 Configuration Management Plan for Digital Medical Devices 
(a)  The organization shall include or reference configuration management information for the 
digital medical device in the development plan, including:  
1)  Safety classification, types, categories, or the list of items to be controlled; 
2)  Software-related configuration management activities and tasks included in the 
digital medical device; 
3)  Organizations 
responsible 
for 
performing 
software-related 
configuration 
management activities included in the digital medical device; 
4)  Relationships with other organizations responsible for software-related development 
or maintenance included in the digital medical device; 
5)  The point at which items are placed under configuration control; 
6)  Points at which the problem-resolution process shall be applied; 
(b)  The organization shall plan for configuration items to be under configuration control prior 
to verification of the configuration items. 
(c)  Items requiring control include tools, items, or settings used for software-related 
development included in the digital medical device, and these items may affect the 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
455 
 
software. 
2.3.2 Configuration Identification for Digital Medical Devices 
(a)  The organization shall establish a plan to uniquely identify configuration items and their 
versions in order to control configuration items in accordance with Section 2.3.1. 
(b)  The organization shall document configuration items for each software of unknown 
provenance (SOUP) used, including the standard library and information such as the title, 
manufacturer, and unique SOUP identifier. 
2.3.3 Configuration Control for Digital Medical Devices 
(a)  The organization shall identify approved change requests that affect the distributed digital 
medical device.  
(b)  The organization shall change and control configuration items identified in accordance 
with Sections 2.3.1 and 2.3.2 only on the basis of approved change requests. 
(c)  The organization shall implement changes as specified in the documentation associated 
with the change request.  
(d)  The organization shall identify and perform all activities that must be repeated as a result 
of the change, including changes to the software safety classification of the software 
system or item. 
(e)  The organization shall verify the change, including repeating any verification invalidated 
by the change. 
(f)  The organization shall maintain records of the dependencies and relationships among 
change requests, related problem reports, and the approvals of those change requests. 
2.3.4 Record Retention for Digital Medical Devices 
The organization shall retain a retrievable record history of controlled configuration items, 
including the system configuration. 
2.3.5 Change Management 
(a)  The organization shall analyze the impact of each change request on the organization, the 
distributed digital medical device software, and systems interfacing with it. 
(b)  The organization shall evaluate and approve change requests that will modify the 
distributed digital medical device software. 
(c)  The organization shall identify and perform the activities in Sections 1 and 2 that must be 
repeated as a result of the change. 
(d)  The organization shall distribute the modified digital medical device software in 
accordance with Section 1.5. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
456 
 
2.4  Problem Resolution Process  
(a)  Preparation of problem reports 
 
The manufacturer shall prepare a report for each problem detected in the software. Each 
problem report shall include additional information that may assist in resolving the 
problem (e.g., affected devices, affected supporting accessories) and a description of the 
problem’s significance (e.g., its impact on performance, safety, or security). 
(b)  Problem investigation 
 
The manufacturer shall perform the following: 
1)  Investigate the problem and identify the cause, where possible; 
2)  Evaluate safety-related issues using risk management (Section 2.1); 
3)  Document the results of the investigation and evaluation; 
4)  The manufacturer shall generate a change request to resolve the problem, or shall 
document the rationale if no problem-resolution activities are necessary. 
(c)  Notification to relevant departments 
 
The manufacturer shall inform the relevant departments that a problem exists. 
(d)  Use of change management process 
 
The manufacturer shall approve and implement all change requests in accordance with the 
requirements of change management (Section 2.3.5). 
(e)  Record maintenance 
 
The manufacturer shall maintain records of the problem reports and of the problem-
resolution activities, including verification. The manufacturer shall update the risk 
management file as appropriate. 
(f)  Analysis of problem trends 
 
The manufacturer shall analyze problem reports to identify trends. 
(g)  Verification of software problem resolution 
 
The manufacturer shall verify the problem resolution to determine: 
1)  Whether the problem has been resolved and the problem report has been closed; 
2)  Whether negative trends have been reversed; 
3)  Whether the change request has been implemented in the appropriate software and 
activities; 
4)  Whether additional problems have emerged. 
(h)  Contents of test documentation 
 
The manufacturer shall include the following information in the test documentation when 
testing, re-testing, or performing regression testing of software items and the system after 
changes: 
1)  Test results; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
457 
 
2)  Detected anomalies; 
3)  Software version tested; 
4)  Relevant hardware and software test configurations; 
5)  Relevant test tools; 
6)  Date of testing; 
7)  Identity of the tester. 
 
 
 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices

[Annex 4] 
Criteria for AI Control Measures Assessment for Digital Medical 
Devices (Related to Article 5) 
1.  General Requirements 
1.1  AI Control Measures 
(a)  The organization shall determine the necessary AI control measures for the quality 
management of AI/ML software systems or items included in digital medical devices and 
shall apply such measures throughout the organization. 
1)  Management 
responsibility, 
including 
management 
involvement, 
policy 
establishment, and implementation; 
2)  Risk management, including identification, evaluation, and mitigation of potential 
risks of AI/ML software; 
3)  Governance structure, including responsibilities, decision-making, and approval 
procedures; 
4)  Data handling, including quality control of training data and data de-identification 
measures; 
5)  Design and implementation of AI models;  
6)  Development of AI/ML software systems combining training data and AI models; 
7)  Operation and monitoring, including periodic accuracy verification of AI/ML 
software. 
(b)  AI control measures defined by the organization shall include the following: 
1)  Process inputs, including, where applicable, outputs from processes performed prior 
to the process input stage and other materials recorded in the document control 
system within the quality control system;  
2)  Procedures for performing activities within the process; 
3)  Process outputs, including the outputs generated from the processes performed.  
(c)  The determined AI control measures may be defined as activities within the existing 
software life cycle processes of the quality management system or as independent 
software life cycle processes. In either case, the measures shall be documented, execution 
records shall be retained, and outputs shall be documented. 
(d)  Where certain requirements are not applicable due to the activities performed by the 
organization or the characteristics of the software, the organization may exclude such 
requirements. Provided, however, that the organization shall record the justification and 
the basis for determining each requirement to be not applicable. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
459 
 
1.2  Management Responsibility 
(a)  Top management shall demonstrate its commitment to the development and 
implementation of AI control measures and to maintaining their effectiveness through the 
following:  
1)  Establishment of an AI policy; 
2)  Establishment of AI objectives; 
3)  Conduct of reviews. 
(b)  Top management shall ensure that the AI Policy: 
1)  Is appropriate to the purpose of the organization; 
2)  Includes a commitment to meeting requirements and maintaining the effectiveness of 
the AI/ML software system; 
3)  Provides a framework for establishing and reviewing AI objectives; 
4)  Is communicated within the organization; 
5)  Is reviewed for continuing suitability. 
(c)  Top management shall ensure that AI Objectives include what is necessary to meet 
applicable regulatory requirements and product requirements, and that they are 
established at relevant functions and levels within the organization.  
(d)  AI Objectives shall be measurable and consistent with the quality policy. 
(e)  Top management shall conduct management reviews that include the following: 
1)  Documentation of procedures for management review related to AI control 
measures; 
2)  Review of AI control measures at documented and planned intervals to ensure their 
continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness; 
3)  Evaluation of the need for changes and opportunities for improvement of AI control 
measures, including the AI policy and AI objectives. 
(f)  Records of management review shall be documented and maintained. 
1.3  Resource Management 
(a)  The organization shall determine and provide the resources needed for: 
1)  Implementation of AI control measures and maintenance of their effectiveness; 
2)  Meeting applicable regulatory requirements and customer requirements. 
(b)  Personnel performing tasks related to AI control measures shall be competent based on 
appropriate education, training, skills, and experience.  
(c)  The organization shall establish the competencies required for personnel involved in the 
operation of AI control measures, provide necessary training, and document processes to 
ensure personnel awareness. 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
460 
 
(d)  The organization shall implement the following for the operation of AI control measures:  
1)  Determine the competencies needed for personnel performing work that affects 
product quality;  
2)  Provide training or implement other actions to achieve or maintain the necessary 
competence;  
3)  Evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken; 
4)  Ensure that personnel are aware of the relevance and importance of their activities 
and how they contribute to the achievement of quality objectives;  
5)  Maintain appropriate records of education, training, skills, and experience. 
2.  Risk Management 
(a)  A risk management plan for AI/ML software systems or items included in digital medical 
devices shall be established and implemented. 
(b)  Risk management for AI/ML software systems or items included in digital medical 
devices shall meet the requirements of Annex 2, Section 7.1. 
3.  Governance Structure 
(a)  The organization shall establish the ethical principles and rules that must be implemented 
internally as follows:  
1)  Adopt and organize laws, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines related to 
medical artificial intelligence, and establish internal guidance and rules to be 
implemented; 
2)  Clearly document the organization’s roles and responsibilities throughout the life 
cycle of artificial intelligence systems. 
(b)  The organization shall establish an artificial intelligence governance structure appropriate 
to the size of the organization and to the AI/ML software systems or items included in the 
digital medical device:  
1)  Structuring the organization to manage the implementation of ethical principles and 
rules; 
2)  Where applicable, structuring the organization to include external experts (e.g., 
physicians, nurses, data scientists, clinical or quality professionals, and relevant 
academic experts).  
(c)  The organization shall manage and oversee the following to ensure proper 
implementation of the artificial intelligence governance structure:  
1)  Compliance with ethical principles and rules to be implemented internally; 
2)  Monitoring of the target performance of AI/ML software systems or items included 
in the digital medical device; 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
461 
 
3)  Decisions on the retirement of AI/ML software systems or items included in the 
digital medical device; 
4)  Documentation of records related to the implementation of the artificial intelligence 
governance structure.  
4.  Reliability Assurance Planning 
The organization shall, where applicable, plan and implement the necessary activities to reduce 
the uncertainty of AI/ML system output results, including the following elements:  
(a)  Establishment of a virtual testing environment using simulators or equivalent tools; 
(b)  Establishment of a consultative framework to determine the expected outputs of AI/ML 
software systems or items included in the digital medical device;  
(c)  Establishment of a user evaluation group to verify the explanation or interpretation of 
expected outputs of AI/ML software systems or items included in the digital medical 
device.  
5.  Management of Training Data for AI/ML Functions 
(a)  The organization shall perform the necessary data collection and processing activities, 
including the following elements, to provide safe and reliable AI/ML functions:  
1)  Detailed information management to support clear understanding and utilization of 
data; 
2)  Recording and management of data sources; 
3)  Identification and inspection of anomalies in the data, where applicable.  
(b)  Where applicable, the organization shall perform the necessary activities for the safety 
and security of training data, including the following elements: 
1)  Defense against attacks such as data poisoning and data leakage; 
2)  Mitigation of bias in training data. 
6.  Development of AI Models Related to AI/ML Functions 
(a)  When using open-source libraries, the organization shall perform risk management related 
to their use and shall document the results.  
1)  Verification of the stability of open-source libraries, including use of actively 
maintained libraries; 
2)  Verification of license compliance for open-source libraries in use; 
3)  Verification of compatibility and security vulnerabilities of open-source libraries in 
use. 
(b)  Where applicable, the organization shall perform the necessary activities to provide the 
safety and reliability of AI models related to AI/ML functions, including the following 

Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) for Digital Medical Devices 
 
462 
 
elements.  
1)  A model specification describing the mechanism, performance, and precautions of 
the AI model; 
2)  Analysis and mitigation of bias in the AI model; 
3)  Establishment of defense measures against attacks on the AI model, such as model 
extraction and model evasion; 
4)  Provision of explanations for the inference results of the AI model. 
7.  Development of Systems Related to AI/ML Functions 
The organization shall perform the necessary activities to ensure the safety and reliability of 
software systems or items related to AI/ML functions included in digital medical devices, 
including the following elements.  
1)  Provision of alert functions in the event of a problem in the artificial intelligence 
system; 
2)  Application of security techniques to enhance the security of the artificial 
intelligence system; 
3)  Mitigation of bias caused by source code and user interfaces, where applicable; 
4)  Establishment and notification of evaluation metrics for performance degradation of 
the artificial intelligence system, where applicable. 
8.  Operation and Monitoring Related to AI/ML Functions 
The organization shall perform the necessary activities to ensure the safety and reliability 
during the operation and monitoring of AI/ML functions, including the following elements.  
1)  Provision of descriptions, such as purpose, scope, constraints, and disclaimers, to 
guide the proper use of the artificial intelligence system; 
2)  Establishment of traceability measures for the decision-making of the artificial 
intelligence system, such as system logs, where applicable.

[Annex 6] 
Selection of Core Products 
(Article 7) 
 
1. 
Where two or more products are applied for, the core product shall be selected in the following 
order for each product group of the relevant manufacturing site or manufacturer. 
(a)  Products that include artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) functions 
(b)  Products with the highest applicable classification 
(c)  Products with the highest production or import performance 
 
2.  Guidelines for selecting the core product 
(a)  Where multiple model names exist within the same product item, the product to be 
assessed shall be selected by comprehensively considering product characteristics, 
structure, raw materials, and other relevant factors. 
(b)  If the core product belonging to the highest classification level has no production or 
import performance, the product with the highest production or import performance 
among products of the next classification level shall be selected. 
(c)  If both the classification and production performance of the products under review are 
identical, the applicant shall select the core product in consultation with the head of the 
agency entrusted with certification-related duties.
